title: Bryce Young sore, will get tests on lower body injury
summary: Panthers quarterback Bryce Young never came out of Sunday's loss to the Browns, but he was moving gingerly after a sack in the first half and he'll be going for some tests to kick off this week.
full_text: ' Panthers quarterback Bryce Young never came out of Sunday's loss to the Browns, but he was moving gingerly after a sack in the first half and he'll be going for some tests to kick off this week. Head coach Dave Canales didn't specify what body part Young injured when he got kicked during the game and said that he thinks the quarterback will be fine for their Week 4 trip to Detroit, but that he'll get imaging done to make sure there's nothing more going on. "He was sore a little bit," Canales said. "I think he took a cleat, I can’t remember exactly where. There was some soreness, he was able to battle through it. Was able to finish. We're looking at him too, we're making sure everything's right." Canales confirmed that the Panthers are set to be without cornerback Jaycee Horn for an indefinite period of time due to a quad injury, so they'll be hoping that everything with Young comes back with positive news.
author: Josh Alper

title: The Vikings swung and missed in effort to find a franchise quarterback
summary: After the 2023 season, the Vikings decided to abandon the veteran quarterback rollercoaster for a potential franchise quarterback.
full_text: After the 2023 season, the Vikings decided to abandon the veteran quarterback rollercoaster for a potential franchise quarterback. The ride ended up being bumper cars without the bumpers. Minnesota had earned the 11th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Four quarterbacks had been drafted in the first eight picks. As the clock ticked toward their pick at No. 11, the Vikings feared being leapfrogged by the Broncos at No. 12. And so the Vikings gave up a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick to move up from No. 11 to No. 10. (They also received a seventh-rounder from the Jets as part of the deal.) They used the pick not to take Oregon quarterback Bo Nix, but to select Michigan quarterback J.J. McCarthy. His rookie season was lost to a meniscus injury during the preseason opener. And while the 2024 season went well with free-agent Sam Darnold stepping in, the Vikings opted to go all-in with McCarthy for 2025, allowing both Darnold and Daniel Jones to leave via free agency. McCarthy won his debut game on a Monday night in Chicago. A Week 2 loss in Atlanta resulted in an ankle injury that caused McCarthy to miss the next five games. He returned in Week 9 with an upset of the Lions in Detroit. Three straight losses followed, and a concussion in Green Bay caused McCarthy to miss what was a 26-0 low point in Seattle with undrafted rookie Max Brosmer at the helm. But then McCarthy returned. He won three in a row, missed the Christmas Day win over the Lions (Brosmer got a little redemption, but not much, in the defense-driven performance), and won the regular-season finale against the Packers. While the Vikings' postseason hopes were dashed after the shutout loss to the Seahawks, the Vikings finished strong under McCarthy. Still, the two-year body of work wasn't enough to keep the Vikings from pouncing on the opportunity to add Kyler Murray in free agency, on a bargain-basement deal (thanks to the Cardinals owing him more than $35 million in 2026). The competition between Murray and McCarthy lingered into training camp, with Murray getting the job in the days before the preseason opener. At that point, it seemed that a fresh start for McCarthy would be beneficial for both sides. The vibes were clearly off, even though the team and the player did their best to conceal any dysfunction. The fact that McCarthy slipped behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart underscored the reality that it was just a matter of time before McCarthy would be gone. Opportunity knocked after the Giants lost Jaxson Dart to a knee injury. Still, the Vikings got merely a fifth-round pick for McCarthy — after giving up the 11th pick in 2024, a fourth-round pick, and a fifth-round pick to get him (with the seventh-round pick in return). It's always prudent for a team that has made a mistake to admit it and move on. Doubling down helps no one. Still, there's a price to be paid for acknowledging to such a major blunder. And while no one knows what was happening behind the scenes, the early-season performances from Murray and Wentz suggested that maybe, at some point in 2026, the Vikings would have needed McCarthy to play. His absence puts more pressure on the team to make it work with Murray and/or Wentz (and, if necessary, with Brosmer). The Vikings also need to quietly hope that McCarthy doesn't become a competent contributor for the Giants. If he does, the Vikings would join the list of franchises that used a high pick on a rookie quarterback, failed to develop him, and folded the tents prematurely.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants to waive QB Jake Haener, intend to re-sign him to practice squad
summary: With the Giants trading for J.J.
full_text: With the Giants trading for J.J. McCarthy, the club will make another roster move to keep just two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, New York will waive Jake Haener but intend to re-sign him to the team's practice squad. Haener was promoted to the active roster on Saturday after Jaxson Dart suffered a long-term knee injury last Monday night. Haener, 27, joined the Giants in August after spending some time with the Chiefs during the offseason program. A fourth-round pick in 2023, Haener has appeared in eight career games with one start. All of his appearances came in 2024 with the Saints.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Todd Bowles: Baker Mayfield out a minimum of three weeks with thumb dislocation
summary: There is more clarity on Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield after he suffered a dislocated thumb late in Sunday’s loss to the Vikings.
full_text: There is more clarity on Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield after he suffered a dislocated thumb late in Sunday’s loss to the Vikings. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters in his Monday press conference that Mayfield will be out for a minimum of three weeks. “It’s consistent with everything we thought it was — a dislocation ,” Bowles said. According to multiple reporters on the Bucs beat, further tests on Mayfield’s thumb did not reveal a fracture or ligament damage. With the current timetable, the Buccaneers are not planning on placing Mayfield on injured reserve right now. But that could change. If the Bucs were to put Mayfield on IR, he’d be out for a minimum of four games. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is set to become the starter in Mayfield’s absence. “Well it’s going to be like every other rookie, but he’s played well in the preseason,” Bowles said. “He’s very bright. He’s not going to be out there by himself — there will be 22 other guys out there helping him out. So, we’re just expecting him to do his job, play at a high level, as he expects from himself.” Bowles added that the Buccaneers will likely add either a veteran or a practice squad quarterback. Only Mayfield and Daniels are on the 53-man roster with Easton Stick on the practice squad.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers CB Jaycee Horn to miss significant time with a quad injury
summary: The Panthers got good news about wide receiver Jalen Coker's quad injury, but cornerback Jaycee Horn did not fare as well.
full_text: ' The Panthers got good news about wide receiver Jalen Coker's quad injury, but cornerback Jaycee Horn did not fare as well. Horn also hurt his quad during Carolina's 21-18 loss to the Browns and multiple reports on Monday say that he has suffered a significant injury. It is believed to be a tear and Horn could be out for the rest of the season depending on what he hears as he solicits more opinions about the injury. Horn signed a four-year extension with the team this offseason, so his future with the club is secure even if he can't make it back on the field before the end of the season. He had six tackles and two pass breakups in his three appearances this year. Mike Jackson, Akayleb Evans and rookie Will Lee also saw time at corner on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Davante Adams: 1-2 start is "nothing to freak out about"
summary: When Davante Adams was a rookie on the Packers — way back in 2014 — the team got off to a 1-2 start.
full_text: When Davante Adams was a rookie on the Packers — way back in 2014 — the team got off to a 1-2 start. Green Bay’s quarterback then famously spelled out a word during a radio interview: “R-E-L-A-X.” Eventually, that Packers team went 12-4 in the regular season, beat the Cowboys in the divisional round, and lost a wild NFC Championship game to the Seahawks. It’s over a decade later, but perhaps that was somewhere in the back of Adams’ mind on Sunday night after the Rams lost to the Broncos, dropping Los Angeles’ record to 1-2. “Stay in, I mean, it’s nothing to freak out about,” Adams said, via transcript from the Broncos, when asked about the team’s 1-2 start. “There’s a lot of football left, and it’s not like we’re not playing good ball, obviously excluding that first game. “Unfortunately, I mean, I don’t know if it’s unfortunate, but based on our situation, unfortunately, this league is about wins and losses, so there’s a lot that we can take from a game like this and feel good about. But there’s no moral victories, so we’re definitely disappointed to not finish it out. But just to get back to what we do, and that’s going back to practice, get back to the drawing board and just find a way to finish off something again.” With Puka Nacua sidelined for the last couple of weeks due to injury, Adams has been the team’s top receiving option — recording back-to-back games of 100 yards for the first time since joining the team last offseason. While Nacua may be back for Week 4, the schedule will not get any easier, as the Rams will travel across the country to face the Eagles on Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Vikings send J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick
summary: Minnesota send 10th pick in 2024 to New York.
full_text: The J.J. McCarthy experiment in Minnesota has ended. In New York, it's just beginning. Per multiple reports, the Vikings have traded the tenth overall pick in the 2024 draft to the Giants. In return, the Vikings will receive a 2027 fifth-round pick. The Giants have a clear need at the position, given the knee injury that will keep Jaxson Dart out for at least the rest of the regular season. On Sunday, the starter was Jameis Winston, with Jake Haener as the understudy. In Minnesota, McCarthy lost the starting job to Kyler Murray before falling behind Carson Wentz to the third spot on the depth chart. From the moment McCarthy was benched, it seemed that he was on borrowed time in Minnesota — even though everyone involved was saying all the right things. For the Giants, the move brings the former Michigan quarterback (coached by Jim Harbaugh) to the NFL team coached by John Harbaugh. For now, Winston is the starter. Whether McCarthy gets an opportunity to play depends on whether Winston is injured — and whether Winston remains sufficiently effective.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Vrabel: Drake Maye needs to "relax"
summary: A year after finishing second in the NFL MVP voting, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye won't have to worry about nearly missing out on the award in 2026.
full_text: A year after finishing second in the NFL MVP voting, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye won't have to worry about nearly missing out on the award in 2026. Through three games of the the third season his career, Maye has regressed. Badly. Last year, he had 31 touchdown passes and eight interceptions. This year, he has one touchdown pass and six interceptions. His passer rating has plummeted from 113.5 to 58.6. Sunday's 35-6 disaster in Duval included three turnovers and no touchdowns. Appearing Monday on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show , coach Mike Vrabel was asked about Maye's obvious issues with decision-making. “I think quarterbacks want to make plays ," Vrabel said, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. "I think they want to throw touchdowns. I think sometimes when Greg and I go golfing, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we’re so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we’re squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways. We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren’t there.” It seems at this point to be more than bad decisions. Simms explained on Monday's PFT Live that Maye has developed mechanical flaws, including a flicking of the wrist before the makes his throws. Also, Simms believes Maye is trying too hard to guide his throws, in lieu of letting it rip. If the Patriots agree with the assessment, it won't be easy to coach these things out of Maye during football season, when there's a fresh train always heading down the tracks. And the next stop is Buffalo. Last year in Week 5, Maye led the Patriots to a win in their final game at the Bills' old stadium. This year in Week 4, Maye has a chance to reverse a troubling trend that has become a full-blown narrative.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dexter Lawrence: Our goal wasn't to go undefeated, we'll own this one
summary: Through two games, the Bengals’ defense looked like it had undergone a significant transformation in the offseason — partially due to the addition of Dexter Lawrence.
full_text: Through two games, the Bengals’ defense looked like it had undergone a significant transformation in the offseason — partially due to the addition of Dexter Lawrence. But then came Sunday’s divisional matchup against the Steelers, with Pittsburgh’s offense generating 411 yards — including 138 on the ground — en route to defeating Cincinnati 30-27. Lawrence, in his eighth pro season, provided some perspective after the game. “I think it's a reminder to show y'all that we’re not going to go undefeated ,” Lawrence said, via Jay Morrison of SI.com. “No year is gonna be perfect. … Our goal wasn’t to go undefeated. So we’ll own this one. We'll come back next week and go out there and play.” Lawrence added that Sunday’s performance “wasn’t us.” “We know we can't allow that; however it comes, however they try to do it,” Lawrence said. “We made a lot of mistakes, and that's what kept the game close and then ultimately helped them win. “A lot of what was going on was self-inflicted. … You watched the game. You know what happened. I don't think it was anything special that they had going on. We just didn't do well on our end.” The Bengals will get another tough opponent next week when the Jaguars come to Cincinnati.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mekhi Becton worked out for the Packers, will sign with the team
summary: The Packers signed guard Laken Tomlinson after last Thursday's loss to the Falcons and they may not be done adding to their offensive line options.
full_text: The Packers signed guard Laken Tomlinson after last Thursday's loss to the Falcons and they may not be done adding to their offensive line options. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that they had Mekhi Becton in for a workout on Monday morning. Becton signed a two-year deal with the Chargers as a free agent in 2025, but he was released in March. He started 14 games during his one season with the team and was the Eagles' right guard when they won the Super Bowl the previous year. Becton also has experience at tackle during his time with the Jets. He was picked in the first round by the Jets in 2020 and spent four years with the team, but missed all but one game in 2021 and 2022 due to injuries. UPDATE 11:39 a.m. ET : Fowler reports that Becton will sign with the Packers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Jalen Coker questionable for Week 4 with a quad strain
summary: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was able to play on Sunday after being listed as questionable due to an ankle injury, but a different injury brought his day to an early end.
full_text: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was able to play on Sunday after being listed as questionable due to an ankle injury, but a different injury brought his day to an early end. Coker left the 21-18 loss to the Browns in the third quarter after injuring his quad. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Coker has a relatively minor strain and that he is considered questionable to play against the Lions on Sunday night in Week 4 as a result. Panthers cornerback Jaycee Horn also suffered a quad injury on Sunday and head coach Dave Canales said after the game that he still needs to be evaluated. Coker had two catches for 18 yards on Sunday. He has 18 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns on the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills overcome five turnovers to defeat Chargers, 24-16
summary: While it was ugly for much of the afternoon, Buffalo was still able to defeat Los Angeles and move to 3-0.
full_text: It’s not often that a team can turn the ball over five times and win. But that’s exactly what happened in Buffalo on Sunday, with the Bills coming from behind to defeat the Chargers 24-16. Los Angeles was able to get off to a 10-0 lead after a fumble from James Cook on the first play from scrimmage and an interception on Buffalo’s third drive. But the Bills were able to tie it up at 10-10 with Josh Allen’s 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Allen had set it up with a 37-yard pass to Keon Coleman with little time before the break. The Bills had three turnovers in the first half. While they had two more fumbles in the second half, the Chargers punted after one and Justin Herbert threw an interception deep in the red zone on the second. Josh Allen powered his way in for another 1-yard touchdown with 7:35 left in the contest to give the Bills their first lead of the day. Then James Cook was actually allowed to run in a touchdown, taking it in from 3 yards out to put the game away. Aside from his fumble, Cook had an excellent day — rushing for 154 yards on 24 carries with his TD. Allen finished 16-of-26 for 204 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble. He had 22 yards on eight carries with two TDs. On the other side, Herbert was 20-of-34 for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception. That was Los Angeles’ lone giveaway of the game, but the +4 advantage in turnover margin was not enough. With the victory, the Bills are now 3-0. They’ll stay at home to host the Patriots next Sunday. The Chargers are 0-3 and staring down the barrel of a long season. They will be on the road to face the defending-champion Seahawks next Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Despite 1-2 start, Rams remain favorites to win the Super Bowl
summary: A disappointing start to the season hasn't changed the Rams' status as the Super Bowl favorites.
full_text: A disappointing start to the season hasn't changed the Rams' status as the Super Bowl favorites. After Sunday night's loss to the Broncos dropped the Rams' record to 1-2, the Rams remain the betting favorites to win it all. The Rams' current odds are +650, which are down from their +500 odds before the season, but still the best odds in the league to win the title. Although the Rams haven't looked like a Super Bowl team yet, it will be hard to bet against them in January if Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua are healthy, and Aaron Donald looks like the Aaron Donald of old. After the Rams, the next-best odds to win it all go to the Bills, at +700. They're followed by the 49ers and Ravens, both at +900, the Seahaks at +1000, the Chiefs at +1100, the Eagles at +1500, the Bengals at +1700, the Lions at +1900 and the Broncos at +2000.
author: Michael David Smith

title: De'Von Achane out for season with torn ACL
summary: Achane exited Sunday's game against the Chiefs in the first quarter.
full_text: The Dolphins will not have one of their best players for the rest of the season. Running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, according to a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network. Head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters in his postgame press conference that news about Achane’s injury did not sound optimistic . Achane went down during the first quarter of Sunday’s contest after recording an 11-yard reception. He was tackled awkwardly before coming off the field gingerly under his own power. The Dolphins signed Achane to a four-year $64 million contract extension during the offseason. Achane led the league with 5.7 yards per carry last season, rushing for 1,350 yards with eight touchdowns. He also caught 67 passes for 488 yards with four TDs in 2025. A third-round pick in 2023, Achane has appeared in 47 career games with 39 starts. He’s rushed for 3,184 yards with 22 touchdowns and caught 179 passes for 1,326 yards with 13 TDs.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Marcus Mariota and the Commanders stun the Seahawks 33-31
summary: A massive upset in Washington as the defending champions lose for the first time this season.
full_text: No Jayden Daniels? No problem for the Commanders today, as backup quarterback Marcus Mariota turned in an incredible effort against the stout Seahawks' defense, leading Washington to a 33-31 win. Mariota sealed the Commanders' win with a nine-yard run on third-and-7 with 1:15 remaining, and that was just the last of a number of spectacular plays by Mariota, who played very well against this Seahawks defense that has shut down so many quarterbacks over the last two years. The 32-year-old Mariota finished 19 of 31 for 183 yards, with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold returned from his Week 1 injury and completed 31 of 45 passes for 379 yards, with four touchdowns and two interceptions. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was, as usual, Darnold's favorite receiver, with 10 catches for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Today's game serves to show just how unpredictable the NFL is, especially early in the season, when there is still so much we don't know about every team. The Seahawks opened the season 2-0 and looking like perhaps the best team in the NFL. The Commanders entered today 0-2 and, without Daniels, looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL. But that's why they play the games.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens beat Cowboys 34-31 on final play in Brazil
summary: The Ravens had only 7 seconds when they got the ball back, but one play got Tyler Loop in position for 56-yard FG.
full_text: In one of the most exciting games of the season, the Ravens pulled out a miraculous 34-31 victory over the Cowboys on the final play in Brazil. Kicker Tyler Loop, who grew up in the Dallas area and had to live the offseason with a missed kick that ultimately kept the Ravens out of the playoffs, nailed a 56-yarder with no time left. After a touchback on the kickoff, the Ravens got the ball back with only seven seconds left. But Lamar Jackson worked his magic, connecting with Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain to the Cowboys 38. The Ravens got a timeout with one second left. It was the third lead change in the final two minutes and improved the Ravens' record to 2-1 and dropped the Cowboys to 1-2. First, Ravens rookie tight end Matt Hibner scored on a 2-yard pass from Jackson on third down to give Baltimore a 31-28 lead. It was too much time for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys. Dallas got a gift from the officials on the nine-play, 60-yard drive. Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins was in position for an interception with 23 seconds left, but Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb hooked Wiggins' arm. The CBS crew argued that it should have been offensive pass interference. Instead, officials threw the flag on Wiggins, giving the Cowboys the ball at the 2. A false start on tight end Luke Schoonmaker kept the Cowboys from a game-winning touchdown with two Prescott incompletions sandwiched between a 2-yard scramble. Brandon Aubrey kicked a chip-shot, 23-yard field goal with seven seconds left. That proved too much time for Jackson and the Ravens. The Cowboys stopped the Ravens twice on fourth down, and the Ravens stopped the Cowboys once on fourth down. The Cowboys had a field goal blocked and lost a controversial fumble that looked like it might have been an incompletion. The Cowboys outgained the Ravens 415 to 378 yards. Jackson was 15-of-20 for 186 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 50 yards on six carries. Zay Flowers catching five passes for 84 yards. Derrick Henry rushed for 89 yards and two touchdowns on 26 carries. Prescott went 25-of-40 for 276 yards and a touchdown. Lamb caught seven passes for 112 yards and George Pickens added seven receptions for 82 yards. Javonte Williams rushed for 98 yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Both teams had a number of significant injuries. The Ravens lost their top two centers late in the game, with both carted to the training room. The absences of Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and Ethan Pocic (knee) forced rookie right guard Olaivavega Ioane to move to center.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aaron Rodgers wins quarterback duel with Joe Burrow, Steelers beat Bengals 30-27
summary: Both quarterbacks played well, but Burrow's late fumble sealed the Bengals' loss.
full_text: Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow battled for 60 minutes today, but a Burrow fumble in the final minute sealed it. With the Steelers leading 30-27 but the Bengals driving with 53 seconds left, Burrow was sacked and fumbled, the Steelers recovered, and Pittsburgh won at home. Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards, with three touchdowns and one interception, a very different game than he had in the first two weeks of this season. Through two games, Rodgers looked old and unreliable, but today he came to life with an outstanding performance. Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions, but that late fumble will haunt him. Steelers running back Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards, and he almost had a much bigger game, but an 87-yard run was called back by a DK Metcalf holding penalty. The Steelers' win leaves both teams at 2-1 and tied for the lead in what looks like it will be a very competitive AFC North. If Rodgers can keep playing like he did today, the Steelers are going to be playoff contenders.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Chiefs take Dolphins' best punch, but move to 3-0 with 24-10 win
summary: The Dolphins were plenty competitive against the Chiefs for much of Sunday afternoon.
full_text: The Dolphins were plenty competitive against the Chiefs for much of Sunday afternoon. But Kansas City’s fourth-down defense proved to be a separator, allowing the club to come away with a 24-10 victory in South Florida. While Miami was able to sustain drives and gain plenty of yards, the club was 0-of-3 on fourth down with chances to pick up points. The Chiefs also picked up a key takeaway to halt a drive in the second quarter. With the score at 17-10 midway through the fourth quarter, Miami elected to go for it on fourth-and-5 from their own 48 with 6:00 left on the clock. But Malik Willis’ pass was incomplete, setting up the Chiefs with good field position. Kansas City took advantage of it, with Patrick Mahomes connecting with Travis Kelce for an 11-yard touchdown to put the game out of reach with 2:55 left in the contest. The Dolphins elected to go for it again on fourth down on their ensuing drive, but Chris Jones tipped Willis’ pass, and George Karlaftis came down with it for an interception to effectively end the game, though Harrison Butker missed a 50-yard field goal that would have given the club three more points. Mahomes was 20-of-24 for 246 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The pick went right off Rashee Rice’s hands and was tipped by another defender before Miami came down with the takeaway. Rice ended up leading the Chiefs with 88 yards on seven receptions. Kelce had two catches for 59 yards with his TD. On the other side, Willis was 20-of-36 for 210 yards with an interception. He also was the leading rusher with 56 yards on nine attempts. The Dolphins played most of the game without De’Von Achane, who exited the contest with a knee injury on the first drive. With the victory, Mahomes has 115 wins in his first 150 starts. That mark is tied with Tom Brady for No. 1 all-time, ahead of Joe Montana’s 108. It’s Kansas City’s fifth 3-0 start since Mahomes became the team’s starter in 2018. The Chiefs will be in Las Vegas next week to take on the division-rival Raiders. The Dolphins will also be on the road in Week 4, facing the Vikings.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Deshaun Watson: I just wanted to finish the game for the fans
summary: Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills.
full_text: Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills. On Sunday, they cheered him. Watson threw a 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 left to lift the Browns to a 21-18 upset of the Panthers. He finished with 144 yards and two touchdowns, along with 45 yards rushing on 11 carries. Winning makes everyone happy. " It was great . It was amazing. I just wanted to finish the job for them," Watson said of the fans, via Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. "There was one moment where I got a little teary-eyed, feeling that energy. I've put in so much work to get here, to be in this moment here and to be able to show I can finish these drives, and finish these games to get W's for this city and this organization. "This is what all the hard work, belief, prayers, everything that I have put myself through the last 22 months. To be able to stand in front of the crowd on that field and to finish the job. I want to keep improving and keep trying to get better each and every day, each week and we have a big one on Thursday [against the Steelers]." After the home fans booed him last month, Watson made it worse by calling it "disrespectful" and "personal." He apologized a few days later, saying his "emotions got the best of me." The only way to win them over was to play well and win, and Watson has done both. The Browns are tied for first place with the other three teams in the division at 2-1, and Watson has completed 63.8 percent of his passes for 587 yards with five touchdowns and one interception. He also has run for 105 yards. He is the first Browns quarterback since Baker Mayfield in Weeks 14 and 15 of 2018 to lead game-winning touchdown drives in the fourth quarter of consecutive games, according to ESPN Research. "We continued to feed off that energy of the crowd, and we wanted to make a special play," Watson said. "I told the guys in the huddle, 'Man, just [believe] in me and I'm going to use my legs.' Whenever that play comes up, make that play, and Harold did."
author: Charean Williams

title: Travis Hunter: "Little bit" of relief to get first interception
summary: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen's talk about giving Travis Hunter more to do in Week 3 didn't result in a major change to his role, but the 2025 first-round pick was able to check off one career milestone.
full_text: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen's talk about giving Travis Hunter more to do in Week 3 didn't result in a major change to his role, but the 2025 first-round pick was able to check off one career milestone. Hunter had the first interception of his NFL career while playing cornerback late in the first half. Hunter snagged a pass from Patriots quarterback Drake Maye to wide receiver Efton Chism in the end zone to keep the Jaguars up 14-3. The Jags went on to win 35-6 and Hunter, who also had four tackles, was asked after the game if it was a relief to finally get his first pick. "A little bit ," Hunter said. "Interceptions are great to catch, but I was focused on winning the game and just continue to focus on the next play." Hunter played five offensive snaps at wide receiver during the game and did not have a catch, but his hands served him well in his other role.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kirk Cousins throws 3 TDs, Raiders move to 3-0 with 35-27 victory over Saints
summary: For just the second time since 2002, the Raiders are 3-0.
full_text: For just the second time since 2002, the Raiders are 3-0. After entering the fourth quarter down 27-22, Las Vegas picked up four takeaways in the final period to defeat New Orleans 35-27. While the Raiders held a 16-13 lead at halftime, the Saints were able to score twice in quick succession in the third quarter to ostensibly take control of the game. Tyler Shough threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson before the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. Shough then connected with Noah Fant for a 16-yard score to put New Orleans up 27-16 with 5:46 left in the third quarter. But it was all Las Vegas from there. Mike Washington scored on a 36-yard touchdown run to cap a quick, five-play drive. The two-point conversion failed, keeping the score at 27-22, New Orleans. That’s when the turnovers began, with Shough losing the ball on a strip-sack in Las Vegas territory on third-and-4 from the Las Vegas 29. Kirk Cousins hit Cody White for a 4-yard touchdown to give the Raiders a 28-27 lead with 9:21 left in regulation. Down by one, Shough then threw an interception that set up Cousins’ 4-yard touchdown to Brock Bowers — who was making his 2026 debut — for a 35-27 lead. For the Saints’ third turnover, Shough was again strip-sacked with 2:21 left in regulation on fourth-and-1 deep in Las Vegas territory. And while the team got the ball back, Johnson fumbled with just under a minute left, and the Raiders recovered to clinch their victory. Sunday’s win was the first time the Raiders scored at least 30 points since defeating the Chargers 63-21 on a Thursday night in December 2023. As noted by the CBS broadcast, the game also tied an NFL record with six touchdown receptions by tight ends. The only other time that had happened was in 1981 in a matchup between the Chargers and Raiders. Cousins finished 22-of-33 for 248 yards with three touchdowns. That makes him the first QB in team history to record at least three passing TDs in each of the club’s first three games. He’s also the first since Lamar Jackson in 2022 to record at least three passing TDs in each of his team’s first three games. After undergoing a meniscus trim, Bowers was as excellent as ever, catching 10 passes on 13 targets for 116 yards with a TD. On the other side, Shough finished 29-of-42 for 255 yards with four touchdowns, an interception, and two lost fumbles. Chris Olave led with nine catches for 107 yards. At 3-0, the Raiders will host an AFC West showdown with the fellow 3-0 Chiefs next weekend. The 1-2 Saints will host the 1-2 Falcons next Monday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kevin O'Connell: Justin Jefferson "got close" to returning, ankle to be evaluated Monday
summary: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson left Sunday's game in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return before the end of Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers.
full_text: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson left Sunday's game in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return before the end of Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers. At a postgame press conference, head coach Kevin O'Connell said that Jefferson "got close" to returning to the game but was ultimately ruled out. O'Connell also said that Jefferson will be evaluated more on Monday. Mike Florio reported on Football Night in America that an MRI will be part of that evaluation and that the Vikings hope Jefferson is dealing with a low-ankle injury. Jefferson had two catches for 32 yards before leaving the game. He has 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season,.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys take 28-24 lead after fourth-down stop of Ravens
summary: The Cowboys were dead in the water, thisclose to being down 10 points.
full_text: The Cowboys were dead in the water, thisclose to being down 10 points. But their beleaguered defense rose up when the Cowboys needed it most. Rookie Jaishawn Barham and defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia teamed up to keep Derrick Henry out of the end zone on a third-and-goal run from the 2. The play was initially ruled a touchdown but reversed on replay review. The Ravens went for it on fourth down, and Braham met Henry in the backfield for a 3-yard loss. The Cowboys needed only seven plays to go 96 yards, with KaVontae Turpin running it in from the 9. They have scored the last 15 points to take a 28-24 lead. The Ravens led 24-13 before Jake Ferguson's 19-yard touchdown reception. Dak Prescott is 22-of-33 for 240 yards and a touchdown, with CeeDee Lamb catching six passes for 98 yards. George Pickens has seven receptions for 82 yards. Javontae Williams has 19 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers improve to 3-0 with hard-fought win over Cardinals
summary: It wasn't as easy as expected, but San Francisco managed to win at home against Arizona.
full_text: In the first two weeks of the season, the 49ers dominated. In Week 3, they had to gut out a surprisingly tough win. Despite the 49ers jumping out to a 14-0 lead, the Cardinals weren't going to go down without a fight, and the game was close until the final moments, when the 49ers finally finished out a 36-30 win. San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy turned in another strong game, throwing for 297 yards with four touchdown passes and no interceptions. Purdy also ran for a 45-yard touchdown late in the game, although that touchdown was called back and turned into only a 35-yard gain because George Kittle was holding deep downfield. Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett also deserves credit for his performance in a losing effort, throwing two touchdown passes and keeping the game close deep into the fourth quarter. The injury-prone 49ers lost wide receiver Mike Evans with a rib injury, which has to be a big concern. They also saw left tackle Trent Williams leave with a stinger, although he was back on the sideline in the second half and looked OK. The 49ers also may be concerned about kicker Eddy Pineiro, who hit a 57-yard field goal but also missed two extra points. At 3-0, the 49ers are one of the best teams in the NFL. The 1-2 Cardinals are playing better than people expected, but they're still a distant fourth in the NFC West.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sunday Night Football: Marvin Mims, Puka Nacua inactive for Broncos-Rams
summary: Both the Rams and Broncos will be without a key receiver on Sunday night in Week 3.
full_text: Both the Rams and Broncos will be without a key receiver on Sunday night in Week 3. Denver’s Marvin Mims and Los Angeles’ Puka Nacua are both inactive for the matchup between the two clubs. Mims is dealing with a foot injury. Nacua has a psoas injury, but could return soon. Denver’s inactives are Mims, quarterback Sam Ehlinger, receiver Lil'Jordan Humphrey, defensive lineman Sai'Vion Jones, offensive lineman Kage Casey, tight end Dallen Bentley, and defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim. Ehlinger is the emergency third quarterback. For the Rams, Nacua, safety Kam Kinchens, receiver CJ Daniels, receiver, Tutu Atwell, quarterback Ty Simpson, safety Maximus Pulley, and offensive lineman Bill Murray. Simpson is Los Angeles’ emergency third quarterback.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Sean McVay didn't have much to say after Sunday night's loss
summary: Anyone hoping to hear a detailed breakdown of why the Rams blew a 16-point halftime lead in Sunday night's loss to the Broncos was left disappointed by head coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference.
full_text: Anyone hoping to hear a detailed breakdown of why the Rams blew a 16-point halftime lead in Sunday night's loss to the Broncos was left disappointed by head coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference. McVay spent about 90 seconds on the podium after the 30-26 loss in Denver and fielded a couple of questions before signing off. The answers to those questions didn't provide much insight into what went wrong for the Rams. “It’s tough, you know what, but this is sports," McVay said. "You sign up for all of it. Love our group, just came up short. Give the Broncos credit, they found a way to get it done. We’ll look at ourselves and figure out how we can improve.” Media members covering the Rams noted that McVay started his press conference before most of them had made it down from the press box — reporters are informed that they should begin making their way down with five minutes left in the game, but it's up to them whether to do it — and that he wrapped it up as they were getting into the room. That's unusual for McVay, who usually has a fair amount to say after games and the brevity may be a sign of how disappointed he was in how the team performed while falling to 1-2 on the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drake Maye attributes fumble to blood on the ball
summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had an unusual moment on Sunday, when he cocked his arm to throw and his hand came forward without the ball in it.
full_text: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had an unusual moment on Sunday, when he cocked his arm to throw and his hand came forward without the ball in it. After the game, Maye had an unusual explanation for it. "[Center] Jared [Wilson] happened to be bleeding on his hand," Maye said. "Got the football and was trying to put one to [receiver] Kyle [Wiliams]. And [it] slipped out of my hand ." It's a twist on Brucie from The Longest Yard, when he attributed his lost grip on the ball to just eating popcorn. Either way, Patriots fans were likely choking on their popcorn while watching Maye's latest performance. The Patriots are now 1-2. And they face the Bills in Buffalo next weekend.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Commanders LB Leo Chenal to have season-ending neck surgery
summary: Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was put on a stretcher and carted off the field during Sunday's home win with a neck injury that will reportedly end his season.
full_text: '' Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was put on a stretcher and carted off the field during Sunday's home win with a neck injury that will reportedly end his season. Chenal could be seen moving his arms and legs as he was on his way out of the stadium, but multiple reports on Monday say that he needs surgery that will keep him off the field for the rest of the year. NFL reporter Jordan Schultz had the initial report about the surgery and reported that Chenal suffered a fracture in his neck. The injury occurred when Chenal dropped his head to tackle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson. He stayed down after the play and was surrounded by teammates as medical personnel responded to the situation. Chenal signed with the Commanders this offseason after spending four years with the Chiefs. He had 18 tackles this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colts kick late FG to pull out 19-17 win over Texans
summary: Colts kicker Spencer Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero.
full_text: Colts kicker Spencer Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero. He kicked field goals of 39, 58, 37 and 53 in the Colts' 19-17 victory over the Texans. His final field goal came with 16 seconds left. The Colts are now 1-2, while the Texans fell to 0-3 for the second consecutive season. Houston rallied to make the playoffs last season, but the odds are against them to do it again. The Colts, who led 13-7 at halftime and 16-7 midway through the fourth quarter, had the lead until 1:48 remained. C.J. Stroud directed a seven-play, 54-yard drive with Woody Marks scoring on a 1-yard run. The Texans, though, botched the kickoff, with Ka'imi Fairbairn kicking it into the end zone. That allowed the Colts to start their game-winning drive at their own 35. DeMeco Ryans then botched the clock management, failing to use his first timeout after Jonathan Taylor's run left more than a minute on the clock. Ryans finally called the timeout with 29 seconds remaining. It left too little time for the Texans to get into field goal range, and Stroud's Hail Mary throw on the final play was both short and out of bounds. The Colts outgained the Texans 300 to 223 yards, with Daniel Jones going 24-of-36 for 235 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also lost two fumbles, though the Texans turned it over on downs after the first one. Jonathan Taylor had 23 carries for 68 yards, and Josh Downs caught five passes for 77 yards. Adetomiwa Adebawore and DeForest Buckner each had 1 1/2 sacks of Stroud. Stroud was 16-of-27 for 167 yards and a touchdown. David Montgomery had 11 carries for 33 yards, and Xavier Hutchinson caught three passes for 51 yards. Texans defensive end Will Anderson had 2.5 sacks of Jones.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean Payton: We have to find a way to play better earlier
summary: The Broncos were down 16-0 against the Rams at halftime on Sunday night, but they put up 30 points in the final 30 minutes to close out the game with their second straight win.
full_text: The Broncos were down 16-0 against the Rams at halftime on Sunday night, but they put up 30 points in the final 30 minutes to close out the game with their second straight win. The first of those wins played out in similar fashion. The Jaguars led the Broncos 13-3 in Week 2, but Denver rallied to score the final 17 points of the game and the two wins now give them 10 fourth quarter comeback wins since Bo Nix became the team's starting quarterback. After the game, Payton said he likes that Nix is at his best in those moments but he believes that the Broncos "have to find a way to play better earlier" because continually falling behind is a recipe for disaster in the long term. "I'm pleased with how we responded ," Payton said. "We can't, like — it’ll cost us in bigger games against teams that are playing better later in the season. It will be something we're frustrated about later if we can't clean it up." Next week's trip to visit the 3-0 49ers would be a good time for the Broncos to show they can hit the ground running rather than giving the opposition a sizable head start.

title: Rams' Matthew Stafford makes surprise cameo in Taylor Swift's new music video
summary: Swift's connection to the NFL continues to grow
full_text:
Taylor Swift fans and football fans might have more in common than you may think. One thing they have in common is that they love to review tape.
For Swifties, this means going back to her music videos, posts and award speeches to find any hint they can at the next album or era. They look for parallels, significant numbers, reoccurring characters, hand signals and colors to painstakingly find every detail they can.
Football fans do this too, reviewing tape to analyze all three phases of the game, looking deep into pocket time, coverages, penalties, missed calls, coaching decisions and stats from each game.
Swifties and NFL fans have collided a lot as of late and her newest music video is just another example. Swift premiered her music video for "Patient Zero" during the Video Music Awards on Sunday night, at the same time the Los Angeles Rams were taking on the Denver Broncos at Mile High Stadium.
Since nothing gets past Swift fans or football fans, they both noticed a familiar face in the video.
As Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford was on the field, he was also on the big screen at the VMAs, with a cameo in the "Patient Zero" music video. His performance in the music video may have exceeded his performance on Sunday Night Football, as he went 30-for-55 for 390 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in the 30-26 loss.
🚨 | LA Rams Quarterback Matthew Stafford makes a cameo in the Patient Zero music video. pic.twitter.com/RzivHcRN7b
Stafford attended Swift and Kansas City Chiefs star tight end Travis Kelce's July 3 wedding with his wife Kelly, who was also seen in the music video. The Staffords have four daughters, who are known Swift fans, so no doubt they were thrilled to see their parents in a music video.
Could Stafford's appearance in the music video be yet another easter egg from the famous singer? I wouldn't put it past her.
Sunday was a big night for the Swift-Kelce household. Swift won Video of the Year for "The Fate of Ophelia" and Kelce and the Chiefs defeated the Miami Dolphins 24-10 to remain a perfect 3-0 on the season. Swift could not attend the game because she was too busy winning the Artist Director Award at the VMAs, but she could be at their Week 4 game against the Las Vegas Raiders , as she has already made game appearances this year.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: J.J. McCarthy experiment unraveled after only 10 starts in Minnesota; can QB pick up the pieces with Giants?
summary: Minnesota bet on the flashes that made McCarthy a top-10 pick. Two years and 10 starts later, he's been traded to the Giants
full_text:
There was always going to be projection involved with J.J. McCarthy .
Two years later, the projection is over in Minnesota. The Vikings traded the quarterback they drafted 10th overall to the Giants on Monday for a 2027 fifth-round pick, ending an unusually short tenure after just 10 NFL starts. McCarthy survived roster cuts in August, but he entered the season behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz , and Minnesota has now officially moved on from a quarterback it traded up to select just 29 months ago.
For the Giants, this is a low-cost swing on a 23-year-old former top-10 pick after losing Jaxson Dart for the season. And it's another chance for McCarthy to prove he can play in the league. For Minnesota, though, the trade answers the question that has followed McCarthy since the Vikings signed Murray this offseason: how long were they willing to keep waiting?
Michigan won a national championship in McCarthy's final college season, went 15-0 and beat Ohio State, Alabama and Washington along the way. McCarthy completed 72.3% of his passes, threw 22 touchdowns against four interceptions and entered the NFL as a 21-year-old with athleticism, arm talent, toughness and a reputation as a winner.
The question was never whether McCarthy could make NFL throws. The question was how often he could make them when his team needed him most.
Michigan rarely required that. McCarthy attempted 332 passes during that 15-game championship season, fewer than 24 per game. During the Wolverines' final four games against Ohio State, Iowa, Alabama and Washington, he threw for a combined 656 yards. He was efficient, protected the football and made several big-time throws in big moments, but the offense was built around its running game, defense and an infrastructure that rarely asked its quarterback to carry the operation.
That was part of my concern in 2024. McCarthy was my QB5 with a second-round grade because the traits were there, but there was still a considerable gap between what Michigan asked of him and what an NFL team would require of him as the face of the franchise.
The tape showed a good athlete with a live-enough arm who could create outside structure and, at times, make high-level throws. But we also saw a quarterback who could become frenetic in clean pockets, struggle to layer the second-level throws and hesitate to pull the trigger on tight-window opportunities. At times, it felt like he didn't trust himself.
There was one area, though, where McCarthy looked much more like the quarterback Minnesota eventually believed it was drafting. On third-and-6-to-10 yards during his final Michigan season, he completed 70% of his passes with five touchdowns, no interceptions and 25 first downs. The ball consistently came out on time, he understood leverage, and there were high-level, tight-window throws on tape that seemed to elude him in other situations. Michigan didn't ask him to carry the offense from snap to snap, but on obvious passing downs, the Wolverines trusted him to make the play -- and more often than not, he did.
That's what made McCarthy so interesting. The best version wasn't theoretical -- it was on the tape if you were willing to look. The issue was how often it showed up. There was a substantial difference between seeing McCarthy make NFL-caliber throws in high-leverage situations and projecting him to consistently operate an NFL offense when those throws were required over and over again.
My second-round grade reflected that gap and the concerns that come with the pressure and expectation of going in Round 1. Minnesota looked at many of the same traits and decided the combination of McCarthy's age, athleticism, arm talent, winning background and flashes of advanced quarterback play was worth betting on much earlier.
The Vikings selected him 10th overall.
And in some ways, the environment made the gamble easier to understand. Kevin O'Connell was one of the league's most respected offensive coaches, and Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson gave McCarthy a collection of weapons. Minnesota appeared as capable as any organization -- including the Rams and 49ers -- of providing the quarterback-friendly infrastructure young passers rarely inherit. If the unanswered parts of McCarthy's game could be developed, there weren't many better places for it to happen.
Instead, the questions from Michigan followed him to the NFL -- and became much harder to hide. Before Minnesota could even begin answering them, McCarthy's rookie season ended before it began.
A torn meniscus suffered during the preseason required surgery and cost him all of 2024. Sam Darnold took over, had the best season of his career and helped Minnesota win 14 games. That created the first major organizational inflection point. The Vikings could have tried to keep Darnold. They instead allowed him to sign with Seattle and handed the offense to McCarthy in 2025.
That's when projection finally had to become production. It never did.
After McCarthy's first six starts last season, the numbers were staggering . Among 35 first-round quarterbacks since 2016 who received meaningful playing time during their first two seasons, McCarthy ranked 34th in EPA per dropback, 34th in turnover-worthy-play rate and last in both interceptions and passer rating. He also had one of the league's worst sack rates despite pressure arriving relatively late, suggesting many of the negative plays weren't simply an offensive line problem. The same pocket issues that appeared intermittently at Michigan now felt all-consuming in Minnesota.
There were flashes, which made the evaluation even more frustrating. McCarthy's EPA and turnover-worthy play rate both ranked in the eighth percentile among quarterbacks going back to 2015, yet his 7.3% big-time throw rate ranked in the 96th percentile. That's basically McCarthy's career in one statistic: the high-end throws were real, but there was far too much bad football between them.
That was the challenge entering this offseason. He didn't need to develop some new superpower. He needed to become more accurate, play on time, manage pressure better and stop letting negative plays overwhelm everything else.
Minnesota apparently decided it couldn't wait. The Vikings signed former No. 1 overall pick Kyler Murray and called the competition legitimate. McCarthy spent the offseason talking about controlling what he could control and improving one rep at a time, while Jefferson said their private work together had helped McCarthy with timing and route anticipation. But Jefferson also offered the more telling assessment: McCarthy "has to step it up a bit."
That was in late April, months before the competition was decided. Jefferson said the added pressure could force McCarthy to "really lock in a little bit," then added: "It's either now or I'm going to take that back seat again."
This wasn't simply another developmental season. It was McCarthy's chance to show Minnesota he was ready to take the job and keep it. But by Aug. 11, the competition was over. O'Connell named Murray the starter before the Vikings had even played a preseason game .
The team insisted that didn't mean they were giving up on McCarthy. O'Connell said his "development and ongoing growth" remained important and called McCarthy an "incredibly important member" of the quarterback room. But actions matter more than August press-conference diplomacy. Naming Murray the starter before Year 3 made clear how dramatically Minnesota's view of McCarthy had changed.
Then it somehow got worse.
McCarthy went 5 of 10 for 81 yards against Baltimore in the preseason, including a 50-yard completion, but again struggled with accuracy and left the game after getting banged up. An ankle injury subsequently kept him out of the preseason finale against Denver. Meanwhile, Carson Wentz began splitting second-team work with him, turning the question from whether McCarthy could win back the starting job to whether he would even enter…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: J.J. McCarthy trade: Giants acquire Vikings QB in wake of Jaxson Dart injury
summary: The Giants will add a former first-round pick to an ailing quarterback group
full_text:
The New York Giants are set to trade for Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy as they attempt to rebuild their signal-caller group in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury. The Giants will send a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Vikings in exchange for the former first-round quarterback. The trade is pending a physical, per the Vikings.
Whether McCarthy steps in as the Giants' starter is to be determined. New York rolled out Jameis Winston in Week 3, but the offense was mostly lifeless in the 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans . All of the Giants' points came by way of field goals.
McCarthy has the pedigree of a potential mid-career breakout as a former No. 10 overall pick, but his Minnesota career was a bust. It would be a surprise if he ever delivered on the high expectations that followed him out of college. The Giants will give him an opportunity to attempt a career revitalization after he slipped to No. 3 on the Vikings' depth chart behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz .
The Giants now have three former first-round picks on their roster, which places them in rare company. Only six other teams in the common draft era constructed their offense in the same fashion.
Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy
Daniel Jones , Anthony Richardson , Philip Rivers
Lamar Jackson , Joe Flacco , Robert Griffin III
Carson Palmer , Jason Campbell, Kyle Boller
Ken O'Brien, Tony Eason, Mark Malone
Jim McMahon, Steve Fuller, Greg Landry
Jim Plunkett, Dan Pastorini, Marc Wilson
Injuries derailed McCarthy's tenure in Minnesota and limited him to just 10 starts over two-plus seasons. He missed his entire rookie campaign with a torn meniscus, and sat nearly half of his second season due to a concussion, wrist fracture and ankle sprain. In the small amount of time he was healthy, McCarthy completed just 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns to 12 interceptions. He also rushed for 181 yards and four scores.
The Giants reportedly made calls across the league this week in search of an addition to their quarterback group and landed on McCarthy over other backups like Justin Fields , Jimmy Garoppolo , Gardner Minshew II and Mac Jones , all of whom have more experience but less potential long-term upside than McCarthy.
If this trade turns into a home run, it is a monumental win for both McCarthy and the Giants. That outcome would start with McCarthy eventually overtaking Winston for the starting job, finding success in a new offense and leading the Giants to a handful of wins. With standouts including Malik Nabers , Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely on his squad, the talent around him could help unlock the breakthrough season that evaded him in Minnesota. A change of scenery is also, in some cases, all it takes to spark progress.
Not only would McCarthy establish himself as a viable starter heading into the final year of his contract, but the Giants would also have tremendous flexibility. They could flip him again and recoup more than the fifth-round pick they traded to acquire him, or they could hold onto him as a premier backup on an expiring deal in 2027.
More realistically, though, the low-stakes bet will not pay dividends. McCarthy could not find his footing even with a superstar receiver in Justin Jefferson by his side, so in that context there is no reason to expect him to reach a new gear without arguably the best wideout in the sport. His development might be permanently stunted because of the recurring injuries, and he could struggle to stay on rosters beyond the end of his contract. It is no guarantee that he will outperform Winston and hold onto the starting role in the first place.
John Harbaugh and Jim Harbaugh have a tendency to look out for each other when it comes to personnel moves. They are known to consult with each other on player acquisitions, and considering McCarthy won a College Football Playoff national championship with Jim Harbaugh at Michigan, it is hard to imagine John Harbaugh did not touch base with his brother on what kind of quarterback he might receive if his team pulled off the trade.
McCarthy joins a laundry list of players to call both brothers their coach. The following are among the notable others who played for both of them.
Perhaps this should provide optimism for McCarthy's outlook in New York. The last coach to get the most out of him was a Harbaugh, so maybe the other can rekindle some of that fire. Granted, there is a difference between winning a championship with McCarthy at the college level and winning games with him in the NFL .
It was only two years ago that McCarthy flew off the draft board as the No. 10 pick in a class that produced six first-round quarterbacks. Now he is a backup who commanded a fifth-rounder on the trade market. The Vikings cut bait after just 10 starts, accepted their failure in using a top pick on a bust and elected to move forward with Murray and Wentz.
McCarthy did not play enough in 2025 to qualify, but his 35.6 QBR in his only season of action with the Vikings would have ranked 27th in the NFL, ahead of only Geno Smith and Cam Ward . That was all Minnesota needed to see in order to move on from him, and it was all the rest of the league needed to see to reset his value.
author: Carter Bahns

title: J.J. McCarthy trade grades: QB could be a downgrade for Giants, Vikings get a clean split
summary: New York is sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to Minnesota for McCarthy
full_text:
The New York Giants were rumored to be making calls all across the NFL in search of some quarterback help, and they've supposedly found their move. On Monday, the club agreed to a trade with the Minnesota Vikings to land former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy . In exchange, New York is sending out a 2027 fifth-round pick.
This all comes after the Giants lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season due to a knee injury he suffered in Week 2. While initially thought to not be too serious, further examination showed the injury was more severe, and Dart has since undergone surgery that'll put him on the shelf for the rest of the year.
That stretched New York's quarterback depth very thin, with Jameis Winston the only other quarterback on the active roster at the time of Dart's injury. Winston got the start in Week 3's win over the Titans on Sunday, with Jake Haener backing him up after being elevated from the practice squad. Despite squeaking out the victory, Winston wasn't sharp and completed just 14 of his 22 passes for 118 yards and no touchdowns.
It's unclear whether McCarthy will come in and usurp Winston as QB1, but it does give the Giants another option, adding someone with 10 career starts under his belt.
This deal puts to bed McCarthy's humdrum tenure in Minnesota. During the 2024 NFL Draft , the Vikings moved up to the No. 10 overall pick to select the Michigan product as their QB of the future. That investment never saw returns, as a knee injury erased his entire rookie season. Then, as they turned the keys over to him in 2025 and allowed Sam Darnold -- who led them to a 14-3 record the previous year -- to leave in free agency, McCarthy struggled mightily. Last season, the team finished with a 9-8 record (6-4 in McCarthy's starts) and missed the playoffs.
That led the Vikings to sign Kyler Murray this offseason, and the veteran was named the starter in the early days of training camp. After McCarthy was relegated to QB3 behind Carson Wentz , the writing was on the wall. He had no future in Minnesota, and a departure -- like we've seen here -- was inevitable.
With this deal now executed, let's figure out who came out on top. Below, you can find our grades for this early-season trade between two NFC squads.
It really depends on how the Giants view McCarthy coming aboard. Is he simply providing depth? Or are they eyeing him to leapfrog Winston on the depth chart and be New York's starter the rest of the way? If it's the latter, it's a risky roll of the dice. While Winston did not look good coming in under duress for Dart in Week 2 or even in Week 3 against Tennessee, there's no guarantee McCarthy is an upgrade. He might even be a downgrade. Sure, he's younger (still only 23 years old), but when he's been on the field thus far, he's left little to be desired.
Last season, McCarthy ranked last among qualified quarterbacks in completion percentage (58%), touchdowns-to-interceptions (11-12), and passer rating (72.6).
Of course, there is a Michigan/Harbaugh connection here. McCarthy played under Jim Harbaugh at Michigan, and the two won a national championship together in 2023. Naturally, one would think Giants head coach John Harbaugh gave his brother a call to vet McCarthy before making this deal, and the current Chargers head coach probably gave the green light.
While it's always possible McCarthy is the latest castoff QB to catch lightning in a bottle and resurrect his career, this feels like a lateral move right now.
It felt like J.J. McCarthy's trade value was nonexistent, so the fact that the Vikings are getting something for him should be looked at as a win. While landing a Day 3 pick will hardly change the fortunes of the franchise, getting a fifth-rounder in what is billed as a loaded 2027 draft isn't nothing. If New York craters post-Dart and with this Winston/McCarthy combination under center, Minnesota could be looking at a pick inside the top 150. They also clear about $4.6 million in cash and cap space.
While McCarthy was already established as QB3, the Vikings moving on from their former first-rounder also removes any potential tension in the QB room. It makes the pecking order of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz as the top two options crystal clear. That aspect of the trade can't be overlooked either.

title: Bucs' Baker Mayfield to miss several weeks after injuring throwing hand during loss to Vikings
summary: An MRI on Monday revealed no significant damage, but Mayfield is expected to miss three weeks with a thumb injury
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without their starting quarterback for a bit. Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield injured the thumb on his throwing hand near the end of the Buccaneers' Week 3 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings and is expected to miss three weeks, according to head coach Todd Bowles.
The MRI he had on Monday revealed there was no fracture and no ligament nor tendon damage, according to ESPN .
The next three games for the Buccaneers are against the Green Bay Packers , Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers . Mayfield would seemingly be good to go, based on Bowles' current timeline, for their game on Oct. 25 against the Carolina Panthers .
The injury took place with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. Facing a fourth-and-13 down four points, Mayfield bought time in the backfield before throwing an interception to Andrew Van Ginkel while being hit. The Bucs' quarterback was seen writhing on the ground in pain and heard screaming as he grasped at his right hand. Mayfield eventually walked off the field with trainers and headed straight for the locker room.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels replaced him under center on the Bucs' next possession. He rushed once for nine yards and failed to complete any of his three passing attempts, including a Hail Mary attempt that was intercepted by Isaiah Rodgers
Baker Mayfield headed to the locker room after an apparent injury 🙏 pic.twitter.com/E4Kcyclbcn
Mayfield completed 17 of 34 passes for 217 yards, one touchdown and one interception before exiting the game. It's been a tough start to the season for the Buccaneers, as they began with losses to the Cincinnati Bengals , Cleveland Browns and Vikings to move to 0-3. Just three weeks ago, Mayfield signed a three-year contract extension that averages $55 million — tying him as the No. 3 highest-paid quarterback in the NFL .
This is the Buccaneers' first 0-3 start since 2014, and they are the sixth team in the past decade to start 0-3 with all three losses coming in one-score games, per CBS Sports Research.

title: De'Von Achane out for season: After losing best player, are Dolphins bound to go 0-17?
summary: Achane's torn ACL could be a death blow for a dreadful roster
full_text:
The 2026 season was always going to be a slog for the Miami Dolphins . A miserable 0-3 start with all three losses coming by double digits cemented that outlook. The Dolphins were non-competitive at full strength, and now they will reportedly be without star running back De'Von Achane for the rest of the year after he sustained a torn ACL in the Week 3 defeat against the Kansas City Chiefs . This campaign could go from terrible to abysmal.
Achane is the most talented player on the Dolphins' roster, and it is not particularly close. The versatile back led the NFL last season in yards per carry and is among the league's most prolific pass-catchers out of the backfield. He was set to be the lifeblood of a young and inexperienced offense. Without him, Miami will find it dreadfully difficult to move the ball.
The Dolphins had a rough go offensively even with Achane in the lineup. They have yet to score more than 13 points in a game, their leading rusher in each contest managed no more than 74 yards, quarterback Malik Willis does not have a game above 220 passing yards and no receiver owns a 100-yard outing. This franchise is in the midst of a talent drain, and Achane's injury exacerbates the issue.
Entering the year, there was a strong argument to be made that this Miami roster is the worst collection of talent the NFL has ever seen . Now it lacks its best player.
The chances of Miami going winless in 2026 are modest simply because it is incredibly difficult to lose 17 games. No team has gone 0-17 since the NFL expanded its regular season in 2021. Before that, the Cleveland Browns were the last squad to lose every contest, and that came in the 16-game 2017 campaign. But if any franchise can be the first to drop every matchup on a 17-game schedule, it is this one.
Severe financial strain prevented the Dolphins from constructing a competitive roster in the offseason. The dead money tied to the contracts of Tua Tagovailoa , Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle and myriad other departed stars totals $183 million, which is by far the largest sum in NFL history. Miami allocated a whopping 60% of its salary cap space to dead money. No team had ever before even gone above the 45% mark.
With so little money to go around, the Dolphins scoured the scrap heap in free agency and allocated its spending to an NFL-leading 13 draft picks. In turn, this is the least experienced team in the league, the youngest roster and the squad with the fewest Pro Bowlers. Achane was the only player to earn a Pro Bowl selection, and now he is unavailable. High-end talent is nonexistent without him.
Based on 2025 win totals, the Dolphins drew the second-toughest schedule in the NFL with an opponent win percentage of .054. It is still early enough in the season that records have not yet normalized, but Miami faces the 11th-toughest remaining schedule by this year's win percentages. Two matchups with the Buffalo Bills are the most daunting games that lie ahead, and contests against the Denver Broncos , Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions are also formidable, to name just a few.
The first game without Achane lines up to be a potential disaster, too. The Dolphins hit the road in Week 4 to take on the Minnesota Vikings , who lead the league in EPA per play allowed and quarterback pressure rate. Willis will be under duress all game against Brian Flores' blitz-happy unit and will not have his Pro Bowl running back to alleviate that stress.
Miami may not be favored in a single game this year. In fact, it will likely be a multi-score underdog in nearly all of them. It faces a 10-point spread against Minnesota this week.
These games project as the most winnable opportunities on the gauntlet:
DraftKings still lists the Dolphins' season win total at 3.5, but to get to four, they would need to reign victorious in all but one of the games above or steal at least one against a postseason hopeful. The best opportunity to pull off a surprise arguably comes in the Week 8 home date with the New England Patriots , who are off to a slow start of their own.
Even flirting with the projected win total is a tall ask for a team that invested so little in its roster. It has to win one before it dreams of winning three or four, and even that seems like a stretch.

title: Buccaneers mired in historically poor 12-game stretch as 0-3 start, Baker Mayfield injury emphasize woes
summary: Tampa Bay defied expectations for the worse dating to the 2025 bye week
full_text:
At their bye week in 2025, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were 6-2 and headed toward a postseason berth. From that point forward, hardly anything has gone their way. The Buccaneers are off to an 0-3 start to begin the 2026 season, their coach is under immense scrutiny, their starting quarterback has a dislocated thumb and the last 12 games have been as disappointing as they come.
In the time since that bye week, the Buccaneers are 0-12 against the spread. That is the longest streak without a cover in the Super Bowl era, according to Action Network . Tampa Bay was the betting favorite in eight of those games and lost each of them outright, including the three where it was a favorite of at least a touchdown.
The struggles are not isolated to the point spread, either. The Buccaneers are just 2-10 outright in that same stretch. But coach Todd Bowles says the first nine games in that sample size are irrelevant to the direction of the franchise.
"We understand that, but it's this season now," Bowles said on Sunday after a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . "Nothing counts last year no matter who you are."
From the perspective of making the 2026 postseason, yes, last year's record has no bearing on what this edition of the Buccaneers can accomplish. But the abysmal conclusion to 2025 also provides important context for this team's momentum. It is why Bowles is widely viewed to have limited job security and why there is an argument to be made that Tampa Bay should not have invested so heavily in its contract extension for quarterback Baker Mayfield .
Mayfield and the Buccaneers were locked into a high-profile contract standoff this summer that appeared as though it would carry into the regular season. The sides surprisingly got a deal done just ahead of Week 1, and they agreed on a lucrative three-year extension that placed Mayfield in a tie as the third-highest-paid quarterback in the NFL on a per-year basis at $55 million.
At his best, Mayfield is worth every penny. He was a dark-horse MVP candidate as recently as two years ago and earned two Pro Bowl selections in his first two years with the franchise. He regressed in 2025, though, and this year is off to an even worse start. From an efficiency standpoint, Mayfield stands in the bottom tier of NFL starting quarterbacks.
Here are his ranks among qualified passers:
Making matters worse is that Mayfield left Sunday's loss with a dislocated thumb. His departure in the fourth quarter left the Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie, Jalon Daniels , atop the offense and raised concerns about his availability in the weeks to come. The team has yet to detail a timeline for his return.
There are only five winless teams through the first three weeks of 2026. The Buccaneers are the only one in the NFC. They stand in lockstep with the Miami Dolphins , Tennessee Titans , Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers in the early race for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 draft, and that is not a conversation this team expected to have when it entered the year in search of a return to the playoffs.
Playing in the worst division in football helps mitigate the disastrous nature of this rough start. The NFC South is the only division in which all four teams hold a losing record. There is still a path to the postseason for the last-place Buccaneers, but they cannot afford to keep digging themselves into a hole even if the teams around them are also uninspiring.
"The funny thing is we're 0-3 and we're a game out of first place," Bowles said. "We have to get our stuff together. We gotta reach down and do more -- to a coach, to a person, to a player. We gotta do more, figure out what we can do more, how can we be better and come back tomorrow and get ready to go."
If this was an isolated three-game losing streak, then it would not take much imagination to picture the Buccaneers righting the ship. But with that 0-12 mark against the spread and 10 losses since last October, there is not much proof of concept.
