title: 49ers' Mike Evans ruled out with injury after taking a hit against Cardinals
summary: Evans was carted off the field after suffering a rib injury during the second quarter
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans was ruled out against the Arizona Cardinals after suffering a rib injury during the second quarter of the Week 3 matchup. After taking a big hit, he went down holding his rib area and was carted off the field.
According to the NFL Network , Evans is dealing with a rib strain and will have a full evaluation tomorrow.
Before going down, Evans had three receptions for 34 yards.
49ers WR Mike Evans being carted into the locker room. pic.twitter.com/BlKhOJWpeP
The six-time Pro Bowler led the team in receiving yards (103) heading into this game. With Evans out, wide receivers Deebo Samuel and Jordan Watkins will be seeing more action.
Evans was dealing with a hip injury this year and was questionable heading into this Week 3 game. He did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday due to the injury and was limited in practice on Friday.
The 49ers are already dealing with numerous significant injuries this season, with many key players on injured reserve. Wide receivers Christian Kirk , Ricky Pearsall , De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson are all on IR and Brandon Aiyuk's estrangement with the team still has not been resolved. The 49ers may need to make moves in terms of adding a pass catcher if Evans is out for a significant amount of time.
This marks the fourth 49ers player to be carted to the locker room this season.
This is Evans' first season with the Niners. The Buccaneers drafted him No. 7 overall, and he stayed through 2025, winning a Super Bowl during that span.
Evans' only season with less than 1,000 yards was in 2025 when he was limited to eight games due to a hamstring injury, concussion and broken clavicle. He is tied with Hall of Famer Jerry Rice for consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons with 11.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL Week 3 winners, losers: Commanders spring season's biggest upset, Baker Mayfield becomes latest injured QB
summary: Plus, Deshaun Watson might have earned himself a longer leash as the Browns' starting quarterback
full_text:
Conventional wisdom suggests the Houston Texans were among the biggest losers from Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. When teams lose divisional games to drop to 0-3, there are generally not many redeeming factors to generate optimism for the rest of the year. But maybe the Texans have the league right where they want it. This team lost its first three games a season ago and managed to roll into the AFC divisional round, after all.
Instead, a couple of offensive coordinators stand in the group of this week's most unfortunate parties. Mike McDaniel and Brian Daboll had days to forget in their teams' losses. League-wide quarterback health is a loser, too, with Baker Mayfield becoming the latest starter to sustain a potentially significant ailment.
For every loser, there is a winner. And in the case of the Washington Commanders , the most surprising victory of the season is plenty enough to put them in the Week 3 winner's circle.
Here are the teams, players and coaches who produced the best and worst performances in the third week of the campaign.
The biggest upset of the young season belongs to the Commanders. Very little about their matchup with the Seattle Seahawks suggested they would come out on top, but they overcame the roster gap between themselves and the reigning Super Bowl champions, the return of Sam Darnold to Seattle's lineup, the absence of Jayden Daniels and miserable weather conditions to pull off a 33-31 stunner.
Vintage Marcus Mariota came out on the game-sealing play when he converted a critical third down with his legs. He was excellent before that key run, too. Mariota passed for three touchdowns in his first start of the year and linked up with nine different receivers. Washington's defense was just as impactful in the upset, even if the 31 points it allowed suggests otherwise. The unit limited the Seahawks to a meager 44 rushing yards and forced three turnovers, including a pivotal pick six by Kain Medrano late in the fourth quarter.
The Commanders may not win many games during Daniels' absence (and their 0-2 start even with him in the starting lineup indicates they could be in for a long year regardless), but this victory is one they can hang their hats on all year.
Among the most prevalent storylines from Weeks 1-3 is the onslaught of quarterback injuries across the league. From the preseason through Week 3, six starting quarterbacks missed time due to injuries. A seventh might soon join them, as Tampa Bay Buccaneers signal-caller Baker Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand late in the 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .
Mayfield's hand made contact with a defender on a fourth-and-13 throw inside the final two minutes of the defeat, and he sat the rest of the contest with an injury that appeared to cause him a tremendous amount of pain. Further testing will determine the extent of the dislocation and whether there are other injuries to his hand, but it is reasonable to envision the Buccaneers turning to backup Jalon Daniels (an undrafted rookie) in Week 4.
How Drake Maye would follow his MVP runner-up campaign was of much intrigue entering the 2026 season because, on one hand, his supporting cast is even better than it was a year ago, and on the other, the New England Patriots ' schedule is far more difficult. Three games in, it appears that the more daunting slate will produce a year of regression.
Maye threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . The three turnovers brought his season total to seven. In contrast, he was responsible for only 11 turnovers all of last year. The Patriots are off to a 1-2 start, and the offense was atrocious in the two losses with a combined 16 points and five Maye interceptions.
How much of this is a product of Maye's No. 1 receiver, A.J. Brown , being unavailable for nearly the entire stretch is to be determined. Brown will miss at least two more games as he remains on injured reserve, so Maye will have to try and bounce back without that safety net. There are a handful of shaky or flat-out bad defenses on the upcoming slate, so perhaps that will aid in the third-year quarterback's attempt to climb out of the mud.
The first NFL game in Rio de Janeiro could not have been much more entertaining. Anyone in Brazil who watched American football for the first time on Sunday might have become a fan for life, because that was quite the introduction to the sport from the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys . The Ravens' 34-31 win immediately went down as an all-time great international game in league history.
A walk-off field goal. Two lead changes and a tie in the fourth quarter. Last-minute penalty drama. Superstar players doing superstar things. It was legitimately the perfect game from a "how can we make this the most exciting game for neutral viewers" perspective.
Plus, how fitting is it that in a soccer country, the game-winning play came from the Ravens' kicker? Tyler Loop made a whole lot of soccer-loving Brazilians proud with his gargantuan boot at the buzzer.
After the first game of the Cleveland Browns ' season, it seemed as though Deshaun Watson was on a collision course with the bench. Not only did he save his job with a bounce-back effort in last week's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , but he might have earned himself a considerably longer leash in Sunday's comeback triumph against the Carolina Panthers .
It was by no means a star-caliber effort for Watson, but he logged a pair of touchdown passes in what was always a close game in Week 3. The second of those scoring plays showed that Watson still has a few ounces of clutch in him. He hit Harold Fannin Jr . in the end zone for the second time with the fourth-quarter strike and converted a two-point conversion to give the Browns a decisive lead with 1:48 to play.
The San Francisco 49ers are 3-0 and already hold two NFC West wins. The second of those divisional triumphs came with a cost, though. The 49ers lost wide receiver Mike Evans and tackle Trent Williams for the game in their 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals , and that is not to mention Nick Bosa's injury in practice leading up to the contest. This team is all too familiar with its best players sitting on the bench and finding itself in tough situations as a result, and when it surrendered 17 fourth-quarter points, there was an eerie feeling that the Week 3 game could go south a la last year's injury-impacted losses.
The positive news for the 49ers is that Evans and Williams appear to have avoided serious injuries. Evans has a rib strain , and Williams sat the rest of the game with a neck stinger. It remains to be seen whether either of them will miss more than part of one game. Bosa, on the other hand, is expected to miss multiple weeks with the calf injury he suffered in practice.
Things are just not working for the Los Angeles Chargers , specifically on offense. The team is 0-3, and it has not scored more than 16 points in a game. That is against two bottom-dwelling opponents and a Buffalo Bills defense that surrendered exactly 31 points in both of its first two games. Sunday's 24-16 loss in upstate New York was another example of how a highly touted offensive coordinator hire is not delivering the expected results for the Chargers.
Mike McDaniel and his offense had every opportunity to put up a big number on the Bills. Los Angeles forced five turnovers but turned those extra possessions into only 10 points. It then blew that 10-0 first-quarter lead by halftime. Not many teams will hold Josh Allen and the Bills to just three touchdowns, and they have to be able to capitalize in order to beat the Super Bowl hopefuls. The Chargers could not do so, and it comes back to an offense that cannot seem to kick it into gear.
In case anyone's morbidly curious, the last time the #Bills won a game with a turnover differential of minus-4 was 09/21/1997 against the Colts. The Colts' QB that day was....... Jim…

title: Vikings' Justin Jefferson ruled out vs. Buccaneers with a knee injury

full_text:
Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson was downgraded to out against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to an ankle injury. Jefferson went into the medical tent to be evaluated in the first quarter, after the Vikings' first drive of the game.
When he exited the blue medical tent, he had tape on both ankles. Jefferson had two catches for 32 yards before going down with the injury. Midway through the second quarter, Jefferson was seen walking to the Vikings' locker room.
With Jefferson sidelined, wide receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson will need to do more heavy lifting.
Jefferson has not missed a game due to injury since 2023, when he suffered a hamstring injury in Week 5.
This season, Jefferson has 11 receptions for 147 yards and two touchdowns. Last week against the Chicago Bears , he led the team with three receptions for 55 yards in a low-scoring divisional battle. He also led the team in their season opener against the Green Bay Packers , finishing with eight receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns.
Jefferson has led the team in receiving yards since joining the Vikings in 2020 as the No. 22 overall pick. The four-time Pro Bowler had 1,048 yards in 2025, 1,533 yards in 2024, 1,074 yards in 2023, 1,809 yards in 2022, 1,616 yards in 2021 and 1,400 yards in 2020.
The offense had positive injury news as quarterback Kyler Murray returned after clearing concussion protocol, but losing Jefferson for any length of time will be a hit to their already struggling passing game.
The Vikings rank last in passing yards (259) and fourth-worst in completion percentage (52.5).
They went into the game against the Buccaneers 2-0, with wins over the Packers and Bears. Up next for the Vikings are the Miami Dolphins , who are 0-3.

title: What happened to Drake Maye? Why his Year 3 collapse is getting harder to explain away
summary: From Trevor Lawrence to Mitchell Trubisky, recent history shows two very different ways this can go
full_text:
Three games into 2026, Drake Maye looks nothing like the quarterback who just helped New England win 14 games.
We live in a world of hyperbole and overreactions, but this is not that. Maye threw eight interceptions in 17 regular-season games during the Patriots ' improbable run from a four-win outfit in 2024 to representing the AFC in the Super Bowl seven months ago.  He already has six through three games in 2026, against just one TD pass. His completion percentage has dropped from 72.0% to 63.8%, his yards per attempt from 8.9 to 7.3, and his passer rating from 113.5 to 58.6.
The most troubling part isn't that the Patriots offense has been worse. It's that Maye has been a big reason why.
Sunday against Jacksonville was the latest manifestation of it. Maye finished 14 of 25 for 199 yards with no touchdowns, two interceptions and a lost fumble in a 35-6 loss.
oh no Drake Maye... pic.twitter.com/uwCHx632lv
That came after three fourth-quarter interceptions against Seattle in Week 1 and another bad pick against Pittsburgh a week later. The Seattle game is what makes the slide so jarring: Maye was 17 of 22 with a TD, no interceptions and a 105.7 passer rating through three quarters before it all imploded in the final three possessions.
It was like you could see him regressing in real time. And that would have, in fact, been a real-time overreaction following the loss in Seattle, but the last nine quarters have been some bad, bad ball.
If you're looking for excuses, there are reasons Maye has looked worse than he has, and they have little to do with Maye himself. The Patriots have played a much tougher schedule. A.J. Brown 's unavailability changes what the passing game looks like. Losing guard Mike Onwenu cannot be overstated. Receivers aren't always separating, and the protection has been shaky, too: coming into the Jaguars game, Maye faced a 43.5% pressure rate, according to PFF, fourth-highest among starting QBs.
But here's the problem: pressure can cause bad plays. Being without a No. 1 receiver can reduce the margin for error. A tougher schedule can lower production. But none of this explains why your franchise quarterback is suddenly turning the ball over like it's part of the job description.
That's where this gets concerning, because Maye's second season wasn't a fluke. The analytics backed it up. As a rookie, Maye averaged minus-0.03 EPA per dropback, averaged 6.7 yards per attempt and posted a 3.5% turnover-worthy-play rate.
In Year 2, everything improved.
That's what makes this different from some of the obvious cautionary tales. (Going to warn you now, this is gonna get ugly, so buckle up.)
I went back through quarterback seasons from 2015-25, looking for players who improved from Year 1 to Year 2, then regressed in Year 3. Mitchell Trubisky and Blake Bortles are two of the cleaner examples.
Trubisky, the second overall pick in 2017, went from a 77.5 passer rating as a rookie to 95.4 in Year 2, threw 24 touchdowns and helped Chicago win 12 games. Then Year 3 arrived: 17 touchdowns, 6.1 yards per attempt and an 83.0 rating.
Bortles, taken with the No. 3 pick in 2014, had an even bigger Year 2 statistically, throwing for 4,428 yards and 35 touchdowns. A year later, he was down to 23 touchdowns, 6.2 yards per attempt and a 78.8 rating.
The difference is that Maye's 2025 season was considerably more convincing. He wasn't simply amassing stats. His EPA improved substantially, his turnover-worthy plays went down, and the deep ball became a real weapon: Maye completed 61.8% of his throws 20-plus yards downfield, one of the highest rates in the league. That looked like legit franchise-QB development, not a false positive.
The biggest difference so far isn't that Maye suddenly can't make NFL throws. He can. It's the mistakes that largely went missing last season that have come back, almost as if they're making up for lost time.
And if you remember Maye going back to North Carolina, some of this feels familiar. The 2022 version was more settled -- working through reads, throwing with touch and anticipation, creating when protection broke down -- while the 2023 tape raised more questions about his feet, accuracy and decision-making, especially when he drifted into pressure or tried to make a harder play than he needed to. He was still the third overall pick in 2024, behind only Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels, but there were some concerns about how he played last season in Chapel Hill.
Maye appeared to put any such questions to rest last season. Now, after an uneven postseason and three weeks of the '26 regular season, we're asking them again.
And it's why history matters. Sometimes Year 3 exposes something Year 2 masked. Sometimes it's just a temporary detour. Other times it's more than that.
95.4 rating, 24TDs, 12 INTs
Never returned to Year 2 level
Brief rebound, never sustained it
Never became long-term high-end starter
Later returned to MVP level
If you're among the glass-half-full contingent, the Lawrence comparison might be the most useful, with two important caveats: his rookie season came in the Urban Meyer mess, and his Year 3 slide was complicated by injuries. Lawrence dealt with knee and ankle injuries, a concussion and a shoulder injury as Jacksonville collapsed from an 8-3 start to 9-8. So when Lawrence slipped from 25 touchdowns and eight interceptions in Year 2 to 21 and 14 in Year 3, there were plenty of reasons beyond simple regression.
That's not especially comforting for Maye, who, as far as we know, is healthy and can't lean on similar excuses to explain away the start to his 2026 campaign.
Lamar Jackson is another reminder that Year 3 regression doesn't have to become the new normal. His MVP sophomore season was ridiculous: 36 touchdowns, just six picks, a 113.3 passer rating and 1,206 rushing yards. A year later, those passing numbers slipped: 26 touchdowns, nine interceptions and a 99.3 rating, while his YPA fell from 7.8 to 7.3. That's still very good quarterback play – just nowhere near his Year 2 level. He's back to playing at an MVP level, and truth be told, the Patriots would gladly welcome Jackson's version of a "down Year 3."
The other group, meanwhile, is where the warnings lie.
Trubisky never recaptured his Year 2 form. Neither did Bortles. Marcus Mariota went from 26 touchdowns and nine interceptions in Year 2 to 13 touchdowns and 15 interceptions a year later, and that second-year promise never became a reality. Josh Freeman went from 25 touchdowns and six interceptions to 16 and 22, and his career unraveled not long after.
That's the range of possibilities here, which is why three games aren't enough to tell us how this ends. But three games are enough to say something is wrong, because the mistakes have been persistent and the turnovers have spiked. (Three games become seven if you add in the four uneven postseason games from earlier this year.)
The Patriots can help Maye. They can protect him better. Getting Brown back on the field matters. You can't do anything about that first-place schedule, but Maye played with less during stretches of last season and still found a way to elevate the offense.
But none of that erases the fact that he has thrown six interceptions in three games, and that's on Maye to fix.  The biggest issue is how those mistakes are happening: he looks less settled, more hesitant and more willing to force throws when the first answer isn't there.
Drake Maye: “I can’t get out of my own way.” pic.twitter.com/cESkGjujVC
The encouraging part for New England is that nobody has to imagine what the good version of Maye looks like. We've already seen it. For an entire regular season, Maye played at an MVP level and got the Pats to the Super Bowl.
So, were his first two seasons the beginning of something special, or the best version of Maye we'll ever see? History says quarterbacks can come back from a third-year regression. It also says sometimes Year 3 is when a temporary slump starts to look more…

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, 49ers Winners & Losers: Arizona loses a heartbreaker
summary: The 1-1-0 Arizona Cardinals were involved in a key division match with the 2-0-0 San Francisco 49ers. There are a ton of media outlets that have placed the Niners in this year’s NFC Championship Game. However, San Fran has a ton of injuries to key players including DE Nick Bosa. We all know this changes […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball during the first quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 1-1-0 Arizona Cardinals were involved in a key division match with the 2-0-0 San Francisco 49ers. There are a ton of media outlets that have placed the Niners in this year’s NFC Championship Game. However, San Fran has a ton of injuries to key players including DE Nick Bosa. We all know this changes the outcome of games. What exactly are the Cardinals this year? Bottom-feeder again? An up-and-comer? Or perhaps a playoff roster? RELATED: CARDINALS NEED OFFENSIVE STARS TO BREAKOUT The Cardinals have their own injury list, and it seems to grow each week. Front and center is CB Will Johnson, who was placed on IR. That is a huge hole. The offense dominated in the first half yet could only score six points. In the end, Arizona came back only to lose 36-30. The loss did show that the Cardinals can stay with the big dogs if they can start converting long drives into touchdowns instead of field goals and punts. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS TE Trey McBride – Can’t this talented player just be a default addition each week? He knows how to get open, although his route tree is pretty limited. But he has great hands and is a huge option in this offense. Had the 18-yard pickup midway in the second quarter for 18 yards. Grabbed a 13-yard pass early in the third quarter. Drew that huge 19-yard pass interference penalty early in the fourth quarter which was then converted into a touchdown. S Andrew Wingard – It is good to have heavy hitters on your defense. Wingard came to play and seemed to be everywhere. On the Niners second possession of the game in Quarter 2, Wingard had four tackles on this drive alone. Led the Cardinals with 10 total tackles. Mike. Willy. pic.twitter.com/YCdGEIWjCU — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 27, 2026 WR Michael Wilson – Excellent conversion of the fourth-and-one seven-yard reception as the second quarter was winding down. Several plays later could not haul in the second-and-goal pass, which became three points instead of six. With 1:11 left in the second quarter, snared the 17-yarder, followed by the completion for 11 yards. Again, Wilson and QB Jacoby Brissett could not hook up on the third-and-14, which netted three points instead of six. It was Brissett to Wilson again on fourth down in the third quarter for the conversion. Then with 3:02 left in Quarter 3, Brissett found Wilson for the five-yard touchdown after he snuck out from the backfield. Led all receivers with 17 targets and 11 receptions for 89 yards. Special teams – K Chad Ryland nailed all three field goal attempts plus was 3-for-3 in PATs. P Blake Gillikin has a sensational game with a 50.3 average per punt on four kicks. Simi Fehoko had the recovery of Gillikin’s punt that ricocheted off the Niners’ blocker. Punt coverage was good as well. There goes that man 💨 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/bQszB9MtWy — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 27, 2026 RB Jeremiyah Love – Starting to see how this young man operates. He does give it everything he has. His longest run was just eight yards, but he puts full effort into every carry. Flared out in the fourth quarter and was wide open for the pass completion, but QB Jacoby Brissett threw it behind Love, who was able to cradle the ball and score. Caught all five targets for 19 yards and led all rushers with 21 carries for 90 yards. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS First-half offense – The Cardinals dominated in the first half in terms of time of possession, 21:01 to San Fran’s 8:59, yet were losing 17-6. The 49ers focused on scoring touchdowns rather than field goals in their limited offensive opportunities. Arizona possessions in the first half: punt, punt, punt, FG, FG. The Cardinals had a first-and-goal on the nine and could not punch it in. On the next drive, the drive stalled at the opponent’s 19. Everyone is in unison that this new offense will need to blossom, but being patient isn’t an easy ask. WR Marv Harrison – Every week, it seems Harrison cannot get separation. What happened to this talented receiver? We get that McBride had 11 targets and Wilson had another 17, but those guys are getting open. Harrison is rarely looked at anymore. Are three catches for 40 yards even newsworthy? Penalties – Ahhhh!! These came at the worst times. DE Josh Sweat was flagged for roughing the passer in the fourth quarter with 9:14 left, on a third-and-six and a first down that eventually became a touchdown after the incompletion. Arizona mounted a very good drive in their first possession, only to have a holding call by Elijah Higgins on a second-and-10 as San Fran’s 36 became a second-and-20 back in Cardinals territory, which eventually turned a 12-play drive into a punting situation. During the Cardinals’ second possession in Quarter 2, the offense was slapped with three penalties that pushed them from close range in enemy territory to their own 47: too many men on the field, LG Isaiah Seumalo false start, illegal shift, and RT Elijah Wilkinson false start. 10 penalties for 86 yards are drive killers. A connection we love to see 🙌 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/6CqyBmFama — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 27, 2026 Pass defense – This became the game’s outcome. RB Christian McCaffrey converted a third-and-seven into a 13-yard gain as the first quarter was winding down. He came out of the backfield as he often does, but CB Garrett Williams was slow to pick him up. Several plays later, WR Jordan Watkins did a simple cross and was wide open for 26 yards after beating CB Max Melton. Three plays later, QB Brock Purdy hit WR Mike Evans for the touchdown after giving CB Denzel Burke a wiggle that he bit on and was open in the end zone. Burke never even looked at the ball, and if he had simply turned his head, he was in position to swat the pass away. Watkins was wide-ass open with 17 seconds left in the second quarter, which became a 34-yard gain with coverage by LB Mack Wilson. Watkins stayed in to block, then flared out without anybody around. The Niners got three points from this blunder. Kittle extending the lead 📈 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/iQXUbg6nGF — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 27, 2026 How many times in the game did we see TE George Kittle catch an 11-yarder, 18-yarder, and other double-digit receptions that became drive extenders like the 10-yard completion for the touchdown late in the fourth quarter? LB Baron Browning made contact with Kittle coming off the line, then released him. He was wide open at the four and did the rest to get into the end zone. Did the Arizona defense not have any idea of how to cover him? Then, on the 49ers’ next possession, guess who was wide open at the five-yard line? Four Cardinals pass defenders were in the center of the field. All Kittle did was come off the line and run a pattern. No head fake, no shoulder bob, nothing. Run a route without any coverage at all. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – It all started with, “Here, hold my beer” QB Jacoby Brissett – So far this season, Brissett has been a middle-of-the-road quarterback. He tossed 52 passes in today’s game and completed 38. The issue is that when the offense drives down and gets into scoring range, Brissett will miss his targets, and the Cardinals will settle for three points instead of six. The third-and-17 throw to Wilson as the second quarter was winding down was nowhere near him, and Arizona had to settle for yet another field goal. He hit Love for the touchdown early in the fourth quarter, but the rookie had to reach back for the pass. He is a good game manager, but can’t get into that elite passer category. Went 38-of-52 for 280 yards, a 5.4 yards-per-completion average, tossed two…

No, the Cardinals […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to the start of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. No, the Cardinals made a big special teams play, got close in the fourth quarter, then immediately decided they to forget how to play defense. And hey, we called it, take the Cardinals to cover and the over in the game. This will be one to look back on as growth or a missed opportunity, but I thought the final half was encouraging.

title: Falcons Week 3, 3 up and 3 down: The offense shows signs of life
summary: The Atlanta Falcons got their first win of the season, and did so in dominant fashion. Michael Penix Jr. returned, and so did the offensive production. On the other side of the ball, CJ Henderson and company stepped up as the team managed multiple injuries. Here’s the Week 3, 3 up and 3 down. 3 […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons got their first win of the season, and did so in dominant fashion. Michael Penix Jr. returned, and so did the offensive production. On the other side of the ball, CJ Henderson and company stepped up as the team managed multiple injuries. Here’s the Week 3, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Bijan Robinson What can’t he do? Bijan Robinson is reaching heights no other Falcons running back before him has. In the first half, he became the 10th player in NFL history to reach 6,000 scrimmage yards before age 25. With Penix managing the game to near perfection, the heavy boxes started to disappear, allowing Bijan to stretch his legs. He finished with 213 total yards and two touchdowns. Robinson is on pace for +2,600 scrimmage yards, which would shatter the franchise record he set last year by 400 yards. Here are all 4 of Bijan Robinson's explosive runs. Postgame, Bijan said he always knows where the free runner is and constantly sets up the 2nd and 3rd level defenders with his eyes and body movements. Compared it to a game of peek-a-boo — Tre’Shon Diaz (@treshon.io) 2026-09-25T21:28:12.416Z Michael Penix Jr. It had been 312 days since Penix Jr. set foot on the gridiron, and that showed during the 1st quarter. After shaking off the rust in the 1st quarter, the 3rd-year quarterback went 16/18 for 234 yards and a touchdown. It was how Penix accumulated these stats that has fans excited. Penix had a career high in both under center snaps and passes between the numbers , incinerating narratives from the Zac Robinson era. He got his best friend Drake London involved, who has been disappointed by the Falcons start, to say the least. London was all smiles after putting up 194 yards, and so were Falcons fans. Penix’s return has shifted the narrative around the team, and now we’ll see what they are truly made of this season. CJ Henderson Henderson may not have had the career many envisioned as the first corner taken from his draft class, but he’s rewriting his story in Atlanta. With A.J. Terrell on IR , Henderson needed to step up for Atlanta, and that’s exactly what he did. He was the best defensive back on the field, forcing three incompletions and only giving up 40 yards on 11 targets . He also had nine tackles on the day, showing he can handle his run support duties just fine. If these performances continue while Terrell is on the mend, the team will need to reevaluate if Mike Hughes is truly the best option as the team’s second boundary corner on the depth chart. Hell of a night for former top 10 pick CJ Henderson! #SFSP #ART pic.twitter.com/sxTDxlSC8N — Oliver Davis II (@I_Am_OD3) September 25, 2026 3 down Zachariah Branch The electric skill player is struggling to find a role and generate a spark. He had an extremely ill-advised punt return that left the team with worse field position than if he’d let it go, and outside of a handful of screens, he’s a nonfactor in the offense. Rookies need time to acclimate to the NFL environment, so a slow start isn’t cause for much concern, but his usage, regardless of whether or not he’s getting the ball, is questionable. Branch has the speed to stretch the field, and while he is smaller in stature, he can still function as a situational X receiver the same way Taylor Gabriel did for the offense almost a decade ago. We’ll see if his role increases as both Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus haven’t done enough to justify their snap shares to this point. Mike Hughes When the Packers offense showed signs of life, Hughes was at the scene of the crime. He allowed five receptions on six targets for 89 yards and a touchdown. He also had a costly pass interference that flipped the field for the Packers offense. Hughes has been the target of Falcons fans’ ire for a couple of seasons, and while sometimes the hate was extreme, there’s no defending the quality of play we’ve seen in the opening window of the season. Hughes’ contract has always made the lapses in play easier to stomach, but with CJ Henderson coming on strong, it’s getting harder and harder to justify his spot in this starting lineup. If he can’t get it together over the next few weeks, he could find himself on the bench when Terrell returns. Mike Hughes has been beat multiple times this season already. #Falcons pic.twitter.com/xXNVDYmNvJ — Miles Garrett (@MilesGarrettTV) September 25, 2026 Kyle Pitts Pitts had a great block on Bijan Robinson’s first rushing touchdown, and while his growth as a blocker has been needed, it isn’t justifying his $53 million extension. When Kevin Stefanski was hired, his ability to get tight ends the ball was highlighted consistently. We still haven’t seen that translate to the field. To be fair, this was the first game the team had a functional quarterback, so there’s still plenty of time for his production to increase. If it doesn’t, fans will once again start questioning his role on this team. The Falcons needed this performance more than they needed air. Starting 0-3 would’ve been an early-season dagger the team and fans wouldn’t have recovered from. They aren’t out of the woods yet, sitting at 1-2, but new life has been injected into the season. The team has the opportunity to reach .500 after facing the Saints in Week 4 and get their playoff hopes back on track.

title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 3: Nnamdi Madubuike makes season debut, offensive line roulette
summary: Offense Carson Vinson played all 64 snaps in his first start at left tackle, as did four of the other five starters. Injuries at center late in the game threw a wrench into the equation. Jovaughn Gwyn left the game after 46 snaps and Ethan Pocic suffered a knee injury following just 10 plays. That […]
full_text: Offense QB: Lamar Jackson 64 RB: Derrick Henry 43, Justice Hill 21 WR: Rashod Bateman 56, Chris Moore 33, Zay Flowers 21, Devontez Walker 17, LaJohntay Wester 11 TE: Durham Smythe 34, Mark Andrews 33, Matthew Hibner 32, Josh Cuevas 16 OL: Carson Vinson 64, Vega Ioane 64, Roger Rosengarten 64, John Simpson 64, Jovaughn Gwyn 46, Ethan Pocic 10, Andrew Vorhees 8, Emery Jones Jr. 3 Carson Vinson played all 64 snaps in his first start at left tackle, as did four of the other five starters. Injuries at center late in the game threw a wrench into the equation. Jovaughn Gwyn left the game after 46 snaps and Ethan Pocic suffered a knee injury following just 10 plays. That forced Vega Ioane to play center for the last handful of offensive plays, which saw Andrew Vorhees plug in at right guard. Emery Jones Jr. also took three snaps. Derrick Henry more than doubled Justice Hill’s snap count (43 to 21) and took a heavy workload with 26 carries. Hill had his most effective game of the year with 33 yards on five carries. At tight end, Durham Smythe had the most snaps with 34 after Mark Andrews was sidelined mid-game with a hand injury. Andrews returned and finished with 33 snaps. Rookies Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas each played their highest snap counts of the year and had three combined catches. Hibner caught the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Zay Flowers was limited to 21 snaps in his return from injury and still easily led the team in receiving with five catches for 84 yards. Flowers also had 20 rushing yards and fell just a couple yards away from scoring. Rashod Bateman played 56 snaps with two catches, and Chris Moore retained a surprisingly big offensive role (33 snaps). Moore continues to play a lot more than Devontez Walker, who took 17 offensive reps. Defense DL: Nnamdi Madubuike 47, Travis Jones 42, Calais Campbell 32, Broderick Washington 26, John Jenkins 12 EDGE: Tavius Robinson 58, Trey Hendrickson 45, Zion Young 26, Mike Green 22 ILB: Roquan Smith 74, Trenton Simpson 46, Teddye Buchanan 3 CB: Nate Wiggins 69, Marlon Humphrey 64, Chandler Rivers 32, Chidobe Awuzie 15 S: Malaki Starks 73, Kyle Hamilton 67, Jaylinn Hawkins 61 Nnamdi Madubuike made his long-awaited return to action and was not limited in playing time. Madubuike led all defensive linemen with 47 snaps. Calais Campbell’s 32 snaps saw him lead the team in quarterback hits with three in his most impactful game of the year so far. Aeneas Peebles was a healthy scratch instead of Broderick Washington and John Jenkins, who combined to play 38 snaps. Tavius Robinson again paced the edge rusher room (58 snaps), followed by Trey Hendrickson at 45 snaps. Zion Young’s snap count increased again and he out-snapped Mike Green 26 to 22. At inside linebacker, Roquan Smith played every defensive snap, the only defender in the game to do so. Teddye Buchanan’s return from injury saw him on the field for only three plays. Trenton Simpson played 46 snaps and doesn’t appear at risk to losing his starting role. In the secondary, Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey were not on the field for nearly every play again. Chidobe Awuzie played a season-high 15 snaps, as did Chandler Rivers with 32 snaps. Rivers seemingly has a strong hold on the nickel cornerback spot over Keyon Martin now for the second straight week. Kyle Hamilton exited the game for a few plays after suffering an injury but quickly returned. Malaki Starks retained a near every-down role with 73 snaps and Jaylinn Hawkins saw his snap share decrease slightly but still played 61 snaps.

title: Ravens Report Card, Week 3: Late-game heroics save the day in winning result
summary: The Baltimore Ravens won a thrilling matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 3, emerging victorious from a high-scoring affair by three points. A game-winning field goal lifted the Ravens to a 34-31 advantage following some heroics in all three phases. Here are report card grades for each position group from the miraculous win. Quarterback: […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Loop #33 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates with teammates after defeating the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens won a thrilling matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 3, emerging victorious from a high-scoring affair by three points. A game-winning field goal lifted the Ravens to a 34-31 advantage following some heroics in all three phases. Here are report card grades for each position group from the miraculous win. Quarterback: B The Ravens made a concentrated effort to stick with the run in this game, which led to Lamar Jackson attempting just 20 passes. He completed 15 of them (75%) for 185 passing yards with two touchdowns and another 50 rushing yards on just six carries. Jackson had less than 100 passing yards entering the fourth quarter but was efficient overall and made key plays late in the game. He had more passes that were off-target this game than in the previous two, including an underthrown deep attempt to Devontez Walker, but only having five incompletions in total is hard to scoff at. Jackson’s passer rating of 136.7 was his best mark of the season thus far. His decisiveness and late-game decision-making help elevate this grade. Running Back: B – Derrick Henry was surprisingly bottled up pretty well by the Cowboys’ defense, as he averaged only 3.4 yards per carry on 26 rushing attempts. Henry was stuffed on multiple third-and-short and fourth-and-short tries. He did score two touchdowns again and had a long run of 29 yards. Justice Hill made an impact with five carries for 33 yards on the ground. Hill had multiple good runs as a change-of-pace to Henry’s bruising downhill style. Neither running back was a factor in the passing attack in this game. Wide Receiver: B – Zay Flowers’ return to the lineup proved to be a saving grace for the Ravens offensively. Despite playing less snaps than usual, he led the team with five catches for 84 yards on six targets. Flowers made the biggest catch of the game for a 27-yard gain with only a few seconds remaining in regulation. He also had a 20-yard run where he fell just short of scoring a touchdown. Rashod Bateman caught two passes for 37 yards and Chris Moore reeled in a short four-yard touchdown catch. Devontez Walker was targeted twice on two long deep shots, neither of which were completed — but the first attempt drew a pass interference call that set up a rushing score. Tight End: C Mark Andrews suffered a hand injury in the middle of the game that sidelined him for a little bit before he returned. Andrews caught three passes for 24 yards, as his target share dipped with the return of Flowers. Both rookie tight ends were more involved this week. Matthew Hibner had a long 21-yard catch-and-run reception and caught the go-ahead score late in the fourth quarter. On that play, Hibner was uncovered in the slot and did a good job making himself available for Jackson. Josh Cuevas also caught a 14-yard pass on a crossing route for a nice first down pickup. In the blocking game, this group’s performance left much to be desired, as they struggled to hold the edge and missed multiple blocks. Offensive Line: C The Ravens surrendered some pressure in this game, but Jackson was not sacked and the Cowboys only recorded one quarterback hit. Carson Vinson appeared to fare pretty well in his first career start at left tackle and Vega Ioane had a cleaner performance than in Week 2 Ioane stepped up to take snaps at center late in the game after both Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic exited with injuries. John Simpson was victim to multiple negative plays, and the Ravens did have a few offensive line penalties again. They also weren’t very effective run blocking in short-yardage situations, where the Ravens failed to gain one yard when needed on multiple conversion attempts. Defensive Line: C+ The Ravens were surprisingly gashed on the ground by the Cowboys’ rushing attack, particularly on the opening drive of the game. They settled in better later in the second half and game script helped with that. The Ravens seemed content with ceding rushing success in lieu of the Cowboys unlocking explosive plays through the air. In total, the Ravens allowed 148 yards, two touchdowns and 4.9 yards per carry. Nnamdi Madubuike had three tackles in over 40 snaps in his return to action. Calais Campbell was a force in this game with a team-high three quarterback hits. Travis Jones had two tackles for loss. The Ravens still need to start getting more consistent interior pressure from their front seven. Edge Rusher: C The Ravens were only able to get home for one sack in this game, which didn’t come from an edge rusher, but did have seven quarterback hits on Dak Prescott. Trey Hendrickson had two and Tavius Robinson had one as well. The rest of team’s pass rushing production came from other position groups. Hendrickson continues to rack up pressures and come up just short of finishing with sacks. Zion Young and Mike Green showed some good physicality but weren’t able to win pass rushing sets with consistency. Linebacker: B- Roquan Smith had a solid all-around game with eight tackles, a sack, tackle for loss and quarterback hit. Smith’s sack came early in the game. Trenton Simpson also made an impact again with two impressive tackles for loss, including one where he blew up a screen play by himself. Teddye Buchanan returned to action but played only a handful of snaps. Simpson seems to have a strong hold on the starting job opposite Smith right now, so it will be interesting to see how Buchanan can factor into the mix over the coming weeks. Cornerback: C The Ravens faced a tall task of matching up with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in pass coverage, and the results weren’t spectacular. They did a good job of limiting big plays for most of the game, but the Cowboys’ wideouts began to have their way in the fourth quarter. Marlon Humphrey in particular was picked on a bit and allowed multiple long passes in coverage, and Nate Wiggins was challenged too especially as a tackler. Lamb and Pickens each had seven catches on a combined 19 targets and totaled 194 yards together. Chidobe Awuzie factored into the cornerback rotation in this game, as did Chandler Rivers again in the slot. Wiggins was flagged for a questionable defensive pass interference on the Cowboys’ final drive of the game but responded with back-to-back incompletions while in coverage in the end zone. Safety: B- Malaki Starks and Jaylinn Hawkins improved from last game and open-field tackling from the team’s safeties appeared to be better. Hawkins had eight tackles and Starks had six tackles. Kyle Hamilton was a force in this game with eight tackles, two passes defended and a tackle for loss. He was involved in multiple plays around the ball at the line of scrimmage and also covered well. The Ravens played a lot of two-high safety looks in this game to keep a lid on the top of the field to eliminate big plays and keep everything in front of them. Special Teams: A Tyler Loop was the hero of the day, nailing a 56-yard field goal to win the game as time expired. That was the best kick of Loop’s young career. He made his other field goal attempt as well and all four extra point tries. LaJohntay Wester had a 24-yard punt return and Ryan Eckley’s three punts averaged 49.7 yards. Keondre Jackson was another special teams standout, blocking a field goal in the third quarter. The Ravens wound up winning by only three points, so Jackson’s blocked field goal was a huge game-defining play.
author: Frank Platko

title: Loop the Redeemed: last-second FG lifts Ravens over Cowboys in Brazil
summary: In the moment, it was easy to miss the irony. The NFL’s latest international push, deep into soccer territory, was decided by a kick. A foot meeting a ball. Fûtbol. Fans in Brazil may have known they were seated for an instant classic after a back-and-forth first half between the Ravens and the Cowboys. But […]
full_text: Football - NFL - Baltimore Ravens v Dallas Cowboys - Estadio Maracana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - September 27, 2026 Baltimore Ravens' Tyler Loop celebrates after kicking a field goal to win the game REUTERS/Brian Snyder | REUTERS In the moment, it was easy to miss the irony. The NFL’s latest international push, deep into soccer territory, was decided by a kick. A foot meeting a ball. Fûtbol. Fans in Brazil may have known they were seated for an instant classic after a back-and-forth first half between the Ravens and the Cowboys. But they had no idea that history was waiting in the second half. Before Baltimore’s win on Sunday, no NFL team had ever started a game-winning possession with seven seconds or fewer remaining, per ESPN’s Ben Solak . Of course, none of those teams had Lamar Jackson. Minutes after driving down the field to re-take a lead his defense simply refused to keep, the two-time MVP trotted out on the field with 31-31 on the scoreboard and 0:07 on the game clock. Within seven seconds, he somehow had to move the ball at least 25 yards and stop the clock before it hit 0:00. Jackson knew the assignment. He took a deep drop to let his receivers get downfield before firing a rocket to Zay Flowers. The pass traveled 36.4 yards in 1.6 seconds ( via Next Gen Stats ) – or 46.5 miles per hour. Flowers shook his coverage out of the slot and leapt for the ball right around the 40-yard line. The television broadcast, apparently not expecting the Ravens to go for the win, hurriedly put up a target field goal range. Jackson raced over to the nearest referee to call a timeout right as his teammate hit the ground. One second remained. Having (once again) donned his superhero cape to will his way to victory, Jackson returned to the sidelines to (once again) watch as the Ravens’ fate was decided by a single kick. To be exact: a 56-yard field goal, to be delivered by none other than Tyler Loop, the second-year kicker whose season-ending miss in January forever altered the course of franchise history. With the iconic Christ the Redeemer statue overlooking Rio de Janeiro’s Maracaña Stadium, Loop stepped up with a chance to exorcise last season’s demons. He took his stance off the left hash mark, sent the ball end-over-end, and snuck it inside the uprights to send the arena into hysterics. The locals may still be learning the finer points of American football, but they are plenty familiar with the euphoria of a game-winning kick. Loop led the Ravens to the corner of the field to hit soccer star Ronaldo’s signature ‘SIU’ celebration with a hearty contribution from the adoring crowd. The Cowboys are America’s team, but the Ravens might be Brazil’s team now. Late-game heroics overshadow Ravens’ recurring issues The last seven seconds of Sunday’s game will be remembered for years to come, but the other 59:53 should concern the Ravens. Jesse Minter’s defense struggled out of the gate and folded in the second half, giving up an 11-point lead with 3:50 left in the third quarter and a three-point lead with just 94 seconds left in the game. overshadowed sloppy showing from Baltimore’s defense and injuries to both of the team’s centers. Starter Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and backup Ethan Pocic (knee) were both carted off the field in the second half, forcing rookie right guard Vega Ioane to close the game out at center. The first-round pick held up for two drives, but the Ravens could be scrambling for depth depending on the diagnoses for Gwyn and Pocic.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens vs. Cowboys game balls: Jackson, Flowers, and Loop seal wild win
summary: The Baltimore Ravens escaped their Week 3 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys with a 34-31 victory thanks to some late heroics by several key players. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s game balls coming out of Brazil: Tyler Loop Take a bow, Tyler Loop. Eight-and-a-half months after he ended the Ravens’ 2025 season with a heartbreaking miss […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Keondre Jackson #39 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates after a turnover during the third quarter of the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens escaped their Week 3 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys with a 34-31 victory thanks to some late heroics by several key players. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s game balls coming out of Brazil: Tyler Loop Take a bow, Tyler Loop. Eight-and-a-half months after he ended the Ravens’ 2025 season with a heartbreaking miss and nudged the franchise towards their offseason overhaul, the second-year kicker got a second chance at immortality – this time, from 56 yards, the second-longest attempt of his young career. Again, Loop was asked to follow up a miraculous Lamar Jackson completion, only adding to the pressure as he trotted out on the field. But he fired away from the left hash and kept the football just inside the upright before sprinting down the field with his teammates in a euphoric celebration that will likely continue through the entire flight home. Loop’s Week 1 performance already inspired plenty of confidence in a bounce-back campaign, and his blocked kick in Week 2 was not exactly his fault, either. But his first career game-winner will finally and fully invite him back into Ravens fans’ good graces. – Nikhil Mehta Lamar Jackson The Ravens offense stumbled through the first half before hitting the big red button labeled ‘LAMAR JACKSON’S LEGS – PRESS IN CASE OF EMERGENCY.’ From there, the greatest offensive weapon in the history of football took over. His deep ball wasn’t perfect on Sunday – it was still good enough to draw multiple defensive pass interference flags – but he peppered the middle of the field and moved the ball with on the ground as needed. And of course, he threw an absolute frozen rope to Zay Flowers to set up Loop’s game-winning field goal – with the wherewithal to call a timeout before the clock hit 0:00. This game proved that the Ravens can win any game with their two-time MVP under center. – Nikhil Mehta Zay Flowers In a game many, including myself, questioned if he should even be playing, Zay Flowers balled out. Between the hamstring injury that’s plagued him for a couple weeks, the poor field conditions in Rio and limited practice during the week, it seemed apparent Flowers wouldn’t play. Instead, a report came out late Saturday night that Flowers planned to test his hamstring in warmup and could potentially go. He got the gameday activation then casually lead the lead with 84 yards on five catches, including catching the missile launched from Lamar Jackson to set the Ravens’ game winning field goal. The Ravens likely don’t come close to winning this game if he doesn’t play. – Zach Canter Keondre Jackson The Ravens only had a chance to win Sunday’s game because of a Baltimore classic in the third quarter: a blocked field goal. With an assist from Chandler Rivers, whose incredible jump off the edge opened a hole, Keondre Jackson sliced through the line of scrimmage and got a full extension in front of Brandon Aubrey – one of the NFL’s best kickers in recent memory – to block his 59-yard attempt. After a rough week, Jackson’s block and Loop’s clutch kick represent a major turnaround for Anthony Levine Sr.’s special teams units. – Nikhil Mehta Vega Ioane In hindsight, this was a disaster waiting to happen. The Ravens only kept two centers on their 53-man roster and lost Corey Bullock to the Panthers on waivers during final cuts without another option on the practice squad. So of course, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic would go down in the second half of the same game and force first-round pick Vega Ioane to move from right guard to center with the game on the line. He only lined up at center a handful of times in college, all in 2024, but he got his snaps off without issue and did just enough to hold down the fort. Is Ioane the plan for the Ravens going forward, or will offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and OL coach Dwyane Ledford have to cook up yet another solution? – Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens Roundtable: Reactions to an exhilarating walk-off victory in Week 3
summary: The Baltimore Ravens escaped their trip to Brazil with a 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys in a high-scoring, back-and-forth affair. Tyler Loop’s game-winning field goal from 56 yards out gave the Ravens a last-second edge with no time remaining. Here are the Baltimore Beatdown staff’s reactions to the victory in Week 3. Just an […]
full_text: Baltimore Ravens' running back #21 Derrick Henry celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the NFL match between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 27, 2026. (Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens escaped their trip to Brazil with a 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys in a high-scoring, back-and-forth affair. Tyler Loop’s game-winning field goal from 56 yards out gave the Ravens a last-second edge with no time remaining. Here are the Baltimore Beatdown staff’s reactions to the victory in Week 3. Just an incredible game and one that might do wonders for the Ravens confidence moving forward. The classic script was unfolding once again as the Ravens witnessed a double-digit lead evaporate in the fourth quarter. At the end of the game, it looked like they were once again going to fall victim to a controversial call as Nate Wiggins was flagged for pass interference on CeeDee Lamb although it was Lamb who had Wiggins’ arm pinned. Then, with just seven seconds left, Lamar Jackson miraculously hit Zay Flowers to set up Tyler Loop for the game winning 56-yard field goal. The performance from the defense was inconsistent again, but ultimately, they managed to hold down the fort when they needed to. The center position is also in complete flux right now and will be something to monitor moving forward. It’s certainly not a perfect product but these are games the Ravens have consistently lost over the last five years, and it feels great to finally be on the winning side. — Stephen Bopst I have no idea what I just watched. A classic Ravens 4th quarter collapse where the Ravens were stuffed on the goal line, allowed a 96-yard touchdown the Cowboys with practically zero resistance than punted immediately after. Then things shifted. A Ravens touchdown drive, the defense holds the Cowboys to a field goal despite a terribly missed OPI call that was instead a DPI. Then with 6-seconds remaining, Lamar Jackson magic. A 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers, who was somehow playing on this terrible field. Then the first clutch moment of hopefully many for Tyler Loop. Redemption at 56-yards. Ravens win. This team still clearly has problems in the fourth quarter. The defense still clearly has issues. The offensive line might have a massive issue with all three centers hurt. This team could still turn out to be bad when the season is over. But for now, they went into Brazil, pulled off a heist, stole the win, and booked it out like it was Fast and Furious 5. — Zach Canter Fans in Brazil were treated to an incredible game. The Ravens somehow, someway pulled out the victory after a bogus pass interference call seemed to doom them at the end. Tyler Loop’s redemption is here and it is magnificent. You have to hope that pulling this game out will help this team’s mentality going forward after nearly blowing another game in which they had a double-digit lead. There are some massive concerns still, most notably at center after both Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic left the game with injuries. I am not sure what Baltimore will do at the position if both players are out for extended time. Zay Flowers showed why he is so vital to this offense in this game after missing Week 2 as he made multiple big plays, including the final catch to set up the Loop field goal. — Dustin Cox The Ravens seemed to be heading towards another blown double-digit lead and crushing loss, which would have been a brutal pill to swallow for two weeks in a row. Instead, they were able to stave off a seemingly inevitable late collapse thanks to heroics in all three phases. It started with the defense getting a three-and-out to give the Ravens’ offense the opportunity to drive down the field for a go-ahead touchdown, which they capitalized on. The defense barely hung on during the next drive but secured a red zone stop to keep the Cowboys from scoring a touchdown. That preluded Lamar Jackson and Zay Flowers’ 27-yard connection with seven seconds remaining to set up Tyler Loop’s game-winning, 56-yard field goal — a sequence that was nothing short of magical. The Ravens clearly have a lot to clean up still and injury concerns continue to pile up, but this was a huge character-building win. — Frank Platko
author: Zach Canter

title: Instant takeaways from the Ravens’ rollercoaster win over the Cowboys
summary: The Baltimore Ravens escaped Marcaña Stadium in Brazil with an electrifying 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Here are the instant takeaways from Baltimore Beatdown’s staff: Loop the Redeemer It was a tough handful of months for Tyler Loop: missing the 44-yard field goal to end the Ravens season in January, taking all the crap […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Loop #33 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates with teammates after defeating the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens escaped Marcaña Stadium in Brazil with an electrifying 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Here are the instant takeaways from Baltimore Beatdown’s staff: Loop the Redeemer It was a tough handful of months for Tyler Loop: missing the 44-yard field goal to end the Ravens season in January, taking all the crap he did on social media, watching competition be brought in right before the season starts after a rough preseason. The trust level in Loop was not high heading into Week 1. Tyler Loop has done nothing be perfect since then. His only miss heading into Week 3 was a block in the Saint game. Then with 1 second remaining in the fourth-quarter, the Ravens likely desperate to avoid overtime and seeing the Cowboys offense once more, Tyler Loop hit the second longest field goal of his career from 56-yards to steal the win for Baltimore in Rio. The trust factor in the kicker is as high as it’s ever been in his career now. — Zach Canter The Ravens have a short yardage problem An offense with Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry should not routinely struggle to pick up a yard or two, but the Cowboys consistently blew up their short-yardage attempts including multiple stops on the goal line. This speaks not only to the Ravens’ issues at offensive line, but also offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s predictability in those moments. Today’s game proved it is not as simple as giving it to Henry and letting him push forward, and Mark Andrews’ hand injury may have ruled out any sneak attempts. Doyle has to figure out which levers to pull and balance feeding his bell cow with change-ups to keep defenses honest. – Nikhil Mehta The Ravens also have a tackling problem Year after year, the Ravens defense preaches physicality and intensity during training camp, and year after year, they start the season with sloppy technique and too many yards after contact. All of the issues were there: defensive backs fly in low and wild, linebackers go for big hits instead of wrapping up, defensive linemen struggle to stay on their feet. This isn’t play-calling or pass-rushing woes; it’s simple fundamentals, and a problem that has persisted for years in Baltimore. It always seems to happen on the back-breaking third downs, too – the opposite of ‘being the best when the best is needed.’ – Nikhil Mehta Center was already a concern. Now, it’s an emergency. The Ravens have a potential emergency on their hands at center after losing both Jovaugn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to injuries during the game. If both players are set to miss extended time, then Baltimore is in a true predicament. Vega Ioane filled in admirably during the game, so the Ravens may choose to stick with the rookie first-rounder going forward, but that means that right guard could now be a weakness again. – Dustin Cox Baltimore’s offense still runs on Lamar Jackson’s legs The Ravens struggled to find offensive consistency throughout the game. But when they needed it, Lamar Jackson would tuck it and run. It was noted before the game that the Cowboys struggled to defend against the quarterback run against Washington. It’s not a trigger the Ravens pull as often when Jackson was younger but he can still do it better than anybody in the NFL when needed. – Zach Canter

(Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers is ACTIVE for the team’s Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil following a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Inactives vs. Cowboys pic.twitter.com/0PBi2NYJrd — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) September 27, 2026 The 26-year-old wideout was listed as questionable after logging just one limited practice on Friday. After his warmup Zay Flowers telling me he’s preparing for a touchdown with this Samba celebration. Said he feels good. All encouraging news that we could see him out here today. #ravens pic.twitter.com/lQ9dBlXu3g — Tracy Wolfson (@tracywolfson) September 27, 2026 Flowers may be on a pitch count during the game, but his first-half explosion in Week 1 proved he can make a massive impact on even a handful of snaps, especially against an undermanned Cowboys secondary. The Ravens will still need Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews to follow up their encouraging Week 2 showings, but Flowers availability ensures Baltimore’s offense can have their best on the field (when the best is needed). With Flowers active, rookie wideout Elijah Sarratt will be a healthy scratch after suiting up last Sunday but not playing a single snap. The deactivation of safety K’Von Wallace is a curious decision since he was just elevated from the practice squad on Saturday. title: Ravens Roundtable: score predictions, X-factors for Week 3 vs. Cowboys
summary: It’s almost time for the Baltimore Ravens to kick off their Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil! Baltimore Beatdown’s staff presents their last minute predictions for the game: Nikhil Mehta I have a bad feeling about this one. Maybe it’s my longtime appreciation for the ethical quarterbacking of Dak […]
full_text: Sep 24, 2026; Rio de Janiero, Brazil; Workers place banners of Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton (14) and Ravens and Dallas Cowboys logos prior to the NFL Rio Game at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s almost time for the Baltimore Ravens to kick off their Week 3 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil! Baltimore Beatdown’s staff presents their last minute predictions for the game: Nikhil Mehta I have a bad feeling about this one. Maybe it’s my longtime appreciation for the ethical quarterbacking of Dak Prescott. Maybe it’s my fear of international games. But all of the vibes in the world cannot overshadow the fact that the Cowboys are missing several starting defenders in Brazil, while the Ravens will have Nnamdi Madubuike and Teddye Buchanan on the field for the first time this year. Positive pre-game updates regarding Zay Flowers also offer some optimism that Baltimore can keep up with Dallas’ offense in a potential shoot-out, too. But X-factor: Malaki Starks. The second-year safety had a rough first two games, and his task will not get any easier against Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. He will need to limit the Cowboys’ explosive plays and prevent this game from turning into a boat race. Score prediction: Ravens 30, Cowboys 27 Frank Platko The Cowboys have a high-powered passing attack led by a star wide receiver duo in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Dak Prescott is good at pushing the ball downfield and the Ravens’ secondary will be challenged. The Ravens need to be much better at tackling pass-catchers in the open field, which was a huge issue last week. If Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey hold up well in man coverage situations and the safeties limit explosive plays, the Ravens should be in good position to win. X-factor: Carson Vinson. Vinson will be making his first start at left tackle in place of Ronnie Stanley. The Ravens can provide support for him with extra blockers, but there will inevitably be times where Vinson is on island in pass protection. The Cowboys have young athletic pass-rushers who will challenge him. With the Ravens’ interior offensive line already being shaky in pass blocking, they can’t afford for Vinson to struggle in this spot. Score prediction: Ravens 27, Cowboys 24 Dustin Cox The Ravens will have to avoid a shootout with a potent Cowboys’ offense considering they will be without Ronnie Stanley and potentially Zay Flowers. If Flowers does play, he will likely be more limited than usual. Baltimore’s defense has to do a better job of ending drives this week, starting with finishing tackles and eliminating yards after the catch. I predict a heavy dosage of Derrick Henry this week after he received just five carries in the second half of Week 2. Ball control and winning time of possession will be key for the Ravens avoiding a shootout that they may not have the firepower to win. X-factor: Nnamdi Madubuike. Madubuike will return to the field in the first time in a year, and while it is unfair to expect him to be the same caliber of player right off the bat, he could still provide critical interior pressure on passing downs to help out Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green on the edges. Pressuring Dak Prescott and not allowing him to find his two superstar wide receivers will be paramount. Score prediction: Ravens 23, Cowboys 21
