full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) throws during the third quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2-0 Cincinnati Bengals traveled to Pittsburgh in Week 3 to take on the 1-1 Steelers. The Steelers came into the game with a sputtering offense, and the Bengals came in with a retooled defense that held the Texans out of the end zone in Week 2. So most fans weren’t expecting the shootout we got on Sunday. When the dust settled, the Bengals fell short, losing to the Steelers by a score of 27-30.. Here are Sunday’s winners and losers: WINNERS Dohnte Meyers With Andrei Iosivas on IR, the Bengals came into their Week 3 game looking for someone else to step up as WR3. Enter Dohnte Meyers, who had one of the best offseason stories in the NFL. He didn’t have a perfect game, but he was there when needed, finishing the game with three receptions for 29 yards and picked up a big first down early in the game. With so much attention on Chase and Higgins, Meyers could really run wild, especially if he gets the ball with space to work. Amarius Mims Mims came into the Bengals’ Week 3 game emerging as one of the best young right tackles in the NFL. He faced off against future Hall of Fame pass rusher T.J. Watt on Sunday. Watt was kept away from Burrow all afternoon and didn’t register a single pressure. Ja’Marr Chase Chase was left out of the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs, only catching two passes. That wasn’t the case in Week 2 or Week 3. He was involved early and often on Sunday. He scored the Bengals’ first touchdown in Pittsburgh, and he finished the game with nine receptions for 98 yards and a touchdown. Joe Burrow Burrow started the game off on fire in Week 3. He completed his first 13 consecutive passes to start the game, which included receptions from multiple receivers and a touchdown. His first incomplete pass came in the second quarter. He finished Sunday completing 28/37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns for a passer rating of 123.9. The late fumble was bad, but he had a great day overall that should have won the game before that final drive. Offensive line The Steelers have one of the better defenses in the league, and one of the best ones the Bengals will face in 2026. The Bengals’ offensive line allowed five sacks in Week 2 and was under the microscope facing off against a talented Steelers’ defensive front featuring Watt and Cam Heyward. The Bengals’ offensive line kept Burrow upright on Sunday throughout the vast majority of the game. The only sack the line gave up in the game came on the last offensive play of the game for Cincinnati. Tee Higgins Higgins is the best WR2 in the NFL, and the only reason he is considered WR2 is that he’s on the same team as the best wide receiver in the NFL, Ja’Marr Chase. Higgins finished the game with six receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown, but it was really one play that puts him on the list. It was a touchdown he caught in the second quarter as he was boxing out the defender and falling down. This goes right up there with some of the other ridiculous touchdowns in Higgins’ career. TEE HIGGINS ARE YOU SERIOUS?! 😱 @CINvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3D6JpNBA3Q — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Dexter Lawrence He wasn’t the run-stopping monster he was in Houston, but Lawrence came up with two key sacks on Rodgers in the second half. The last sack he had was on third-and-goal. He was able to hold on to Rodgers until the whistle blew, forcing the Steelers to settle for a field goal instead of a touchdown. Lawrence, in his monstrous frame, is showing he can do it all. LOSERS Colbie Young Like Meyers, Young had an opportunity to make himself known against the Steelers with Iosivas on IR. Unfortunately, Young tweaked his knee after catching Burrow’s first pass on the afternoon and would later leave the game. It’ll be a few weeks before Iosivas is eligible to return, so hopefully Young’s knee is okay, and he’ll be out there helping the offense move the ball in the coming games. Bengals’ Pass Rush The Bengals’ defense came into Week 3 with eight sacks, which tied them with the Raiders for the lead in the league. The Steelers were starting a new right guard and right tackle, and Rodgers, at 42 years old, isn’t going to make anybody miss, right? Right?!? No. The Bengals’ defensive front got no consistent pressure on Rodgers, allowing him to sit in the pocket and pick the secondary apart. The Steelers had the 31st-ranked offense heading into Week 3, but the Bengals’ retooled defensive front just couldn’t get things going. They allowed Rodgers to dance around in the backfield and scramble like he was 20 years younger. Cedric Johnson After the Bengals took their first lead of the game early in the third quarter, the defense forced a stop. As the ball left Kaden Wetjen’s foot, Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson slid into the punter’s plant leg, drawing an easy 15-yard penalty. The Steelers retook the lead after scoring a touchdown a few plays later. Secondary DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman are NFL wide receivers, but they cannot be compared to Chase and Higgins. The Bengals’ secondary, which faced off against the best wide receiver duo in the NFL throughout the offseason and in practice, allowed 292 passing yards and three touchdowns. There were five Steelers receivers with catches over 20 yards. It all came to a head with a Rodgers touchdown pass to Metcalf that saw two Bengals cornerbacks run into each other. Cue the Benny Hill music…. Hill & Turner run into each other. 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/ef0WYooUq7 — ZIM (@zimwhodey) September 27, 2026 The Bengals’ secondary will face much better offenses than the Steelers. While the lack of a pass rush didn’t help, a secondary as talented as the Bengals’ has to do better. Run defense Dexter Lawrence and the Bengals’ defensive front absolutely shut the run down heading into Week 3, especially in Houston in Week 2. Again, with an offensive line featuring a couple of new starters, the Steelers were able to lean on the running game. Jaylen Warren carried the ball 17 times for 127 yards and averaged 7.5 yards per carry. There was even a holding call on Metcalf that brought back an 87-yard run from Warren that would have made things so much worse. Ke’Shawn Williams In the fourth quarter, nursing a three-point lead, the Bengals’ defense forced a punt. This time the ball was kicked cleanly, but it hit Williams, the return man, right in the facemask. PJ Jules wasn’t able to recover the ball and lost it to the Steelers, who recovered the ball and took over on their own 14-yard line. The Steelers took a three-point lead after the muffed punt and kept it until the final whistle blew. Darrin Simmons Simmons has been the special teams coach in Cincinnati since 2003 and is the longest-tenured coach by far on the Bengals’ staff. He’s largely considered one of the best coordinators in the league, but his unit cost the team 10 points, all from the punt return team. Special teams is made up of more than just the kicking game. Simmons needs to work with his guys because the two special teams snafus were the difference in the game, translating into 10 points for the Steelers. Zac Taylor The Bengals should have won this game. They’re the more talented team on offense and defense, and the Bengals just kept shooting themselves in the foot. In the end, it all falls on Taylor. It’s his responsibility to put together the game plan and adjust it if need be. He had a shot to start at 3-0 for the first time in his career, but was out-coached by Mike McCarthy.

title: Browns Week 4: Steelers’ 2 wins have come in completely different ways
summary: When the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers kick off Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North will be on the line. The winner will run their early season record to 3-1, with the loser dropping back to .500 during the first quarter of the season. For both teams, their […]
full_text: When the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers kick off Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North will be on the line . The winner will run their early season record to 3-1, with the loser dropping back to .500 during the first quarter of the season. For both teams, their Week 1 performances would not have indicated that winning was in the near future. The Browns were humiliated in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Steelers won in a game that seemed to set back football a little bit. Cleveland has bounced back with two straight victories, while Pittsburgh only put up three points in a Week 2 loss before beating the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. With Thursday Night right around the corner, a quick turnaround for both teams, as well as fans and media. A look at the Steelers’ two victories, tells completely different stories about the team. In Week 1, against an Atlanta Falcons team playing their third string quarterback, the defense was able to limit everyone but RB Bijan Robinson who had over 170 total yards and the Falcons lone touchdown. On offense, nothing was really rolling. QB Aaron Rodgers completed just 24 of his 40 passes for 221 yards and a touchdown. RB Jaylen Warren had just 10 carries for 46 yards, while RB Rico Dowdle had eight rushes for a paltry 15 yards. The Week 1 win was far from impressive. This week, versus the Bengals, was a different story. Cincinnati still gave the game away late with a fumble, but Steelers’ offense was able to get going, and its defense was able to limit RB Chase Brown to just 61 yards on 13 carries. In Week 3, Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. While star WR DK Metcalf has continued to struggle to get going, Rodgers was able to spread the ball around to a number of targets to put up almost 300 yards passing. The big difference was in the running game, with Warren rushing for 127 yards on just 17 carries. The versatile back also caught three passes for 49 yards. Pittsburgh’s defense did allow Cincinnati’s potent passing offense to be productive, with QB Joe Burrow throwing for 282 yards and three scores. They also forced the huge Burrow fumble late in the game, with the Bengals in field goal position to tie the score with less than a minute left. Cincinnati helped the Steelers cause on special teams with Ke’Shawn Williams fumbling a punt that led to an easy field goal a few plays later. In all, Pittsburgh has been helped greatly by their opponents in both of their victories, but the offense was far more explosive in Week 3, while the defense has figured out how to take away key parts of the opposing offense in those weeks. The Week 2 loss to the now 1-2 New England Patriots was a team failure, including a poor performance by Rodgers and company. While the Steelers are 2-1 and lead the AFC North due to tiebreakers, do you think they are any good? What do you think the Browns must do in Week 4 to take the division lead with a win? full_text: How fun is this? While we are going to write about the Cleveland Browns NFL draft positioning , it isn’t about the Cleveland Browns being bad. Instead, with the Browns having the Los Angeles Rams’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, “ Rams Watch ” is squarely on. For the Browns, NFL playoff positioning is far more interesting , especially because a win on Thursday Night Football would vault them into first place in the AFC North. For the Rams, starting out 1-2 by blowing a big halftime lead on Sunday Night Football has been exacerbated by their Week 1 trip to Australia and injuries to WR Puka Nacua and Garrett. Their draft positioning, with only three games in the books, is highly dependent on tiebreakers at this point. Right now, 17 teams have one win or are winless. The 1-1 Chicago Bears could move that number down one with a victory over the 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but Caleb Williams will miss a few weeks due to injury. title: Browns Week 3: 2025 winning carried over, team win but new star, Deshaun Watson enough
summary: I vividly remember the Cleveland Browns losing their season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and the entire city was miserable for an entire week. Funny how things have changed. In front of their fans, the Browns found a way to pull off another win against an NFC South opponent in the Carolina Panthers. It wasn’t […]
full_text: I vividly remember the Cleveland Browns losing their season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and the entire city was miserable for an entire week . Funny how things have changed. In front of their fans, the Browns found a way to pull off another win against an NFC South opponent in the Carolina Panthers . It wasn’t pretty, but winning in the NFL is hard, and finding a way to get a victory is all that matters. Time for “4 Downs” thoughts on Week 3’s victory: 1st Down: Resilience from last year carries over to this year Despite the Browns having a losing record from last season, the one that team did last season was fight week in and week out. Two weeks in, the team has shown a similar trait from last season that has translated over to this season, under a new head coach. The resilience trait. A lot of things didn’t go the Browns way against the Panthers, but somehow, this team continued to fight. Young teams might not have the high end talent that contenders have but the one thing they have that you can’t measure is fight. Cleveland has that. It might be small but it’s something that most should notice about this current iteration of the Cleveland Browns is how resilient they are in these two victories, and that started with the late wins last year. 2nd Down: Deshaun Watson finds a way when it mattered From a statistical standpoint, it wasn’t a great day for Watson. However, when it mattered the most Watson found a way to come through. It would’ve been easy for Watson to fold, as some have seen him do in the past, but he didn’t. Whether it was using his legs when it was required or finding a way to get the ball to the talented playmakers, Watson found a way to help the team when it was his time to make a play. that's ✌️ scores on the day for Harold! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/gYzHTbpmYR — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 During Watson’s postgame interview with FOX NFL reporter Jennifer Hale, the answers that Watson gave were pretty telling: The @Browns improve to 2-1 on the season! @JenHale504 caught up with Cleveland QB Deshaun Watson after the 21-18 victory over Carolina pic.twitter.com/ELMrzxQr88 — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 27, 2026 It wasn’t long ago the fans were booing Watson in a preseason game, now the fans are cheering and supporting him. Regardless of what you think of Watson, the one thing to respect is his work ethic. Whether it was him tearing his shoulder labrum or tearing his Achilles twice, the fact that he came back instead of quitting speaks volumes. In the above interviewn he finally gave the right answers, and the answers seemed sincere, but if you play well, then the fans will support you. It’s as simple as that. 3rd Down: Defense rises to occasion, Mason Graham slowly becoming a star If one unit deserves a game ball, it’s the Browns defense. The defense is undergoing an overhaul with losing future Hall of Famer Myles Garrett, but the good news is that the unit is filled with young talent that have emerged going back to last year. It’s not a hot take, but defensive tackle Mason Graham is the best player on the Browns defensive line. Three games in, the tape and the stats back that up. Mason Graham gets home for the SACK 💪 @CARvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5feCV43oaN — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Mason Graham collects his second sack of the day! Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/8YFKbq32K6 https://t.co/zCUOpeOrRO pic.twitter.com/rP65C217Zi — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) September 27, 2026 Carolina’s offense was averaging 35 points coming into this matchup, and they only managed to reach the endzone once while being held on 4/15 on 3rd down. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg was creative in terms of being more flexible in terms of calling the defense; defensive end Jared Verse made his presence known, and the secondary kept the explosive plays to a minimum. It seems that Week 1 performance was more of an outlier, and the past two weeks are the real Browns defense we are watching. 4th Down: Thursday night is suddenly an important game The last time the Browns were 2-1, it was 2023. Everyone knows how that season went, but if not, for a refresher, Cleveland made the playoffs that season. Fast forward to now, the team is 2-1 and the Thursday night tilt against the Pittsburgh Steelers is suddenly important. Every team in the AFC North is 2-1, but the one team that can make a statement on Thursday is the team in Northeast Ohio. If you find a way to win at home against a hated rival, conversations will begin to start. Nationally televised games can be billed as “statement” games. From a distance, I don’t think the Steelers are that good and are beatable. If the team finds a way to win, not only will you find yourself in first place in the division, but you also have a chance to send a statement to the rest of the country. I don’t believe the Browns are as bad of a team as many thought after Week 1, but is this team is capable of winning the big games? The Browns already did it twice against two teams expected to contend for the NFL playoffs; can they do it again on Thursday? Extra points Cleveland was penalized 12 times for 84 yards. Some of the penalties were egregious, but most were just pre-snap penalties that will get cleaned up, have to get cleaned up. Can’t win many games if you have more penalties than the other team. Not pushing the panic button on RT Tytus Howard, but Sunday wasn’t a great day for him. Considering how bad the offensive line was last season, fans can’t be picky about who the team has out there now. The Browns are rarely on FOX, but whenever they are, they usually get stuck with Myers/Schlereth. Rather hear Albert/Vilma or Kugler/Johnston, but beggars can’t be choosers. Browns offense couldn’t get anything going in the 3rd quarter: 8 yards in a single quarter is insane. The Steelers might be 2-1, but I am not moved by them at all. Thursday night will be interesting to watch. What are your takeaways from Week 3’s Browns vs Panthers? How excited are you for TNF versus the Steelers? Join the conversation! full_text: Two weeks ago, no one could have imagined that talking about Cleveland Browns playoff positioning would be a rational thing to do. The NFL is a “week-to-week league,” as HC Todd Monken has said multiple times, but Week 1 was so bad that many Browns fans were already making plans for what they would be doing while their team was being trounced week in and week out. Following the completion of Week 3, with two NFC teams playing on Monday Night Football, Cleveland is riding high with two straight victories over NFC South opponents , with the Pittsburgh Steelers coming to town for Thursday Night Football , which promises to be “rocking.” The AFC playoff race is an interesting one. There are nine teams with two or more victories, including the Browns, three with just one win, and four winless teams, including the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans. All four AFC North teams sit at 2-1, with the early-season tiebreakers pushing Cleveland to the third spot. AFC Playoff Picture After Week 3 Kansas City Chiefs: 3-0 Buffalo Bills: 3-0 Jacksonville Jaguars: 2-1 Pittsburgh Steelers: 2-1 Las Vegas Raiders: 3-0 Baltimore Ravens: 2-1 Denver Broncos: 2-1 Cleveland Browns: 2-1 Cincinnati Bengals: 2-1 New York Jets: 1-2 New England Patriots: 1-2 Indianapolis Colts: 1-2 Tennessee Titans: 0-3 Miami Dolphins: 0-3 Los Angeles Chargers: 0-3 Houston Texans: 0-3 As the season goes on, the tiebreakers will become important. The first two tend to decide most standings: Head-to-head and winning percentage within the conference (for Wild Card spots) or division games (for deciding who takes the division). full_text: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) fumbles as he is sacked by Cleveland Browns safety Grant Delpit (9) (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns opened as 2.5-point home underdogs against the Pittsburgh Steelers ahead of their Week 4 match-up on Thursday Night Football, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under on the game is 37.5. The Browns (2-1) are coming off of a 21-18 victory over the Carolina Panthers . Cleveland’s defense continued to have a stellar day, including pressuring QB Bryce Young on 51% of his dropbacks. They may have given up a lot of excess yardage late, but they still held on and forced several turnovers on downs. The offense, meanwhile, is slow-but-steady. The penalties by the offensive line are still too much, but QB Deshaun Watson — besides some errant misfires — is making some good runs, and delivering some clutch passes in the red zone. After being blown out in the first game, no one expected Cleveland to be 2-1 heading into this game. The Steelers (2-1) are coming off what I would deem to be a surprising 30-27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals. After scraping by the first week with a win over the Falcons, Pittsburgh was dominated by the Patriots in Week 2 by a score of 20-3, and looked like an offense that was in trouble. Instead, they had 411 yards of offense against the Bengals “new-look defense,” and Aaron Rodgers tossed three touchdown passes. This is the second home game in a row in which the Browns are home underdogs. It’s not often that you see that happen, unless there is a clear better team on the other side. However, with Cleveland’s momentum in these last two games, and them not facing a team that is projected to be Super Bowl-bound, seeing the Browns as underdogs is a bit of a surprise. It’s possible the sportsbooks haven’t caught up yet to the Browns being good. The over/under for the game is 37.5. What odds would you take if you were placing a bet? title: Browns vs. Panthers Week 3: Winners and losers from a big day
summary: The Cleveland Browns enjoyed their Victory Monday in Week 2 so much that they decided to keep the party going this week. They left it late, but the Browns walked out of Huntington Bank Field on Sunday with a 21-18 victory over the Carolina Panthers.  It wasn’t always pretty – especially on offense – and […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns enjoyed their Victory Monday in Week 2 so much that they decided to keep the party going this week. They left it late, but the Browns walked out of Huntington Bank Field on Sunday with a 21-18 victory over the Carolina Panthers. It wasn’t always pretty – especially on offense – and it wasn’t easy, but the win leaves the Browns in a tie for first place in the AFC North Division with the Pittsburgh Steelers coming to town for a national TV game on Thursday night. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves, as there are Brownies and Frownies to hand out for today’s big win. atta boy Mason 💪 #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/AaFHWbjhUM — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Week 3 Winners: Brownies Most of the high points from the game involved the defense, most notably: Defensive tackle Mason Graham, who finished with two sacks and three tackles for loss in what was arguably the best game of his young career. Graham is the first Cleveland defensive player to have a sack in each of the first three games of a season since a guy named Myles Garrett in 2019. Carolina came into the game averaging 35.5 points per game. On Sunday? Just 18 points against a Cleveland defense that got after the Panthers all game long. The defense was effective on third and fourth downs, holding the Panthers to a combined four-of-18. While the defense carried much of the water for the day, the offense and special teams did their part as well: Andre Szmyt converted both of his field-goal attempts to extend his streak to 20 consecutive made field goals, dating back to last season. Not content to let Szmyt have all the fun, punter Corey Bojorquez dropped three of his five punts inside the 20-yard line. that's ✌️ scores on the day for Harold! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/gYzHTbpmYR — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 After a quiet start to the season with just two receptions in Week 1, tight end Harold Fannin Jr. has picked up the pace over the past two weeks. On Sunday, he had a team-high seven receptions for 51 yards, and added a pair of touchdown catches – one at the end of the first half and the game-winner with 1:48 remaining in the fourth quarter. It wasn’t always easy, but the Browns kept pounding away with the run game against Carolina’s defense and found some success by averaging 4.4 yards per carry, with Quinshon Judkins leading the way with 70 rushing yards. Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a rocky day – more on that in a moment – but he came up big on third downs (five-of-seven for 44 yards and that fourth-quarter touchdown to Fannin). He also avoided turning the ball over, which is always helpful. Watson saved his best for last as he completed three passes for 34 yards and added a 21-yard run on the game-winning touchdown drive. In the fourth quarter, Watson was six-of-nine for 77 yards and the touchdown. The Browns still struggled on third down, finishing just 5-of-15, but did convert their first third down in the first half of a game, so baby steps. Second half starting off strong 🔥 #CARvsCLE 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/8kL4rhfD2C — Carolina Panthers (@Panthers) September 27, 2026 Week 3 Losers: Frownies There was much rejoicing when the Browns hired Todd Monken as head coach because the team would finally have a “hard-nosed coach” who would “put a stop” to the pre-snap penalties that have plagued the team. Well, on Sunday against the Panthers, the Browns were penalized 12 times, which included one offensive drive in the second quarter with five penalties called on the offensive line – three false starts, an illegal formation, and a holding call. The Browns deferred after winning the opening coin toss and were in prime position to build on their 10-3 lead when they received the kickoff to open the second half. But a penalty on the Panthers forced a re-kick, and returner Malachi Corley fumbled the return away to the Panthers. The defense held Carolina to just a field goal, but it was enough momentum to get the Panthers back in the game. The third quarter offense was as bad as it has ever been. The Browns had three offensive possessions in the quarter and ran a total of nine plays for 3 yards of total offense. The inability to get anything going allowed the Panthers to get back into the game as they took a 12-10 lead on Ryan Fitzgerald’s fourth field goal of the day on the drive after Cleveland’s final three-and-out of the third quarter. Week 3 Quick Hits: Milk Bones On Cleveland’s final touchdown drive, Watson took a big hit and had to leave the field for one play. Enter Shedeur Sanders for his first action of the season. Despite having no first-team reps since the preseason, Sanders finished the game one-of-one passing for zero yards, making him the only quarterback (probably) on the day to complete every pass he attempted. Who are your winners and losers for Week 3 Browns vs. the Panthers?
author: Thomas Moore

title: Browns vs Panthers: 15 takeaways from Week 3 as Cleveland wins again
summary: If most of us are being honest, after Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, there was little hope for the Cleveland Browns. The defense seemed to have nothing without Jim Schwartz and Myles Garrett, while the offense was downright terrible with QB Deshaun Watson at the helm. Two weeks and two wins later, the […]
full_text: If most of us are being honest, after Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season , there was little hope for the Cleveland Browns. The defense seemed to have nothing without Jim Schwartz and Myles Garrett , while the offense was downright terrible with QB Deshaun Watson at the helm . Two weeks and two wins later, the Browns head into Thursday Night Football tied for the AFC North lead and a chance to take over the top spot all by themselves by knocking off the Pittsburgh Steelers. A nail-biter victory in Week 3 , in the home opener against the Carolina Panthers, has Cleveland fans spinning a different tune than we all were just two weeks ago. How? Really, a total team effort, a lot of big plays when needed, and two wins over NFC South teams that were expected to compete for the NFL playoffs this season. Here are 15 takeaways from Browns vs. Panthers: Coaching adjustments key: Some big, some small The Browns have been far from perfect in the two victories, but the coaching staff has made a few big changes, including a more flexible defense with more man coverage. In Week 3, DC Mike Rutenberg brought a ton of blitzes from all over the place, moving players like Jared Verse in different spots, and kept QB Bryce Young guessing about who was going to blitz. HC Todd Monken also made some adjustments early and late in the game to get the offense moving. Getting Watson out on the move, using KC Concepcion’s motions as a distraction, and a few key duo blocks to get Quinshon Judkins moving forward, Monken is setting up plays from game to game. Mason Graham continues to excel The new MG might not be the physical talent that the old MG (Garrett) on the Browns defensive line, but his impact is needed and impressive. On Sunday, Graham had seven tackles, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits. Interior pressure generally has a bigger impact on offenses than the edge, and Graham has four sacks through three games Deshaun Watson’s legs help and open things up Even before his 21-yard gallop late in the game, Watson’s legs kept drives going and kept defenders frozen at times, including the first touchdown pass to TE Harold Fannin Jr. Defenses can’t be too aggressive in attacking Watson, and had a spy watching him, taking one defender out of coverage on Fannin’s long over route score. Later in the game, Watson’s big run put them in position to score, then got out on the move, drawing defenders, which allowed Fannin space to get open for his second score. Watson wasn’t perfect, but his legs are important even when his passing stats are not big. Isaiah McGuire, moving Jared Verse, blitzing all needed for pass rush This Cleveland defense may not have someone like Garrett to create quick pressure, but the coverage from Carson Schwesinger, Quincy Williams, Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell, Ronnie Hickman, and Grant Delpit means Rutenberg can get creative with his blitzes. That creativity is needed if the Browns are going to put pressure on the quarterback from the outside, instead of just from Graham and company on the inside. DE Isaiah McGuire was able to get a couple of quick pressures off the edge, something that can be really helpful when it happens. Any edge rush, with a blitz or not, will impact the game hugely with the interior line’s abilities. HOW MANY PENALTIES? 12. Seriously. 12 penalties, not all good calls by the refs, for 84 yards. They have to get better, by a decent amount, when it comes to discipline, especially some of the offensive ones with not lining up in an appropriate formation. OLine, especially Tytus Howard, struggling Rookie Spencer Fano put on an island; looked like a rookie much of the game. Cleveland’s offense didn’t give him a lot of help and expected him to hold up. Unfortunately, it looks like film from the first two games showed that Fano could be beaten inside because Carolina attacked him there a lot. Howard continues to really struggle, not just with penalties: Browns RT Tytus Howard has been flagged for three false starts today, which ties him with Garrett Bradbury for the second-most penalties among offensive linemen this season (via ESPN Research). — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 27, 2026 Can’t beat the refs and the opponent too often There were a few bad calls, including “roughing the passer” where Young fell down and another where his lineman pushed him into a Browns defender. This missed called is wild given where the ref is looking: The ref is looking RIGHT AT DESHAUN WATSON. WTF pic.twitter.com/XKDCbCP9nm — Nick Wilson (@NickWilsonSays) September 27, 2026 Not taking out Malachi Corley Corley got hit hard on a kickoff, but a penalty led to another kickoff and Corley fumbled. The big hit should have led Cleveland’s coaches to play it safe on the re-kick. Instead, Corley quickly put Carolina in a position to score coming out of halftime. A missed detail where caution would have been huge. Browns defense imperfect, impressive given offense’s struggles A lot of credit has to go to Cleveland’s defense for the win. Carolina scored 81 points in their first two games but the Browns held them to 18 despite a lot of struggles from their offense. It helped that Xavier Legette missed the game and Jalen Coker left the game injured, but Cleveland did it without Tyson Campbell . A lot of credit is due to the Browns defense: 3 quarters of undisciplined offensive football by Browns… and they’re still in it. Just hope the defense doesn’t wear down in 4th, because they’ve played HARD. — LeCharles Bentley (@64AMDG) September 27, 2026 Browns defense hasn’t given up a touchdown to a team that’s scored at least 30 points the first two weeks and they’re losing lol — Colb (@___Colb___) September 27, 2026 While Cleveland gave up a touchdown after the above post, it doesn’t change how impressive the defense was. Grant Delpit looked a step slow, limited Just a quick note that Delpit’s shoulder injury might be worse than some believe because he looked less aggressive than he normally is in tackling and was slow in coverage. Nothing that hurt the team too much, but notable heading into a short week and something the Steelers will likely see on film. Panthers O adjusted to pressure Sometimes, it’s important to note how the opponent deserves some credit. Blitzes often lead to zone defense and open areas if pressure doesn’t hit. The Browns were causing a lot of issues with their pressure, so Carolina ran more crossers and quick hitters to take advantage of that. They also moved Young off his spot more, to create more openings. Credit to the Panthers, but Rutenberg adjusted enough in big moments and later in the game instead of just doing the same thing over and over again. Watson does just enough, improves late in game As many of the messages in our game thread, DMs, and texts communicated, Watson wasn’t good enough for most of the second half. Instead of folding or making things worse, Watson was able to do just enough and make a few big plays when it mattered most. “All the fans wanted to see is for us to score a damn touchdown,” as Monken said during his post-game press conference. Watson was a part of that, did just enough. Jaycee Horn injury huge for 2-point conversion A small thing, but without Horn in the game for the late 2-point conversion, Denzel Boston was left without the top cornerback on the other side on the 2-point conversion. Those two points were huge to push the lead to three points, and Horn’s injury was very notable as Boston converted. Todd Monken’s risky 4th down, 4th quarter call “We get to 4th and 1… to me, it’s 50/50…” – Monken, in his post-game press conference. In the end, it worked out. “A lot of it was Browns hurting Browns,” as Monken said, including himself, but had the Panthers tied the game or won the game in regulation, the head coach would have put himself squarely in the crosshairs of the fans and media. Instead, now it’s just a footnote from this game. Given the slim margin of error the young Cleveland team…
author: Jared Mueller

title: Carolina Panthers vs. Cleveland Browns recap: Deshaun Watson, defense play complete game to win home opener
summary: It was a down-to-the-wire home opener for the Cleveland Browns. The defense was dominant in the first half, while the offense made some plays to have a 10-3 lead. Cleveland got cold in the second half, though, allowing Carolina to chip away and eventually take the lead. In the fourth quarter, QB Deshaun Watson had […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 27: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns carries the ball against Derrick Brown #95 of the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field on September 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a down-to-the-wire home opener for the Cleveland Browns. The defense was dominant in the first half, while the offense made some plays to have a 10-3 lead. Cleveland got cold in the second half, though, allowing Carolina to chip away and eventually take the lead. In the fourth quarter, QB Deshaun Watson had a shot at leading a game-winning drive, with the Browns in the red zone. He found TE Harold Fannin for his second touchdown of the game to give Cleveland a 21-18 lead. With two minutes to go, it was QB Bryce Young’s chance to lead another late-game rally. The defense came up big and the Browns won! Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Panthers vs. Browns The Panthers got the ball first this week. After QB Bryce Young completed one quick hitter for a first down, the Browns’ defense clamped down by getting pressure on him and forcing an intentional grounding. Carolina ran the ball on third down as a give up play before punting it away. On the punt return, an illegal block in the back penalty forced QB Deshaun Watson to start his first drive back at the 8 yard line. Watson used his legs to pick up a pair of first downs, including somehow dodging a free blitzer on 3rd-and-6 to take off up the middle. 4 on the move! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/JQSyFRCEaJ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Watson then tried throwing, but overshot TE Harold Fannin deep, and then was nearly picked off on a short pass to WR KC Concepcion . On third down, Watson again dodged pressure, but his completion to RB Raheim Sanders was short of a first down, leading to a punt. P Corey Bojorquez’ punt was fair caught at the 19 yard line. Young again got one first down through the air before the Browns’ defense came up with several nice stops again, including S Ronnie Hickman coming up with a nice third down tackle on a crossing route to force another punt. Carolina’s punt was downed at the 9 yard line. The Browns strung together a nice-looking drive for the rest of the quarter, with Watson getting a few completions, and then the ground game getting going with RB Quinshon Judkins . A pass interference penalty on a route by WR Jerry Jeudy also gained 17 yards. Cleveland then faced a 3rd-and-short in field goal range, but RG Austin Barber and RT Tytus Howard had back-to-back false starts. After a completion to Sanders, the Browns faced a 4th-and-3 to end the quarter from the 37 yard line. 2nd Quarter – Panthers vs. Browns The Browns went for it to start the fourth quarter, and Watson hit Concepcion on the quick out to move the chains. The offensive line continued hurting the offense, this time with LT Spencer Fano committing a hold that negated a downfield completion to WR Denzel Boston . On 2nd-and-20, Watson tried to buy time but was sacked. However, instead of being 3rd-and-22, a defensive hold was signaled on the Panthers to give Cleveland a fresh set of downs. Two plays later, Johnson had another false start in a drive that was getting ridiculous now. Facing 2nd-and-14, Watson tried firing a pass to Boston, but he couldn’t hang on amidst the tight coverage. On 3rd-and-14, Watson threw the ball away and the punt unit had to come on, ending a drive that took up nine minutes of game clock but led to nothing. Bojorquez’ punt was out of bounds at the 16 yard line. The Panthers’ third drive started like the others — a first down completion, and then a run play that was stuffed. Young evaded pressure and found a tight end that just barely got beyond the sticks. Young then found WR Jalen Coker to midfield as the passing game continued to find success. Facing a 3rd-and-3, Young dropped a nice pass to Coker up the left sideline, but he couldn’t haul it in. On 4th-and-3, the Panthers lined up to go for it at the 43 yard line. Carolina took a timeout, but still kept the offense out there to go for it. Young took the snap and was pressured, with DT Mason Graham notching his third sack of the season for a 10-yard loss, all the way back to the Panthers’ 47 yard line with 8:33 to go in the second quarter. MASON FLYIN' IN! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/mKrCqhjAss — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Cleveland began their drive with a screen pass to Judkins that was good for 9 yards. Two plays later, a quarterback sneak moved the chains. Then, on 2nd-and-10, Watson hit Fannin for 8 yards to set up 3rd-and-2. The pressure came and the defense would’ve drilled Sanders on a run. Watson kept it, and the defense still got to him for a loss of 3 yards. K Andre Szmyt came on for a 48-yard field goal, and it was good right down the middle to give Cleveland a 3-0 lead with 5:43 left in the half. Three straight runs to Hubbard made it 4th-and-short, but at Carolina’s own 40 yard line. They lined up to go for it again, and off of the play fake by Young, pressure came in his face, forcing an erratic throw to an open receiver and a turnover on downs. Judkins got the carry to begin Cleveland’s drive, and found a hole right up the middle for 11 yards and a first down. After a short run by Judkins, Sanders came on and got the handoff from Shotgun, finding open space for 17 yards to the 10-yard line at the two-minute warning. Rocket goin' off for 17 yards! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/63Nhy5dV4e — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 After the two-minute warning, Judkins gained 3 yards and the Panthers took a timeout. On 2nd-and-goal from the 7 yard line, the call was a quarterback draw, but it was stopped after a gain of just a yard. On 3rd-and-goal from the 6 yard line, Watson took off again, but only got to the 3 yard line. On 4th-and-goal from the 3 yard line, Cleveland went for it. The initial read wasn’t open, but Watson stayed patient and found Fannin breaking open to the right corner of the end zone for the touchdown and a 10-0 lead with 1:37 to go in the half. catch in the corner for Harold! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/JP0yIUl3Gr — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Carolina threw two straight incomplete passes before Young got a completion to the sideline for a first down. Then, a bogus roughing the passer penalty called on DT Mike Hall gave Carolina new life. A couple plays later, Young got a dumpoff to Hubbard, who broke free for 30 yards, with another roughing the passer penalty tacked on, to set up 1st-and-goal at the 8 yard line. The defense held tight after that, including DE Isaiah McGuire getting a sack on third down to hold Carolina to a 35-yard field goal to make it a 10-3 game at the half. Isaiah stayed on it for the shoelace sack! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/YS3Y8BiM7s — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 3rd Quarter – Panthers vs. Browns It was a bad start to the second half for Cleveland. On the opening kickoff, a penalty was called on Carolina, so the Browns opted to have them re-kick. On the second return, WR Malachi Corley fumbled and the Panthers recovered. Second half starting off strong 🔥 #CARvsCLE 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/8kL4rhfD2C — Carolina Panthers (@Panthers) September 27, 2026 Starting in Cleveland territory, the Panthers have two short plays to Hubbard to set up 3rd-and-2. On third down, Young had another poor throw off of a rollout. Instead of going for it again, the field goal unit came on from 41 yards out to cut the Browns’ lead to 10-6, at least minimizing the damage. On the Browns’ opening drive of the half, on 3rd-and-6, Watson tried to escape from pressure, but a defender got a clear rip of the facemask. Even though the official had a clear line of sight of the play, the flag never came, and Watson was sacked, leading to a punt. The three-and-out led the Panthers to take over at the 20 yard…

full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: Tyson Campbell #7 of the Cleveland Browns and Josh Hines-Allen #41 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hug after an NFL football game at Everbank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. title: The Cowboys defense did enough in Brazil, relative to expectation
summary: We have all said it. Many times. The Dallas Cowboys defense simply has to be average. To be clear it is not my assertion that the Cowboys defense was average on Sunday in Brazil. They were severely outplayed by the Baltimore Ravens and were mostly not average. At times they were very far from average. […]
full_text: REUTERS/Brian Snyder | REUTERS We have all said it. Many times. The Dallas Cowboys defense simply has to be average. To be clear it is not my assertion that the Cowboys defense was average on Sunday in Brazil. They were severely outplayed by the Baltimore Ravens and were mostly not average. At times they were very far from average. But they did enough. The Cowboys defense did their part The first two Baltimore possessions of the game resulted in zero points. Initially the Ravens went three and out and then the Cowboys stopped them on fourth down to give their offense the ball at the Baltimore 30-yard line. Talk about a huge advantage. Dallas would go on to capitalize on that specific possession with a touchdown. The Cowboys also converted the other fourth-down stop that their defense produced with a touchdown. This one was more impressive and came when the stakes were much higher as Dallas stopped Baltimore from their own one-yard line with a three-yard TFL. Perfect harmony like that, fourth-down stops that lead to touchdowns, is generally how you win football games, but the Cowboys lost this one so everyone is pointing fingers and trying to figure out who to blame. The whole point here isn’t to deflect any blame at all from the defense. Blame them. They certainly deserve it in some respects. Injuries didn’t help, the field was obviously a tough situation for everybody, but they allowed Baltimore to get into field goal range with seven seconds left in the game and ultimately lost because of it. But to say that they specifically lost the game for the team seems unfair. The defense was not average in a measurable sense, but they produced two fourth-down stops that the offense turned into scores as noted. We expect the offense to be that good. It is held to a higher standard than the defense. We know this, we have known it, and because of it we say that average is all that is necessary from the defense to win. Well consider that the ‘Not Average’ defense did more than produce an opening punt and two other fourth-down stops. They pitched a second three-and-out after the Cowboys took the lead in the fourth quarter and gave the offense the ball with a 28-24 lead to protect. The Cowboys offense responded by going three and out themselves which led to a Baltimore touchdown. Isn’t that enough? Relative to context and expectation? Isn’t it enough that the defense answered the call so heroically in the fourth quarter like that? Sure, they bent and also broke at many points throughout the game, but when they absolutely had to they absolutely delivered late in the game. Twice! This is one of the biggest signs of optimism moving forward after the loss. Perhaps the defense is starting to find itself. They were not perfect in Brazil by any means, but they were certainly enough. Do you agree?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 5 key plays that led to the Cowboys loss
summary: Whether you blame personnel, injuries, or the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium, the Dallas Cowboys’ defense struggled to contain the Baltimore Ravens. Rookies Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham offered some bright spots, but those flashes weren’t consistent enough to win. On the other side, the Cowboys offense blew opportunities in the redzone through poor execution […]
full_text: Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images | Getty Images Whether you blame personnel, injuries, or the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium, the Dallas Cowboys’ defense struggled to contain the Baltimore Ravens. Rookies Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham offered some bright spots, but those flashes weren’t consistent enough to win. On the other side, the Cowboys offense blew opportunities in the redzone through poor execution and play-calling, while other mistakes plagued them between the 20s. The loss drops Dallas to 1-2 with plenty still to address. The team has a long flight home to begin sorting it out. Here are the five critical plays that sealed a gut-wrenching defeat in Brazil. Lamar Jackson’s 21-yard run The defensive collapse was foreshadowed early in the first quarter. After Dallas took a 10-0 lead, there was hope the Cowboys could keep the pressure on and force Baltimore into one-dimensional football. That never happened. The lid came off right after Brandon Aubrey’s kickoff—one of two he sent out of bounds, both of which gifted the Ravens strong starting field position. Facing 1st-and-15, Lamar Jackson got around the edge on a zone-read with an escort block from Mark Andrews. From that point, Baltimore used misdirection in the run game to create lanes and throwing windows while exposing the Cowboys’ eye discipline at the second level. The drive ended with a wildcat touchdown run by Derrick Henry, and many more points followed for the Ravens. 49-yard penalty on Markquese Bell Penalties repeatedly altered the game’s complexion—some questionable, others clear. Clinging to a three-point lead, the Cowboys had a chance to force Baltimore behind the sticks. Instead, Lamar Jackson scrambled free and threw a slightly underthrown pass toward Devontez Walker. Markquese Bell arrived early in coverage and made illegal contact, drawing a massive 49-yard pass-interference flag. It was the second such call of the drive (the first, on DaRon Bland, was highly debatable). Bell’s penalty proved especially costly as Derrick Henry scored on the next play. Terence Steele’s hold takes away the first down Dallas caught a tough break when a Jake Ferguson reception was ruled a fumble even though replay suggested he never had full control. Desperate to stop the bleeding, the Cowboys forced a stop on the ensuing Ravens possession. The offense was finally gaining traction. On a critical 3rd-and-9, Dak Prescott appeared to hit George Pickens for a 20-yard gain—until a Terence Steele holding penalty wiped it out. Forced into a long field-goal try, Brandon Aubrey’s 59-yard attempt was blocked by Keondre Jackson, one of several special-teams miscues on the day. How much Steele contributed to the blocked kick remains unclear, but the sequence was painful for the veteran tackle. Schoonmaker’s false start changes the play sheet Dallas did a solid job managing the clock to set up one final possession in regulation. When CeeDee Lamb drew a pass-interference call at the two-yard line with 23 seconds left, the entire playbook opened up. The Cowboys went aggressive with a fade to George Pickens that fell incomplete. On second down they could have handed the ball to Javonte Williams, who had run effectively all night. Instead, Luke Schoonmaker’s false start removed all doubt. Those five costly yards forced Dallas into a throw-only situation, handed Baltimore breathing room, and set up the final sequence. Ran out of bodies Failing to score the go-ahead touchdown on that last drive was disappointing. What no one expected was the defense completely disintegrating and allowing easy access to field-goal range. Already depleted after losing multiple safeties and then watching Shavon Revel exit with a knee injury, the Cowboys generated no pressure on Lamar Jackson. He had all day to find Zay Flowers open for the 27-yard gain that set up Tyler Loop’s 56-yard game-winner. Jackson called timeout with one second remaining, and Loop delivered the dagger. Think about the agonizing losses in Cowboys history—Jared Cook’s toe-drag, Matt Stafford’s fake spike into a quarterback sneak. This one ranks among the worst in the last 15 years, with injuries taking center stage at the bitter end. This one is going to hurt for a while.
author: LP Cruz

title: Why the Cowboys not trusting Brandon Aubrey led to loss
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost in absolutely brutal fashion on Sunday in Brazil. You know what happened. We will never be able to forget it. In case you want to re-live it though, the Cowboys tied things up with seven seconds left and seemed of the mind that their opponents were as willing as they were […]
full_text: Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost in absolutely brutal fashion on Sunday in Brazil. You know what happened. We will never be able to forget it. In case you want to re-live it though, the Cowboys tied things up with seven seconds left and seemed of the mind that their opponents were as willing as they were to go to overtime and figure things out there. Perhaps the Ravens were good with that, but if they were they likely changed their mind after the kickoff put them at the 35-yard line. To be clear it wasn’t the kickoff return that did this. It was the kickoff that Brandon Aubrey sent through the endzone, and him doing so took none of the seven seconds that remained in the game off of the clock. In the aftermath of the loss many Cowboys fans wondered how and why that sequence unfolded. Brian Schottenheimer provided the answer in his postgame presser by saying that Aubrey was told to boot it through the endzone given his trouble keeping things in bounds earlier in the game. Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer said the decision to do this stemmed from Brandon Aubrey kicking it out of bounds twice before, among other things. https://t.co/1Qz9f3nroC — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) September 28, 2026 Aubrey actually let multiple kicks get out of bounds before that point in the game. It makes sense that Cowboys brass wouldn’t trust him given that context. But was the lack of a trust something that should have outweighed the risk that this decision carried? The risk that ultimately burned the team? And shouldn’t the highest-paid kicker in the NFL not be one that can’t be trusted in critical situations like this? There is no other way to look at this whole situation as anything other than a failure within the game. Brandon Aubrey failed by creating doubt within his coaching staff, and the staff themselves failed by miscalculating and misplaying the situation. Everyone involved has to be better.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys 34-31 loss to the Ravens
summary: What an insane game! Who knew that football in Brazil would be so wild? International fans were treated to an exciting one, while fans back in the States were shown that, even playing on a different continent, this team will still find ways to break our hearts. The Dallas Cowboys lost a thriller in Rio […]
full_text: Reuters/Brian Snyder | Reuters What an insane game! Who knew that football in Brazil would be so wild? International fans were treated to an exciting one, while fans back in the States were shown that, even playing on a different continent, this team will still find ways to break our hearts. The Dallas Cowboys lost a thriller in Rio de Janeiro, falling 34-31 to the Baltimore Ravens. It was so close to turning out differently and turning our frowns upside down. But it didn’t. Here are 10 thoughts on this wild and crazy contest south of the equator. 1. Cowboys strike first The game started off fantastically! The defense forced a three-and-out, and the Cowboys marched down the field and got points. On the Ravens’ next possession, it got even better as the defense forced a four-and-out when Baltimore stubbornly went for it on fourth down, only to be stonewalled by a couple of rookie defenders. The Cowboys’ offense again marched down the field and got points. Before you could blink an eye, they were up 10-0. Were we witnessing a blowout in the making? Spoiler alert: We were not. 2. Ravens answer back It was great to see the Cowboys jump out to an early lead, but it did not last long. The Ravens answered, and they answered quickly. Baltimore scored touchdowns on their next two drives to take the lead 14-10 early in the second quarter. They went on to score 17 unanswered points and a 24-3 run that lasted late into the third quarter. As happy as we were early, the tide had shifted, and it shifted in a big way. 3. Digging their own grave After trailing at halftime, the Cowboys were driving down the field on their opening second-half drive, when the ball slipped out of their hands. Literally. The offense was threatening, but Jake Ferguson couldn’t handle a shovel pass, and the ball hit the turf. The officials took a close look at the play, as all turnovers are reviewed, but still chose to uphold the call despite the broadcast team believing it should have been ruled an incomplete pass. A promising drive turned into a whole lot of nothing. 4. More bad breaks It looked like the Cowboys were going to put that drive-stalling fumble behind them when they forced a three-and-out and were marching back down the field again. Javonte Williams got loose on a 22-yard run, and Dak Prescott connected with George Pickens for a 20-yard gain; however, the play came back after Terence Steele was called for holding. The Cowboys tried to get a long field goal out of it, but the kick was blocked, giving the Ravens great field position. Baltimore scored another touchdown, and the game appeared to be slowly slipping away. 5. Was he offsides? I don’t know if this is just the emotion talking, but when the Ravens blocked that field goal, were they offsides? It sure seemed like the edge guy came across early, forcing Terence Steele to slide outside and leaving the inside rusher with a clear lane to the kicker. If they were, it was a good trick. Steele has enough trouble blocking one guy, let alone two. 6. Staying alive Down 24-13 late in the third quarter, the Cowboys needed a big drive in the worst way. Fortunately, that’s exactly what they got. The Cowboys fought back into the game with a six-play, 67-yard drive that took less than two minutes. Prescott found Pickens for 19 yards, with another 15 yards tacked on for a roughing the quarterback. Prescott turned around and found Jake Ferguson for a 19-yard touchdown pass, with a CeeDee Lamb two-point conversion to make it a 24-21 game. Things were suddenly getting interesting. 7. Game-changing stop It’s really a shame the game ended the way it did because it would be lovely to be talking all week about those remarkable fourth-down stops by the Cowboys rookie defenders. Safety Caleb Downs was the hero early when he crashed through the line to make the first fourth-down stop on Henry. Then, linebacker Jaishawn Barham made an even more impressive tackle for a loss at an even more critical moment of the game, fending off a potential go-ahead touchdown late in the game. It was truly amazing, even if the final result didn’t work out like we hoped. 8. Too many big plays This is one of those games where the defense made a few splash plays, but they made far more bad plays where they allowed big gains. While they can stuff the short stuff, they absolutely struggled mightily to stop the run. The Ravens ran for 192 yards, rushing the ball 38 times for over five yards per carry. They wouldn’t stop, and why would they? The Cowboys couldn’t stop them. Three different Ravens players had runs of 20+ yards – Jackson, Henry, and Flowers. And the big plays came in the passing game as well as again, three different players had receptions of 20+ yards. The defense has its moments, but they are still downright terrible far too often. 9. Goal line woes In a nail-biter like this one, every point counts. That’s why it’s extra frustrating to see the offense drive the ball all the way near the goal line, only to have to settle for a field goal. That happened to the Cowboys offense twice, on their first possession of the game and their last. The offense had golden opportunities to punch it in, but couldn’t do it. On the first possession, they abandoned the run for reasons unknown, resulting in an incompletion followed by a sack. On their last possession they committed a penalty, and none of their plays seemed to give them a fighting chance. It was very unpleasant. 10. Total collapse The only thing worse than not coming away with the go-ahead touchdown at the end was leaving the Ravens seven seconds left, because apparently, that’s a lot of time. Aubrey kicked it out of the end zone because trying one of his squibbers was too risky after kicking the ball out of bounds twice in this game. They absolutely didn’t want to give Baltimore the ball at the 40-yard-line. Just play it safe and kick it out of the end zone. It’s not like the Ravens can connect on a 27-yard play and still leave one second on the clock for the game-winning field goal, amiright?
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas loses in last-second heartbreak to Ravens
summary: It was a game of runs. Dallas’ defense started off hot and gave the offense room to get up to an early 10-0 lead. However, Lamar Jackson and the Ravens’ offense came storming back, holding a lead for most of the game. Then in the fourth quarter, Jaishawn Barham and the Dallas defensive line woke […]
full_text: Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images | Getty Images It was a game of runs. Dallas’ defense started off hot and gave the offense room to get up to an early 10-0 lead. However, Lamar Jackson and the Ravens’ offense came storming back, holding a lead for most of the game. Then in the fourth quarter, Jaishawn Barham and the Dallas defensive line woke back up again, allowing the Cowboys to go into the final seconds tied 31-31. The seven seconds Dallas had left on the board was too much, as one Zay Flowers completion and one Tyler Loop field goal later, the Cowboys left Rio with a loss. DALLAS COWBOYS LOSE TO BALTIMORE RAVENS 34-31 IN WEEK 3 – Mark Heaney, Inside The Star It’s still week three, so it’s difficult to place a lot of weight on this game. Especially given the Cowboys were underdogs. However, if the season comes down to the wire, Dallas fans will be circling this game as one they could have won. If you thought we were for sure going to OT, you wouldn’t be alone. We should have been headed there, but the Cowboys’ defense had different plans. They allowed a 27-yard reception, and Baltimore called a timeout with two seconds to play. Tyler Loop then drilled a 56-yard game-winner at the buzzer to send Dallas back home in embarrassing fashion. Cowboys Nation, make the SB Nation app part of game day! From the opening kick to the final snap, join fellow Cowboys fans to discuss every play in real time. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Move seamlessly between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Game Recap: Cowboys lose in Rio, 34-31- Kurt Daniels, DallasCowboys.com This one is a tough one to re-live. However, don’t forget the big plays that put the Cowboys in an opportunity to steal one in Rio. But Baltimore was again on the move as the clock ticked over into the final 15 minutes, with Jackson throwing a 31-yard pass to Rashod Bateman to end the third quarter and Flowers running around the left end for a 20-yard pickup to start the fourth. And then the defense came up huge. The Ravens had a first-and-goal at the Dallas 3-yard line, but Jackson was stopped on a 1-yard loss, and Henry was stood up for gains of only 2 and 1, setting up a fourth-and-1 on the doorstep. 7 instant reactions to Cowboys’ soul-crushing loss to the Ravens- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat The blame this week will certainly fall on the Cowboys’ defense for failing to send this game to OT. However, don’t forget that Dallas could have gone up four points but failed to score from the one-yard line. Brian Schottenheimer awful red zone play-calling Baltimore had zero answer for Javonte Williams on Dallas’ opening drive. Schottenheimer called Williams’ number on four straight plays, and he bulldozed the Cowboys right to the doorstep of a touchdown. On 2nd-and-goal, he dialed up a play-action pass that was doomed from the start. Ryan Flournoy couldn’t fight through traffic, and Prescott’s pass fell incomplete. On third-and-goal, Schotty called another pass out of the shotgun. No dice. Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys’ Crushing Last-Second Week 3 Loss to Ravens in Rio- Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated Dallas corners about the field condition came to fruition as they saw several contributors leave due to injury. Including two names from a secondary that was already thin. More injury concerns for the secondary As if the Cowboys needed more injuries in their already banged-up secondary. Starting safety Jalen Thompson exited the contest in the first half and did not return for the remainder of the game. He was listed with a hamstring injury . Sources: Cowboys, Lions make trade inquiries on Joey Porter Jr.- Adam Schefter, ESPN In more positive news, Dallas could be looking to beef up their secondary. With the Quinnen Williams trade, the Cowboys are draft-capital poor and would likely need to run themselves dry in 2027 picks to pull this off. A handful of teams, including the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions, have begun making inquiries about the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., league sources told ESPN. The Steelers would be willing to listen to trade offers for Porter, according to sources, but they would want a strong compensation package if they were to deal the fourth-year star. Cowboys lose to Ravens in Brazil thanks to last-second, costly mistake – RJ Ochoa, Blogging The Boys Fans knew that the begging of the season was going to be tough. However, after dropping another game to the Ravens Dallas is in an early hole and needs to steal one soon. The Cowboys are now 1-2 on the season and have to get ready to take on a winless Houston Texans team next week. For now though… everything hurts.
