title: 3 things we learned from Cowboys vs Ravens
summary: The Dallas Cowboys fell to the Baltimore Ravens on a last-second miracle play by Lamar Jackson and company. Here are three things we learned about the Cowboys during the game. Offensive play calls are too cute Brian Schottenheimer cost his team on multiple occasions. And that’s putting it nicely. The head coach and offensive play […]
full_text: Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys fell to the Baltimore Ravens on a last-second miracle play by Lamar Jackson and company. Here are three things we learned about the Cowboys during the game. Offensive play calls are too cute Brian Schottenheimer cost his team on multiple occasions. And that’s putting it nicely. The head coach and offensive play caller just cannot figure out what to do inside the five-yard line and at times struggles with continuity when his offense is having success. After forcing a three-and-out on defense on the opening drive, the Cowboys offense marched down the field behind Javonte Williams with ease. However after getting to the one-yard line, the offense sputtered after an incompletion and a sack. They missed out on four points in a game they lost by three. Later in the game on the first drive in the second half, Dak Prescott and the offense led a nine-play drive into scoring territory that was cut short by a questionable Jake Ferguson fumble. Dak had no issues throwing the ball around to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the drive, and even took off himself on a nice run. But then Schottenheimer called a shovel pass to the tight end which ended up popping out and was recovered by Baltimore. That’s a play normally reserved for short yardage and goal line situations; not something you see on a first and ten. Another three points, at mininum, left off the board. Finally on the Cowboys final possession of the night, the offense was absolutely on fire. They marched down the field in an attempt to win the game, once again reaching the two-yard line. With a timeout in pocket, conventional wisdom would tell you to run the ball on first down for the game-winning touchdown with 23 seconds left. Instead the play call would be a fade ball to Pickens, broken up by the defensive back. Before the offense could snap the ball on second down, Luke Schoonmaker was flagged for a false start, moving them back five yards. After two more snaps, Dallas settled for the game-tying field goal. Another four points left on the board. By my count, that’s eleven points left off the board that can be tied to Schottenheimer’s play-calling. That is just plain unacceptable from your head coach. Rookie defenders are making plays You’ll look at the scoreboard and call me crazy. How can we say the defense show up when they allowed 34 points on the board? There were several occasions where the players on the defensive side of the ball stood tall and got the ball back into the hands of the offense. Jaishawn Barham officially announced his entry to the NFL. He was absolutely instrumental on three short-yardage stops. The first-year linebacker stuffed Derrick Henry on a fourth and one (officially credited to Caleb Downs, but Barham was there), a third and two, and a fourth-down goal line stand. Without the individual effort from Barham, this game could have gotten ugly for the Cowboys. #Cowboys Jaishawn Barham with the 4th down stop at the goal line. Massive play by the rookie. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/MI7W7XiJYm — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) September 27, 2026 Caleb Downs also continues to show why he was the 11th overall pick in this year’s draft. He too made a handful of impactful plays and continues to live in the opposing team’s backfield. Downs was a key player in the early fourth down stop, alongside Barham and Donovan Ezeiruaku. #Cowboys rookies Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham stopping Derrick Henry on 4th and 1. Great stand by the Dallas defense. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/U6WgZ1rcI3 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) September 27, 2026 The defense isn’t close to perfect. Maybe not even in the same ballpark. But their rookies are starting to make drive ending plays and that’s a good sign. The defense is on the right track and will need to continue to grow as a unit. As tough a pill as it is to swallow right now, the defense is getting better. Health is a massive issue on defense The Cowboys were already without defensive backs Malik Hooker, Cobie Durant, P.J. Locke and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Tonight resulted in even more hits to that defense. Jalen Thompson left the game in the second quarter with a hamstring injury. Shavon Revel went out in the fourth with what looked to be a concerning knee injury. Other players were banged up but eventually returned. But by the Ravens last possession, the Cowboys were shuffling Alijah Clark and Reddy Steward in the game. Depending on the severity of the injuries to Thompson and Revel, the Dallas secondary may absolutely be in a break glass in case of emergency situation. Injuries continue to hammer this defense and it shows on the field. The two defenders on the broadcast screen during the final Ravens throw of the game were Reddy Steward and Alijah Clark. Those are not the names you want on the field during the most important moment of the game. Unfortunately, due to the mounting injuries, Dallas didn’t have much of a choice.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs. Ravens: Winners and losers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys traveled more than 5,000 miles to Brazil for their Week 3 meeting with the Baltimore Ravens, and the first NFL game played at the Maracanã Stadium produced plenty to talk about. It was a dramatic finish that left Dallas returning home after losing to the Ravens 34-31 in literally the final second […]
full_text: Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys traveled more than 5,000 miles to Brazil for their Week 3 meeting with the Baltimore Ravens, and the first NFL game played at the Maracanã Stadium produced plenty to talk about. It was a dramatic finish that left Dallas returning home after losing to the Ravens 34-31 in literally the final second of the game. Dallas had stretches where it looked capable of controlling the game, particularly through its rushing attack, but Baltimore repeatedly found ways to punish mistakes and attack a Cowboys defense dealing with significant injuries. Some players strengthened their case with excellent individual performances, while other areas of the roster had a much more difficult afternoon. Here are this week’s Cowboys winners and losers from today’s tense and disappointing loss. Winner: Javonte Williams If there was one thing Dallas badly needed to find in Brazil, it was a running game. Javonte Williams provided it. After being held to 41 rushing yards against the Giants and just 30 yards against Washington, Williams finally found room to operate against Baltimore. He reached 98 rushing yards on 19 carries, with one touchdown, averaging 5.2 yards per attempt, and consistently gave Dallas manageable situations. What made the performance particularly encouraging was how different it looked compared with the opening two weeks. There were hard runs between the tackles, patience behind his blockers and, most importantly, explosive plays. Dallas has spent the opening weeks looking for evidence that its rushing attack could become a genuine part of the offense rather than something used simply to keep defenses honest. Javonte Williams with the first TD in Rio! @BALvsDAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PNQTgbelQn — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Winner: T.J. Bass Tyler Smith cannot return quickly enough, but T.J. Bass continues to make the Cowboys feel considerably better about surviving without him. Bass entered this game as one of Dallas’ better performers through the opening two weeks. According PFF grades, his 71.1 overall grade ranked eighth on the team, with his pass protection a highlight of his strength. The assignment became considerably harder against Baltimore’s defensive front, but Bass continued to hold his own while also being part of Dallas’ best rushing performance of the young season. That matters because the Cowboys haven’t been getting enough movement from their offensive line. Dallas’ own staff pointed out during the week that Williams had regularly been dealing with contact behind the line of scrimmage and that the absence of Smith was being felt. Williams was getting great success when he got behind Bass and Tyler Guyton, this was a big stress point for the Ravens defense. 12 personnel is working early on for the Cowboys. Always ideal when the LT is extra and is working to a CB. Cooper Beebe getting to the second level and sealing the LB. Mingo sealing. Brevyn Spann-Ford clearing the lane. TJ Bass finishing with a pancake. Great stuff. https://t.co/iKAkZUE8Vk pic.twitter.com/xGtlXdQSHo — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 27, 2026 Winner: Jaishawn Barham This was not a perfect game from Jaishawn Barham, but it might have been his most encouraging one yet. Early on, the rookie linebacker looked like exactly that, a rookie trying to diagnose one of the most difficult offenses in football. Lamar Jackson’s ability to hold the football on option plays, Derrick Henry’s downhill running and Baltimore’s misdirection repeatedly forced Dallas’ linebackers to make decisions in a hurry. Barham was caught out on some of those early snaps. What matters is how he responded. As Dallas fought its way back into the game, Barham became noticeably more decisive. Instead of waiting for plays to develop, he started attacking downhill and getting into the backfield. One of his biggest moments came midway through the fourth quarter with Dallas protecting a 28-24 lead. Henry took the ball to the left side, but Barham shot into the play and dropped him for a loss on fourth down. He made more impactful plays to stress the Baltimore ground game and these are exactly the type of plays Dallas needed from its rookie linebacker in the that moment. JJ Watt was fired up after this play by Jaishawn Barham 🗣️ @BALvsDAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tdUNwUbSg7 — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Loser: DaRon Bland This was always going to be one of the toughest assignments of the season for Dallas’ secondary, and DaRon Bland had an afternoon that was more frustrating than productive. Bland was involved in a costly pass interference call as Baltimore tested Dallas downfield, adding to a Cowboys penalty total that repeatedly made life harder on the defense. Against Lamar Jackson, giving away free yardage is particularly damaging because Baltimore already forces defenders to account for so much before the ball is even thrown. The larger problem was that Dallas needed its most experienced cornerback to help stabilize an injury-hit secondary, and Baltimore continued generating advantageous situations against the back end of the defense. Bland isn’t solely responsible for those problems, but when you’re the established starter surrounded by backups and inexperienced players, the expectations become higher. This wasn’t the kind of stabilizing performance Dallas needed from him. Bland ended his day with one tackle, zero pass breakups, and a long list of targets for catches against him, including a TD. Chris Moore for 6 and the @ravens are rolling in Rio 🐦‍⬛ @NFLBrasil @BALvsDAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OZpDLfLN8R — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Loser: Field-goal unit This one shouldn’t be placed solely on Brandon Aubrey. Aubrey had already converted from 28 and 38 yards and once again looked perfectly comfortable kicking in conditions that had generated plenty of discussion before the game. Dallas sent Aubrey out for a 59-yard attempt while trailing 17-13. Baltimore got penetration and Korie Jackson blocked the kick, immediately giving the Ravens life. What happened next made the mistake considerably more painful. Derrick Henry broke loose for 29 yards on Baltimore’s next possession and the Ravens eventually reached the end zone, stretching the advantage from four points to 11. That’s why this goes down against the entire field-goal unit rather than Aubrey individually. On a long attempt, protection has to hold up long enough for one of the NFL’s strongest legs to get the football away cleanly. Dallas didn’t do that. RAVENS BLOCK THE FIELD GOAL @JJWatt was fired up 🤣 pic.twitter.com/12MWOYEcXT — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 27, 2026 Loser: Secondary depth This isn’t necessarily about blaming one backup defensive back. It’s about Dallas discovering just how quickly injuries can expose the bottom of a depth chart. The Cowboys entered Brazil without Malik Hooker, P.J. Locke and Cobie Durant. Hooker is recovering from a fractured forearm, Locke suffered a torn plantar fascia and Durant has been dealing with a hamstring strain. That left Dallas asking considerably more from players such as Markquese Bell, Alijah Clark and Shavon Revel. Baltimore eventually found them. Late in the third quarter, the Ravens started producing explosive plays almost one after another. Matt Hibner gained 21 yards, Rashod Bateman followed with a 31-yard reception, and Zay Flowers then opened the fourth quarter by taking an end-around 20 yards to the Dallas 3-yard line. That sequence demonstrated exactly what Dallas feared entering the game. The starters don’t just give a defense better individual players. They allow the coordinator to disguise coverages, communicate more effectively and trust defenders with difficult assignments. Take several of those players away at the same time and every weakness becomes magnified. Dallas knew its secondary depth was going to be tested in…
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys lose to Ravens in Brazil thanks to last-second, costly mistake
summary: You have to play through the final whistle. The Dallas Cowboys fought back against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in Brazil, and it looked like they earned overtime to try and snatch away a win after being huge underdogs. It was the Ravens who snatched things away, though. The Cowboys got caught not ready for […]
full_text: RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 27: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs with the ball during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images) | Getty Images You have to play through the final whistle. The Dallas Cowboys fought back against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in Brazil, and it looked like they earned overtime to try and snatch away a win after being huge underdogs. It was the Ravens who snatched things away, though. The Cowboys got caught not ready for the final 7 seconds of the game and the Ravens proved to be the better team. There really is no other way to say it. The Cowboys are now 1-2 on the season and have to get ready to take on a winless Houston Texans team next week. For now though… everything hurts. Below you will find our recap of how it all unfolded. First Quarter The Cowboys won the toss and deferred which put the defense up first. Talk about setting the stage given the opponent. Amazingly, the defense stood tall and did so right away. They held Baltimore to a three and out which surprised every Cowboys fan in the world given how the defense has looked recently. The offense was no shock though as they began to move with relative ease. What was shocking though was that they did so on the ground. Javonte Williams was moving and grooving, and the Cowboys just about punched things in for an opening touchdown until Dak Prescott was sacked on 3rd and Goal. Dallas kicked a field goal for the game’s first points, though. Shortly after the offense was back at work once more. This was the case as Baltimore went for it on fourth down, by way of Derrick Henry of all people, and was denied. Seriously. Shocking stuff. As the Cowboys got back on offense they began to flirt with the endzone once more, and KaVontae Turpin was a big reason why thanks to some serious effort. TURP pic.twitter.com/GKMIR3JAP9 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Shortly after Javonte Williams finished the job and gave the Cowboys a 10-0 lead. JAVONTE TD!!! pic.twitter.com/0KSiuAUjEM — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Unfortunately the Ravens remain a solid NFL team. They were able to march down the field, they started with great field position after Brandon Aubrey put the kickoff out of bounds, and cashed in with a touchdown of their own to narrow things to 10-7. It was Derrick Henry who found the endzone because of course it was. Dallas’ offense came up why their next time out and ended the quarter with the punt team set to come out. Second Quarter The Cowboys did indeed punt the ball away to start the second quarter which put Lamar Jackson and co. back on the field. It looked like the Cowboys were going to pull Jackson off of the field once more. It was 3rd and 11 and everyone held their breath… but then a yellow flag came out to signal pass interference and the Ravens picked up 49 yards as a result. Right after Henry was back in the endzone and Baltimore had a 14-10 lead. The Cowboys offense took over facing a deficit for the first time in the game and that stress seemed to show. They reached fourth and short just behind midfield, and after calling a timeout to get things together… the Cowboys did not get it. In fact, Javonte Williams fumbled to make it all the more frustrating. pain pic.twitter.com/96lH3GMFDZ — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 The Ravens moved down the field once more, but at the very least the Cowboys defense held them out of the endzone entirely. Baltimore did pick up a field goal to give them a full touchdown lead and the Cowboys took things back over from there. Notably, Dallas took over at their own 35-yard line with 4:44 left before halftime. Given that they deferred to start the game this set them up for an opportunity for the proverbial double-dip. The Cowboys established the first half of it by way of a Brandon Aubrey field goal, and points are always welcome. The teams went to their respective locker rooms with Baltimore up 17-13. Third Quarter The Cowboys got the ball after Ricky Martin performed at halftime (the NFL really wanted to make the Brazil game a spectacle) and began to move the ball with some urgency. It was great to see. Unfortunately the good vibes did not last long. When it seemed inevitable that the Cowboys were going to score, even after they boldly converted a 4th and 3, a shovel pass from Jake Ferguson resulted in a fumble. The broadcast did not believe Ferguson ever had possession, but it was reviewed as all turnovers are and the Ravens were awarded possession as they recovered it. Thankfully, the Cowboys defense stood tall. This really appeared to be a moment that had the potential to unravel the entire game for Dallas, but a quick stop gave their offense the ball back still down by four. It was a bit more of the same for the offense. They moved a little, but they got stuck and couldn’t move all the way. They settled for a 59-yard field goal attempt… that was blocked. Baltimore began the next drive with their best field position of the day as they started at their own 49-yard line. It took four plays for Lamar Jackson to find Chris Moore for a touchdown and to give the Ravens a 24-13 lead. It was clear that the Cowboys were going to have to play perfect football from this point on to stand a chance. They took the first step of that by marching down the field and finally finding the endzone. Dak Prescott found Jake Ferguson for the score, and right after he found CeeDee Lamb to make it a 24-21 game. FERG TD!!! pic.twitter.com/fW0Z5LxH0N — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zzUNmFykjJ — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 The quarter ended with Baltimore threatening to score once more. Fourth Quarter It was not looking good. The Ravens were right on the goal line. In fact, they faced a 4th and Goal with the opportunity to really twist the knife. It should be noted it was only deemed 4th and Goal after a review on the down before that proved Derrick Henry did not get in. Baltimore went that route on the critical fourth down… and he did not get in again! Jaishawn Barham had the critical play! BARHAM pic.twitter.com/arPMyIqZCX — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Being up against your own goal line can feel intimidating in general, but especially so in circumstances like this. Shortly into the drive… Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb opened things up big time. !!!!! pic.twitter.com/kx7q4PyOIr — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Things were moving fast and chaotically. It felt like blinking would mean you missed something massive. KaVontae Turpin really proved that as he found the endzone right after! It took just 7 plays for the Cowboys to travel 96 yards for this score! TURPIN pic.twitter.com/BlLumyXqM8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Everyone tried to catch their breath after all of that action. There was still almost the entire fourth quarter left after the mini marathon. The Ravens looked to be attempting to act this way. Calm. Cool. Conservative. Nobody was trying to be a hero. But then a hero emerged and his name was Jaishawn Barham. He earned yet another stop for the Cowboys defense. JAISHAWN pic.twitter.com/Fksi19vhiV — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 27, 2026 Unfortunately the Cowboys were not able to do much with the ball after Baltimore punted it away. They had to punt it back themselves and the Ravens took over with just under six minutes left in the game. This was easily a more successful drive for Baltimore than the one before it. It looked like the Cowboys might pull it off again, though. They certainly sold out to do so in terms of burning resources like timeouts. But the Ravens found the endzone by way of a Lamar Jackson touchdown to Matthew Hibner. They took the lead back 31-28 and…
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys vs Ravens discussion: Week 3 game day live
summary: The Dallas Cowboys come into their Week 3 game with a 1-1 record. title: Game balls for the Broncos comeback win over the Rams
summary: The Denver Broncos replicated the kind of magic it had last year in that 33-point fourth quarter nuke it dropped on the New York Giants. Except this time, they executed a comeback against a true Super Bowl contender in the Los Angeles Rams, which makes the comeback even more impressive than that one last year. […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Nate Adkins #45 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with teammate Jaylen Waddle #17 after scoring a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the third quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos replicated the kind of magic it had last year in that 33-point fourth quarter nuke it dropped on the New York Giants. Except this time, they executed a comeback against a true Super Bowl contender in the Los Angeles Rams, which makes the comeback even more impressive than that one last year. Join the conversation! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The game was a tale of two halves — seems like that is a typical statement with these Broncos — with the Rams completely dominating and smothering Denver on both sides of the ball for a 16-0 halftime lead. The caveat being that the Broncos’ defense made all of the red zone stops it needed to keep hope alive heading into the third quarter. The third quarter had plenty of lucky breaks for the Broncos, including a fumble that turned into a bigger gain. They scored touchdowns and two-point conversions in back-to-back drives to tie the game and swing all of the momentum their way and they would close out the win with more big plays in the fourth quarter. It was a heckuva comeback win and the drama lasted to the final play. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to: Talanoa Hufanga Talanoa Hufanga gets my game ball this week. He made a game-changing pick-six right after the Broncos had lost momentum. He sealed the game on the last play with another interception. He had a chance at another interception earlier in the game that he dropped, but made plays when it mattered. He also had an absolutely beautifully timed safety blitz to blow up Stafford and force a field goal on a 3rd and long. Safeties don’t get games much better than what we saw from Hufanga this week. Fa’afetai tele, Talanoa! – Sadaraine TALANOA HUFANGA PICK 6 pic.twitter.com/ZjpkslYHx1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Bo Nix My game ball goes to Bo Nix, after a forgettable first half in which he had two interception worthy throws that should have been picked, Bo came out and put on a show in the second half. Nix was 6/12 for 53 yards in the first half. The Broncos had four drives, two of which were three and out. The one drive with any potency ended with a doinked 43 yard FG. While Bo was only 11/22 for 133 yards in the second half, he made the throws when he needed to. Like this throw on the second 2-pt conversion: WADDLE WITH AN EXCELLENT CATCH FOR 2 POINTS! 🐧 pic.twitter.com/BNsmvMkrR1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Bo also accounted for all three of the Bronco TDs on the game throwing for two and running for one. The Bronco second half drives after the 3-and-out to start the half: TD, TD, INT, punt, TD. – Joe Mahoney Pat Bryant My game ball goes to Pat Bryant. He had a touchdown catch, a two-point conversion, and a 39-yard catch and run that put the Broncos in scoring position late in the fourth quarter. Every time he was targeted, he came down with the ball. Bryant was also on point recovering a J.K. Dobbins fumble in the game to advance it and keep the Rams from making it a turnover. Hopefully his performance tonight is the sign bigger things are still in store for the talented second-year wide receiver. – Chris Hart BIG PLAY PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/WeWDOu8xa1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Brandon Jones Talanoa Hufanga stole the show on the big play front, but it was Brandon Jones mopping up the dirty work on the field. He finished with 12 total tackles, a tackle for a loss, a pass defensed, and a quarterback hit. Both safeties played an outstanding game after the first half struggles and in the red zone they dominated. I was tempted to give my game ball to the officiating crew for that bogus DPI call, but we’ve been screwed by plenty a questionable call so I’ll just call that one a small payout for all the other bad calls that went against Denver. – Tim Lynch Davis Webb After that dismal first half against LA, Broncos Country was ready for Sean Payton to take the play calling back from Webb. No rhythm. No flow. The offense looked like it had never played before. But as bad as Denver’s offense was in the first half, it was even better in the second. And Webb is a big reason why. The young play caller dialed up some fantastic plays and Nix and the Broncos executed masterfully. There’s always going to be growing pains and a learning curve with a young playcaller, but this should give Webb, the team, and the fanbase the confidence he’s got this. – Ian St. Clair Zach Allen Zach Allen has been a monster through 3 weeks. He notched his 3rd sack of the season against the Rams, but that and his 2 tackles fall well short of telling the full tale of Allen’s impact on the game. The Broncos’ disruptive defensive end was a headache for LA all evening, clogging up the defensive center and keeping Matt Stafford uncomfortable. – Taylor Kothe SACK ALLEN! 💪 pic.twitter.com/x6nfkUcQFo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Rams game? title: Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 3 Comeback Win vs. Rams
summary: What a thriller! The Broncos move to 2-1 after an improbable, thrilling second-half comeback win. It was a tale of two halves for the Broncos, who trailed the Rams 16-0 at halftime before scoring 30 points in the second half. They had three offensive touchdowns, two successful two-point conversions, a pick-six, and a game-winning interception […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a thriller! The Broncos move to 2-1 after an improbable, thrilling second-half comeback win. It was a tale of two halves for the Broncos, who trailed the Rams 16-0 at halftime before scoring 30 points in the second half. They had three offensive touchdowns, two successful two-point conversions, a pick-six, and a game-winning interception in the end zone. It was a crazy game that kept Broncos fans on the edge of their seat until the very end. It is also a complicated one for stock up and stock down because this game had multiple layers of good and bad throughout. So, we have plenty of players with their stock going up and others, unfortunately, with their stock going down. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. After a bounce-back performance like that on Sunday, we are going to see a lot more stock-ups than we did last week. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up: It was a complicated night for the Broncos quarterback. He was on the struggle bus in the first half and nearly had two ugly interceptions. The offense looked lifeless, and Nix simply was not playing well. However, this was a classic Bo Nix/Denver Broncos comeback victory. That means Nix came alive in the second half and had three touchdowns, including the eventual game-winner. His only blemish was an interception after a defender hit his arm. This allowed the Rams to take a 4th quarter lead, which is exactly what Nix wanted. He would go on to get yet another 4th-quarter comeback win. It wasn’t all great, and the stat book will not wow you, but the Broncos came back and beat a team many believe to be a Super Bowl contender. Nix had a great second half, and while it would be great if he could put together a complete game for once, I will take whatever leads to a Denver Broncos victory. Jarret Stidham – Unchanged : Is the veteran backup QB Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the emergency third-string quarterback Running Back JK Dobbins – Stock down: We simply need more from Dobbins, who does not look like the back who was top 3 in rushing last season before his injury. He averaged a poor 2.9 yards per carry and never really got anything going in the run game. He did have a few nice first-down carries, but overall, we need more from Dobbins. RJ Harvey – Stock up: Harvey didn’t do much in the run game, but he did have 6 receptions for 41 yards and led the team in receptions. It wasn’t anything to write home about, but he is filling his role and contributing as a pass catcher. Jonah Coleman – Stock down: I am including him here even though he is on the IR. Injuries suck, and he was on the verge of carving out a real role in this backfield. Unfortunately, he suffered a high ankle sprain vs. the Jaguars and played through it. This showed his toughness, and that game showcased his talent, but it was a poorly timed injury that killed the momentum he built in Week 2. Tyler Badie – Stock up: Like Harvey, he is playing his role and doing it well. He served as the third-down pass blocker and even went one-on-one vs. Aaron Donald and held his own. Badie also had 1 reception for 12 yards. Again, nothing crazy, but he’s playing his role and doing well at it. Adam Prentice – Stock down: Why did they even keep a fullback? 3rd-and-1 shotgun plays, and Prentice only played 4 offensive snaps. Could have used him a few times last night. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock down: Waddle’s stock was high last week, but it came crashing back down in Week 3. He had 2 catches for 10 yards and struggled to get anything going against this talented Rams secondary. You expect more from Waddle in these big games, but he simply didn’t produce. He did have a nice two-point conversion catch, which was big, but outside of that, it was a pretty forgettable night for the Broncos playmaker. Courtland Sutton – Unchanged: Sutton had a mostly quiet night, but did see 7 targets, which led to 3 receptions for 46 yards. Again, nothing to write home about, but a decent showing by the Broncos veteran pass catcher. Pat Bryant – Stock up: Bryant was the star of the night on the offensive side of the ball. He only caught two passes, but he turned those two passes into 2 catches for 44 yards and 1 touchdown. He also added a two-point conversion in there as well. His touchdown got the team on the board in the second half and his two pointer would tie the game at 16-16. He would later have a 39-yard catch-and-run on a 2nd and 20 late in the 4th quarter to set up the Broncos eventual game-winning touchdown. Bryant also drew the controversial DPI call late to give the Broncos an automatic 1st down and extend their late 4th quarter drive. Troy Franklin – Unchanged: Franklin played just 12 snaps and saw 1 target but like last week, he made the most of that 1 target. After Bryant’s 39-yard catch-and-run, Franklin followed that up with a 21-yard reception to get the Broncos offense rolling. His role is certainly diminished, but with Mims sidelined, he is making the most of his limited opportunities. Marvin Mims – Stock down: He has been hampered by injuries and not having a great start to his contract year. Hopefully, he can get healthy, and the Broncos can get their All-Pro returner and big-play specialist back. Lil ’ Jordan Humphrey – Stock down: Was inactive and doesn’t seem to be playing as much with Davis Webb running the offense. Kolbe Katsis – Stock up: The undrafted rookie had an adventurous night that included a couple of bobbled punt returns, a big return that sparked the offense, and attempting to hurdle multiple Rams players only to get hammered. Still, he made his NFL debut and has appeared in more games than most of the Broncos’ 2026 rookie class. Tight End Adam Trautman – Unchanged: He played in 40% of the Broncos’ offensive snaps but did trail Evan Engram in snaps, which is interesting. Evan Engram – Stock up: The production isn’t there, but the usage is. Engram had 2 targets and 0 catches on the night, but did play 60% of the snaps, which led all tight ends. He is getting the playing time, but the production hasn’t matched yet. Nate Adkins – Stock up: Is Nate Adkins the true Joker? Adkins caught his second touchdown of the season and now has back-to-back games with a touchdown. He played 34% of the snaps but seems to have a trusted role in the passing game when out there. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: The rookie tight end continued to be inactive. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: The veteran LT has had a great start to the season, and while he did see a penalty called on him late in the game, he played well overall. I am, again, not an offensive line expert. Ben Powers – Unchanged: Looks like he struggled with the interior pass rush a few times, which is a strength of this Rams defense, but I did not notice him being good or bad either way. Luke Wattenberg – Unchanged: Like Powers, he struggled with the interior rush at times, but I did not notice him being good or bad throughout the game. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: He sent Aaron Donald back to retirement. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: Had some issues with the speed rush, which is normal with McGlinchey, but from my untrained eye, he played solid. Alex Palczewski – Stock up: He played just 6 snaps, but that’s an increase. I would like to see the Broncos utilize their heavy packages more and pound the ball. Matt Peart – Unchanged: He didn’t play Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: He did not play Kage Casey – Unchanged: Inactive Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: The Broncos’ pass rush ran hot and cold throughout the night, but when it was on, it was due to Allen being a disruptor. He had…

title: Top plays from Broncos win over Rams
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! With such a great comeback win, I thought I’d select my favorite play from each phase of the Denver Broncos comeback win over the Los Angeles Rams last night. Frankly, it was a game Denver should not have won. The Rams had twice as many first downs, outgained the Broncos 482-257, […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Talanoa Hufanga (9) of the Denver Broncos celebrates his game-ending interception on a pass by Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 30-26 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! With such a great comeback win, I thought I’d select my favorite play from each phase of the Denver Broncos comeback win over the Los Angeles Rams last night. Frankly, it was a game Denver should not have won. The Rams had twice as many first downs, outgained the Broncos 482-257, and held nearly a 10 minute advantage in time of possession. Yet, they lost the turnover battle and had nearly three times as many penalties as Denver did. It just goes to show how deadly both can be to winning in the NFL. Each phase of the ball at a big play that I picked and I feel each fed into the momentum swing to led to Denver’s victory. Offense Bo Nix and the offense had to make a lot of plays in the second half to complete the comeback, but the most impressive came in the third quarter on a two-point conversion. They had just scored their first points of the game and needed a two-point conversion to make it a one score game. If they miss that conversion its not a game-killer, but the momentum they achieved with the insane throw and insane catch gave the whole team a spark. This was the moment I thought, “Okay, this team is going to comeback aren’t they?” WADDLE WITH AN EXCELLENT CATCH FOR 2 POINTS! 🐧 pic.twitter.com/BNsmvMkrR1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Defense By all accounts, the defense had a bad night. Where they made up for is with the big game-changing plays. It seemed like Talanoa Hufanga was in on nearly all of them in the fourth quarter. Jeremy Crawshaw had a create corner kick and Kolbe Katsis had a nice return, but the play I feel was a momentum-swinging game changer was the Que Robinson tackle. Que Robinson continues to make plays on defense and special teams pic.twitter.com/lZ7K79lg51 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 What were you top plays from the game? title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 30-26 victory over the Los Angeles Rams
summary: Oh my god. The Denver Broncos just had the most Denver Broncos thrilling, memorable victory. They trailed 16-0 at halftime, and everything looked awful. Offense, defense, special teams, coaching, and everything else. A lifeless effort and a team that looked to be on the verge of yet another blowout loss on primetime. As usual, that […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Talanoa Hufanga #9 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass to win the the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Oh my god. The Denver Broncos just had the most Denver Broncos thrilling, memorable victory. They trailed 16-0 at halftime, and everything looked awful. Offense, defense, special teams, coaching, and everything else. A lifeless effort and a team that looked to be on the verge of yet another blowout loss on primetime. As usual, that is exactly where the Broncos wanted them. From there, the Broncos would score 30 points in the second half and complete the thrilling comeback victory over the Rams. There is A LOT to unpack from this up-and-down rollercoaster of emotions thriller that thankfully ended in a Broncos victory. So, here are my winners and losers from the Broncos’ 30-26 victory over the Rams. LOSER – First-half performance Like the game, we are starting with the bad. What the hell was that? The offense was bad, lifeless, and could not get anything going. The defense had no pass rush; they were whiffing on tackles again, and the Rams had no problem moving the ball on them. The special teams even struggled when usually reliable kicker Wil Lutz doinked one off the goalpost. We were talking about Davis Webb giving up play calling again, talking about Vance Joseph’s defense struggling against backs and tight ends, and they were trailing 16-0 at half against a good team and staring down a 1-2 record and another blowout loss on primetime. It was bad, but we have to remember, this is the Denver Broncos. WINNER – Second-half performance WHY DO I CONTINUE TO DOUBT YOU? They started out the second half with a predictable three-and-out right after an interview where Sean Payton said that series was a very important series for the team. Not great. The defense would get the ball back, and then it was game on from there. Touchdown to Nate Adkins, a crazy two-pointer by Jaylen Waddle, defense gets the ball back to the offense, touchdown and two-pointer to Pat Bryant, and suddenly, we have a tie game in the third quarter. Where the hell did that come from? Rams would then drive down for a field goal to take a 3-point lead, but then it happened. Talanoa Hufanga CAUGHT THE BALL! Not only did he catch it, but he also took it back for a touchdown! Holy shit, the Broncos are going to win this game! Matthew Stafford said NOT SO FAST after Riley Moss was cooked on a double move, and the Rams would take a 26-23 lead. Those doubts started to creep back in as the Rams successfully took back the momentum, but again, remember. This is the Denver Broncos. What do the Denver Broncos do? They win football games in the 4th quarter. Fourth-quarter magician Bo Nix led yet another 4th quarter comeback with chunk plays to Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin to get deep into Rams territory. After some controversial calls FINALLY fell in the Broncos’ favor, Bo Nix called his number (twice) and would score what would end up being the game-winning touchdown. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, the Rams had time to go down and score a game-winning touchdown, and they got pretty damn close. Unfortunately for the Rams, Talanoa Hufanga learned how to catch a football, and on the final play of the game, as the clock hit zero, Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time and end the game. BRONCOS WIN WINNER – S Talanoa Hufanga Talanoa Hufanga cannot catch interceptions. He dropped like 10 last season and had two near picks early in this game. We pleaded, “PLEASE CATCH THE FOOTBALL,” and the football gods listened and granted Hufanga the ability to catch. He would go on to have a game-changing pick 6 of Matthew Stafford and later pick Stafford again in the end zone on the final play of the game, sealing the victory for the Broncos. TALANOA HUFANGA PICK 6 pic.twitter.com/ZjpkslYHx1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 What a big-time effort by the Broncos’ team leader. The Broncos did not force many turnovers last season, and they wanted to change that this season. We saw a game changing INT last week vs. the Jaguars and now, the Broncos had two big ones vs. the Rams. If Hufanga can start coming down with these interceptions, he will put himself in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation. WINNER – WR Pat Bryant Bryant was targeted a bunch in Week 1 but was mostly invisible in Week 2 while Jaylen Waddle was having his breakout performance. Well, he wasn’t invisible tonight. He had just 2 targets, but he turned those 2 targets into 2 catches for 44 yards and 1 touchdown. He also caught one of the two Broncos’ two-point conversions. BIG PLAY PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/WeWDOu8xa1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 His second and final catch came on a 2nd-and-20 play with 3:25 left deep in their own territory. The Broncos were coming off a penalty, and things were looking bleak, but he would get open, and Nix would hit him for a 39-yard catch-and-run to set the Broncos up in field goal range. Bryant would contribute later when he drew a controversial DPI on the Rams to give the Broncos an automatic first down and extend their drive. That drive would go on to end with what would end up being the game-winning touchdown. WINNER – QB Bo Nix The first half was ugly. He looked flustered and had two near-ugly interceptions, but that is just first-half Bo Nix. After halftime, second-half Bo Nix showed up and led the Broncos to three touchdown drives, including his game-winning QB sneak for the lead late in the 4th quarter. BO NIX FOR THE LEAD! pic.twitter.com/yV4AusftHo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Bo Nix now has 11 4th quarter comeback wins since 2024, which leads the NFL. It may not always be pretty; the analytical darlings hate him, the media disrespects him, but you cannot deny that Bo Nix is a gamer and has that magic to him. When the Broncos scored their first touchdown and converted the two-point conversion, I knew the comeback was on. We have seen this script before, and Nix has ice water in his veins. If he and the Broncos can ever put together a complete game, they could beat anyone at any time. Other notable Winners and Losers LOSER – CB Pat Surtain II: I do not type this often, and I believe it might be the first time that I have, but it’s a fact. Davante Adams had Surtain’s number tonight. PS2 is still an elite corner who will lock down opposing WRs more often than not, but tonight was not his night. WINNER – TE Nate Adkins: Adkins caught his second touchdown of the season and now has a touchdown in back-to-back games. While the tight end position may not have an elite playmaker, if Adkins can score within the red zone, he can be a real weapon for this team. WINNER – WR/KR Kolbe Katsis : It wasn’t a perfect night for him, but he had a big return, which sparked the Broncos’ comeback. LOSER – LB Alex Singleton: Missed tackles, poor coverage, and more missed tackles. I noticed him much more in the first half, but it didn’t seem like a strong night for him. LOSER – CB Riley Moss: Moss has had a nice start to the season, but he had a rough one tonight. Most of the Broncos’ corners struggled tonight, but Moss was called for an ugly DPI, gave up some plays throughout, and was burned on a double move for a long touchdown. WINNER – Broncos pass rush: It did disappear at times, but it came alive in the second half and had 4 sacks of Matthew Stafford. Bonitto, Allen, Hufanga, and Uwazurike all combined for 4 sacks. LOSER – WR Jaylen Waddle: He did have that nice two-point catch, but finished the night with 2 catches for 10 yards and had a couple of drops. The Rams had good coverage on him, but I was hoping for more from the Broncos’ playmaking wide receiver. LOSER – K Wil Lutz: Missed a FG LOSER – RB JK Dobbins : We simply need more…

title: Instant Reaction: Broncos defeat Rams in thriller on Sunday Night Football
summary: The Denver Broncos battled the Los Angeles Rams under the bright lights of Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday Night Football. It was an epic back and forth gridiron battle that came down to the final play of the game to find a victor. In the end, it was the Broncos who earned another […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos battled the Los Angeles Rams under the bright lights of Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday Night Football . It was an epic back and forth gridiron battle that came down to the final play of the game to find a victor. In the end, it was the Broncos who earned another comeback victory on the season defeating the Rams 30-26. Here are my instant reactions from tonight’s primetime matchup. Broncos’ Jekyll and Hyde offense strikes again For the third straight week, Denver’s offense had an abysmal to start the game. The Broncos gained just 67 yards in the first half and secured just five first downs. They managed to call just 21 plays, averaged a measly three yards per play, and had the ball for just ten minutes. That’s a recipe for failure. Meanwhile, the Rams looked fantastic. They had 274 yards on offense in the first half on 47 plays and averaged six yards per play. Whether it was through the air or on the ground, they absolutely dominated. They won the time of possession battle having the ball for nearly twenty minutes. It was an absolute masterclass effort by Sean McVay and his players. They outperformed Davis Webb and the Broncos’ offense through fifteen minutes on Sunday Night Football . After some halftime adjustments, Denver’s offense seemed to find a rhythm in the third quarter. Operating with some more under center looks, Bo Nix and his teammates performed much better. The ground game was more successful on early downs, and Nix was able to hit a variety of receivers for big plays. Notching two quality scoring drives and two-point conversions, the Broncos were able to tie the Rams at 16 by the end of the third quarter. Unfortunately, their third quarter success didn’t continue into the fourth until the last drive off the game. Edge rusher Dallas Turner was able to hit Nix’s arm and force a poor throw that resulted in an interception on the first outing of the quarter. On the subsequent drive, a third and short pass intended for Evan Engram was batted down by nickel corner Josh Watson. Nix and the Broncos offense would get one last chance with under four minutes left to try and find a way to tie or win the game. On second and twenty, a 39-yard catch and run by Pat Bryant got Denver within scoring distance. With under a minute to go on third and goal, Nix jumped over Luke Wattenberg and extended the ball to break the plan and give the Broncos the lead. Defense struggles early on with Rams’ heavy personnel and play action, performs much better in second half With the Broncos’ offense struggling to get going, that put enormous pressure on the defense. Truth be told, holding them to just sixteen points all things considered wasn’t terrible. Though it’s safe to say there were a handful of issues on display throughout the evening. After a rebound performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, inside linebacker Alex Singleton had another poor outing. He was routinely picked on by quarterback Matthew Stafford in pass coverage and had multiple missed tackles on Kyren Williams. Even All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II didn’t have a great start to the night going up against future Hall of Famer Davante Adams. In the second half, Vance Joseph’s defense made some good adjustments. They dialed up the heat on Stafford and for the most part played a lot better. They had a few issues, mainly Riley Moss getting caught peeking in coverage and giving up a big touchdown. However, safety Talanoa Hufanga’s pix-six on Stafford was a game-changing play the Broncos’ defense desperately needed. Hufanga also had the game-sealing interception on the last play of the game. What a statement victory for the Broncos! Whew! Week 3 had its fair share of one-score games. It was a fantastic weekend of football, but this Broncos win over the Rams is the icing on the cake. Early on, it looked like a sure-fire loss with nothing going well for the team. Kudos to the coaching staff and players for never giving up and making the right changes at halftime to gut out another incredible victory. Can you believe it, Broncos Country? Magic strikes twice for the second week in a row. Denver is now 2-1 on the season heading into next week’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. This game should give them a lot of confidence going up a well-coached Kyle Shanahan squad.

title: Broncos turn lopsided first half into wild back and forth finish vs. Rams
summary: What a wild game that was. In the first half, the Los Angeles Rams were in such complete control of the game that it surely looked like a blowout was in full effect. At one point, the Rams were on pace to drop nearly 600 yards of offense. However, the Denver Broncos defense did one […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos passes the ball against the Los Angeles Rams during the second quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a wild game that was. In the first half, the Los Angeles Rams were in such complete control of the game that it surely looked like a blowout was in full effect. At one point, the Rams were on pace to drop nearly 600 yards of offense. However, the Denver Broncos defense did one good thing and that was limiting them to field goals all through the second quarter. Down 16-0, Bo Nix and the Broncos charged back in the third quarter with two touchdown drives and converting both two-point conversions to tie the game. Then an absolutely wild fourth quarter where both teams would make big plays before Nix and the Broncos drove down the field in the final four minutes to take the lead in the final minute. Broncos vs. Rams final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Los Angeles Rams 7 9 0 10 26 Denver Broncos 0 0 16 14 30 First Quarter The first quarter started out promising with the Broncos’ defense coming up with a huge third down sack to end the Rams first drive. Nik Bonitto with the SACK! 💪 pic.twitter.com/FgCoh08KE2 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 But that was when the good times ended in the first quarter. The Rams second drive would have them march down the field converting a fourth down along the way to put up the first touchdown, then the Broncos would answer with a drive that ended in a doinked field goal attempt from Wil Lutz. Matthew Stafford and the Rams would then charge back down the field on their next drive and would be in field goal range again before the first quarter ended. The Broncos’ defense would hold on that drive and only give up a field goal early in the second quarter. Rams 7, Broncos 0. Full first quarter recap . Second Quarter The Broncos’ defense would hold on that drive and only give up a field goal early in the second quarter. However, it was a tail of a predictable and ineffective offensive game plan getting their butts whipped on every drive with the Broncos defense hanging on by a thread giving up three field goals in the second quarter — but it was clear the game was slipping away from Denver. The Rams walk into halftime with a 40-yard field goal and a 16-0 lead. Denver has been outscored 40-10 in the first half so far this season. LA has a 273-67 advantage in total yardage and a 17-5 edge in first downs tonight. Broncos being whipped in every possible way. — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) September 28, 2026 The Rams outgained Denver massively in the first half running 46 plays for 273 yards to the Broncos’ 21 plays and 67 yards. The only good thing about that first half for Denver was that the defense was holding Los Angeles to field goals. Rams 16, Broncos 0. Full second quarter recap . Third Quarter Things looked pretty bleak for Denver when they began the half punting it away, but that’s just because they like to toy with our emotions. What followed was the cardiac cat comeback kids. They would find a way to keep the drive alive and finished with a touchdown and two-point conversion on one drive. TOUCHDOWN PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/NwhfivF9mo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Then, after a terrible punt, marched down the field on the next drive with another touchdown and two-point conversion. PAT BRYANT MAKES IT A TIE GAME!! pic.twitter.com/a2jJd4JTuF — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 The comeback was so efficient and quick that I am sure the Rams were a bit shell-shocked to be in a tie game after dominating the first thirty minutes of the game. Such is life. Such is the Bo Nix experience. Broncos 16, Rams 16. Full third quarter recap . Fourth Quarter After forcing a three-and-out on the Rams, Nix and the Broncos’ offense picked up right where they left off. Nix hit Courtland Sutton on a deep pass down the sideline for 27-yards into Rams territory. WHAT A CATCH BY COURTLAND SUTTON pic.twitter.com/BxRRtBdg6a — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Disaster struck two plays later, though, when Nix had his arm hit as he threw and the wounded duck of a throw went straight into the arms of a Rams defender who returned it to the Broncos’ 36-yard line. Denver’s defense gave up a few first downs, but when they needed a play on third and give it was Talanoa Hufanga who came up big with the sack Hufanga SACK! pic.twitter.com/WlhTCUZtxu — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 That would force the field goal to put the Rams back on top 19-16. But holding them to a field goal was a win after the turnover. The Broncos had two good runs on first and second down, but on third and one they went clear pass formation and the ball was batted at the line. A fantastic punt by Jeremy Crawshaw would pin the Rams at their own six yard line for their next drive. It didn’t matter because Vance Joseph decided to play zone with Justin Strnad and other inside linebackers covering Davante Adams. The result was a 49 yard catch and run into Broncos’ territory. Denver’s defense woke up immediately after as Hufanga made the play of the game with a 66-yard interception return for a touchdown to put Denver up 23-19. TALANOA HUFANGA PICK 6 pic.twitter.com/ZjpkslYHx1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Like sharks with blood in the water, the Broncos defense came out with a sack on Stafford on the first play after the pick six. Of course, the elation would deflate quickly after Riley Moss bit hard on a double move to leave the wide receiver wide open for the easy touchdown to put the Rams back up 26-23. With less than four minutes remaining, the game would come down to a Bo Nix comeback attempt. A holding penalty on Garett Bolles seemed to be a death blow, but of course, the cardiac cats found a way with Pat Bryant streaking across the middle of the field for a 40 yard catch and run followed by a quick pass to Troy Franklin into the red zone to bring the game to the two minute warning. BIG PLAY PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/WeWDOu8xa1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 From the Rams 15 yard line, Nix handed off to J.K. Dobbins who gained a couple of yards. Nix would hit RJ Harvey for another two yards to the 10 yard line. On third and six, a defensive pass interference call gave the Broncos an automatic first down at the seven yard line with a minute to go. They would find themselves in a third and goal from the five. They’d be stopped again, but an illegal hands to the face penalty would set them up inside of the five for yet another fresh set of downs. Two plays later, Bo Nix from an empty set would run it in himself outside diving to the pilon to give Denver the lead with 45 seconds left. After review, the touchdown was overturned. It was all good because Nix would sneak it in on the next play anyway. BO NIX FOR THE LEAD! pic.twitter.com/yV4AusftHo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 The game came down to the final plays with the Rams streaking downfield and quickly found themselves at the Broncos’ 34-yard line with 21 seconds left. It would tick to 16 seconds after an incomplete pass to Adams. A big play to the Broncos 14-yard line with the clock stopped with 2 seconds. On the next play after a false start penalty, Stafford would get intercepted again by Hufanga for the game-clinching turnover. What a wild finish… Broncos 30, Rams 26.

summary: The Denver Broncos got the ball back to start the third quarter, but it certainly felt like the game was already slipping away with the Los Angeles Rams up 16-0 and dominant in all phases of the game in the first half. The stats back it up as Denver is 5-95-1 when trailing by 15 […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with teammate Jaylen Waddle #17 after scoring a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the third quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The stats back it up as Denver is 5-95-1 when trailing by 15 or more points at halftime. The Broncos are 5-95-1 all-time when trailing by at least 15 points at halftime. — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) September 28, 2026 Bo Nix and the Broncos started off their next drive with an inside run with J.K. title: Broncos vs. Rams second quarter recap
summary: Already in field goal range on the their third drive, the Los Angeles Rams would look to extend the 7-0 lead early in the second quarter. On the first play, Matthew Stafford hit Kyren Williams on a wheel route to the 17 yard line for another red zone opportunity. Alex Singleton was burned on the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Higbee #89 of the Los Angeles Rams scores a touchdown defended by Riley Moss #21 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Already in field goal range on the their third drive, the Los Angeles Rams would look to extend the 7-0 lead early in the second quarter. On the first play, Matthew Stafford hit Kyren Williams on a wheel route to the 17 yard line for another red zone opportunity. Alex Singleton was burned on the play. Williams would then force a missed tackle to get the ball down to the 8 yard line. On third and two, they would convert but would be called for offensive holding to back them up a third and long. Denver’s defense would hold and force the field goal. Rams 10, Broncos 0. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey were both on the field to start the Broncos next drive and it was Dobbins to took the handoff for three yards. Bo Nix would then fake the handoff to Dobbins before tossing to him out in the flat where he’d gain four yards. On third and three, Nix had his pass to Jaylen Waddle knocked away for another three-and-out for Denver’s offense. Denver’s defense almost forced their own three-and-out, but Riley Moss would commit a fairly easy pass interference call to give the Rams the first down. They’d force the Rams into another third and seven on the next series and the Broncos got torched by a tight end screen play for a first down our near midfield. Two plays later they’d again face a third and long — this time 11 yards — where Stafford finds a wide open pitch and catch for the first down. The Rams were making it look easy against Vance Joseph’s defense in the first half. Denver was fortunate to only be down 10 at this point in the game. That would quickly change. Davante Adams would smoke Pat Surtain on deep pass down the sideline for a 22 yard gain and yet another red zone opportunity for the Rams. After a delay of game on the Rams, Malcolm Roach batted down a pass to make it second and 15. Stafford was then hit when he threw to find Adams for the first down inside the five yard line with Talanoa Hufanga in coverage. He was wide open because of offensive pass interference that pushed the Rams all the back to the 40 yard line. Due to the penalties, that drive would end in another field goal. Rams 13, Broncos 0. The Rams had outgained the Broncos 214 yards to 36 yards after that drive. The defense doing everything it can to hold the line, but the offense needed to put a drive together if they were to stay in the game. A penalty looked like it would derail the next Broncos’ drive early, but RJ Harvey leaked out on the next play taking a Nix pass for 19 yards and a first down. A short run and a dropped pass to an open Jaylen Waddle brought up a third and eight where Waddle would redeem himself with a comeback catch to pick up the first down. Nix connects with Waddle to get the 1st down pic.twitter.com/1moRjTeEaO — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 Nix would take an RPO himself for four yards and then handed off to J.K. Dobbins for another four yards to bring up third and two at the two minute warning. You’d think they’d consider this four-down territory and beef up and run goal line twice to gain two yards. Nope, they go shotgun and take a sack to punt it away. This team is frustratingly predictable. The air was so deflated from the stadium and the team, the Rams offense came out and easily moved down the field and across midfield in two plays to two wide open receivers. They would close out the half with even more points making the Broncos look silly in all areas. Rams 16, Broncos 0.

title: The secondary is bad, but the Detroit Lions are not
summary: The Detroit Lions are 2-1, adding to their win column after knocking off an up-and-coming New York Jets team. But if you check the temperature of the more reactionary corners of the fanbase, they’re unimpressed and uninspired. After the shortcomings on defense snowballed—yet again—in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game, those unimpressed feel little confidence […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the New York Jets with Jameson Williams #1 during the third quarter at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions are 2-1, adding to their win column after knocking off an up-and-coming New York Jets team. But if you check the temperature of the more reactionary corners of the fanbase, they’re unimpressed and uninspired. After the shortcomings on defense snowballed—yet again—in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game, those unimpressed feel little confidence in this team’s chances when it comes to accomplishing big-picture goals. But really though, why care so much in the here and now about the ultimate objective of Super Bowl viability? Why are people talking about this team like the playoffs start in a couple weeks? It’s not even October! The team with a winning record has some warts in the secondary, but after spending a weekend out and about, chatting with folks from the grocery store to the golf course and dive bars in between, you would have thought they were a winless bunch of sucks; a hopeless group watching their window slam shut on their fingers. The secondary is bad. That doesn’t mean the Lions are bad. And coming to a verdict on their ceiling based on their performances through three weeks is premature. That’s not me being dismissive of the very serious problems in the secondary. Be it some mix of coaching, scheme, and/or personnel, Geno Smith shouldn’t have done what he did in Week 3. Smith’s +21.1 completion percentage over expected, defined by NFL Next Gen Stats as, “the difference between a quarterback’s actual completion percentage and expected completion percentage controlling for the level of difficulty of each pass,” was nearly 11% higher than the quarterback who finished second in Week 3 (Patrick Mahomes, +10.25). Smith was second in tight-window rate (27%), the percentage of passes where the targeted receiver has less than 1 yard of separation when the pass arrives. It appears as though Nevin Lawson crawled so Roger McCreary could also come up just shy of making a play . The secondary was in better position to make plays this week, but there were still missed assignments, miscommunication, and missed opportunities to make a play and get off the field on third down. The guys on the backend still have to make plays in coverage, not just on blitzes where they’re forcing game-winning turnovers—nothing like waiting until the very last moment, Chuck Clark! It’s with much regret that it’s my job to inform you the secondary for the Detroit Lions is in rough shape. Despite you knowing that their starting safeties are both on PUP, and their No. 1 cornerback as of three months ago is now facing up to life in prison as a member of the Seattle Seahawks, here’s a chance to remind you the most turbulent spot on the roster is experiencing some choppy air while they’re attempting to build the plane with the wheels up. The issues in the secondary are all anyone can talk about, so we’re going to see people ignore the rest of the defense’s performance against the Jets. “I just can’t ignore the secondary’s play and pretend like this is a team capable of contending for a Super Bowl” is the low-hanging, drive-time topic of conversation after this most recent game. They’ll ignore Geno Smith getting sacked five times for 44 yards. Pretty sweet the pass rush is second in time to pressure (2.46 seconds) and 10th in quarterback pressure rate (39.0%)! And what about that run defense, eh? 3.1 yards per carry, third in stuff rate (percentage of run plays resulting in no gain or loss: 26.3%), and sixth in rushing EPA per play allowed (-0.23). Some things to hang your hat on if you’re Kelvin Sheppard, but it doesn’t mean it’s time to rest. It never is in the NFL, and there’s still plenty of work to be done. Also, more good news: there’s no reason to assume the secondary you see now will be the one this team has in January! It sure doesn’t sound like Brad Holmes and the front office are waiting until it’s too late to try and improve at the cornerback position after early-morning reports Sunday about the Lions showing interest in Joey Porter Jr. If it doesn’t end up being the big name in Porter Jr., maybe that player Detroit needs could come from any other number of the 0-3 teams with their playoff hopes actually on life support. Imagine watching that game against the Jets, getting to see Jahmyr Gibbs pass Billy Sims for second place in rushing touchdowns by a Detroit Lion in eight fewer games, and still letting the secondary ruin your afternoon. The offense scored 30+ points for the third consecutive game without a Ben Johnson in sight and you’re letting the cornerbacks get you bent out of shape? Are you new here? Were you around when the practice field hill was built and the ping pong tables removed? At the end of the day, the Lions won despite their significant weakness in the secondary rearing its ugly head at the worst possible moment, but there is plenty of time for roster tinkering that could address their glaring weaknesses. Detroit is 2-1, and you haven’t even nailed down a date for a trip to the pumpkin patch. Take a look around the NFC: if there’s a world beater, point ‘em out. There isn’t a single team around here that is free from defects. There’s a long way between now and Week 18, so until then, buckle up if you’re in for the ride.

title: Panthers could be down 2 key defensive backs vs. Lions
summary: The Detroit Lions are entering Week 4 as three-point favorites over the Carolina Panthers in their Sunday night showdown, but some injury news from Monday could see that line shift (note: it’s already jumped to 3.5). According to NFL reporter Tom Pelissero, the Panthers’ No. 1 cornerback Jaycee Horn is out indefinitely after suffering a […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaycee Horn #8 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions are entering Week 4 as three-point favorites over the Carolina Panthers in their Sunday night showdown, but some injury news from Monday could see that line shift (note: it’s already jumped to 3.5). According to NFL reporter Tom Pelissero, the Panthers’ No. 1 cornerback Jaycee Horn is out indefinitely after suffering a quad injury on Sunday against the Browns. Horn is coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons with the Panthers, and he signed a four-year, $100 million extension last offseason. He was off to another decent start to the season, allowing just five catches on 10 targets for 63 yard and two pass breakups, according to PFF. To make matters worse for the Panthers, in Sunday’s loss to the Browns, they also lost their other starting outside cornerback Mike Jackson to a groin injury. There has yet to be an update on his status, but he suffered the injury in the first half and did not return to the game. Jackson is an eight-year vet who actually spent some brief time with the Lions in 2019, but has really turned things around lately. In 2025, Jackson produced an NFL-high 19 passes defended and also logged four interception. Left in the Panthers’ cornerback room is fourth-round rookie Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans, and nickel corner Chau Smith-Wade. Carolina also has three practice squad cornerbacks: undrafted rookie DeVonta Smith, and two undrafted players from the 2025 class: Zion Childress and Corey Thornton. Of the three, only Thornton has any real experience at the NFL level, playing in 12 games and 127 defensive snaps last season. This will be something to monitor as the week goes on, but I would expect the Panthers to add to that room as they prepare for a dynamic Detroit Lions passing attack that currently ranks eighth in passing yards (247.7 per game), third in passer rating (116.1), and tied for second in passing touchdowns (eight).

title: Detroit Lions Week 3 snap counts: Breaking down defensive changes vs. Jets
summary: After starting the season 1-1 with glaring holes in defensive execution, the Detroit Lions made some significant changes to their personnel, some of which helped them get back on track, leading to a 31-24 win over the New York Jets in Week 3. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what […]

(Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After starting the season 1-1 with glaring holes in defensive execution, the Detroit Lions made some significant changes to their personnel, some of which helped them get back on track, leading to a 31-24 win over the New York Jets in Week 3. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Jared Goff: 65 (100%) Josh Dobbs: Did Not Play After a bumpy start to the game, Goff settled in quickly and continued his high level of play. While you’d like to see the offense sharp from start to finish, it’s hard to argue with the offense putting up 31 points in all three games so far this season. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs: 45 (69%) Sione Vaki: 20 (31%) — 15 special teams snaps (65%) Jacob Saylors: 2 (3%) — 15 (65%) Gibbs was once again a human highlight reel in this game, but Aaron Glenn’s Jets exposed a possible weakness: pass protection. Glenn’s repeated A-gap blitzes were a problem for Gibbs, and likely why Vaki saw his snaps increase, as he was terrific in pass protection. Vaki’s ability to contribute in the run and pass game proved to teams that he’s not just a one-trick player that will tip the offensive play call. Vaki talked with Pride of Detroit after the game and discussed his growth since the beginning of the season: “The preparation going into these past two weeks, going out there and letting loose, and not being afraid to mess up. Being able to believe in myself, supported by (running backs) coach (Tashard) Choice and the boys in the room, has helped push me forward and has been a real confidence builder.” Vaki went on to discuss how he tries to be the aggressor in pass protection: “It’s definitely a conscious choice. Watching the film of (Jets) Demario Davis, being the great linebacker that he is, we knew he was going to try and run through our faces, and I just knew I had to respond by stuffing my face in there. There’s still some things to clean up, but today’s game did feel good.” And for those worried that threatening the blitz could be a way for defenses to get Gibbs off the field, the Lions did respond by running some 21 personnel, with both Gibbs and Vaki on the field at the same time. A nice counterpunch by offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. Wide receiver Jameson Williams: 53 (82%) Amon-Ra St. Brown: 48 (74%) Isaac TeSlaa: 31 (48%) Tay Martin: 2 (3%) — 15 (65%) Tom Kennedy: 0 (0%) — 8 (35%) With the Lions deploying some heavier sets against the Jets—13 personnel and Jumbo packages saw upticks in usage—the Lions wide receivers saw their opportunities scaled back a tick. Snap distribution remains very similar to past weeks, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this is St. Brown’s lowest snap count this season. Tight end Sam LaPorta: 60 (92%) Brock Wright: 38 (58%) — 10 (43%) Jackson Meeks: 10 (15%) — 2 (9%) Tyler Conklin: DNP ( INACTIVE ) As mentioned above, the Lions deployed a fair amount of 13 personnel in this game, with the wrinkle being that they split Meeks out wide to stretch the Jets’ Base defense. There will be games moving forward that the Lions will want a more balanced TE3 like Conklin on the field, but this new wrinkle with Meeks illustrates the versatility this group has. Offensive line LT Penei Sewell: 65 (100%) LG Christian Mahogany: 65 (100%) — 5 (22%) C Juice Scruggs: 65 (100%) — 5 (22%) RG Tate Ratledge: 65 (100%) — 5 (22%) RT Blake Miller: 65 (100%) — 5 (22%) T Larry Borom: 15 (23%) — 5 (22%) G/T Miles Frazier: 0 (0%) — 5 (22%) C Seth McLaughlin: DNP LG Ben Bartch: DNP ( INJURED ) With their preferred starting five healthy again, the offensive line played very well in this game, slowing down a Jets defense near the top of all defensive rankings entering Week 3. Overall, the Lions gave up just eight pressures and two sacks, but the offensive line accounted for only five pressures and was not to blame for either sack. As previously mentioned, the Lions leaned on their Jumbo sets in this game, utilizing Borom as a sixth offensive lineman for nearly a quarter of offensive snaps. With McNeill scaling back a bit, that opened up the opportunities for his backup, rookie Skyler Gill-Howard, to increase his workload, and he rewarded them with three pressures and a half-sack (he split with Aidan Hutchinson). Gill-Howard spoke with Pride of Detroit following the game and discussed his first NFL sack: “The guard (Jordan Meridith), he was the second one because the first (Dylan Parham) got hurt—I knew I could beat him laterally, so that’s what I did; I took an inside counter, and while I got a little past the quarterback, the D-line did a good job of forcing him up, allowing me to spin out and get it—and of course, Hutch was right there.” Gill-Howard also saw one snap on offense on a goal-line run that resulted in a Gibbs touchdown. Although the play went in the opposite direction of Gill-Howard’s block, it looks like a precursor to something the Lions could build on moving forward. “You know coach (Dan) Campbell. You’ve seen those types of plays throughout his tenure here.
