title: Chargers vs. Seahawks Opening Odds: Bolts underdogs again in Week 4
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-3 after falling to the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 3. The schedule doesn’t get much easier as the Seattle Seahawks are on deck in Week 4. The Seahawks are the defending champions, but they also lost their most recent game in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers throws a pass against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-3 after falling to the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 3. The schedule doesn’t get much easier as the Seattle Seahawks are on deck in Week 4. The Seahawks are the defending champions, but they also lost their most recent game in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. The Bolts entered this week as 6.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 44.5. The Chargers looked good in the first three quarters of their game against the Bills. They started off with a 10-0 lead in the first quarter, but gave up that many points in the second to take the game to a tie at halftime. The Chargers held the Bills scoreless in the third while tacking on a chip-shot field goal, but the fourth quarter is when everything unraveled. They allowed a pair of touchdowns, one each to Josh Allen and James Cook, that broke the game open for Buffalo. The game proved that the Chargers can be competitive against some of these tough teams on their schedule, and the Seahawks should be no exception. Seattle has dealt with injuries this season. Sam Darnold missed the team’s Week 2 contest against the Arizona Cardinals with a glute injury, but he is healthy now. Seattle hopes that another full week of practice should have him closer to his usual self. The Chargers will have to disrupt his rhythm if they want a chance at pulling off the big upset.

title: Chargers-Bills Game Recap: Bolts lose despite 5 takeaways by defense
summary: The Chargers fan base is somehow used these types of game, and that’s saying something when that “type of game” is one where your defense records five takeaways from the league’s best offense and still loses. That’s what happened on Sunday in Buffalo. MVP-frontrunner Josh Allen entered the game with nine total touchdowns and zero […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers running back Omarion Hampton (8) runs the ball for a gain during an NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA.(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers fan base is somehow used these types of game, and that’s saying something when that “type of game” is one where your defense records five takeaways from the league’s best offense and still loses. That’s what happened on Sunday in Buffalo. MVP-frontrunner Josh Allen entered the game with nine total touchdowns and zero interceptions. Against the Chargers, he threw two picks and the offense fumbled the ball away three more times. The Bills lost the turnover battle 1-5, yet somehow the one turnover by the Chargers was vastly more impactful than any of their giveaways. But that’s what this season has become in just three short weeks. After winning 22 games over the last two seasons, the Chargers are 0-3 and once again losing in historically-rare ways. In the seasons that led to the franchise eventually firing Anthony Lynn and Brandon Staley, the Chargers were dropping games they had no business losing at an alarming rate. Every week there was a new stat proclaiming that the Chargers were “the first team to ever lose after ______” or “the Chargers are the first team since (pick a year) to lose after _____.” Every week was deja vu. New week, new wacky found to lose a game. This week, the Chargers became the third team since 2016 to lose a game despite winning the turnover margin by four or more. They only scored 10 points off their turnovers, including a missed 45-yard field goal by Cameron Dicker who is now 1-for-3 on kicks in 2026. Chris O’Leary’s unit fought their tails off. Khalil Mack forced a strip sack and rookie Akheem Mesidor recorded his first full sack. Rookie safety Genesis Smith snagged the first two interceptions of his career against the league’s best quarterback. There were so many moments for the Chargers that, if they were any other team, would have given you supreme confidence that they were going to beat the Bills on the road despite the 0-2 start. And for a moment, that was the case. It was surreal but you could feel the positivity bubbling up inside of everyone donning the powder blue. But then Dicker missed that field goal which would have given the Chargers a 13-0 lead midway through the second quarter. Instead, the miss gave the Bill good starting field position and it was only a matter of time before Allen and Co. found their rhythm. The Bills scored 10 straight and it was a tie game at the break. The Chargers looked energized coming out of the locker room and took the lead back with a field goal on the opening drive of the half. But that was the final points they’d score in the game. To reiterate: The Chargers had FIVE(!) takeaways against the Bills, but somehow, someway, the turnover that felt like it had the largest impact on the game was the Chargers’ only giveaway. That was Herbert’s interception that came just three plays after the defense recorded the fifth turnover. And it didn’t help that it was one of the most egregious passes thrown by Herbert this year, and maybe even his career. Herbert, with three wideouts flanking his left, dropped back and scanned through his progressions. At the top of his drop, Herbert fired over the middle of the field to veteran and new Chargers receiver Marquez Valdez-Scantling who was crossing into the end zone. The problem? Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was hovering in the middle of the field the entire time and he swiftly undercut the pass before returning it 41 yards the other way. The Chargers needed to create some distance and were still up by three following the latest takeaway, and Herbert essentially handed the ball right back to them in a pivotal and high-pressure moment. You want to talk about the margins and how important they are in the NFL? Well, I guess those margins are only razor-thin when you’re the Chargers, because it sure didn’t matter for Buffalo on Sunday. The Bolts’ quarterback finished with 226 passing yards, one touchdown, and the aforementioned interception on 20-of-34 passing. He also added 17 rushing yards. Mike McDaniel leaned on Keaton Mitchell more against the Bills as he finished with eight carries for 52 yards (6.5 YPC). Omarion Hampton took 15 carries for 56 yards (3.7) in a quiet day against a top-10 run defense. Tre’ Harris had one of his best games as a pro while leading the team with six receptions and 76 receiving yards. Ladd McConkey was behind him with four catches and 66 yards. Quentin Johnston, who had a costly drop on third down in the second half, finished with season-highs of three catches and 40 yards, 21 of which came right before halftime on a play essentially given to the Chargers to run out the clock. Tuli Tuipulotu had 1.5 sacks to lead the defense while Khalil Mack and Akheem Mesidor each had one. Linebacker Daiyan Henley led the team with nine tackles and recorded the Chargers’ first fumble recovery of the day. We’re officially in rare territory. The Chargers are 0-3 and head to Seattle in Week Four. They then face the Broncos and Chiefs before their bye in Week Seven. The issues they’re facing do not look like they can be fixed in the middle of a season. Three games is a large enough sample size to paint a clearer picture of who and what this team is. Right now, in a results-based business, the Chargers are bad. They’re actually very bad and it’s not unheard of for teams to start making drastic moves to half the bleeding as soon as possible. Will that happen in the days to come? Will they weather the storm and let the season play out before making such decisions? I would think everything is on the table right now. First Quarter Josh Allen and the Bills offense was up first after receiving the opening kickoff. However, that lasted just one play as defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe crashed down on running back James Cook to force a fumble that was recovered near midfield by linebacker Daiyan Henley. With the sudden change in momentum just seconds into the game, Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense got to work. On the first play of the drive, Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb was flagged for roughing the passer which pushed the Chargers 15 yards further into Buffalo territory. On their first third down opportunity, Mike McDaniel called a zone read play that Herbert took for a seven-yard gain to move the chains. After mixing in some runs by Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, the Chargers had first-and-goal at the Buffalo seven-yard line. Hampton took a handoff for four tough yards before inching forward another two yards to the one-yard line. On third down, Herbert handed a jet sweep to Keaton Mitchell who stutter-stepped by a defender before hitting the gas and beating the defense to the pylon for a touchdown. The Bills began their second drive with a pair of eight-yard gains by wideout D.J. Moore and Cook. From their, the Chargers defense clamped down with Tuli Tuipulotu earning his first sack of the year by bringing down Allen on third down. The second drive for the Chargers was a short three-and-out. After a qucik seven-yard pass to McConkey to get them ahead of the chains, Mitchell was dropped for a loss of six on second down after bringing in a swing pass. Los Angeles punted after a third-down incompletion. Buffalo’s rough start on offense continued with Allen firing a pass over the middle of the field to Moore that was intercepted by rookie safety Genesis Smith who closed and undercut the route with haste. With the ball back, Herbert and the offense went 30 yards in six plays before falling short on third down at the Buffalo-15-yard line. Dicker came on and converted his first field goal of the season from 31 yards out. Second Quarter On the first play of the quarter, Allen faked a handoff…

title: Pass protection is more valuable than ever for Matthew Stafford and the Rams
summary: Matthew Stafford did not have his finest game against the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t a complete disaster by any means for the reigning NFL MVP in Week 3. He completed a subpar 54.5% of his passes for a gaudy 390 yards and a pair of touchdowns, but it took him 55 attempts to get there […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams looks at the clock as the last seconds tick off during the third quarter of the Denver Broncos' 30-26 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 27, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Matthew Stafford did not have his finest game against the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t a complete disaster by any means for the reigning NFL MVP in Week 3. He completed a subpar 54.5% of his passes for a gaudy 390 yards and a pair of touchdowns, but it took him 55 attempts to get there and he also threw a pair of interceptions, both of which came in the fourth quarter (one of which was returned for a touchdown, one of which was on the final snap of the game). When you dive into the advanced numbers, it’s more of the same. In the loss, Stafford posted just .03 EPA/play, a success rate of just 43% and -0.1 completion percentage over expectation ( all according to RBSDM.com ). Through three weeks, Stafford’s PFF grade is a flat 60.0 , dead-on average by their grading scale. Now, PFF’s grading has always been flawed and is especially unreliable now given what that company has gone through in the last year, but a middling grade at least somewhat matches the eye test through three games. There is one distinct and easy-to-grasp area in which the Rams and their star quarterback are struggling mightily, and it came to a head against the Broncos: pressure. Talanoa Hufanga's 66-yard pick six swung the @Broncos ' win probability by 55.4 percentage points. 🔸 Before INT: 16.3% 🔸 After INT: 71.7% 🔸 WP Swing: +55.4% #LARvsDEN | #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/mLmDq82zBe — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 28, 2026 According to Next Gen Stats, when under pressure on Sunday night, Stafford was just 5-of-18 passing for 61 yards with the first interception of the night and he was also sacked four times. From a clean pocket, his fortunes couldn’t have been farther in the opposite direction, save for one play. He went 25-of-35 when kept clean, throwing for 329 yards and two touchdowns plus the desperation pick to close the game. That’s 3.4 yards per attempt while under pressure, 9.4 yards per attempt from a clean pocket. It’s easy to understand why that is so devastating to an offense. Obviously, no quarterback in the NFL is ever going to be free from pressure on every snap throughout a game, let alone a season. You have to deal with pressure constantly, especially going up against the league’s best defenses (a group you can still consider the Broncos to be included in). But when the disparity in success is that enormous, it puts even more emphasis on holding the line for your quarterback. Things were even more stark in the second half when Denver made its comeback. The Broncos pressured Stafford on 57.7% of his second-half dropbacks this weekend, compared to just 23.5% in the first half (again from Next Gen Stats). It goes without saying that this is something the Rams have to clean up going forward. Concerningly, this has been a trend through the first sixth of this season. Against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, Stafford was pressured on 44% of his dropbacks, the highest pressure rate he had faced since Dec. 2024. No one is going to tell you the offense was spectacular or even good in the opener, and no one is going to tell you they were impressed by the offense in the second half of Week 3. Generate pressure on Matthew Stafford and he is not the same QB. If you cannot generate pressure on the Rams, Stafford will slice and dice you up. Difference between the first and second half of this game. Broncos need to keep Stafford uncomfortable in the pocket. *stats shown… https://t.co/pc7IiDZcDC pic.twitter.com/26wS85EJQl — Investments & Sports Club (@StocksSportsRE) September 28, 2026 Against the Giants in Week 2, by the way, Stafford only faced pressure on five dropbacks and torched that defense. The offensive line was one area that drew some concern, or at least some sideways glances, leading into the season. There’s time to improve and it’s not like they’re wholly lacking talent. But this is a legitimate concern and one that needs to be fixed as quickly as possible. With an aging quarterback who’s not exactly fleet of foot, keeping him upright needs to be addressed urgently. It’s too early to throw in the towel on this team, even at 1-2. That should be a given. But if there’s anything that can derail a title-contending season, your quarterback falling under constant siege and suffering the consequences of it would be at the top of the list.

title: The refs didn’t give up a second and twenty, the Rams did
summary: You can blame the officiating for the latest Los Angeles Rams loss to the Denver Broncos, but I think that misses the point. The Rams had a 16-0 lead lost, retook the lead, late and had the Broncos deep in their own territory on a second and twenty after a holding call against the Broncos. […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams shakes hands with head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos after the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Rams 30-26. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images You can blame the officiating for the latest Los Angeles Rams loss to the Denver Broncos, but I think that misses the point. The Rams had a 16-0 lead lost, retook the lead, late and had the Broncos deep in their own territory on a second and twenty after a holding call against the Broncos. The Rams allowed the Broncos to convert easily, keeping them in the game. BIG PLAY PAT BRYANT pic.twitter.com/WeWDOu8xa1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 28, 2026 A great game is a story and a great story isn’t about one chapter, but the entire novel. One play didn’t cost the Rams. A number of plays did. The officiating didn’t cost the Rams the game, the Rams put the game in the hands of the officials by not sealing the deal when they were up 16-0. They let the Broncos back in the game, the Broncos won. That’s math. You can find silver linings such as the Rams built the lead in the first place, they played without Puka Nacua, the defense at times looks so much better than last year with Trent McDuffie, the running back room is solid, the special teams didn’t miss a field goal Sunday Night, but the Rams lost. It should hurt for the team and for the fans who take this sport too seriously (like me). This is supposed to be a fun game, but it’s hard to find any fun after that loss, and if you’re paying attention, some of the same problems from 2025 are showing up in 2026. The biggest issue, the failure to close out games while leading. If teams didn’t know they were in a Rams game until the very final whistle, they do now. Blame the refs, blame McVay, blame the pick-six by Matthew Stafford, blame me! I was there! But it doesn’t change the fact that THE RAMS lost. The Broncos won, and in the history books, that’s the part that’ll matters most in the NFL. This season isn’t over, but it’s off to a rough start and this particular loss should sting. If the Rams don’t want to feel this way again, they need to play better. That’s math. Broncos turn lopsided first half into wild back and forth finish vs. Rams (milehighreport) “In the first half, the Los Angeles Rams were in such complete control of the game that it surely looked like a blowout was in full effect. At one point, the Rams were on pace to drop nearly 600 yards of offense. However, the Denver Broncos defense did one good thing and that was limiting them to field goals all through the second quarter. Down 16-0, Bo Nix and the Broncos charged back in the third quarter with two touchdown drives and converting both two-point conversions to tie the game. Then an absolutely wild fourth quarter where both teams would make big plays before Nix and the Broncos drove down the field in the final four minutes to take the lead in the final minute.“ Rams clap back on narrative of Sean McVay ditching media after collapse vs Broncos (sports.yahoo0) “This caused a stir amongst media members as the Rams head coach seemingly ditched the postgame press conference. Nate Atkins of The Athletic revealed how shocking the move by McVay was in a post on X. “Sean McVay ducked out of his press conference before Rams media could get into it, only 10 minutes after the final whistle. Not sure I have ever seen that in this league before,” Atkins wrote . Rams Vice President of Communications Artis Twyman quickly countered the senior NFL writer on X. “Again Nathan, I will not let you get on here and not represent the truth. In the press box, they announce that media that want to attend the post game news conference, leave at the five-minute mark. You chose to stay until the end of the game, which made you late,” Twyman wrote .“ When will Garrett, Nacua return for Rams? (nbcsports) “Mike Florio and Chris Simms assess the timeline for Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua to return from injury, and for the latter, how contract negotiations may affect it.” Bo Nix and Talanoa Hufanga lead the Broncos past the Rams 30-26 in a Sunday night thriller (espn.com) “Nix’s keeper from inches outside the goal line with 47 seconds left capped a wild final five minutes that included a 66-yard pick-6 by Hufanga, a quick touchdown response by Los Angeles and a game-sealing second picked-off pass by Denver’s do-everything safety. “I actually had to have a pep talk with myself,” after dropping two interceptions earlier in the game, said Hufanga, who finished with a sack, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hit and three pass breakups to go with his pair of interceptions.“ Matt Stafford-Taylor Swift cameo, explained: Why Rams QB is appearing in star’s latest music video (sportingnews) “Swift showcased her new music video while accepting the inaugural Artist Director Honors at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards show on Sunday. While the Rams were busy taking on the Broncos , Stafford went viral for making a surprise cameo, wearing a tuxedo in the background. Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell joined Stafford among the notable faces in the video:“ From the Podium: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford and Josh Wallace recap Rams narrow loss to Broncos on Sunday Night Football (therams.com) “DENVER — With three lead changes in the final five minutes of the game, Sunday Night Football between the Rams and Broncos went down to the final play. Unable to score on the final play of the game, Denver ultimately prevailed, 30-26. Rams head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford and cornerback Josh Wallace gave their thoughts on the game from the podium.“ ‘No panic but there’s frustration.’ Rams blow 16-point lead in stunning loss to Broncos (latimes.com) “DENVER — Mile sigh. A heavy one. The what-the-heck-just-happened kind. That’s how the stunned Rams felt Sunday night. Coach Sean McVay and his team came here aiming to put together a second consecutive impressive prime-time performance. And through the first half against the Denver Broncos, it looked like the Rams would do just that.“ HIGHLIGHTS: Rams top plays in Week 3 vs. Broncos | Josh Wallace’s INT, Tyler Higbee’s TD & more (therams.com) “Watch the Los Angeles Rams’ best plays from the Week 3 matchup against the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football.” Broncos vs. Rams final score: Bo Nix caps second-half comeback with late TD as Denver stuns L.A. (cbssports) “The Rams dominated the first half and showed no ill effects of being without the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and a superstar wide receiver. The absences of Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua were a relative afterthought while Los Angeles constructed a 16-0 lead. They out-gained the Broncos 256 to 72 before the break, and they were in total control. But then the Broncos flipped the game on its head. On the other side of the halftime break, Bo Nix connected with Pat Bryant II and Nate Adkins for back-to-back touchdowns and converted the two-point conversion on both of them to level the score before the third quarter had even expired. Denver’s defense also stepped up, as it held the Rams to a meager 19 yards in the frame.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 3: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Rams feel Puka’s absence. A week after Davante Adams turned back the clock and scorched the Giants for 195 yards and a pair of touchdowns, he was stellar again. He racked up game-highs of 137 yards and seven receptions — his 332 yards over the last two weeks are the highest two-game total in his career. But the absence of Puka Nacua , one of the game’s best receivers, was surely felt. By game’s end, Stafford had 390 yards on 30-of-55 passing, but when the Rams offense lulled, it was apparent how beneficial having a second elite WR option would be. Konata Mumpfield had the game of his short career with four grabs for 93 yards and a 48-yard TD catch. But three of…

title: Bill Vinovich is simply awful!
summary: Bill Vinovich has officiated multiple Super Bowls and numerous conference championship games, and the league has repeatedly assigned him to some of its biggest games. But experience and reputation do not make an official immune from criticism when the calls on the field become game-changing. And on Sunday night, Vinovich and his crew once again […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Referee Bill Vinovich looks on in a preseason game between the Denver Broncos and the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bill Vinovich has officiated multiple Super Bowls and numerous conference championship games, and the league has repeatedly assigned him to some of its biggest games. But experience and reputation do not make an official immune from criticism when the calls on the field become game-changing. Bill Vinovich will be the referee for Broncos-Rams on Sunday Night Football. Denver has a 5-11 lifetime record in games officiated by Vinovich, including a 1-6 mark at home. Vinovich's crew called 14 accepted penalties in Week 2, about 18% above the NFL average. pic.twitter.com/fYmDcbbuyc — Zack Kelberman (@KelbermanNFL) September 23, 2026 And on Sunday night, Vinovich and his crew once again found themselves at the center of a controversial finish involving the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams lost to the Denver Broncos 30-26 , but one particular decision late in the fourth quarter deserves enormous scrutiny. With Denver facing third-and-6 at the Los Angeles 11-yard line with 1:15 remaining, Bo Nix’s pass intended for Pat Bryant fell incomplete. Josh Wallace was flagged for defensive pass interference , giving Denver an automatic first down. The official play-by-play confirms the penalty and the fact that the play was wiped out. this was called DPI… thoughts? pic.twitter.com/ea6STqux1i — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) September 28, 2026 From the Rams’ perspective, it was an absolutely brutal call. Wallace appeared to make a play on the football, and the replay created an even bigger question about whether Bryant was the player who actually initiated the contact. If anything, the Rams had a legitimate argument that the penalty should have gone the other way for offensive pass interference. Instead, Denver received a fresh set of downs. That changed everything. Rather than forcing the Broncos to face fourth down in the red zone, the penalty allowed Denver to continue the drive. The Broncos subsequently moved closer to the end zone and completed their comeback, turning what could have been a potential Rams victory into a devastating four-point loss. And this is where Vinovich’s history becomes relevant. The most infamous example came in the 2018 NFC Championship Game between Sean Payton’s New Orleans Saints and Sean McVay’s Rams. With the Saints driving late, Rams defensive back Nickell Robey-Coleman made significant contact with Tommylee Lewis before the ball arrived. No pass interference penalty was called. The NFL subsequently acknowledged that the officiating crew missed defensive pass interference and a helmet-to-helmet penalty on the play. Vinovich was the referee for that game. That missed call ultimately helped send the Rams to Super Bowl LIII. Nearly eight years later, Vinovich was again at the center of a critical Rams game — and once again, an officiating decision became a defining moment. To be clear, the Rams made plenty of mistakes themselves. Matthew Stafford threw a pick-six, Denver produced a massive 39-yard conversion on second-and-20, and Stafford’s final pass was intercepted. This was not a perfect Rams performance. But that does not make the Wallace penalty any less significant. Had the interception stood, or had the play been ruled differently, Denver’s drive would have ended in Los Angeles territory. Instead, the Broncos received new life and ultimately completed the comeback. For Rams fans, that is going to make the Vinovich name awfully familiar again — and not for the right reasons.

title: PFF grades: The short-handed Rams really need someone to step up
summary: If you’re looking for silver linings with the Los Angeles currently 1-2 and tied for last place in the NFC West, you probably won’t find them in this week’s grades from Pro Football Focus (PFF). Sunday night’s loss to the Denver Broncos was heartbreaking all around. LA is short-handed. Usually reliable contributors are not performing […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams runs downfield against Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re looking for silver linings with the Los Angeles currently 1-2 and tied for last place in the NFC West, you probably won’t find them in this week’s grades from Pro Football Focus (PFF). Sunday night’s loss to the Denver Broncos was heartbreaking all around. LA is short-handed. Usually reliable contributors are not performing up to their individual standards. The Rams desperately need someone to step up and alter the course of the season . So far that hasn’t happened. The team will seemingly continue on this unfortunate trajectory with upcoming tough games against the Eagles, Bills, better-than-expected Cardinals, and the 3-0 Raiders. What can we glean from Sunday night’s shortcomings? Top five grades on offense 1 – Kyren Williams, RB: 85.0 Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards. He averaged 5.9 yards per carry. He also added six catches for 70 yards through the air. The only thing he did wrong was not carry the ball more, and that is on the offensive play caller. The Rams were quick to shift away from the run and it didn’t play out in their favor. 2 – Tyler Higbee, TE: 81.0 Higbee received a large workload with both Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson limited because of injury. The veteran tight end caught eight of his 11 targets for 62 yards and a score. It’s nice that, even when short-handed, the Rams can turn to a quality and dependable tight end like Higbee. He’s probably not someone you want to run your offense through, however. 3 – Warren McClendon, RT: 69.5 While McClendon led the offensive line in PFF grading, it wasn’t a clean night for the right tackle. He allowed seven pressures in pass protection and was flagged two times. Kevin Dotson was the lowest performer of the group with three pressures. 4 – Davante Adams, WR: 68.0 Adams received the highest target total on offense with 13, although he finished behind Higbee in catches with seven. The veteran ripped off 137 yards in a tough matchup against Patrick Surtain. 52 of Adams’ yards came after the catch point. He dropped one pass. 5 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 65.9 Second-year receiver Konata Mumpfield came out of nowhere to catch a 48-yard wide open touchdown when his team needed him the most. Mumpfield caught four of his eight targets for 93 yards. He also dropped one pass. Other notes on offense Matthew Stafford finished with a grade of 60.0, which was ninth on the offense overall. Through three weeks, Stafford is PFF’s 27th quarterback in offensive grade and 24th in passing grade. Interceptions have been a major concern. He’s tied for second in the NFL with four behind Drake Maye. More concerning is that the Rams offense has found very little success on the deep ball. Stafford is just 5/13 for 194 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions—good for a PFF passing grade of 58.3. That ranks him 30th in the NFL. How do we explain Stafford’s drop off from last season? Is this late-career decline? Could there be something systemically wrong with LA’s approach? No matter, the Rams need Matthew Stafford to perform better and fast. Top five grades on defense 1 – Omar Speights, MLB: 89.8 Speights earned an impressive sack on Bo Nix that came at an opportune time. He notched two pressures on six pass rushing attempts. His run defense grade of 90.3 led the defense and he recorded two stops. 2 – Jaylen Watson, CB: 83.5 Watson played only 20 snaps before injuring his shoulder and exiting the game. The Rams defense had the Broncos bottled up until that point, and there was a clear drop off when his replacements came in. LA must cross their fingers that Watson doesn’t miss much time moving forward. 3 – Josh Wallace, CB: 78.7 Put the controversial defensive pass interference call aside, Josh Wallace was still stingy in coverage. He allowed a single catch on three targets for 27 yards and caught an interception on a pass disrupted by Kobie Turner. If Watson misses time, Wallace should be the next man up. 4 – Quentin Lake, DB: 78.4 Lake allowed three catches on four targets, but he minimized the damage in terms of yards with 15. He’s started the season off well and added another two pass break ups in this game. 5 – Byron Young, EDGE: 77.4 Young led the Rams with seven pressures. The next closest total was two and there were four players: Speights, Aaron Donald, Josaiah Stewart, and Braden Fiske. Kobie Turner and Tyler Davis each had one. That production isn’t good enough. All attention will be on slowing down Young while Myles Garrett is out. Someone else needs to step up. Other notes on defense It wasn’t the best night for Trent McDuffie, although he faced a tough matchup in Jaylen Waddle. McDuffie finished eighth in defensive grading and allowed two passes on five targets for 48 yards with a pass break up. Nate Landman earned a coverage grade of 62.9 but allowed a passing touchdown on his lone target.
author: JB Scott

title: Four down territory: Rams must dig out of 1-2 start
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are 1-2 after blowing a 16-0 halftime lead in a 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. The Rams controlled much of the first half before Denver rallied behind Bo Nix in the second half. Matthew Stafford threw two interceptions, including one returned for a touchdown, while costly […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 12: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts to an apparent leg injury during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are 1-2 after blowing a 16-0 halftime lead in a 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. The Rams controlled much of the first half before Denver rallied behind Bo Nix in the second half. Matthew Stafford threw two interceptions, including one returned for a touchdown, while costly penalties and special teams mistakes continued to haunt Los Angeles. The Broncos eventually took the lead on a late Nix touchdown run, leaving the Rams with another frustrating loss. Through three weeks, there are four important reflections on where this Rams team currently stands. 1. Injury Concern: Rams are great, but not elite without their stars There is no question that the Rams have enough talent to compete with anyone when their roster is healthy. The problem is that the margin for error becomes significantly smaller when their stars are unavailable. Puka Nacua missed his second consecutive game against Denver because of a hip/groin injury, while Myles Garrett remains on injured reserve following knee surgery. Garrett is guaranteed to miss at least four games, while Nacua was considered doubtful entering Sunday’s game. The injuries don’t stop with the stars. Colby Parkinson has been dealing with a knee injury, Terrance Ferguson has been battling an ankle issue, and Kamren Kinchens missed Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury. Jaylen Watson also joined the injury list after Sunday’s loss. Those players may not carry the same star power as Nacua or Garrett, but they are important complimentary pieces. The Rams can overcome one or two absences. As the list grows, however, the team’s margin for error shrinks. 2. Delay of Games & Penalties Yes, Bill Vinovich was a thorn to the Rams in this one. But the Rams also had a self-inflicted penalties. The Rams had two delay of games penalties that stalled the offense on more than one occasion. The Rams had almost as many penalties in Week 3 as they did combined in Weeks 1 & 2. 3. Run more, Pass less Sean McVay has developed a reputation for occasionally getting away from the running game, and Week 3 was another example. The Rams attempted 55 passes against Denver, while their running backs received considerably fewer opportunities. That approach is particularly questionable against a Broncos defense that has established itself as one of the league’s more difficult units to attack through the air. The Rams don’t need to abandon the passing game. Matthew Stafford is still the quarterback who gives this offense its highest ceiling. But there needs to be greater balance. Stafford’s two interceptions ultimately proved costly, including a pick-six that helped Denver erase Los Angeles’ early advantage. When playing a strong defense on the road, consistently putting the ball in the quarterback’s hands 55 times creates unnecessary opportunities for mistakes. The Rams need to lean on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum more consistently. Establish the run, stay ahead of the chains and force opposing defenses to respect the entire offense. 4. Special Teams: New Story, Same Result The Rams continue to find ways to hurt themselves on special teams. Against Denver, Emmanuel Forbes was flagged for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on special teams. It was another avoidable mistake that contributed to the larger problem: the Rams cannot continue giving opponents free yardage and additional opportunities. This isn’t necessarily about one player. It’s about a recurring problem. The Rams have enough talent to overcome an occasional mistake. But when penalties, turnovers and special teams miscues pile up in the same game, the margin disappears. And that is ultimately what makes the 1-2 start so frustrating. The Rams have shown enough through three weeks to believe they are capable of being a very good football team. But being very good isn’t enough if they can’t stay healthy, protect the football, establish the run and eliminate self-inflicted mistakes. At 1-2, the Rams don’t need to panic. They do, however, need to dig themselves out.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Sean McVay after Rams’ loss, “You sign up for all of it”
summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost a tight game to the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football by a final score of 30-26, and Sean McVay didn’t have much to say after the loss, other than to reflect, “You sign up for all of it.” Meaning the good times, and the bad. The wins and the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on from the sideline during the second quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams lost a tight game to the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football by a final score of 30-26 , and Sean McVay didn’t have much to say after the loss, other than to reflect, “You sign up for all of it.” Meaning the good times, and the bad. The wins and the losses. That’s sports. That’s life. You can watch the post-game interview(s) below, but no one waxed poetic at the podium. McVay says his piece about signing up for exactly what he signed up for, and he gives little updates on any injury or player. He credits the Broncos for finding a way, something the Rams didn’t do in Week 3. Said McVay after the loss about embracing the hard parts of the game while still loving his team: “It’s tough, you know what, but this is sports. You sign up for all of it, and…love our group…just came up short. Give the Broncos credit, they found a way to get it done. We’ll look at ourselves and figure out how we can improve.” There’s a bit more to chew on, though not much, if you watch the whole 6-minute video, but it was perhaps the shortest (or one of the shortest) post-game interviews McVay has given as a head coach. The Rams went from being up 16-0 at the half to losing. What is there to say? The good news for the Rams is they are 1-2 with 14 games left in the regular season. Their season is not over. The bad news is if the Rams continue to lose games, blow double digit leads (and or leads in general) while failing to defeat the best opponents in the NFL, their season will be over and quickly. The Rams get a chance to right their ship next week to rise to a .500 record four weeks into the season, or they’ll go deeper down the rabbit hole.
author: Danny Stone

title: 5 key plays that led to Rams’ collapse against Broncos
summary: The Los Angeles Rams appeared to have control of Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos, but a series of pivotal plays helped Denver rally for a 30-26 comeback victory. The Rams had opportunities to put the game away, but mistakes, a controversial penalty and two late interceptions ultimately swung the game toward Denver. Here are […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams appeared to have control of Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos, but a series of pivotal plays helped Denver rally for a 30-26 comeback victory . The Rams had opportunities to put the game away, but mistakes, a controversial penalty and two late interceptions ultimately swung the game toward Denver. Here are five plays that played a major role in the Broncos’ comeback. 1. Emmanuel Forbes’ Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalty on Special Teams With just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter, the Rams appeared to have created a favorable special-teams situation. Denver’s Kaden Katsis muffed the punt and recovered at the Broncos’ 15-yard line before being tackled at the nine. Broncos went from starting at their own 9 to starting at their 48 because of that Emmanuel Forbes Jr. penalty and Ethan Evans' poor punt. Special. Teams. Matter. — Cameron DaSilva (@camdasilva) September 28, 2026 However, Emmanuel Forbes was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct. The 13-yard penalty was enforced from the previous spot, moving the Rams back and forcing them to punt again from their own 12-yard line. The second punt traveled to the Denver 48, giving the Broncos much better field position. Instead of potentially pinning Denver deep after the muff, the penalty essentially gave the Broncos another opportunity with favorable field position. 2. Matthew Stafford Throws a Pick-Six The biggest swing came with 4:49 remaining. Leading 19-16, Matthew Stafford and the Rams had a chance to grab more momentum after a poor third quarter showing. Instead, Stafford attempted a short pass toward Kyren Williams that was intercepted by Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga. Hufanga did not simply stop the drive. He returned the interception 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver a 23-19 lead after the extra point. The turnover was a huge momentum shift and injected life throughout the Broncos sideline and fanbase. 3. Bo Nix Finds Pat Bryant for 39 Yards on 2nd-and-20 Denver’s offense delivered a huge conversion on its game-tying drive. With 3:26 remaining and facing second-and-20 from the Denver 25, Bo Nix connected with Pat Bryant for 39 yards. Bryant took the pass all the way to the Los Angeles 36, flipping the field and keeping the Broncos’ comeback hopes alive. The play was particularly damaging because the Rams had Denver facing a long-yardage situation. Instead of forcing a punt or another difficult third-down attempt, Nix found Bryant for a chunk gain that put Denver deep into Rams territory. 4. Controversial DPI Call on Josh Wallace A few plays later, the Rams appeared to come up with a potential stop. On third-and-6 from the Los Angeles 11-yard line with 1:15 remaining, Nix’s pass intended for Bryant fell incomplete. Josh Wallace was flagged for defensive pass interference, however, giving Denver four yards and an automatic first down. NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay did not believe Rams CB Josh Wallace should have been flagged for pass interference, in what may have otherwise been an interception. The Broncos went on to score what would serve as the game-winning TD. pic.twitter.com/A0YDJ8ZmZl — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 28, 2026 The call was a clear miss. Not only was it an interception by Josh Wallace but replay showed that it was actually offensive pass interference (if anything) on Pat Bryant. Bill Vinovich strikes again… From there, the Broncos were able to run additional clock and get the go-ahead score. 5. Stafford’s Final Pass Picked Off The Rams still had one final opportunity. After Stafford connected with Konata Mumpfield for a 48-yard touchdown with 3:38 remaining, Los Angeles cut Denver’s lead to 23-22. The Rams then needed one more defensive stop and a chance to complete the comeback themselves. That opportunity came late, but Stafford’s final pass was intercepted by Hufanga, who had already delivered the pick-six earlier in the fourth quarter. The turnover ended the Rams’ final possession and secured Denver’s comeback victory. For the Rams, the loss wasn’t determined by one play. The Forbes penalty, Stafford’s pick-six, Bryant’s 39-yard catch, the Wallace DPI and the final interception collectively created the sequence that allowed Denver to erase a late deficit and escape with a four-point victory.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams Winners & Losers: Broncos expose L.A.’s flaws
summary: A lot went right for the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night. They took a commanding 16-0 lead over the Denver Broncos and by the end of the game outgained Denver 482 yards to 257. But the scoreboard doesn’t lie. It’s the only stat that matters when the clock reaches zero. The Rams fell to […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Jaylen Watson #35 of the Los Angeles Rams leaves the field with an apparent injury during the second quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images A lot went right for the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night. They took a commanding 16-0 lead over the Denver Broncos and by the end of the game outgained Denver 482 yards to 257. But the scoreboard doesn’t lie. It’s the only stat that matters when the clock reaches zero. The Rams fell to the Broncos 26-30 and they are now 1-2 on the season. Things are as bad as they seem. We can look for silver linings and understand that Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett are coming back at some point . Sunday night’s loss was still symbolic of the early season struggles so far. The Rams may not be who we expected them to be, and there continue to be signs to suggest that. For example, corner Jaylen Watson and tight end Terrance Ferguson joined Nacua and Garrett on the injury list. Their respective sides of the ball looked drastically different without them in the lineup. In the second half we saw the Melbourne Rams. The defense couldn’t get off the field. Matthew Stafford and the offense had very little working until a little-too-late comeback attempt. Which individual efforts are responsible for the heartbreaking loss? Winners Kyren Williams, RB With six receptions for 70 yards, this was one of Kyren Williams’ most productive receiving outings in his career. He was an important contributor on the last-minute comeback attempt. Pass catching is a positive element Williams has added to his repertoire and it has been on display in recent weeks. While there were talks of Blake Corum possibly passing Williams on the depth chart last week, Williams made his understudy obsolete on Sunday night. Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards (5.9 average). He was the one consistent part of the offense against the Broncos. Kyren Williams gets loose for 31 yards! @LARvsDEN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1YLoydl5y8 — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 Davante Adams, WR I had written off the idea that Davante Adams would contribute in a meaningful way in Denver. He was matched up against the best corner in the NFL, Patrick Surtain, and still found a way to get open. Adams hauled in seven of 13 targets for 137 yards. Most of his damage was done against Surtain. How can you not feel encouraged about Adams moving forward? He still has it. Another 22-yard gain for Devante Adams @LARvsDEN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wZUcgXvIDz — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 Kobie Turner, DT Without Garrett, the Rams need someone to take a leadership role on the defense and make a play in the game’s biggest moments. Against the Broncos, that person was Kobie Turner. Turner hit Bo Nix’s arm to force an interception caught by Josh Wallace. This came in the second half when Denver was roaring back and the Rams had little going offensively. The takeaway helped LA regain the lead, although it was a matter of time before it was surrendered. Kobie Turner tips the pass and Josh Wallace comes down with the INT! Since 2023, Turner has forced 154 pressures, the 4th-most among DTs @LARvsDEN on NBC/Peacock Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UZpomdko6M — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) September 28, 2026 Tyler Higbee, TE Colby Parkinson was questionable for the game. He suited up but didn’t participate as a focal point. Terrance Ferguson, who we will get to, left with an injury in the first quarter. The Rams are fortunate they can turn to a backup as capable as Tyler Higbee, especially when he’s considered third or fourth string at this point. The veteran caught eight of 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown. Stafford to Higbee for the TD! @LARvsDEN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/APIN1HPzEm — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 Harrison Mevis, K Mevis made all four of his field goals from 36, 35, 40, and 48 plus two extra points. It’s not his fault that he was so busy, but it’s not a positive that LA settled for four kicks. At least when the team settled for three, Mevis was effectively automatic. Losers Matthew Stafford, QB Stafford completed 30 of 55 passes (55%) for 390 yards, two scores, and two interceptions. The first half was volume. The second half was Talanoa Hufanga. And while the numbers were stellar in the first half, Stafford wasn’t exactly perfect. The Rams offense settled for field goals instead of taking care of business in the opposition’s territory. Stafford threw an interceptable pass just before halftime that could have dramatically shifted momentum. And yes, the comeback attempt was impressive. Stafford and the Rams were up against a high degree of difficulty. Still, you don’t get credit for setting the house on fire and putting it out. Stafford came alive too late into the fourth quarter. He needed to play at that level earlier. Simply put, Stafford has taken a significant step back from his play last year. He hasn’t been good enough through three games. Part of that is a reduced cast of pass catchers. But you don’t pay your quarterback top dollar only to make excuses for him. Stafford must be better. And soon. HUFANGA PICK-6! DENVER IS LOUD! @LARvsDEN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/53CZ9kkDpf — NFL (@NFL) September 28, 2026 Terrance Ferguson, TE Following an encouraging but far from perfect breakout performance on Monday Night Football last week, Sunday night’s game in Denver was setup perfectly for a “star is born” opportunity. It wasn’t entirely Ferguson’s fault for that not to come to fruition. He has recently battled an ankle injury that he re-aggravated in the first quarter and then did not return. It’s mostly frustrating that Ferguson should have been a major part of the Rams offense without Nacua. It was the perfect opening for him to step up. While Higbee was productive in relief, I can only assume the offense would have been better off if all of Higbee’s 11 targets instead went to the more athletic and potent pass catcher in Ferguson. We are still awaiting Ferguson’s coming out party. Emmanuel Forbes & Josh Wallace, CB The Rams spent all offseason adding talent on the defensive side of the ball. The Broncos won the game largely because they were able to take advantage of Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace. Why were they on the field? Well, part of it is because someone must play outside if Trent McDuffie shifts to the slot. The primary reason was that Jaylen Watson suffered a shoulder injury. And most Rams fans didn’t feel that positive about Watson’s start to his career in LA. We should appreciate him more after seeing the alternatives in his place. Forbes and Wallace were major steps down in performance. This should have been a game sealing interception for the Rams Instead, it’s pass interference. Another BRUTAL mistake by the refs this week. pic.twitter.com/FBEGfVHUZV — JPA (@jasrifootball) September 28, 2026 Blake Corum, RB LA didn’t really need Corum in this game. Wuilliams handled the running back duties well. But usually Corum is good for an injection of energy into the offense. They desperately needed that in the second half. It never came. Corum finished with just 15 yards on six carries (2.5 average) and he managed zero yards on two catches. The running game works best when both Williams and Corum are contributing consistently. Penalties & undisciplined football The Broncos kept penalties to a minimum at five flags for 38 yards. Denver gained four first downs because of penalties. The Rams were not so fortunate and drew 13 penalties for 91 yards. You won’t win many games asking your quarterback to throw 55 passes as Stafford did. This was not a game script that favored the Rams nor is it how they want to play. Penalties played a major role for both teams, usually with the Rams in the crosshairs.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams vs. Broncos final score: Refs fall for Denver’s II act
summary: The Los Angeles Rams blew a 16-point first half lead to the Denver Broncos and lost 30-26 on Sunday Night Football to drop their record to 1-2. The story could have been a fair game fought between two quality teams, but instead the attention should be on a phantom pass interference penalty against the Rams […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams blew a 16-point first half lead to the Denver Broncos and lost 30-26 on Sunday Night Football to drop their record to 1-2. The story could have been a fair game fought between two quality teams, but instead the attention should be on a phantom pass interference penalty against the Rams that ultimately cost them the win. And I thought all the actors were in L.A., but apparently some of them are in Denver too. Broncos receiver Pat Bryant II pulled off an incredible acting performance to draw a critical pass interference penalty against Josh Wallace that wiped off Wallace’s incredible interception that would have probably iced the game late in the fourth quarter. The penalty also gave Denver a first down when they were down 26-23 with barely over a minute left on the clock. Josh Wallace Was Called For Defensive Pass Interference On This Play. He Ended Up Picking This Ball Off, So It Turned Into A HUGE Play. I Don’t Know, Man… This One Is CLOSE. 👀 pic.twitter.com/DRYEAm8cYN — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) September 28, 2026 A few plays later, on third down, Quentin Lake was called for a soft “hands to the face” penalty against Evan Engram that gave the Broncos yet another first down with a minute left. Nix appeared to punch it in two players later to give Denver a 30-26 lead, but on review the call was overturned and setup third-and-Goal with :48 seconds left. Still, Nix punched it on the next play to give the Broncos the 30-26 lead. The Rams made a valiant effort to win, driving the field to set up a single last shot into the end zone, but Talanoa Hufanga intercepted Matthew Stafford for the second time of the night. It was a poetic ending to an up-and-down night for Stafford. Up when he appeared to put the Rams in position to win with a 48-yard touchdown to Konata Mumpfield. That gave the Rams a 26-23 lead with just under 4 minutes remaining. HOW DID MUMPFIELD GET THAT OPEN 🤯 pic.twitter.com/bERrMjdpIv — DraftKings (@DraftKings) September 28, 2026 Down when he threw his two interceptions to Hufanga. Stafford was inconsistent throughout the night and finished 30-of-55 for 390 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Both interceptions were extremely costly, including a pick-six and a game-ender. The Rams may need Puka Nacua more than Nacua needs the Rams. Broncos outscored Rams 30-10 in second half The game doesn’t go in the Rams’ favor, but will be one of the highlights of the NFL season as a whole. The Rams took a 16-0 lead into halftime, holding the Broncos to 67 total yards and five first downs in the first half. Conversely, L.A. had 17 first downs and 253 yards in the first half. But the tide turned in the third quarter, as the Rams’ first two drives of the second half went for a combined -6 yards and resulted in punts, both times resulting in bad special teams plays by L.A. that gave Denver the ball at midfield. The Broncos scored 16 unanswered points in the third quarter — two touchdowns, two two-point conversions — including a pair of touchdown passes by Bo Nix. Nix also converted both two-point conversions with his arm. This goal line double move by Jaylen Waddle 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/DR9zP4wGBJ — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 28, 2026 In the fourth quarter, Kobie Turner hit Nix as he was attempting a pass and the ball fluttered into the arms of Josh Wallace for an interception. The Rams were unable to capitalize with a touchdown drive, but Harrison Mevis connected on a 48-yard field goal to give L.A. a 19-16 lead in the middle of the fourth quarter. But then the wheels came off minutes later, as Hufanga picked off Stafford and returned it 66 yards for a touchdown, giving the Broncos a 23-19 lead with 4:49 to go. MATTHEW STAFFORD PICK-SIX AND THE BRONCOS TAKE THE LEAD! Mike Tirico has the Rams-Broncos SNF call for NBC. 🏈🔥🎙️ #NFL pic.twitter.com/SG37CLr9x6 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 28, 2026 Stafford struggled on deep passes for most of the night, clearly missing his favorite target Puka Nacua, and obviously not on the same page with anybody except for Davante Adams. Mumpfield did step up, and so did Tyler Higbee on a huge sideline catch on the final drive, but it was too little and too late. The Rams settled for three field goals in the second quarter, when they should have scored touchdowns. Then they were completely shut out in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, L.A.’s first drive was another dud, and then coming off of a Nix interception, they settled for another field goal. Many of Stafford’s passing yards were fruitless, empty yards. The Rams needed touchdowns, they settled for kicks. Sean McVay won’t be happy with the refs, but many of the problems have to be found by looking within. This is a team that is desperate for better options when Puka is out. The Rams simply left too much out on the field.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: We’re witnessing a different breed of Raiders as team drops Saints 35-27
summary: How easy would it have been for the Silver & Black to wilt after the opposition not only scored a touchdown to take the lead, but recovered the fumble on the ensuing kick off, and two plays later, made another end zone visit. But Klint Kubiak, his coaching staff, and players apparently don’t like to […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images How easy would it have been for the Silver & Black to wilt after the opposition not only scored a touchdown to take the lead, but recovered the fumble on the ensuing kick off, and two plays later, made another end zone visit. But Klint Kubiak, his coaching staff, and players apparently don’t like to do things “easy”. For the third straight game on the young 2026 season, Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders stared down adversity in the face, smirked, got the job done. This time, it was on the road against the New Orleans Saints, and instead of succumbing to quick-sand situations the Raiders were well-accustomed to do in year’s past, Las Vegas answered the ball, rose to the occasion, and earned an impressive 35-27 victory. Once more we saw complementary Raiders football where the defense picked up the offense and vice versa, despite special teams gaffes. Instead of collapsing under the immense pressure — on the road against a quailty New Orleans squad, Las Vegas persevered and won. The performances and results harken on the old adage: Once is an accident, twice is a coincidence, three times is a pattern. The first time the Raiders showcased resolve to win in the season opener against the Miami Dolphins was eyebrow raising. The second time they did it by beating the Los Angeles Chargers piqued interest. Doing it for the third time at New Orleans certainly firmly establishes a pattern. And it harkens on this: We’re witnessing a different breed of Silver & Black with Kubiak at the helm. RAIDERS FORCE ANOTHER FUMBLE AND CALL GAME ‼️ pic.twitter.com/oGMruwoPuT — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 After trading touchdowns in the second quarter to knot the score at 13, Las Vegas moved the ball into the red zone during a two-minute drill and hit a field goal to take a 16-13 lead into halftime. The potential double-dip was thwarted, however, as the Raiders did receive the second-half kick off only to go three-and-out. And this began the downward spiral for the Silver & Black. Kellen Moore’s Saints offense went on an impressive 12-play, 87-yard touchdown drive that chewed 6:50 off the clock. And with 20-16 lead in hand, New Orleans scooped up in inexplicable fumble by Las Vegas running back and kick return man Dylan Laube. Like noted above, two plays and 32 yards later, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough found tight end Noah Fant for a 16-yard touchdown, 27-16 New Orleans. Instead of wallowing in the series of unfortunate events, however, Kubiak’s offense ran five plays culminating in rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. finding daylight and immolating New Orleans defense on a 36-yard touchdown run. Trailing just 27-22 after the two teams traded punts to close the third quarter, the Saints went on a spiral of their own. As our Matt Holder noted shortly after the game, all four of the Saints’ possessions in the fourth quarter ended in turnovers . That great equalizer gave the Raiders ample runway for two final stanza touchdowns — a four-yard touchdown strike from quarterback Kirk Cousins to wide receiver Cody White and four-yard dime from Cousins to tight end Brock Bowers, 35-27 Las Vegas. Brock Bowers came back and immediately looked like Brock Bowers again. 10 REC, 116 REC YDS, 1 TD vs Saints Can Bowers help push the Raiders into the playoffs? https://t.co/cvv8di0xYV pic.twitter.com/uNetudtQdk — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 27, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Rob Leonard’s Raiders defense took the ball away from the Saints: —Cousins went 22 of 33 for 248 yards with three touchdowns , no interceptions, while getting sacked three times against the Saints. The veteran quarterback has thrown three touchdown passes in the first trio of games validating Kubiak’s decision to roll with the 38-year-old signal caller over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. —“Brock-tober Fest” arrived early as Bowers’ had an outstanding season debut with 10 catches for 116 yards and one touchdown. The tight end lined up all over the formation from traditional in-line and split tight end and even in the slot and perimeter that’s normally reserved for a wide receiver. —Raiders starting running back Ashton Jeanty carried the rock 19 times for 56 yards and a paltry 2.9 yards per carry average. One has to wonder if his ankle is 100 percent but Washington provided juice of his own with five carries for 54 yards including the scintillating touchdown. —Linebacker Nakobe Dean is proving the Raiders wise for giving him a big-money deal in free agency as the veteran paced the team with 12 total tackles, a stop for loss, and a forced fumble to slam the door on the Saints collective faces. This after he forced a key fumble to help Las Vegas win last week. —Leonard’s defense forced four turnovers from the Saints. A trio were forced fumbles — two on sacks; one from defensive end Malcolm Koonce and the other from strong safety Jeremy Chinn — and the other an interception by rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses (his third pick on the young season). Fair to say Raiders LB Nakobe Dean has been a good signing 27 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 3 FF & 3 Wins pic.twitter.com/uJWmuVzp24 https://t.co/zPO8QG05Su — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) September 27, 2026 —Getting rookie safety Treydan Stukes back in the Raiders secondary can’t happen soon enough. Inactive due to a concussion sustained in Week 2, veteran Isaiah Pola-Mao got the start and the Saints picked on him frequently as he was charted giving up three of Shough’s four touchdown passes. Quotes of Note “When I hit him, I saw the ball come up. I thought the ball was going forward so I just assumed it was a strip sack. It was very rewarding. We knew whole time (in) the second half, we knew the defense was going to have to show up.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Malcolm Koonce on his forced fumble “We knew we had to rally back, we had to start back playing our type of football. And that’s our style of play, taking the ball away. We got a goal every week, ‘How many takeaways are we going to get?’ We had none in the first half, so we had to come back in the second half strong.” —Las Vegas Raiders middle linebacker Nakobe Dean on defense’s mentality Up Next It’s a battle of AFC West unbeatens next Sunday when the Raiders (3-0) host the unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) who picked up their first road win of the season with a 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday. Powered by Patrick Mahomes efficient afternoon and running back Kenneth Walker III’s two-touchdown outing (one rushing, another receiving) the Chiefs sit atop the division alongside the Raiders. It’s an AFC West that features Kansas City and Las Vegas on top, the Denver Broncos at 2-1 and the Los Angeles Chargers at 0-3.

title: Klink Kubiak’s culture change fuels Las Vegas Raiders’ 4th-quarter comeback against New Orleans Saints
summary: For the second week in a row, the Las Vegas Raiders won a game that they typically would have lost in past years with their Week 3 35-27 victory over the New Orleans Saints. The Raiders started the second half about as poorly as they could, going three-and-out and fumbling a kickoff return to fall […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Las Vegas Raiders won a game that they typically would have lost in past years with their Week 3 35-27 victory over the New Orleans Saints . The Raiders started the second half about as poorly as they could, going three-and-out and fumbling a kickoff return to fall behind by two possessions with a little more than 20 minutes of game time left. The Saints had all of the momentum, signalling a classic loss that Las Vegas has come accustomed to under the previous regimes. However, new head coach Klint Kubiak has changed the culture, and the Silver and Black never stopped fighting or gave in. The Raiders defense certainly didn’t have its best performance, giving up a season-high 27 points. But when it mattered most in the fourth quarter, the unit managed to create a turnover on every drive the Saints had with three fumbles and an interception during the final frame. On top of that, Kubiak engineered two touchdown drives to play complementary football. That puts the Silver and Black at a perfect 3-0 heading into October, making the culture change feel tangible. The vibes are high in Sin City, leading us into the internet’s reaction to the hot start. There’s a much different tune in the locker room compared to this point in the season last year. title: Raiders-Saints: 17 things we learned
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are a quality football team. It’s true. They are. They are doing what winning teams do. They fight through adversity and they make the big plays when needed. They are not perfect. but they have been the best team on the field in all three games. Yes, their three opponents are […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are a quality football team. It’s true. They are. They are doing what winning teams do. They fight through adversity and they make the big plays when needed. They are not perfect. but they have been the best team on the field in all three games. Yes, their three opponents are a combined 1-8 to start the season, but the Raiders made the plays at the right time. That’s what winning teams do. That are Klint Kubiak’s team is a winning team. And it’s quite fun. Las Vegas is 3-0 for the third time since 1991 and teams that start 3-0 have a 73 percent chance of making the playoffs. They have already equaled their win total from last season. The Raiders, who have been underdogs the past two games, are one of three 3-0 teams in the AFC, joining the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs, who they both play next month. The Raiders scored more than 30 points in their 35-27 win at the New Orleans Saints on Sunday for the first team since 2023. The defense had four more turnovers. They scored 19 unanswered points to win the game. This wild stuff. Here is a look at all the madness: Cousins is balling: Raiders’ quarterback Kirk Cousins was so efficient again. He has thrown three touchdown passes in all three games and he is a big reason why this team is 3-0. He is really been impressive and he is buying Fernando Mendoza more time to develop. Welcome back, Brock: Raiders’ star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut after missing two games with a knee injury. He was his brilliant self as he had 10 catches for 116 yards and s core. He is going to be so special in Kubiak’s offense. He had three catches on the first drive of the game. Kubiak couldn’t wait to get his new toy involved. Turnover machine: The Raiders forced four turnovers and have nine this season. They have had multiple turnovers in all three games. Nakobe Dean, who has been a great free-agent addition, sealed the game with a forced fumble for the second straight game. Mayer contributes as well: The Raiders used double tight ends often and Michael Mayer had three catches for 32 yards and a score. He and Bowers can do a lot of damage together. Koonce stops up: The Raiders’ pass-rush was quiet for most of the game. but rotational rusher Malcolm Koonce came alive late and had a forced sack and made some plays. Hello Mike Washington Jr.: The rookie running back flashed his big-time speed with a 36-yard touchdown run as the Raiders began their comeback in the third quarter. He had five carries for 54 yards. He has 15 carries this season. If he can provide this type of spark on a regular basis, the Raiders will be in business. Bring on the Chiefs: The Raiders-Chiefs game will be one of the very biggest in Week 4 and it will get a lot of attention as these two 3-0 teams battle. It will be the biggest game at Allegiant Stadium since the Week 18 against the Chargers to end the 2021 season. Chiefs fans have rountiely taken over Allegiant Stadium. That can’t happen this week. Jeanty quiet again: Starting running back Ashton Jeanty had 56 yards on 19 carries (we averaged less than three yards a carry) and had three cathces for 37 yards. After a big Week 1, Jeanty hasn’t made a huge impact. Raiders win kicking battle: Matt Gay made all three of his field-goal attempt. Daniel Carlson, who Gay replaced, missed an extra point in this kicking battle. Third-down defense needs to improve: The Saints converted on third down nine of 15 times. It’s something the Raiders need to work on this week. Masses is the starter: Rookie cornerback Zeke Masses started for the second straight week. But this time, Darien Porter, the Week 1 starter, was healthy. He missed last week with a foot injury. Masses, a fifth-round draft pick, responded by having two interceptions and winning the AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. Now, he is a true starter. Masses gave up some plays to Saints’ standout wide receiver Chris Olave but made a huge play, intercepting Tyler Shough in the fourth quarter for his third pick in two weeks. White should get the call up: Wide receiver Jack Bech suffered a forearm injury and NFL Media reported he will go on the injured reserve with a chance of playing later this season. The Raiders will likely promote receiver Cody White from the practice squad. He had a another touchdown catch Sunday and has three in the past two games. He has been elevated all three games and can’t play a again unless he is promoted to the 53-man roster. Pola-Mao struggles: The Saints attacked safety Isaiah Pola-Mao as he gave up two touchdown in coverage in the first half. He is playing with rookie starter Tredyan Stukes out with a concussion. Stukes may have a chance to return next week against the Chiefs Big breaks: The Saints stopped the Raiders on third down twice in a row in the red zone in the second quarter, but they were called for penalties twice. The Raiders made them pay as Cousins hit Mayer for a three-yard touchdown pass to give Las Vegas a 13-6 lead with 5:46 to go in the quarter. First-half success: The Raiders have led at halftime in all three games this season. According to the Raiders, it’s the first time they has happened since the team moved to Las Vegas in 2020. Good start for D again: The Raiders forced a three-and-out on the first drive of the game. Las Vegas opponents have not scored on its opening drive in six straight games dating back to last year. It’s the second longest current streak in the NFL. Something new for Saints: New Orleans led 6-3 after the first quarter. It was its first lead going into the second quarter since December, 2024.

The Raiders did block the extra point attempt by former Las Vegas kicker Daniel Carlson. It was a 13-yard, 79-yard drive. The Saints converted all four of their third-down plays on that drive. Second quarter: . The Raiders moved the ball but had to settle for a Matt gay 37-yard field goal to tie the game at 6-6. Gay is winning the kicking battle s0 far. The Saints committed penalties on back-to-back third downs in the red zone to give the Raiders more opportunities and it bit them. Kirk Cousins hit tight end Michael Mayer for a three-yard touchdown pass to give Las Vegas a 13-6 lead with 5:46 to go in the quarter. The Saints came back on a touchdown pass from Shough to Noah Fant. It is tied at 13-13 with 1:54 to go in the first half. The Saints are 6 for 8 on third down. The Raiders went down the field quickly, but they had to settle for a third Gay field goal to take a16-13 lead at the half. The Raiders made it to the red zone and scored in all four of the possessions in the first half. Third quarter: The Raiders were forced to punt for the first time as they opened the second half with a three and out. The Saints went 87 yards on 12 plays to take a 20-16 lead with 6:40 to go in the third quarter. Dylan Laube lost a fumble on the ensuing kickoff at the Raiders’ 32-yard line. The Saints quickly cashed in scoring twice in less than a minute as Shough threw his fourth touchdown pass of he day to make it a 27-16 game. Raiders’ rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. showed his explosiion with 36-yard touchdown run, but the Raiders missed the two-point conversion. They trail 27-22 with 2:48 to go in the quarter. Fourth quarter: Malcolm Koonce forced a fumble on a sack and Maxx Crosby recovered at the Raiders’ 45 with 12:55 to go. This is their shot. The Raiders cruised down the field as Cousins hit Cody White for his third touchdown in two weeks. The two-point conversion was no good. The Raiders lead 28-27 with 9:21 remaining. Wow, Zeke Massses picked off Tyler Shough and got the ball into the red zone/ The Cousins hit Bowers for a touchdown, The Raiders have scored 19 unanswered points and lead 35-27 with just more than six minutes to go. The Raiders forced yet another turnover see a win. Final score: Raiders 35, Saints 27 Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-0. The New Orleans Saints are 1-2. What the win means for the Raiders: Wow, the Raiders are 3-0 for the third time since 1991 and first time since 2021. Teams that start 3-0 have a73 percent chance to make the playoffs. This is real folks. Turning point of the game: The Raiders were down by 11 points in the third quarter, but the defense forced one turnover after another and the Raiders scored 19 unanswered points to take the win. Injury report: Raiders’ wide receiver Jack Bech left the game with a forearm injury . Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson was banged up late in the game witha groin injury and Caleb Rogers spelled him. NFL Media reported Sunday afternoon Bech will go on the injured reserve with a chance to return later this season. Perhaps the Raiders could promote receiver Cody White from the practice squad. He has been elevated all three games and can’t playa again unless he is promoted to the 53-man roster. After the game, Kubiak said Bech fractured his forearm.

title: Raiders-Saints inactives: Brock Bowers will play
summary: As expected, Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers is active and he will make his 2026 regular-season debut Sunday at the New Orleans Saints. He was listed as questionable on the injury report Friday. He didn’t practice Friday, but he was limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said […]
full_text: (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images As expected, Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers is active and he will make his 2026 regular-season debut Sunday at the New Orleans Saints. He was listed as questionable on the injury report Friday. He didn’t practice Friday, but he was limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday keeping Bowers out of practice Friday was part of the team’s plan and he said he is optimistic Bowers will play Sunday. Bowers missed the first two games of the season, both Raiders’ victories, after having knee surgery 19 days ago. Meanwhile, starting defensive end Kwity Paye is active as well. He was questionable after being out Thursday with an illness and being limited Friday. Rookie starting safety Treydan Stukes has been in the concussion protocol all week and he is out Sunday. Isaiah Pola-Mao, who Stukes beat out in training camp, is in line to start. Number three quarterback Aidan O’Connell is out Sunday . He announced his father has died and he has been away from the team since Sept. 17 Here are the Raiders’ other inactive players Sunday: Inactives for #LVvsNO pic.twitter.com/kpScxZLlag — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) September 27, 2026 There’s no surprises on this list.
