title: Miami Dolphins excluded from the NFL Coat of Arms
summary: I watched yesterday’s game where the Miami Dolphins fell to the KC Chiefs 10-10 and the NFL referees 14-0. The combined score was KC/NFL Refs 24 – Miami/out of favors 10.  I can’t even talk about the Dolphins performance until I unpack the completed slanted officiating. Unless the “anointed team” completely no shows, the refs […]
full_text: OTTAWA, CANADA MARCH 8:The official seal of the United States is displayed outside the U.S. Embassy, in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, on March 8, 2025. (Photo by Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images I watched yesterday’s game where the Miami Dolphins fell to the KC Chiefs 10-10 and the NFL referees 14-0. The combined score was KC/NFL Refs 24 – Miami/out of favors 10. I can’t even talk about the Dolphins performance until I unpack the completed slanted officiating. Unless the “anointed team” completely no shows, the refs in every sport will put their hoofs on the scales of justice to benefit whatever team is anointed. I remember the Heat beating the Chicago Bulls in Jordan’s heyday at the old Miami Arena. I was in attendance. Steffi Graf, Jack Nickalus, Cal Ripken, Jr. and I think Ferdie Pacheco were also there to watch the GOAT. However, Rex Champman hit like 7 or 8 3-pointers and the Heat beat down the Bulls. If the game would’ve been closer, the refs would have carried the Bulls over the finish line as they usually did for MJ. We saw this in full effect today. The NFL officiating is the biggest embarrassment in the history of the American experience. There is no attempt to improve it. It really makes you think that the NFL decides who will win each game before the season begins in some type of Star Chamber (check out this Michael Douglas movie if you can). In the olden days in England, powerful folks would meet outside at night under the stars to decide the guilt or innocence of some individual and then they would carry out the sentence(hence the term Star Chamber). It makes you think the powers that be have money on the game. I could literally write a hundred pages on how many garbage calls have went against the Dolphins over the last 40 years. I know other teams get screwed too but our pendulum is stuck to the bad. Many of these calls are simply inexplicable. And if you complain, the NFL punishes you. I still do not understand how the NFL gets aways with this, KNOWING they have an anti-trust exemption from the U.S. government. In what other American endeavor outside of sports can a member of that organization NOT criticize a corporation publicly? If I worked at Acme and criticized them, yes they would fire me and rightfully so and I can go public if I have evidence of their wrong doing However, again Acme does not have an anti-trust exemption or at least that is what the Coyote told me 😊. There is NOTHING less American than the NFL stifling free speech. The NFL practices in gross negligence and then has the buffoonish broadcasters and their “so called officiating expert” Gene Steratore come out and bless every single call. For those of you who don’t know, Steratore was the absolute buffoon moron who screwed the Dolphins against the Steelers in Miami (2010, I think) where the Steelers fumbled the ball in the end zone, THE FINS RECOVERED THE DAMN BALL, and this complete moron said there wasn’t a clear recovery and gave the ball back to the Steelers. It turns out this guy grew up in Pittsburgh and was allowed to ref an NFL with the Steelers. How in the name of God can this happen? So, this is the buffoon who was asked about the sissy roughing the passer call against Chop Robinson? This was a total garbage call because what was Chop supposed to do, sack Mahomes and use his “Homelander” super powers to fly away at the last nano-second? Momentum and gravity made Chop land on Mahomes, not intent. But Mahomes is the anointed one by the NFL, just like Brady was. It you launch an “air biscuit” against Brady or Mahomes it is an automatic 15-yard penalty. They cannot be touched. Period. So Steratore weighed in on that one but where was Steratore when Malik’s helmet was pulled off? Nowhere to be found. Where was Steratore when the player pulled Achane’s facemask on the play where he was hurt? Nowhere to be found. The NFL officiating cannot be criticized and it NEVER makes a mistake. In the legal world, attorneys must avoid EVEN the appearance of impropriety. Not the NFL. In my many travels to London, I noticed many stores (usually the elite ones like Harrod’s) have these shields up on the top corner of the store entrances. I asked what those were and I was told there was an official process to apply for the shield. These shields let the general public know that this business is preferred by the royal family; I just read that they had to be updated for the transition to King Charles. So I want to figure out how the Dolphins can earn the NFL preferred shield? Do we need to run ads with Malik’s and Devon’s shirts off? Maybe Jacob Rodriguez can appear on the cover of Men’s Fitness magazine with his shirt off? I am wide open to suggestions. Maybe I will reach out to King Charles?

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week three loss
summary: The Miami Dolphins showed signs of life against the Kansas City Chiefs — keeping the deficit to just one score until a late touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to Travis Kelce sealed their fate. Unfortunately, “keeping it close” doesn’t amount to a hill of beans in the win/loss column. However, like head coach Jeff Hafley […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Chris Bell #18 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before the NFL game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins showed signs of life against the Kansas City Chiefs — keeping the deficit to just one score until a late touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to Travis Kelce sealed their fate. Unfortunately, “keeping it close” doesn’t amount to a hill of beans in the win/loss column. However, like head coach Jeff Hafley has preached since he took the job in Miami, this year isn’t necessarily about winning or losing — it’s about showing growth, building a solid foundation and getting better every time the team takes the field. I believe they did that against the Chiefs. So, whose stock is up and whose stock is down after week three’s loss to Kansas City? FINS UP Our Fins Up player from Miami’s week three loss is rookie receiver Chris Bell. Fellow standout rookie Caleb Douglas sat out this week’s game due to an ankle injury, giving Bell an opportunity to shine. He did just that — nabbing four receptions for a team leading 67 yards receiving — nearly 1/3 of quarterback Malik Willis’ 210 yards passing. Bell’s quick return to action following a late-season ACL tear last November while playing in college at Louisville is nothing short of astounding. He’s shown flashes of the player who was talked about as a late first-round selection in the 2026 NFL Draft prior to his knee injury, and as he continues to work his way back to full strength, the Dolphins will continue to benefit from his solid play. I don’t think we’re too far away from Bell’s first touchdown grab as a member of the Miami Dolphins. Can he find paydirt this weekend against the Minnesota Vikings? Stay tuned! FINS DOWN Through no fault of his own, running back De’Von Achane earns this week’s Fins Down designation. On just his third carry of the game against Kansas City, Miami’s electric running back went down with a seemingly innocuous knee injury. Unfortunately, it was anything but. Achane wouldn’t return to the game — further hampering Miami’s already wounded rushing attack. The Dolphins would amass just 46 yards rushing from players not named Achane or Malik Willis for the rest of the tilt against the Chiefs. Following the loss, Hafley said the early outlooks regarding Achane’s knee “ do not sound very optimistic. ” Those are not the words any Dolphins’ fan wants to hear when it comes to the team’s most dangerous weapon.
author: Marek Brave

title: De’Von Achane injury: What free agents are available for Miami Dolphins?
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost running back De’Von Achane to a torn ACL on Sunday, ending the season for the team’s top rusher and a 2025 Pro Bowl selection. Miami currently has two running backs, Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II, on the 53-man roster, with Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., on the practice squad. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Kareem Hunt #29 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up before the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Kansas City Chiefs 14-12. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost running back De’Von Achane to a torn ACL on Sunday, ending the season for the team’s top rusher and a 2025 Pro Bowl selection. Miami currently has two running backs, Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II, on the 53-man roster, with Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., on the practice squad. Miami could look to move forward with that group, but they could also look to add a veteran free agent. But who is available? Miami is not going to break the bank to sign someone, but they could look to add a veteran on a minimum deal, making sure they have the depth needed to get through the season. The Dolphins’ running game is the focal point of the offensive system, and they are going to need increased depth at the position without Achane. Kareem Hunt The former Kansas City Chiefs running back was a Pro Bowl selection in 2017 as a rookie when he led the league in rushing yards. He finished last year with 163 carriers for 611 yards and eight touchdowns. He is not a direct replacement for Achane, but could provide another power option with Gordon, serving as a compliment to Wright’s speed. He would not be a workload carrying running back at this point in his career, but he could be a good veteran rotation guy who can handle 10 carries a game. Raheem Mostert Could Miami bring back former Dolphins runner Mostert to solidify the group? Mostert has bounced around the league throughout much of his career, but had extended periods with the San Francisco 49ers (2016-2021) and Miami (2022-2024). He was selected to the Pro Bowl in 2023 when he led the league in rushing touchdowns with Miami. In 12 games with the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he recorded just 22 carries for yards. He clearly would not be the number one option, but could serve as a rotational player when Wright and Gordon need a break. Joe Mixon The Dolphins could look to add Mixon if he clears the medical concerns that cost him the entire 2025 season. If his foot is healthy, and that is obviously a question mark, he could still be the played that picked up 1,016 yards in 2024 with the Houston Texans. He could be a workhorse, taking a large number of carries, but he is not going to be a direct replacement for Achane. Miami could consider him as the second option, letting Wright lead the group. Nick Chubb Chubb just re-signed with the Cleveland Browns to ceremony retire as a member of the team, but the Dolphins could look to sign him for the remainder of the year. Wright would likely remain the top option for Miami, but Chubb could be a more physical rotational playe with him. He might slide ahead of Gordon on the depth chart once he is fully engaged in the offense. Chubb sustained a knee injury in 2023 and did not return to full form in 2024 or 2025. He only has 224 carries and 838 yards the last two seasons. Cam Akers Akers is only 27 years old, so there is potential to still land a running back with potential to reach. However, after being a second-round pick in 2020, he has played for five different teams in seven different stretches. He was at his best with his first team, the Los Angeles Rams, from 2020 through 2023, and he has a great combination of speed and power. But, in 2025, he only appeared in three games with no carries for Seattle. He would only be a rotational player with the Dolphins, giving Wright a break when needed. Other options Other players Miami could consider include Dalvin Cook, Antonio Gibson, D’Onta Foreman, Ronald Jones II, Alexander Mattison, and Miles Sanders. Would you consider any of them? Was there someone not on the list you would consider?
author: Kevin Nogle

title: De’Von Achane injury: Dolphins lose running back for season
summary: Miami Dolphins running back De’Von Achane left the team’s Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter with a knee injury. He was soon ruled out of a return to the game, then head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game he was not “optimistic” about the injury. On Monday morning, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 28: De'Von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins walks off the field after beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an NFL football game at Hard Rock Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins running back De’Von Achane left the team’s Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter with a knee injury. He was soon ruled out of a return to the game, then head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game he was not “optimistic” about the injury. On Monday morning, that lack of optimism was confirmed with Achane’s injury confirmed. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Achane sustained a torn ACL and will be out for the remainder of the season. Achane was the center of the Dolphins’ offense this year as they work their way through a rebuild. As Miami focuses on the development of their younger players, including rookie wide receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr., Achane provided a veteran stabilizing presence to the attack. Miami will now have to figure out how to replace the man around who they built their entire offensive system. Achane was selected to his first Pro Bowl after last season when he tallied 1,350 rushing yard. He was injured as he was tackled on an 11-yard run. Kansas City Chiefs safety Alohi Gillman tackled Achane by his head, twisting the running back’s body awkwardly around his left leg. The running back slowly got up from the field and slowly walked off the field, flanked by trainers. He spent time walking on the sideline before heading back to the locker room. He eventually returned to the sideline during the game, but was never able to get back on the field. Miami’s running back group is now headlined by Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II. Wright missed the team’s Week 3 game with a stringer and foot injury. Wide receiver Malik Washington was used as a running back to provide relief to Gordon following Achane’s injury. Running backs Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington, Jr., are on Miami’s practice squad. The team could also look to sign a free agent to provide depth at the position. Achane will likely be on a timeline to return during training camp or just before the regular season in 2027, depending on how he recovers from surgery. This story will be updated with more information as it is available.
author: Kevin Nogle

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The Miami Dolphins welcomed Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Ken Walker III and the rest of the star-studded Kansas City Chiefs’ roster to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday for Miami’s first home game of the 2026 regular season. While Jeff Hafley’s crew fought hard, the firepower possessed by Kansas City’s offense was too much for the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: De'von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins carries the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins welcomed Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Ken Walker III and the rest of the star-studded Kansas City Chiefs’ roster to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday for Miami’s first home game of the 2026 regular season. While Jeff Hafley’s crew fought hard, the firepower possessed by Kansas City’s offense was too much for the Dolphins in the end — and the team ultimately fell by a score of 24-10. Unfortunately for Miami, they didn’t just suffer a loss on the scoreboard on Sunday — as electric running back, De’Von Achane, left early in the contest with a knee injury. He would not return to play for the entire afternoon. More on that later… In a year where losses will be plentiful, all you can ask for from this Dolphins team are showings that are marked by heart, grittiness and foundation building performances. On Sunday against the Chiefs, Miami accomplished those things, in my humble opinion. As we do after each game, let’s take a look at the good, bad and ugly from Sunday’s loss. GOOD Jacob Rodriguez nabs first career interception for improved Dolphins defense After giving up 35 points to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2, the Dolphins defense needed to show some signs of life in order to give its fanbase something encouraging to latch onto. They did. Kansas City managed 334 total yards, but Miami’s defense repeatedly came up with plays to keep Patrick Mahomes and company from running away with the game. The Dolphins also held the Chiefs to just three points during the third quarter, allowing Miami to remain within striking distance heading into the final period. A major factor in Miami’s step-forward on defense was the play of rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. Rodriguez intercepted Mahomes late in the second quarter — the first interception in his young career — making an impressive play on a deeply thrown tipped pass. He finished the contest with six tackles, including three tackles for loss. For a team relying heavily on young players this season, seeing Rodriguez continue to develop is exactly the kind of thing Dolphins fans should be cheering for while watching. There were still plenty of problems on defense, but Sunday’s game was a noticeable step forward from what we saw against the San Francisco 49ers one week ago. BAD Dolphins cannot sack an opposing quarterback Three games. Zero sacks. That’s where Miami currently stands after Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs. The Dolphins managed to hit Mahomes five times Sunday, but none of those pressures resulted in a sack. At one point, it appeared Chop Robinson had finally gotten home for a huge play, only for the third-year EDGE defender to be flagged for a questionable roughing the passer penalty in the endzone. It’s becoming increasingly difficult to ignore this problem. Mahomes is one of the game’s most accomplished passers, and the Dolphins weren’t able to consistently make him uncomfortable. As a result, the Chiefs quarterback eventually found Travis Kelce for an 11-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to effectively put the game away. Miami’s defense has shown flashes. Rodriguez is developing. There are young players making plays. However, until the Dolphins can consistently pressure opposing quarterbacks, it’s going to be difficult for this defense to become a reliable unit. UGLY De’Von Achane goes down early with knee injury; doesn’t return The Dolphins were already dealing with a limited collection of offensive weapons coming into Sunday’s game — with second-string running back Jaylen Wright missing the contest in addition to rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas riding the pine this week due to injury. Then the worst thing possible happened — De’Von Achane went down in a heap. Achane suffered a knee injury on his third carry of the afternoon and was eventually ruled out. The Dolphins’ offense was already struggling to generate consistent production, and losing arguably the team’s most dynamic offensive player made that task considerably more difficult. Miami managed just 10 points against Kansas City and has now failed to score more than 13 points in any of its first three games. That’s a problem. The Dolphins don’t have the veteran playmakers of previous seasons surrounding Malik Willis. The offense is young, inexperienced and still trying to find an identity — and Achane was one of the few players capable of changing a game with the ball in his hands. We’ll keep our fingers crossed that his injury isn’t as serious as it seems, although Jeff Hafley didn’t have good news following the game. “ To be honest with you, it does not sound very optimistic, ” said Miami’s coach during his postgame availability. If Achane is forced to miss significant time — and that’s what it’s looking like at the time of this writing — Miami’s offense is going to have an even tougher time finding its footing moving forward. ___ The Dolphins find themselves sitting at 0-3 to begin the Jeff Hafley era in Miami. To make matters worse, they just lost their most dangerous offensive weapon with a potentially season-ending injury . Is this already a lost season in South Florida? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: The Phinsider Mailbag a late Week 3 release
summary: The Phinsider Mailbag returns this morning to answer your Week 3 questions about the Dolphins. Yes, the Dolphins have already played their Week 3 game against the Kansas City Chiefs, losing 24-10 Sunday afternoon. This should have been posted before the game, but it got lost in a busy weekend and I apologize for that. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) is tackled by Miami Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (10) during a NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Miami Dolphins, on Sunday September 27, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL.(Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Phinsider Mailbag returns this morning to answer your Week 3 questions about the Dolphins. Yes, the Dolphins have already played their Week 3 game against the Kansas City Chiefs, losing 24-10 Sunday afternoon. This should have been posted before the game, but it got lost in a busy weekend and I apologize for that. We will make sure the Week 4 mailbag is posted before the team’s Week 4 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Since it is already late, we should probably just dive on in. Thanks to Marek Brave for again joining me in this discussion: KN: No, I do not think Walker reaches 200 yards, but I understand the point of the question. Miami’s defense has…struggled…this year. They are allowing 112.5 yards per game on the ground right now, and they are facing the number two rushing offense in the league, with the Chiefs picking up an average of 186.0 yards on the ground. Walker leads the league with 145.0 yards per game – nearly 40 yards a game more than second-place Derrick Henry. Miami is going to be facing an incredibly difficult task on Sunday, but I do not think it gets to 200-yards bad. I would not expect Swift to be at the game. The MTA Video Music Awards are Sunday in Los Angeles. I would anticipate her being there. And, no, I do not think 70 is in play this weekend for the Chiefs. MB: Ken Walker III has been amazing this season, but the Chiefs know he can’t sustain his touches rate through an entire season considering his injury history. Look for rookie running back Emmett Johnson to get some run in this game to keep Walker fresh. Taylor Swift probably won’t be there, but if she is, look for her to mix in for a couple carries too. Anyone can run on this Dolphins defense. No, I don’t think Kansas City scores 70 points against Miami on Sunday. A nice 69 points will suffice. KN: I think Willis, for whatever reason, is trying to be a pocket passer and prove he can hold on to the Dolphins’ starting position. He seems like he is trying to stand tall and wait for a player to come open, sometimes longer than he should. They have to get him playing instinctually, running when he feels the pressure and get out of the pocket. They also need to convince him to throw the ball away when he does get out of the pocket. He ran himself out of bounds multiple times last week, taking a sack rather than throwing an incomplete pass. The coaches need to make him realize an incomplete pass is much better than a sack. I think we saw some of the RPO play calling show up last week. I would expect more of it this week. At the end of the day, however, the offense should run through running back De’Von Achane. Willis keeping the ball instead of handing it to Achane takes touches away from the runner. I do not know that there should be an emphasis on not giving the ball to Achane. No, the Dolphins pass rush is not “historically” bad. Are they having a rough time rushing the passer right now? Absolutely. They are the only team without a sack this season, but the Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys, two teams expected to compete for a deep playoff run, have only recorded two sacks this season. Does Miami need to fix this and find a way to get after the quarterback? Of course. But, the sacks will come. Just like everything with this team, they just have to grow into them. MB: Malik Willis is still growing into the starter role. He has just a little over half a season of starting experience in the National Football League, so expect him to get better in all facets of his game as the season rolls on — including knowing when to tuck the ball and use his legs to help this offense.\ Miami’s pass rush is non-existent right now. Chop Robinson missing last week’s game didn’t help matters. He’s back for this week’s game and Patrick Mahomes likes to hold onto the ball and run a bit behind his offensive line. I expect the Dolphins to get their first sack this weekend. KN: I really hope it is the Jets. First, Miami needs to get their pass rush working. But, it is just hysterical to think that the last time the Jets intercepted a pass was Week 18 of 2024. It really does not mean anything in the long run, but the longer it lasts, the funnier it is. MB: I think Miami gets a sack this week against the Chiefs (see above), so can the Jets match that with an interception against Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions this weekend? I’m guessing no. Fins up! KN: I think it is both. We all watched them tear down the roster, so it is not a surprise that they are having a rough start to the year. The massive turnover alone could cause some of the problems we are seeing – a bunch of players who have not played together in a new system still being established struggling with communication and responsibilities is not unexpected. Miami has had rookies play 841 snaps this season, which is over 100 more than any other team has had through the first two games in a season since at least 2006 ( via the AP’s Josh Dubow ). Over a quarter of the snaps Miami has played this year have been from rookies: Rookie Snap Count % through Week 2 1. MIA 27.6% 2. CLE 16.4% 3. NYG 15.1% … 30. ARI 2.3% 31. DEN 1.1% 32. LAR 0.7% pic.twitter.com/dA2rPZ8FZV — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 22, 2026 The rookies are gaining experience, but they are making rookie mistakes as they grow. The key for them, and for the Dolphins this year, is to get better. If the Dolphins look better in Week 18 than they did in Week 1 and Week 2, then they are headed in the right direction. MB: I think the Dolphins are really bad right now. But that’s okay. There’s still plenty of season left. As bad as it has been, it hasn’t been nearly as bad as the start to the 2019 season — Brian Flores’ first year as the team’s head coach. That year, they started their first three games with a 59-10 loss at home to the Ravens, a 43-0 loss at home to the Patriots, and a 31-6 loss on the road to the Cowboys. Things looked absolutely broken — yet, they finished the final nine games that season with a 5-4 record. Do I think Miami has that in them this year? It’s not looking great so far, but stranger things have happened.

title: Dolphins vs. Chiefs final score: 5 Immediate Reactions for Week 3
summary: Final Score: Chiefs 24 – 10 Dolphins Immediate Winner: Jacob Rodriguez Immediate Loser: De’Von Achane Immediate Reactions De’Von Achane Goes Down After a week of promising more involvement for running back De’Von Achane, the first quarter couldn’t have gone worse for the Dolphins. On just his third carry of the game, Achane awkwardly went down […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins runs the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Final Score: Chiefs 24 – 10 Dolphins Immediate Winner: Jacob Rodriguez Immediate Loser: De’Von Achane Immediate Reactions De’Von Achane Goes Down After a week of promising more involvement for running back De’Von Achane, the first quarter couldn’t have gone worse for the Dolphins. On just his third carry of the game, Achane awkwardly went down after a tackle. He limped off the field, and was soon taken to the locker room for additional testing. He did not return to the field, and was later ruled out due to a knee injury. Arguably Miami’s best player, the Dolphins offense will continue to struggle without his presence. The team has yet to put more than 13 points across three games, and I don’t see that getting easier without Achane. It’s currently unclear how serious the injury is, and if Achane will miss an extended period of time. Jacob Rodriguez Shows Promise Like many, I had high hopes for linebacker Jacob Rodriguez entering this season. The Dolphins selected Rodriguez in the second round of the 2026 NFL draft, and so far, he’s been promising. He currently leads all rookies in tackles, and looks to be a future stalwart of Miami’s defense. He also wears the “green dot” for the Dolphins on defense, which means he is able to communicate with coaches and receives the play calls—very impressive for a rookie. Against the Chiefs, Rodriguez recorded his first career NFL interception, diving to catch a tipped pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. He also recored six total tackles, three of which were for a loss. Though allowing 24 points is far from ideal, Rodriguez looks to be a stud, and is getting better every week. No Rush, No Dice Through three games, the Miami Dolphins have zero sacks, ranked dead last in the NFL. This was an area of concern for the team in the offseason, and not much has changed after three weeks. The Dolphins managed five quarterback hits against the Chiefs, but none of them resulted in a sack. Third year edge rusher Chop Robinson managed a big hit on Mahomes, but was flagged for roughing the passer. Robinson is still chasing the numbers and success from his rookie year, where he looked to be one of the league’s best young pass rushers. Alongside him, veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler was once again disappointing against the Chiefs. The Dolphins must improve at getting to the quarterback, or their defense won’t be able to a nosebleed. Young Receiving Core Has Something The Dolphins spent significant draft capital on wide receivers this offseason, and so far, they’ve looked decent. Although rookie Caleb Douglas (Round 3, Pick 75) missed this game through injury, his fellow rookie Chris Bell (Round 3, Pick 94) snagged four catches for 67 yards against the Chiefs, including a 44-yard catch-and-run. Third year wideout Malik Washington looked good as well, catching five catches for 56 yards. It’s a long way from the days of Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, but Miami’s young receiving core seems to be getting better each week. The touchdowns haven’t come yet, but they surely will with time. Kicking Must Improve Miami’s special teams unit was abysmal in Week 2, and not much has changed in. Though no major mistakes were made, it’s increasingly clear that the Dolphins don’t trust kicker Riley Patterson from distance. Faced with an opportunity to kick a 55-yard field goal at the end of the first half, the Dolphins opted to take a delay-of-game penalty and punt. While accurate, Patterson does not have the leg required for long field goals. He made 27 of 29 field goal attempts in 2025, but his longest was just 54 yards. In 2026, kickers have never been better. In a league where kickers can regularly hit 60+ yard field goals, the Dolphins cannot persist with a kicker if they do not trust his leg from distance.

title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Vikings at Buccaneers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings won on the road in Tampa Bay, in an ugly game. There were 17 punts, 3 Interceptions, and 17 penalties. Three different times, the teams combined for five consecutive possessions ending in punts. The teams averaged less than 17 yards per possession in a defensive battle. The two defenses are stout, but […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings is congratulated after a touchdown in the first half during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings won on the road in Tampa Bay, in an ugly game. There were 17 punts, 3 Interceptions, and 17 penalties. Three different times, the teams combined for five consecutive possessions ending in punts. The teams averaged less than 17 yards per possession in a defensive battle. The two defenses are stout, but they were assisted with some questionable offensive play by both teams’ QB and OL. The team is 3-0 overall, 2-0 in the NFC North, and 2-0 on the road. It’s a great start and we’ll just have to hope the offense figures things out eventually. Here are my nominees for Player of the Game. Eric Wilson It was another fantastic defensive performance and Eric Wilson was at the center of most of the action. He was flying around the field yesterday. Wilson led the team with 10 total tackles and added 1.5 sacks. Jordan Addison Addison was the lone bright spot on offense. He has been open quite often this year and hasn’t received the service he deserves. He took advantage of his opportunity after Jefferson went down with 5 catches for 90 yards and a beautiful 41-yard touchdown. He almost pulled down another bomb later in the game, but he was unable to corral an underthrown deep ball. Myles Price Sometimes all you need is a spark. Price’s punt return touchdown gave the Vikings the breathing room they needed to keep the pressure on Tampa’s offense all day. Price looked electric on punts and kicks all day. If he finds a crease, he’s dangerous. Will Reichard Another week, another perfect day for Will Reichard. Will is a weapon and the way this team is playing, they’re going to be needing him a lot this season. Kyle Van Noy Van Noy had his first sack for the Vikings in the 2nd quarter. It was part of four consecutive three-and-outs (2 for each team). He also had a couple of more tackles for loss in the run game. Van Noy has quickly become another weapon in Brian Flores’ arsenal. Honorable Mention: Johnny Hekker – Hekker was solid all day, nothing insanely good, but solid. Great on holds too! Jalen Redmond – another solid performance from Redmond. His deflection almost resulted in an interception. Dallas Turner – Turner was disruptive all game once again. At some point we’re going to run out of ways to say he’s playing great football. Blake Cashman – he could’ve been listed up there with Eric Wilson, but his best pass breakup was friednly fire on the ball that was tipped by Redmond.

McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with Justin Jefferson #18 after his touchdown pass against the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. So, the Vikings have decided to trade the highest-drafted quarterback in franchise history, a player they took with the #10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, after just ten NFL starts. This also puts the Vikings in a situation where they have no quarterbacks under contract for the 2027 season. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz are both here on one-year deals. Honestly, after watching that performance from Murray on Sunday and knowing the injury histories that both Murray and Wentz have, it boggles the mind that you would rather be two snaps from having your season rest on the right arm of Max Brosmer than potentially having J.J. McCarthy back there instead. I’m sure that there will be plenty more on this in the coming days, but that’s the big story as it stands right now. The Vikings are, in fact, trading J.J. title: The Vikings Could Be Without Josh Oliver For A While
summary: The Minnesota Vikings lost a significantly underrated part of their offense on Sunday, and the fear is that he could be out for a long time. . .potentially for the remainder of the season. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network is reporting that the Vikings believe that tight end Josh Oliver may have suffered a […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - JANUARY 04: Minnesota Vikings tight end Josh Oliver (84) warms up before the NFL game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings on January 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings lost a significantly underrated part of their offense on Sunday, and the fear is that he could be out for a long time. . .potentially for the remainder of the season. #Vikings TE Josh Oliver is feared to have suffered a torn biceps in Sunday’s game and will have an MRI today determine if that is the case, sources say. Oliver would be out indefinitely if the testing confirms. pic.twitter.com/pHZG0hj8kX — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026 Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network is reporting that the Vikings believe that tight end Josh Oliver may have suffered a torn bicep in Sunday’s victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and that the injury may require surgery. If that’s the case, he could be out indefinitely. Oliver has been one of the best blocking tight ends in football for quite a while now, and signed a new three-year contract extension with the team in 2025. If the Vikings are without him for any length of time, it will impact a running game that has already had its issues through the first three weeks of the season. In Oliver’s absence, the role of the second tight end would likely be filled by Gavin Bartholomew. Bartholomew was the Vikings’ seventh-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, but did not play at all in his rookie season while dealing with a back injury that left him on the Physically Unable to Perform List for the majority of the year. Bartholomew has played just four snaps on offense through the first three games this season. The Vikings also have former Cincinnati Bengals tight end Cam Grandy on the practice squad, though Grandy has mostly been a special teamer to this point in his NFL career. Here’s hoping that the injury to Josh Oliver isn’t as severe as the Vikings are fearing that it is and he’ll be back in the fold sooner rather than later.

title: Vikings Week 3 Stock Market Report
summary: The Vikings eked out another ugly road win in Tampa 23-16 on the strength of Brian Flores’ defense, a Myles Price punt return touchdown, a bomb from Kyler Murray to Jordan Addison, and another flawless performance from Will Reichard. Stock Up Will Reichard. Nailed a couple 50+ field goals without breaking a sweat or even […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a touchdown pass above Jacob Parrish #25 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings eked out another ugly road win in Tampa 23-16 on the strength of Brian Flores’ defense, a Myles Price punt return touchdown, a bomb from Kyler Murray to Jordan Addison, and another flawless performance from Will Reichard. Stock Up Will Reichard . Nailed a couple 50+ field goals without breaking a sweat or even a jump in heart rate. Cool as a cucumber, the prince of darkness for opposing teams. 11 total points on 3 field goals and two extra points. Myles Price. First punt return for a touchdown in ten years came at a good time. Price has improved as a returner so far this year and this is the second game he’s impacted in a positive way with his returns this season. Kyle Van Noy . Van Noy had a sack, but also has been all-around solid in rotation. Nice late acquisition for the Vikings to shore up depth off the edge. Isaiah Rodgers . He was targeted 5 times and allowed one reception for one yard. He also had three stops and the interception to end the game. Jordan Addison. His 5 receptions for 90 yards was pretty much the Vikings entire passing game after Justin Jefferson went out after the first drive. Much needed explosives that made a difference. Eric Wilson . He gave up a big reception but was relentless as a pass rusher, credited with 5 pressures including 2 sacks according to PFF. Stock Down Josh Metellus . Metellus gave up the big touchdown reception to Ted Hurst and it wasn’t close. He did okay outside of that but I find it hard to believe he is the best safety on the roster. He’s the only safety playing all the defensive snaps. Jauan Jennings. He had one reception on two targets for one yard. His yards per route run was 0.04. At this point, Jennings has been a significant disappointment. Tai Felton. Felton didn’t have a reception- and only one target- after filling in for Justin Jefferson after the first drive. A whole lot of not so much in his first significant opportunity to show what he’s got. Buy Jefferson and Addison’s ability to get open and make the catch. Sell Every other receiver’s ability to get open and make the catch when Jefferson is out. Buy How good these early wins will look in hindsight if the offense improves. Sell The Vikings chances of continuing to win like this if the offense doesn’t improve. Buy Not drawing conclusions on the Murray-led offense after his first full game, especially given Justin Jefferson was out after the first drive. Sell The Vikings offense ability to cope without Justin Jefferson. Buy Road wins- any which way they come. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Vikings Lose Jefferson Early, Win Ugly Again Against Buccaneers
summary: For the second week in a row, the Minnesota Vikings’ offense struggled, but the defense and the special teams managed to find a way to bring home a victory on the road anyway. Sparked by the team’s first punt return for a touchdown in a decade and three more field goals from Will Reichard, the […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings returns a punt for a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second week in a row, the Minnesota Vikings’ offense struggled, but the defense and the special teams managed to find a way to bring home a victory on the road anyway. Sparked by the team’s first punt return for a touchdown in a decade and three more field goals from Will Reichard, the Vikings overcame another lackluster offensive performance and the loss of wide receiver Justin Jefferson after their first possession to get a 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 3 NFL action. The Vikings got the football first, as for the second straight week, they won the opening coin toss and elected to receive. Kyler Murray found Justin Jefferson on the very first snap for a 22-yard gain, and a run by Aaron Jones put the Vikings into Tampa Bay territory in just two plays. After that, a hold on Donovan Jackson pushed the Vikings into a third-and-long, and though they recovered some of the yardage, they wound up settling for a 54-yard field goal from Will Reichard to take a 3-0 lead just under five minutes into the game. On that drive, Jefferson suffered an ankle injury that saw him go into the blue medical tent and later into the locker room. He was first declared questionable to return, and later ruled out for the remainder of the game. This is, obviously, a situation that we will be monitoring for the upcoming week. Tampa started their first drive at their own 40-yard line after a nice return from Kenny Gainwell on the ensuing kickoff. But Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers’ offense couldn’t move the football and went three-and-out, and they punted the ball away. Myles Price took the punt at his own 14-yard line and, after a couple of moves, found himself in the open field and sprinting into the end zone for an 86-yard punt return touchdown to make it 10-0 in favor of the purple. 86 yards. To. The. Crib. @myles_price3 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/c7HfjpmGr2 — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 27, 2026 That punt return touchdown was the first one for the Vikings in almost a full decade. The last one came courtesy of Marcus Sherels against the Houston Texans at U.S. Bank Stadium on 9 October 2016. Tampa’s offense responded loudly on their next possession, as Mayfield found Cade Otton for a quick completion to pick up the Bucs’ initial first down of the afternoon and, after a couple of runs from Bucky Irving and a personal foul on Dallas Turner, Mayfield found rookie Ted Hurst for a 40-yard catch-and-run to get the Buccaneers into the end zone and cut the Minnesota lead to 10-7. It was the first touchdown catch of Hurst’s career. He was Tampa’s third-round pick in this April’s NFL Draft out of Georgia State. The Vikings got the ball back and got out to near midfield, but the drive stalled out, and they were forced to punt it away. Johnny Hekker, in this week for the injured Brett Thorson, kicked it away, and the Bucs got the ball to their own 25-yard line to start their next possession. They went three-and-out again, thanks to a nice tackle by Isaiah Rodgers to stop Emeka Egbuka short of the sticks on a third-down completion. Unfortunately, with Justin Jefferson on the sideline with some sort of ankle issue, the Vikings’ offense continued to struggle, and they answered with a three-and-out of their own that spanned the gap between the first and second quarters. Tampa Bay took over at their own 39 after the punt, and their drive started with Kyle Van Noy picking up his first sack as a Viking as he dropped Mayfield for a seven-yard loss. That was enough to stop the Bucs’ offense, and they punted it away again. Minnesota’s offense continued to struggle without Jefferson on the field, as Murray was sacked by David Walker to force yet another three-and-out, with Hekker’s punt just barely reaching midfield to set the Buccaneers up with great field position again. On the next third down, Mayfield found Cade Otton for a big 37-yard catch-and-run that gave the Bucs a goal-to-go situation. Fortunately for the Vikings, a couple of holding penalties pushed the Buccaneers back, and they couldn’t overcome them enough to get into the end zone and had to settle for a 28-yard field goal from Chase McLaughlin to tie things at 10-10 with five and a half minutes left in the first half. The Vikings’ offense came back to life on the next drive behind the previously hibernating Jordan Addison. On the first play of the drive, Murray found him for a 30-yard completion that was challenged by the Buccaneers and upheld on review as a catch, and three plays later Murray launched a deep ball for him that he hauled in just in front of the end zone and tumbled into the end zone for a 41-yard touchdown, his first score of the year, to give the Vikings the lead back at 17-10 with four minutes left before halftime. 3️⃣ ball! 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/O3YBcdovkc — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 27, 2026 The two teams then exchanged punts, following Murray and Addison nearly connecting on another deep ball that could have been another long touchdown but was underthrown by Murray. They went into the locker rooms at Raymond James Stadium with the Vikings up by a touchdown at 17-10. Tampa Bay got the ball to start the second half, and after picking up one first down, the Vikings forced them to punt it away and got the ball back at their own 20-yard line. The Vikings also managed one first down on their initial possession of the second half but couldn’t get much more than that, responding with a punt of their own and putting the Buccaneers inside their own 20. The Bucs then very quickly went three-and-out again, with Mayfield missing a pair of attempts to Egbuka. The Bucs punted again, but on the ensuing Vikings possession, Murray had a pass deflected by Vita Vea into the hands of A’Shawn Robinson for an interception, setting the Buccaneers’ offense up at the Minnesota 22-yard line. Fortunately, the Vikings’ defense stood strong once again, and the Buccaneers had to settle for a 38-yard field goal from McLaughlin to make it a four-point game at 17-13 with just over seven minutes left in the third quarter. The Vikings again, thanks in part to a delay of game penalty, went three-and-out on their next possession and gave the ball back to the Buccaneers in rapid fashion. The Bucs found themselves in a 3rd-and-30 and looked to have an 85-yard touchdown pass from Mayfield to Chris Godwin, but the Buccaneers were called for holding to negate the big play and instead had to punt it away. Tampa then got another field goal, this one a 54-yarder from McLaughlin, after a penalty on Josh Metellus wiped out what would have been a stop on a 3rd-and-29 play. That kick made it 17-16 with nine minutes left in regulation. A personal foul on the ensuing kickoff return gave the Vikings the ball at the 45-yard line to start their next possession, and once again the offense managed to struggle its way into range for another long Will Reichard field goal attempt. This one was a 56-yarder, and he once again put it through the uprights to make it 20-16 with just over three minutes remaining in regulation. The Buccaneers got the ball back and, once again, the Minnesota defense kept them from moving the football. They faced a 4th-and-13, and after Mayfield scrambled for a significant length of time, he threw one up for grabs, and it was intercepted by Andrew Van Ginkel. title: Justin Jefferson Suffers Ankle Injury Against Buccaneers
summary: Early on in their contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Minnesota Vikings lost their best player, and it is not yet known how long he will be out. Wide receiver Justin Jefferson was injured on the opening drive of the game for the Vikings. He went into the blue medical tent to have his […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Early on in their contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Minnesota Vikings lost their best player, and it is not yet known how long he will be out. Wide receiver Justin Jefferson was injured on the opening drive of the game for the Vikings. He went into the blue medical tent to have his ankle looked at and was declared questionable to return. He then went back to the locker room and did not come out to the sideline with the rest of the team when the second half started, and shortly after that, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game. The injury occurred on a long third-down play where the Vikings called a screen pass to Jefferson that gained enough yardage to set up a 54-yard Will Reichard field goal for the first points of the game. He did not come back into the game again after that. This is, obviously, a situation that we will be monitoring for the remainder of this week as we go forward, with the Vikings getting prepared to host the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 4. Once again, Vikings’ wide receiver Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle injury on the first drive of the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and did not (and will not) return to the game.

title: Patriots vs. Jaguars: Fan observations from Week 3 loss
summary: Well that sucked. After a Week 2 that saw them get their first win and look fairly stifling on defense against a Steelers team that just hung 30 on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Patriots went down to Jacksonville and laid an absolute egg. Just a listless, lifeless, lame performance all around. It’s still early in […]
full_text: Well that sucked. After a Week 2 that saw them get their first win and look fairly stifling on defense against a Steelers team that just hung 30 on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Patriots went down to Jacksonville and laid an absolute egg . Just a listless, lifeless, lame performance all around. It’s still early in the season, I know. But yikes. Yesterday saw the entire Northeast blanketed with rain, wind, and overall nastiness as the Patriots enjoyed a balmy, sunny game down in Florida. There was once a time when I would have lamented the fact that New England wasn’t playing at home, because I would have been at the game in a cheap poncho while doing my absolute best to get as much liquid down my gullet as I was getting all over my body. But I have long since aged out of that nonsense, and had (what was supposed to be) a very nice afternoon on the couch in my jammies with the first fire of the season coupled with the first nut brown ale of autumn. A little slice of heaven. Something else that comes with getting older: the realization that summer is wildly overrated. Everywhere is crowded, everything is expensive, and there’s all this pressure to really live it up between Memorial Day and Labor Day, as if there aren’t any other opportunities to be happy the other nine months of the year. Well I say nuts to that. Give me cooler weather, crisp nights, the smell of leaves and woodsmoke in the air, delicious beers, open windows, and all the sports back on TV. Not to mention a significantly lower electricity bill for those of us who may or may not be married to a woman who may or may not insist on sleeping in full pajamas with a down quilt on no matter the outside temperature and thus may or may not blast the AC at borderline-unholy temperatures. And “borderline-unholy” is as good enough a phrase as any to describe some of the things that came out of my mouth while I was watching that game. It wouldn’t be overly hard to chalk this one up as just one of those games. Every team has games like this where nothing seems to go right. Bad penalties, lame turnovers, missed kicks, inaccurate throws, poor tackling, lackluster play-calling… it happens. Brady and Belichick had more than a handful of games like that. And it’s easy to point out that if a few plays had gone differently — a made FG, a Drake Maye TD run not called back from holding, a little less air under a pass — we could be singing a different tune this morning. But given what we’ve seen through three weeks thus far, with an offense that has two TDs on a long run and a DPI-induced goal-to-go, it’s tough to just shrug this one off as a bump in the road. And it isn’t entirely on Drake Maye, but a lot of it is. What really has me worried right now (not to the point of panic, but the panic police are in the neighborhood and asking questions) is that maybe that shoulder injury Maye suffered last season was hidden or mismanaged and never fully healed right, and now he’s the latest RG3 or Carson Wentz who just never quite came back to his old self. I don’t mind physical errors. Balls slip out of hands (heh). You can trip over your own feet on occasion, a behavior that is widely gaining notoriety as “The Pop Douglas.” That happens. But we’re now seeing at least one horrendous decision per game from the quarterback that directly take points off the board. On the Travis Hunter pick, at absolutely no point was Efton Chism even remotely open. He was completely blanketed. The play was busted. You run out of bounds, you take the points, then you get back to work. These panic throws are just ruining everything, and I’m not sure what to do about it. The 2025 Patriots seemed to open every single game by letting their opponent march right down the field and score a TD before they actually got going. The 2026 Patriots seem to have abandoned that strategy and have instead opted for a promising drive short-circuited by an atrocious turnover. What he really needs is a get right game. A slump buster, if you will. Which makes me really happy that the Patriots have to go to Buffalo next week, that should be just what the doctor ordered. What I dislike the most, I think, is that I’m starting to get strong 2023 vibes from this team. In 2023, if the Patriots were down by seven or more at any point, that was more or less the game. They didn’t have the ability to come back from a two-score deficit. I haven’t seen anything from the 2026 team that gives me faith that they can do the same. And there’s no way you can sit here and say that this is all because A.J. Brown is out. He isn’t some magic fix-all that’s going to get this offense off the schneid. Unless the coaching staff built their entire system around a talented but enigmatic WR in his first year with a new team. And if that’s the case, we have much bigger problems than a QB with a bad case of the yips. Carlton Davis almost picked off a quick screen early in the second quarter just before Jacksonville’s first TD of the day, and I found myself remembering the time that Kyle Dugger picked off the exact same play against the Raiders a few years back. I had completely forgotten about that guy and had to look up what became of him (he plays for the Bengals in case you didn’t know or, like me, forgot he existed). Talk about a ton of upward momentum suddenly and inexplicably stopped for a guy who was slated to be a cornerstone of the team but then just kind of vanished. I wish that the Jags had had a 1st-and-10 inside the 20 which led to a touchdown that got called back which then became 1st-and-30 at the 40 which then became some razzle-dazzle nonsense that was a lucky break more than anything to scratching just enough yards back for the field goal attempt. Because that’s an objectively funny series of events and I would have liked to laugh at it. What’s going on with Kyle Williams? Where is he? Why isn’t he more involved? And if Maye so deeply trusted Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte, why are they both gone? As I mentioned earlier, I spent this game on the couch, in my pajamas, in front of a roaring fire. And I feel like I was significantly less comfortable than Trevor Lawrence was all day. This team needs some players back, and soon. The defense isn’t playing poorly, per se, although they did seem to have some real tackling issues yesterday and gave up almost 140 yards on the ground. But it has to wear on a unit when your counterpart isn’t pulling their weight. We saw a 70-yard field goal attempt to close out the first half of this game. Cam Little had the distance, he just pulled it a little wide to the right. It’s just a matter of time before someone hits one. That means that the NFL is extremely close to presenting fans with a scenario where a touchback and one first down puts a team into scoring position. The sounds I have found myself making every time Drake Maye releases the ball are foreign to me. When Andy Borregales straight-up shanked that 38-yard attempt at the beginning of the third quarter, that was it. If you turned the TV off at that point, I don’t blame you. You didn’t miss much after that. I don’t think that the Jags looked overly dominant yesterday. That isn’t a knock on them at all; they did what they needed to do to win. But this wasn’t a scenario where the Jags straight up dominated the Patriots. New England just never showed up, at any level. And that might be the most troubling part. The good news is — and real good news this time, not the “laugh so you don’t cry” kind of stuff — after Buffalo, the Patriots enter a relatively soft (on paper, at least) part of the schedule. And outside of the Bills and the Chiefs, the entire AFC seems to be a mess of mediocrity. So things are far from over. Patriots seasons of yore are replete with early slumps that turned positive. So let’s all keep the faith. For now. This is the NFL, so watch the Patriots go to Buffalo next week and win 30-6. But, man, do I find myself wishing that this game was taking place at literary…
