author: Chris Pflum

title: Is Giants’ QB Jameis Winston about to lose his job? Harbaugh says no, but…
summary: The New York Giants signed quarterback Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million contract extension the week before the 2026 season started. The Giants obviously believed in Winston. He’s emerged as a leader in the locker room, is charismatic, and is a former first overall pick. The Giants had confidence that Winston was the best […]
full_text: Jameis Winston vs. the Rams. | Getty Images The New York Giants signed quarterback Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million contract extension the week before the 2026 season started. The Giants obviously believed in Winston. He’s emerged as a leader in the locker room, is charismatic, and is a former first overall pick. The Giants had confidence that Winston was the best player available to step in if something happened to Jaxson Dart. Then the Giants’ nightmare scenario happened during the first series of their Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Dart suffered a significant knee injury and was lost for the year, and in an instant Winston became The Guy. The early results weren’t pretty. Winston looked unsure of his reads, and didn’t appear to trust his receivers or his protection against the Rams. Excuses were made and Winston’s performance was blamed on the gutpunch of losing Dart, as well as a jury-rigged game plan that was built for Dart but adapted to the relatively immobile Winston. It was hoped that Winston would improve with a truncated week of practice with the starters and a game plan tailored to his skill set. The Giants got the win over the Tennessee Titans, but it’s tough to say it was because of Winston. He once again appeared unsure of his receivers and only had 118 yards passing. He was slow going through his progressions and consistently under-threw his receivers. Rumors have circulated since the Giants lost Dart that the Giants would bring in a new quarterback. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game that Winston’s play hasn’t influenced the Giants’ plan at quarterback. “Not at all,” Harbaugh said. “The plans are the plans. The opportunities that you have are the opportunities you have. No matter what, we’re going to do everything we can to make our team as strong as we can based on what options we have.” As far as options are concerned, Jay Glazer reported before the game that the Giants are interested in Jimmy Garoppolo and Justin Fields . Garoppolo is a free agent. To get Fields, the Giants would need to engineer a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs. Jay Glazer says the Giants could bring in two QB’s this week Mentioned Justin Fields & Jimmy Garoppalo. Joe Flacco, Mac Jones & Gardner Minshew are not happening. pic.twitter.com/QFyL2DNw0A — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) September 27, 2026 The Giants reiterated that Winston did what was necessary to win. For his part, Winston was just happy to get his first win as the Giants starting quarterback. “Every quarterback is really judged off if they won or lost the game. So, I’m grateful that I get to be judged off of a win, not a loss. And I’ve had games where I’ve thrown for 500 yards, right, and the game didn’t turn out the way I wanted it to be. And anytime, any day, I would rather win. “I am so happy and grateful that the New York Football Giants won the football game. Anything else that is outside of me, it is what it is. I’m grateful that we get to celebrate as a team.” We’ll see what happens, but it seems like a very likely outcome that the outcome that the Giants add a quarterback soon. At the very least, they probably don’t want to rely on Jake Haener as QB2.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants-Titans ‘winners and losers’: Jevon Holland the hero as New York survives
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants won a football game on Sunday. The 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans wasn’t pretty. Maybe you consider it fortunate. It was historic in its own warped way: Regardless, it was a victory that moved the Giants to 2-1. Let’s get to the ‘Kudos and Wet Willies.’ […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, Jevon Holland and the Giants emerged with a victory on Sunday. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants won a football game on Sunday. The 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans wasn’t pretty. Maybe you consider it fortunate. It was historic in its own warped way: Giants had 238 total yards and 0 TD in their 12-7 win vs Titans. It's the first time the Giants won a game with 0 TD and fewer than 300 total yds since Nov 14, 1976 — Katie Sharp (@SharpStats17) September 27, 2026 Regardless, it was a victory that moved the Giants to 2-1. Let’s get to the ‘Kudos and Wet Willies.’ Kudos to … Jevon Holland — The veteran safety saved the Giants from what looked like it was about to be a 2025-style fourth-quarter meltdown on Sunday. With the Titans at the Giants’ 7-yard line and threatening to take the lead, Holland intercepted a horrible Cam Ward pass in the end zone to rescue the Giants. Holland has been a difference-making star for the Giants so far this season. He now has a career-high three interceptions, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery. Dominic Zvada — The rookie field goal kicker made kicks of 39, 27, 39, and 30 yards. The Giants should have had more points than that, but it’s all they got — and all they needed. Najee Harris — The veteran running back got his most extensive action thus far, and responded with 52 yards on nine carries, 5.8 yards per attempt. On his first series, Harris helped the Giants get a field goal by carries five times for 36 yards. Cam Skattebo — The game did not start well for Skattebo. At one point, he had 10 carries for 4 yards. He lost 7 yards on a second-quarter Wildcat play from the Tennessee 5-yard line. Still, he finished with 60 yards on 20 carries, and three catches for 40 yards. One of those, a 30-yarder, set up one of the four Zvada field goals. Arvell Reese — The rookie inside linebacker played his best game of the season on Sunday with 12 tackles, one for loss, and a pass defensed. This was a big step forward for the No. 5 overall pick in the draft. Darnell Mooney — His numbers are not fantastic — two catches in three targets for 20 yards, and one run for 9 yards. Two of his touches, though, created first downs in third-and-long situations that led to points. Zaire Barnes and Malik Harrison — The two special teamers combined for a turnover on the game’s first play. Barnes formed a Chimere Dike fumble and Harrison recovered at the Tennessee 37-yard line. It isn’t their fault the offense couldn’t take advantage. Greg Newsome — The veteran cornerback gave up just three receptions for 25 yards in seven targets, per Pro Football Focus. He also added two passes defensed. I wasn’t sure about the Newsome signing this offseason, but so far, so good. Jordan Stout — At times, the Giants’ offensive strategy on Sunday seemed to be not to screw up and turn the ball over, then just let Stout kick the ball into the ozone and get them out of trouble. He kept doing it. Stout had six punts for an average of 50.5 yards (44.2 net average). He had punts of 74 and 64 yards, and had three punts downed inside the 20-yard line. Wet Willies to … Penalties — This game could have been much more lopsided if not for all of the costly penalties the Giants committed. They had an unacceptable 10 penalties for 88 yards. Some of them cost the Giants points, and one late-game special teams penalty nearly helped doom the Giants to a devastating loss. Jermaine Eluemunor had two holding penalties, one on second-and-goal at the 7-yard line. John Michael Schmitz had a holding penalty that negated a first down at the Titans’ 16-yard line. Jon Runyan had a false start. The Giants also committed an illegal shift on second-and-goal at the 2-yard line on their first drive of the third quarter, and were eventually forced to settle for 3 points. Special teamer Elijah Campbell committed a 15-yard kick catch interference penalty with 3:03 to play that moved the ball from the Tennessee 8-yard line to the 23, setting up the Titans’ final drive. In all honesty, it was a startling lack of discipline from a John Harbaugh team. Kwillies to … Jameis Winston — The Giants won, and Winston did not make any major mistakes. He did little, though, to quell the groundswell of speculation that the Giants will not only be looking to bring in at least one more backup quarterback as soon as possible, but could be looking for someone who might eventually be able to take the reigns from Winston. Winston finished 14 of 22 for 118 yards with — critically — no turnovers. He made a couple of big throws for first downs, and used his legs on a 15-yard scramble. The Giants got by with him. Giants’ defense — The Giants held Tennessee to one first down and 54 yards in the first half. Tennessee finished with 17 first downs, one more than the Giants, and 262 total yards, 24 more than New York. The Giants gave up second-half drives of 68, 91, and 70 yards and got bailed out by Holland’s heady interception of Ward. Holland said he read Ward’s intent to throw rather than run , and stayed in the end zone rather than attack the line of scrimmage. The Giants’ pass rush was non-existent for the third straight game. New York totalled two quarterback hits in the game, and Pro Football Focus credited New York with just two hurries on Ward’s 36 pass attempts. That has got to change, and the potential long-term absence of Brian Burns makes you wonder how it will.
author: Ed Valentine

title: What did we learn from the Giants’ 12-7 ‘victory’ over the Tennessee Titans?
summary: We don’t want to draw too many conclusions from a game like today’s that was played in the rain and wind. Still, you have to think that John Harbaugh is wondering whether he should have taken a few more interviews before signing on the dotted line with the New York Giants after last Monday’s and […]
full_text: Greg Newsome (20) and Jevon Holland celebrate breaking up a pass. | Getty Images We don’t want to draw too many conclusions from a game like today’s that was played in the rain and wind. Still, you have to think that John Harbaugh is wondering whether he should have taken a few more interviews before signing on the dotted line with the New York Giants after last Monday’s and today’s games. This is a team that everyone pegged to make a big improvement this season. For one week, it looked that way. Since then, though… Let’s see what we learned from the Giants’ 12-7 “victory” over the Tennessee Titans, a game that did not inspire much hope for the rest of the 2026 season. Is Jaxson Dart better than we thought? We gave the Giants’ offense a pass last Monday because they had to adjust on the fly early in the game against a great Los Angeles Rams defense. And again, the conditions were poor at MetLife. Nonetheless, this was the Giants’ offense today: This guy is single-handedly beating the Tennessee Titans 12-0 rn pic.twitter.com/wqjbaHsyZh — Justin (@__This__Justin) September 27, 2026 I really don’t want to think my team has to go through the season counting on a guy who looks like he’s still in high school (and on the Mathletes team rather than the football team) for points. Give Dominic Zvada credit, though, he’s 6 for 6 in his Giants career and accounted for all their points today. As for the rest of the offense… the less said, the better. Again, the conditions were poor, but Jameis Winston was leaving almost all his throws short in the first quarter at least. The Giants did manage to put together a few drives, but coming up short of a TD every time is not winning football. Winston only threw one pass beyond 20 yards…and he completed it. 17 of his 21 attempts were shorter than 10 yards or behind the line of scrimmage. He totaled 117 yards on the day. Last year Winston threw 6 times beyond 20 yards and another 13 times between 10-20 yards in the Giants’ game in Detroit. We’re not seeing anything like that so far in 2026. There’s still time – the Giants’ opponent next week, Arizona, does not have a strong defense. But at some point this team has to develop an attacking mentality. Winston is not Dart…but he is a quarterback who can put points on the board if you let him try. I do worry that the Matt Nagy-Greg Roman offense is not a good match for Winston’s skill set. An interesting development today was that Najee Harris began to take on a bigger role in the running game, getting 52 yards on nine carries. He’s a useful complement to Cam Skattebo, who simultaneously is very valuable to the offense with his ability to get beyond first contact and change direction, but who also gets high on his supply at times with regrettable decisions he makes to keep trying to get more yards rather than just going down. If today is any indication, Harris is now RB2. And if you believe the best offense is a good defense, then we have to mention Jordan Stout, who bailed the offense out all day with more terrific punts. Today he had 6 punts averaging 49.8 yards with a net (punt – return) of 46.0 yards. I’d rather my offense be the ones to move the ball downfield, but between Stout and Zvada the Giants’ kicking game is in its best shape since…I don’t know when. The John Michael Schmitz era is nearing its end When you are in Year 3 and you still haven’t been able to clean up your pass blocking, you know you’re not long for the starting lineup. JMS has been a decent run blocker since he entered the league, but today he had another rough outing in pass protection, giving up a sack, after struggling against the Rams last week. Granted, it was against Jeffery Simmons, one of the best pass rushing interior defensive linemen in the NFL. A second round IOL in his fourth season has gotten about as good as he’s going to get. Today hurt especially because we got to see Austin Schlottman on the opponent’s offensive line. Schlottman has been a very solid center for several years now, and while it was a foregone conclusion that he would leave the Giants for a chance to start in Tennessee, it hurts to see him playing well while JMS continues to struggle. Where is the attacking Dennard Wilson defense? After three games, it is fair to be very concerned that the 2026 Giants defense is no, or not much, better than the horrid 2025 defense led by Shane Bowen. The run defense is improved with Tremaine Edmunds and Arvell Reese, and D.J. Reader has solidified the middle to some extent. The pass defense, though, is mostly horrendous with one or two notable exceptions. The biggest disappointment is the pass rush. The Giants pressured Cam Ward only four times all game and didn’t have a single sack…after only pressuring Matthew Stafford six times last week. This is the second year in a row that we’ve been sold on the Giants having one of the best pass rushes in the league, and it’s just not happening. Thank goodness for Jevon Holland Without a pass rush, the Giants’ secondary is ripe for the picking. Today it wasn’t exploited too much until the fourth quarter, because Cam Ward is still learning and hasn’t really gotten to the point where he can go through read progressions on a consistent basis. Still, his 179 yards passing went far beyond what the Giants could do. Greg Newsome was solid. Colton Hood is being picked on (6 targets, 5 receptions and a TD). Granted, Deonte Banks and Paulson Adebo are sidelined, but it’s not as if we can count on either to be shutdown-caliber. The only saving grace…and I do mean saving… was Jevon Holland. Holland snatched victory from the jaws of defeat with an end zone interception in the final minute as Ward was driving the Titans for what would have been the winning score. He is playing terrific ball this season on a consistent basis. That’s his third interception of the season already, one more than the number of receptions he’s allowed.
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: Giants’ Jevon Holland breaks down game-winning interception vs. Titans
summary: The New York Giants are celebrating after a 12-7 victory against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3 at MetLife Stadium. The Giants held the Titans off the scoreboard for most of the game, but surrendered a fourth-quarter touchdown. The Titans had one more chance to score as the game was winding down, and Tennessee was […]
full_text: Jevon Holland celebrates his game-winning interception on Sunday. | Getty Images The New York Giants are celebrating after a 12-7 victory against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3 at MetLife Stadium. The Giants held the Titans off the scoreboard for most of the game, but surrendered a fourth-quarter touchdown. The Titans had one more chance to score as the game was winding down, and Tennessee was on the doorstep of scoring in the red zone. Giants defensive back Jevon Holland had other plans, though. He picked off Titans quarterback Cam Ward in the end zone, sealing the victory for Big Blue. “As I seen him break the pocket, I’m the free player so I was going to hold him up. If he sees me running at him, he might stop and try to let the ball go. But then I seen him step to stay lateral and find people. He does scramble with his eyes on the field and I just stayed around the front of the end zone,” Holland said postgame. Is there a safety in the league playing better ball than Jevon Holland this season? pic.twitter.com/WUXHQiElt4 — Jason McCourty (@JasonMcCourty) September 27, 2026 The pick was Holland’s third in as many weeks, giving him the league lead. Having his playmaking skills on the back end of the Giants defense is huge and it’s part of why the team is 2-1 through the first three games of the year. Quarterback Jameis Winston said after the game that he told Holland on Friday he would make the key play to win the game on Sunday. Winston proved prescient. Holland’s three interceptions already mark a career high for the sixth-year pro, following his four seasons with the Miami Dolphins and two with the Giants. Holland spoke about why he is seeing a great deal of success out of the gate. “The ball’s just coming my way. I don’t know if anybody can tell you, there’s no rhyme or reason to it. I’m just trying to catch the ones that throw to me. I have been on the jugs though every day, just in case they do this. But other than that, they come in bunches. So the ball’s just been coming my way and I’ve been trying to make sure I’m on my keys and techniques so I’m in the right spot,“ Holland said. Holland and the Giants are back in action in Week 4 as they host the Arizona Cardinals. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside MetLife Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on Paramount Plus.
author: Jeremy Brener

title: Giants-Titans grades: A position-by-position look at Sunday’s victory
summary: The New York Giants escaped sloppy conditions at home with a 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Cam Ward led a 13-play, 70-yard drive at the end of the game that put the Titans in position to score, but Jevon Holland had other plans. The veteran safety intercepted the second-year quarterback and sent […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images The New York Giants escaped sloppy conditions at home with a 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Cam Ward led a 13-play, 70-yard drive at the end of the game that put the Titans in position to score, but Jevon Holland had other plans. The veteran safety intercepted the second-year quarterback and sent his former coach back to Tennessee without a win. The Giants had 238 yards and the Titans finished with 262 yards — 161 of which came on their final two drives. The Giants defense surrendered a 12-play and a 13-play drive on the Titans’ final three possessions, after forcing Ward and Daboll into five straight three-and-outs. New York’s inability to score touchdowns made the situation precarious, but Dominic Zvada’s leg was enough to secure the win. Here are the grades. Quarterback Jameis Winston provided some excitement, but frustrations that have followed Winston’s career were present throughout the game. The offense’s timing was completely off, and the weather made it worse. Winston finished 14 of 22 for 118 yards with two carries for 13 yards. The conditions were rough, but Winston did little to inspire hope as the Giants continue to search for quarterback depth. Grade: C- Running back Cam Skattebo was the only running back used in the first quarter, but the Giants saw a healthy mix of Najee Harris on their 11-play, 44-yard field goal drive; Tyrone Tracy Jr. converted a third-and-2 crack-toss play on his first touch during that drive. Cam Skattebo’s 25-yard gain on third down gave the Giants an opportunity to put points on the board in this sloppy game. The Giants rushed for 138 yards on 33 carries ( 4.2 YPC ). Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards, and Najee Harris had nine carries for 52 yards; Harris looked good, averaging 5.8 yards on the ground. Grade: B Wide receiver The conditions led both offenses to play conservatively. Malik Nabers’ third-and-seven conversion before the first half ended led to a valuable field goal for the Giants. Nabers caught five of six targets for just 25 yards with an important 11-yard slant that secured a first down. Darnell Mooney caught two of three of his targets for 20 yards, and Malachi Fields secured both his targets for 19 yards. The receivers weren’t asked to do too much in the game. Grade: B- Tight end Isaiah Likely was targeted, but the Giants’ passing attack was not in sync. We did, however, see multiple heavy personnel packages that included Patrick Ricard and Chris Manhertz. Likely caught two of his five targets for just 13 yards. The blocking seemed adequate up front from the tight ends, as the Giants found success to the edges of the Titans’ defense Grade: B Offensive line John Michael Schmitz took a holding penalty on the first drive, which spoiled Zaire Barnes’s effort to punch the football out of Chimere Dike’s arms on the opening kickoff. The Giants’ center remains an issue for New York. Andrew Thomas surrendered a third-down sack to rookie Keldric Faulk on an E/T twist up front, and Jermaine Eluemunor had multiple penalties. The Giants did enough with their rushing attack, but the offensive line is surrendering pressures and sacks and suffering penalties that raise concerns. Grade: C- Defensive line D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris were both STOUT at the point of attack. Tennessee wasn’t generating much on the ground; the linebackers were quick to fit, and the line was solid. Harris did, however, accidentally rip Cam Ward down by the facemask. Overall, the defensive line did enough to not get bullied, holding the Titans to just 3.9 yards per carry. Tennessee caught the Giants in some lighter personnel packages, and Tony Pollard ripped off a few runs, which brought his average up to 4.4 YPC. I don’t love how the Titans sustained several drives in the second half. Grade: B Edge A T/E game led to a second-quarter quarterback hit that almost resulted in an intentional grounding penalty. It was good to see Brian Burns draped on a quarterback, who left the game in the fourth quarter with a right knee injury — he dealt with a left ankle injury through the week. There weren’t many impact plays from Kayvon Thibodeaux or Abdul Carter, but Chauncey Golston made two STOPs in the run game, including one with just over a minute left in the game; without Burns on the field, Golston was aligned as an EDGE rusher in crunch time. Grade: B- Linebacker Reese set the tone early on the Titans’ first possession; Tony Pollard hit the line of scrimmage on a second-down run, and Reese met him for a STOP. Reese also made a strong tackle for a loss in the flat. Reese also annihilated a running back in pass protection on a third-down blitz. Tremaine Edmunds was called for a crucial fourth-and-one encroachment penalty that extended the Titans’ drive with 50 seconds remaining. The linebackers flew around the field and made solid plays, but there still seems to be room for improvement. Grade: B- Cornerback Greg Newsome II was sticky and technically sound against Tennessee. He knocked a pass away from Elic Ayomanor on second-and-7 on the Titans’ final drive. He missed one tackle that led to a solid Pollard gain, but was good overall. Colton Hood was not challenged much in the game until he surrendered a touchdown to Wan’Dale Robinson in the fourth quarter. Hood had left the field earlier in the drive, but returned. His leverage was soft to the outside, and Cam Ward took advantage of the rookie’s positioning. Dru Phillips did an excellent job getting his eyes on the football, but could not secure an important interception in the third quarter on a rub concept. Brian Daboll found success in the second half by attacking the Giants with out routes against softer leverage against both Dru Phillips and Hood. Grade: C+ Safety Jevon Holland is a pick MACHINE! A game-winning interception by Holland, who has been the leader of the Giants’ defense. Tyler Nubin did not dress in the game, which put Ar’Darius Washington into the starting lineup. Washington was around the line of scrimmage often in the rainy game, but it was Jevon Holland, again, who continues to make a difference. Holland knocked a ball away from Wan’Dale Robinson on an important third-down when the underneath defender attacked the flat in the smash concept; it was an exceptional effort from Holland. Pinnock made a big tackle for a loss on the outside of a crack-toss play to the boundary. Grade: A + Special teams The Special teams really earned their money against the Tennessee Titans. Giants’ linebacker Zaire Barnes punched the football out of Chimere Dike’s grasp on the opening kickoff – a massive momentum swing caused by special teams that the offense couldn’t turn into points. Jordan Stout continues to be one of the best assets on the Giants. He had a 73-yard punt early in the second quarter. Stout averaged 53 yards on five punts — stud! Dominic Zvada was the Giants’ offense; he booted four field goals: 59, 50, 44, and 30 yards. However, Elijah Campbell’s kick-catch interference negated one of Stout’s punts and gave Tennessee better field position at the end of the game. Grade: A

title: What happened on that last play for the Jets in their loss to the Lions?
summary: In the final minute of their Week 3 loss to the Lions, the Jets had the ball in Detroit territory attempting to put up a game-tying (or perhaps with a two point conversion game-winning) touchdown. Unfortunately for them, former Jets safety Chuck Clark blitzed, and became a free runner. He was able to get a […]
full_text: Detroit Lions edge rusher DJ Wonnum (98) celebrates a sack of New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In the final minute of their Week 3 loss to the Lions, the Jets had the ball in Detroit territory attempting to put up a game-tying (or perhaps with a two point conversion game-winning) touchdown. Unfortunately for them, former Jets safety Chuck Clark blitzed, and became a free runner. He was able to get a strip sack on Geno Smith that Detroit recovered, effectively ending the game. What went wrong? How did Clark get free? As always, I wasn’t in the huddle. I didn’t call the play, and I don’t have access to the Jets’ playbook so all I can do is my best to reverse engineer. In addition to the standard two edges and two interior linemen, the Lions have stuck off ball linebacker Jack Campbell right in the A gap at the line of scrimmage and Clark close to the line of scrimmage threatening a blitz. It looks to me like the Jets put on a three man slide (to the left from the offense’s perspective and to the right from the defense’s and our perspective. This will put the Jets in solid position to block the two defensive linemen (yellow circles) and one of Clark or linebacker (55) Derrick Barnes (blue circles) if either of them blitzes. On the other side, you always want to block defensive linemen with offensive linemen. This leaves Braelon Allen to pick up Campbell if the linebacker blitzes. I would also imagine that Allen would have either Clark or Barnes in a world where Campbell drops into coverage, and both Barnes and Clark blitz. Remember, even with their three man slide, the Jets have four potential Lions blitzers on that side of the defensive formation. If Allen is freed of his responsibility to take Campbell, he can help. Off the snap, you will see that Myers is sliding to his left (our right). Backup left guard Jordan Meredith who came on for an injured Dylan Parham has defensive tackle Alim McNeill, but seems to be sliding with the defensive tackle towards Myers. Braelon Allen meanwhile is moving over to pick up the blitzing Campbell. Based on the protection, my guess is that Meredith was supposed to pass McNeill off to Myers, and then jump out to get the blitzing Clark. Instead, Clark gets home as a free runner and gets the strip sack that clinches the game. View Link It’s easy to pin this on some miscommunication with a backup offensive lineman who just entered the game missing his assignment. And that is a big part of the story here. Still, I think Geno Smith and Josh Myers have to take an appreciable share of the blame for this play. It’s tough for me to look at this front, and think the Jets were in the optimal protection scheme. If my read on this play is correct, the Jets were sliding away from a linebacker threatening the A gap and asking Braelon Allen to go across the formation to pick him up. Then they were asking a newly inserted guard to pass off a defensive tackle aligned to his outside to the lineman on his inside and pick up a blitzing safety in short order. This strikes me as a much easier protection to execute if the Jets just slide Myers to the linebacker threatening the A gap and let Allen pick up the blitzing safety to his side. I know it isn’t always easy to tell who is blitzing, but we are just talking about the ease of these blocks based on the alignment here. I think you’d rather have the center protecting the A gap with a linebacker mugging the line of scrimmage as a potential blitzer than force a running back to go across the formation to pick that up. My guess is the Jets thought number 55 Derrick Barnes was a more likely blitzer than Clark. In that case, Myers would likely get him, and the slide to the offense’s left/defense’s right could have worked. In any event, I strongly suspect Smith and Myers should have reset the protection here. What I can say with 100 percent confidence is this play ended the Jets’ chances at an upset victory.
author: John B

title: Jets vs. Lions: The joys of finding silver linings in a loss
summary: When you watch a team like the 2026 New York Jets take the field, I think you need to judge them simultaneously in parallel ways. Of course the result of that day’s game matters. You would rather win than lose. But the Jets are also focusing on the long term, attempting to finally launch a […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Kenyon Sadiq #16 of the New York Jets celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you watch a team like the 2026 New York Jets take the field, I think you need to judge them simultaneously in parallel ways. Of course the result of that day’s game matters. You would rather win than lose. But the Jets are also focusing on the long term, attempting to finally launch a successful rebuild after a decade and a half of failure to do so. The Jets this season are unlikely to have a winning record. They just don’t have the talent to win more than they lose. There are different types of losses, though. Sometimes you can take legitimate positives from a defeat. So often in recent years with the Jets the concept of “moral victories” comes up when the Jets fall short on the scoreboard. I generally don’t believe in moral victories in the NFL. But when I say that I think it’s important to explain how I personally define a moral victory. To me a moral victory is being happy with a loss because the team can’t do any better. That’s not how I feel after most Jets losses, and that isn’t how I feel after their Week 3 defeat to Detroit. There are many areas where the team fell short in the game. For starters, I think we can say that anybody declaring the Jets an elite defense before this game got way ahead of themselves. Shutting down the hapless Titans and the struggling Packers is one thing. Against one of the best collections of offensive talent in the league, the Jets played a quality first half on the defensive side of the ball. However, the second half was ugly. It wasn’t just that Detroit had more talent than the Jets. The Jets just didn’t play effective or smart football. Detroit’s success was as much about the Jets’ failures as its own execution. There were failures elsewhere from special teams to the offensive line. The Jets just didn’t make enough plays in what turned into a coin flip game. This team should be frustrated and disappointed for letting a winnable game get away. Moral victories should be off the table. With that said, I don’t think noting several positive indicators from this game for the future constitutes a moral victory. The biggest was arguably the play of rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq. The Jets desperately needed Sadiq to step up with three major contributors at wide receiver and tight end sidelined by injury. Sadiq had been kept on a pitch count in the early phases of the season recovering from his own injury. This was a true breakout game. Sadiq made a spectacular 24 yard touchdown catch in the second quarter. It was just the start. Sadiq made play after play in the game on his way to a 7 catch, 105 yard game, joining Garrett Wilson as the Jets put a pair of receivers over the century mark. This Sadiq breakout is important for the Jets for reasons that go beyond the generic, “We want our rookie tight end to look good,” hopes (although those are important too). The Jets are a team likely to pick a quarterback in the early rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft. If there is one thing that the New York Jets have proven as a franchise over the past two decades it’s that the surroundings of a young quarterback matter a lot. College offenses just don’t train quarterbacks to be successful in the NFL. Without a strong infrastructure, most young quarterbacks will fail in the pros. If Sadiq reaches his potential and becomes a true matchup nightmare on this level, the Jets will be able to put a young quarterback into an offense with a dynamic one-two punch of Kenyon Sadiq and Garrett Wilson. That could provide critical support to an inexperienced signal caller. Just as significant is what Sadiq represents for the franchise’s long-term health. The Draft pick used to select Sadiq in April did not appear out of thin air. The Jets traded one of their best players, Sauce Gardner, eleven months ago to get it along with an additional first rounder. The team also traded another of its best players, Quinnen Williams to get two additional Draft selections. These picks are at the heart of the Jets’ current rebuild attempts. As seasoned NFL fans know, it is nice to extract good value in Draft pick compensation trading away star players. At the end of the day, though, how you use the picks is the most important thing. Early signs are the Jets have nailed the Sadiq selection, which should inspire confidence in a regime that had a very shaky first year, albeit under trying circumstances. Another positive that comes to mind is simply the way the Jets fought back in this game to tie it up after the Lions took a two touchdown lead in the fourth quarter. Seasoned watchers of the Jets could have been forgiven for feeling like they had seen this story before. The Jets give a superior opponent a tough game for two and a half to three quarters and then fade. The game gets out of hand. It felt like we were headed in that direction. Then the Jets mounted a rally. For me it was how they mounted a rally. A year ago, the Jets overcame a 20 point fourth quarter deficit in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to briefly take the lead, but it felt more like the Tampa Bay’s conservative play and a flukey field goal block were bigger contributors to the comeback than anything the Jets did. One year later, we saw another Week 3 comeback, but this was different. The Jets were making plays and looked like a professional football operation, executing plays against a respected opponent. In a year where showing competence is at the top of the list for objectives, this comeback should be notable for that reason. I’m sure some of you are reading this and asking yourself, “Didn’t you just complain about the team’s play last week against the Packers because they lost? What’s the difference?” Well reasonable people can disagree, but I wasn’t overly impressed by Green Bay. Past success aside, I saw in the Packers what looked like a mediocre football team through the first two weeks of the season, and the Jets let a winnable game get away. I don’t think what happened on Thursday night did much to change my view. Almost any team would have been competitive against Green Bay last week the way that team played. Detroit in Ford Field is a different story. Plenty of past Jets teams would have been run out of the building in this game. Winning this one was a tall order. That isn’t to say the Jets should be satisfied by losing. Merely I will say that what we want to see from this season are big time Sadiq performances and the Jets playing professional football. The performance the Jets showed in Week 3 will win them games against lesser opponents. That matters in a season like 2026 for this team.
author: John B

A week ago the Jets dominated the Green Bay Packers for most of the game. They led by double digits early in the fourth quarter before imploding and letting […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 27: Chase Claypool #10 of the Chicago Bears gets tackled by Soloman Thomas #94 and C.J. Mosley #57 of New York Jets in the first half at MetLife Stadium on November 27, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. On Sunday the Jets suffered another devastating loss. Unfortunately, the Lions rallied, retaking the lead at 31 – 24 with just under two minutes to play. They will play their third game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football this week. The Bears suffered a costly injury to their starting quarterback Caleb Williams last week. Without Williams the Bears offense struggled badly, putting up just three points in a 9 – 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings last week. Tyson Bagent stepped in for Williams and was ineffective. If Williams remains out against the Jets that will greatly improve the Jets’ chances to get back on the winning track next week. title: Kenyon Sadiq makes history in Jets loss
summary: The New York Jets came up just short on Sunday in a 31 – 24 loss to the Detroit Lions. With just under a minute left in regulation, the Jets were deep in Lions territory, driving for the potential game winning touchdown. Geno Smith dropped back to pass, Chuck Clark of the Lions blitzed unblocked, […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: tight end Kenyon Sadiq #16 of the New York Jets runs the ball against cornerback D.J. Reed #4 of the Detroit Lions during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The New York Jets came up just short on Sunday in a 31 – 24 loss to the Detroit Lions. With just under a minute left in regulation, the Jets were deep in Lions territory, driving for the potential game winning touchdown. Geno Smith dropped back to pass, Chuck Clark of the Lions blitzed unblocked, and Clark stripped the ball from Geno. The Lions recovered the fumble and with the Jets out of timeouts, that was essentially the ballgame. It was the second straight heartbreaking loss for the Jets after losing in overtime to the Green Bay Packers the week prior. Despite the devastating loss, there were some positives to take from the game. Geno Smith played well for the most part at quarterback and racked up more than 300 yards passing, something no Jets quarterback accomplished all of last season. Garrett Wilson played a dominant game at wide receiver, with 10 receptions for 107 yards and a touchdown. It was the first 100 yard receiving game for Wilson since December 2024. Those were very encouraging performances, but perhaps the most encouraging performance on offense for the Jets was turned in by rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq was drafted by the Jets with the 16th overall selection in the first round of the 2026 NFL draft. He was expected to be a difference maker for the Jets offense, but he suffered a setback with a hernia injury that required surgery in the offseason. Sadiq missed virtually all of the Jets OTAs, virtually all of training camp and all of the Jets preseason games. With so much missed time it was difficult to know what to expect from Sadiq this season as he worked hard to catch up with his teammates. Sadiq was worked into the lineup slowly by the Jets as they explored how much they could put on his plate to start the season. Through two games Sadiq had just five receptions on six targets, good for a modest 38 yards, along with a three yard touchdown on the ground. It was a perfectly fine start given the circumstances, but Jets fans craved more. On Sunday the Jets needed more from the young tight end. The Jets were down to just two receivers from the original 53 man roster of just two weeks prior. They had Garrett Wilson. They had Isaiah Williams. And they had a whole bunch of question marks. The Jets needed Sadiq to step up. Boy did he ever. Sadiq broke loose for seven receptions and 105 yards on eight targets, including a spectacular diving grab for a touchdown early in the game. It was more than anyone could have reasonably expected from the young tight end so early in his career. As it turns out, it was a historic performance. No rookie Jets tight end has had a 100+ yard game earlier than Sadiq in the history of the New York Jets. You have to go all the way back to the early 70s to find anyone matching Sadiq’s precocious brilliance. In 1970 Jets rookie tight end Rich Caster had a four reception, 138 yards performance in his third NFL game. Two years later Jerome Barkum put up a six reception, 102 yards performance in his third NFL game. Those are arguably the two greatest tight ends in Jets history, with Mickey Shuler the only other player who might stake a claim. Two all time great Jets matched what Sadiq pulled off on Sunday, and nobody has done it since. Just one other Jets rookie tight end has had a 100 yard performance at any point in their rookie season. In 2008 Dustin Keller turned the trick in the ninth game of his rookie year. Just three games into his career, Kenyon Sadiq is already up there with Jets royalty, despite missing virtually all of his first NFL offseason. He is undoubtedly the most physically talented tight end the Jets have ever drafted. He may be the most physically talented tight end ever to don an NFL uniform. He is certainly in the upper echelons in that regard. Physical talent alone won’t make Sadiq a star. Long time Jets fans might remember a similarly talented Jets tight end named Johnny Mitchell, drafted by the Jets with the 15th overall selection in the 1992 NFL draft. Mitchell was a physical freak, but he was also a bonehead. He never optimized all his talent; never really came close. Within five years Mitchell was out of the league, having squandered his other worldly physical gifts. Talent alone won’t get it done, but Sadiq appears to have the temperament, the intelligence and the drive to make the most of his. It’s much too early to predict great things from Kenyon Sadiq, but my goodness, he certainly made a statement on Sunday. Sadiq made history. Jets fans may be forgiven if visions of the best tight end in Jets history are dancing through their heads right now. It’s up to Sadiq to make those visions a reality.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets vs Lions: Jets turn the ball over late, sealing a hard fought loss to Lions
summary: In the New York Jets’ third game of the 2026 season, under the dome in Ford Field, Detroit, Michigan, the Jets fell to the Detroit Lions, 31 – 24. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They went nowhere and punted. The Lions returned the favor. Then the Jets followed suit. The Lions again […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions scores a touchdown against the New York Jets during the second quarter at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ third game of the 2026 season, under the dome in Ford Field, Detroit, Michigan, the Jets fell to the Detroit Lions, 31 – 24. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They went nowhere and punted. The Lions returned the favor. Then the Jets followed suit. The Lions again returned the favor. So it went through a scintillating scoreless first quarter. The Jets punted the ball to the Lions to start the second quarter. The Lions proceeded to put together the best drive of the game thus far. A heavy dose of Jahmyr Gibbs brought the ball deep into Jets territory before the drive bogged down and the Lions had to settle for a short field goal and an early 3 – 0 lead. The Jets stormed back with a long drive that ended when Geno Smith threaded the needle into an ultra-tight window to Kenyon Sadiq in the end zone for a touchdown The extra point gave the Jets a 7 – 3 lead late in the half. The Lions roared right back as the dormant offenses on both sides came to life. Detroit put together a long drive culminating in a touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown to give the Lions the lead at 10 – 7 with less than two minutes left in the first half. The Jets then ran one of their patented two minute drills in which they looked utterly lost. The drive ended without incident and the Jets went into the locker room at halftime down by three points at Lions 10, Jets 7. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. It did not go well. The Jets defense offered only token resistance as the Lions basically took whatever they wanted on their opening drive of the second half. Jahmyr Gibbs closed it out with a brilliant 17 yard touchdown run, reversing fields and weaving through a helpless Jets defense. The Lions touchdown gave them a double digit lead at 17 – 7 to start the third quarter. The Jets were left in a position they could not afford, needing to play catch up in a shootout in Detroit. The Jets responded with a drive highlighted by a spectacular 32 yard grab by Garrett Wilson. They got the ball down inside the Lions’ 10 yard line before back-to-back sacks of Geno Smith resulted in a 42 yard Jason Sanders field goal and a seven point Lions lead at 17 – 10 midway through the third quarter. The Lions then put together a long drive featuring heavy doses of Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs. As the third quarter ended the Lions were inside the Jets one yard line, looking to take a two touchdown lead. On the first play of the fourth quarter Jahmyr Gibbs ran it in. It was the Lions’ fourth consecutive scoring drive as the Jets vaunted defense had no answers for the Lions’ offense. The score was now 24 – 10 in favor of the Lions. The Jets fought back. They put together a long drive ending with a Geno Smith strike to Jeremy Ruckert in the end zone. A two point attempt was stopped and the Jets trailed the Lions 24 – 16 with a little more than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter. If the Jets were to have a chance to win, they would need to stop the Lions offense on the next drive for the first time since the first quarter of the game. The Jets defense came up big here. They stopped the Lions on fourth and two and the Jets offense took over near midfield with excellent field position and more than eight minutes left in regulation. Geno Smith and the Jets went to work. On fourth and six just outside the Lions 20 yard line Aaron Glenn took a chance. He went for the first down instead of the field goal, and he was rewarded. Geno threw a strike to Garrett Wilson at the goal line and the Jets trailed 24 – 22. A two point conversion attempt found paydirt with Sterling Shepard and the game was tied at 24 with just over four minutes left. It didn’t last. The Lions roared back with a quick drive highlighted by a 49 yard completion to Isaac Teslaa. A few plays later Jared Goff found Jahmyr Gibbs for a touchdown and a 31 – 24 lead with just over two minutes remaining in a barnburner. The Jets got the ball down inside the Lions’ 30 yard line with just under a minute to play. It looked like they just might tie the game. Then disaster struck. Old friend Chuck Clark blitzed Geno Smith for a strip sack. The Lions recovered the fumble. The Jets were out of timeouts, so the game effectively ended on that play. Final score: Lions 31, Jets 24. The Jets fought hard and got themselves into position to possibly win the game late, but in the end they fell short in a disappointing loss. The loss brought the Jets’ record to 1-2. The Jets stay on the road next week as they head to Chicago, Illinois to take on the Bears, looking to avoid a 1-3 start to the season.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets vs Lions Game Thread
summary: Last week the New York Jets had their 2026 home opener against the Green Bay Packers. It did not go well. Today the Jets try to get back on the winning track as they take to the road against the Detroit Lions. Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 1 PM under the dome at Ford […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 18: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions throws the ball during the first half against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 18, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They led by double digits early in the fourth quarter. A 2-0 start to the season looked imminent. Then it all fell apart. title: J.J. McCarthy joins the NFC East
summary: There’s a new quarterback in the NFC East. In the aftermath of Jaxson Dart suffering a season-ending injury last week, the New York Giants have reportedly acquired J.J. McCarthy in a trade with Minnesota Vikings. McCarthy has become a meme (quite literally) since his NFL career hasn’t gone well for him thus far. The No. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the start of a preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Ravens defeated the Vikings 13-3. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a new quarterback in the NFC East. In the aftermath of Jaxson Dart suffering a season-ending injury last week, the New York Giants have reportedly acquired J.J. McCarthy in a trade with Minnesota Vikings. McCarthy has become a meme ( quite literally ) since his NFL career hasn’t gone well for him thus far. The No. 10 overall pick from the 2024 NFL Draft missed his entire rookie season due to injury before throwing 11 touchdowns to 12 interceptions for a 72.6 passer rating last year. With the Vikings adding Kyler Murray and re-signing Carson Wentz, McCarthy’s struggles dropped him to being Minnesota’ third quarterback option. Not great. From an optics standpoint, I can get why people think it’s funny for the Giants to trade for him as it relates to any improbable effort to help keep their season alive. But I don’t think this is a bad trade for the G-Men. What’s the downside? Giving up a 2027 fifth-round pick? They already were projected to have two of them in that round so they still have one. McCarthy, who turns 24 in January, probably stinks. He might not even get on the field ahead of Jameis Winston? But McCarthy is probably better than Jake Haener, who was QB2 in Week 3. And if the Giants reach a point later this season where they’re eliminated, there’s really nothing to learn from playing Winston. They could look to play McCarthy and hope he shows some potential, either as a future option for them (backup or otherwise) or a potential trade piece in the offseason. McCarthy is under contract for the 2027 season. Unless Winston gets hurt or egregiously struggles, I’m guessing the Philadelphia Eagles won’t see McCarthy when the Birds face the Giants in Week 9. But maybe he’ll be starting by the time the Eagles take on the Giants again in Week 18.

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In light of the Philadelphia Eagles’ interior offensive line struggles, some have wondered if the team might be interested in bringing Mekhi Becton back to Philly. There have been calls for a reunion from some community members here at Bleeding Green Nation: Becton is no longer a free agent after signing to the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad on Monday morning, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler . Becton also reportedly drew interest from the Pittsburgh Steelers. No word of any interest from the Eagles, who currently still have an open roster spot. There was reporting on the Eagles’ lack of interest in Becton earlier this year from Tony Pauline: “During Shrine Bowl week, I was told that Becton has returned to many of his former ways, including firing the agency that helped get his game back on track, and that has raised red flags with the Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles were surprised (if not shocked) and disappointed by the turn of events.“ Becton’s career has taken a turn for the worse ever since his Super Bowl LIX success. After the 2024 season, he left Philly to sign with the Los Angeles Chargers in free agency. Becton struggled and got benched while the Bolts fielded one of the worst offensive lines in the NFL. Becton was cut by the Chargers after 2025 and remained available as a free agent until joining the Packers, who are in desperate need of offensive line help. If the Eagles felt like Becton was part of the solution moving forward, they would’ve made a better effort to bring him back.

title: Eagles News: Saquon Barkley says Philadelphia’s run game is “going to be something scary”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles’ run game is already something scary! Just … not in a good way at the moment. Philadelphia ranks tied for 18th in yards per carry (3.9). Will it get significantly better than this? Maybe. Perhaps Cam Jurgens and Drew […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles’ run game is already something scary! Just … not in a good way at the moment. Philadelphia ranks tied for 18th in yards per carry (3.9). Will it get significantly better than this? Maybe. Perhaps Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall get more comfortable in their new roles. Instead of merely banking on that, it could be good for the Eagles to try to pass more often to set up the running game as opposed to the other way around. What’s your confidence in this running game finding their groove? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … ‘Going to be a beautiful thing:’ Saquon Barkley believes running game is close – NBCSP “It’s not a finished product and we don’t want it to be a finished product in week two, week three,” Barkley said. “You want to continue to go like this (motions upward), just got to buy in, continue to buy in. It’s all relatively new to all of us in the run game. We’re still learning and trying to continue to buy into something new. We’re going out there and we’re seeing some funky looks and weird looks. It’s a sign that the defense (is) still respecting the run game, which has opened up other things, but it’s going to be a beautiful thing when we’re all firing at the same page. You know, and talking to (Jalen) and the guys about it and talking to the o-line, it’s not like a sense of any panic. Everybody wants the big numbers, but I’m in a good spot of knowing that the work that’s being put in and just continue to focus on our process and the results will come. I wish I could tell you that they were going to come in Week One. I wish I could guarantee it’s going to come in Week Three. You just never know, but I know that the results will come and when we get this thing rolling, it’s going to be something scary.” Eagles mailbag: Riq Woolen is good, offensive scheme issues, and more – PhillyVoice First, the run game has to work. If the Eagles fail to get that going throughout the season, they’re already dead in the water. Big picture, the Eagles have had their special seasons when the run game is dominant. When it’s not, they’re an easy out in the playoffs. But then also, the run game has to work for the scheme to run the way it’s intended. A huge feature of this scheme is that at the snap, run plays and pass plays look alike. The marriage of the run and pass keeps defenses off balance and guessing, and that’s when the play action game can really start humming. Absent an efficient run game, the scheme is simply not going to operate at a high level. Over the course of the season, the offensive line is going to have to figure it out and gel together, and the only way to do that is to continue to run it. So, spoiler: They’re going to continue to run it, a lot. That said, in the short term, it does make sense to lean on Hurts while he is balling and the run game is struggling. Also, running into brick walls for two or fewer yards on every first down play, and then converting on long third downs is not going to be sustainable. So there’s a balance. They can’t just quit on the run game, but at the same time they can’t let their crappy run game kill their offense. Tough situation. Eagles-Bears burning questions: What can Zach Ertz offer? Will the run game finally click? – The Athletic Berman: I expect Barkley to be unaffected by the injury, aside from the cowboy collar and a return to his college stance. Whether that invigorates the rushing attack is a bigger question. The Eagles simply aren’t getting the easy yards. They entered the week 25th in yards before contact and 23rd in rushes for zero or negative yards. That’s not a problem a healthy running back solves; that’s on the offensive line to play better. I’d be confident that if the line can create yards, Barkley can explode for big runs. He doesn’t have space to navigate at this point. Eagles will reportedly face Case Keenum as the Bears’ starting quarterback – BGN After a lot uncertainty leading up to the Eagles’ Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Bears, NFL insider Jay Glazer reported on Sunday that Chicago plans to give third-string QB Case Keenum the start, and Tyson Bagent will serve as the backup. This will be Keenum’s first regular season action since 2023. Caleb Williams was confirmed to have a grade 2 hamstring injury which will sideline him for several weeks, and while Bagent is typically the Bears QB2, he was in the concussion protocol for the majority of the week and unable to prepare much heading into Monday night’s game. Bagent was cleared to play over the weekend, so he’ll at least be available, but putting him in to lead an offense with little to no starting reps, apparently wasn’t the ideal move in Ben Johnson’s mind. Chicago Bears vs. Philadelphia Eagles Game Picks and Predictions – Windy City Gridiron Lester: Bears win a close one, 23-21. Chicago gets back to its ground-and-pound identity, and they establish the run, while the quarterbacking, whoever it may be, is under 200 yards but efficient with several schemed-up short completions. The Eagles try to pick on rookie Malik Muhammad, but he rises to the moment with an interception. Tory Taylor has his banana ball floating around, and he keeps Philly’s returners off balance. Eagles vs. Bears: Predictions, odds, injury updates, and why people are talking about kickoffs again – Inquirer Once again, the way the Eagles interpret a rule and how they use it to their advantage, is under the microscope. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Friday that special teams coordinators were meeting Friday to clarify a rule “that some teams are believed to have misunderstood — or found a loophole in — through the first two weeks of the season.” Did you notice Braden Mann on the field holding for Jake Elliott on kickoffs in Week 2? It was really hot in Nashville, but it wasn’t windy. Special teams coordinator Michael Clay watches every snap of special teams play on Monday mornings. He noticed the Atlanta Falcons using a holder in Week 1 and decided to have the Eagles work on it. Mann angled the ball a certain way, and Elliott liked the way it looked in practice enough to use it in the game. The Eagles allowed 30.8 yards per kick return on five attempts in Week 1 and 25.3 on four returns in Week 2. “I’m sure it’s different for every kicker, but just the way I was able to make the ball move in the air, I liked what I was able to accomplish with that,” Elliott said Friday. Now, apparently, there’s an effort to make sure the 12th player on the field acting as the holder puts the ball on a tee and not the ground. Elliott said he didn’t think adding a tee to the equation would impact Mann’s ability to angle the ball for him to kick. Young Eagles defender was picked apart. Now, things are different: ‘Ain’t no telling with Vic’ – NJ.com Andrew Mukuba played through a knee injury, but he claims that it did not affect his performance. “It ain’t no telling with Vic,” Mukuba said about Fangio’s positive review of his Week 2 performance. “So he might be proud, he might be happy, he might be not so happy. So it ain’t no telling with Vic. But I’m always holding the standard high for myself. But it’s always good to hear your DC saying you’re doing what you’re supposed to do. But I got a higher standard for myself, though.” Mukuba finished with six tackles against the Titans, but he could have made more. “With me, I’m always leaning on being hard on myself,” Mukuba said. “I could have done a lot of things better. Vic going to say that, but for me personally, I feel I could have played a better game, to be honest. Not that I played a bad game,…

title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 30-27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: And just like that, the Steelers aren’t bad again. Following a listless performance on offense in Week 2, Pittsburgh won a shootout over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3 . As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Steelers show resiliency Following last week’s ugly defeat at the hands of the New […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Roman Wilson #14 celebrates his touchdown with Max Iheanachor #71 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images And just like that, the Steelers aren’t bad again. Following a listless performance on offense in Week 2, Pittsburgh won a shootout over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3 . As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. Steelers show resiliency Following last week’s ugly defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots, I wrote that I wanted to see how the Steelers would respond to a loss under the team’s new coaching staff. It’s safe to say the team made the right adjustments under head coach Mike McCarthy. After a horribly incompetent Week 2 on offense, the Steelers dropped 30 points on a Bengals defense that has been surprisingly solid to open the season. That’s not to say it was a perfect showing, but it was a far cry from the unit’s multi-level failures last week. “Resiliency is critical to any type of success, whether it’s playing one division game or overcoming a loss last week.” McCarthy said postgame. “Momentum is a huge part of our game. It’s a hard-working football team. … Once you get through the first of everything as a team, there’s usually bumps that you go through, so, they’ve stayed the course.” While the Patriots loss was an abnormally bad game, it’s fair to say that there was always going to be some turbulence early in the McCarthy era as Pittsburgh adjusted to its first new head coach since 2007. The ride has indeed been bumpy through three games, but the team showed the poise to not let a disaster last week spiral out of control. It’s still difficult to get a read on the 2026 Steelers. But given the improvement this week from the last, that’s a good problem to have at the moment. 2. The offensive line shows up One of the through lines of last week’s loss was how thoroughly Pittsburgh’s offensive front was dominated by the Patriots’ defensive line. Not one player in Pittsburgh’s starting five had a good game. But despite playing against an improved Cincinnati front on Sunday led by all-world nose tackle Dexter Lawrence, the Steelers’ offensive line was largely fantastic in both the run and pass game. Pittsburgh averaged an impressive six yards per rush, while quarterback Aaron Rodgers was sacked only twice — once on a blitz pickup miscommunication, and another on an extended play. Of course, Pittsburgh’s sudden success in this area of the game clearly correlates with a significant change this week, swapping out right tackle Dylan Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson for first-round rookie Max Iheanachor and veteran backup Brock Hoffman, respectively. While I wasn’t able to keep an eye on him on every play, Iheanachor seemed to have a stellar debut. His easy athleticism shines in his mirroring in pass protection and explosion off the ball as a run blocker. His initial charting backed the eye test — according to New Gen Stats, he only allowed three pressures on 36 pass-blocking reps, including a 75% one-on-one rate. look at Iheanachor firing out of his stance https://t.co/ijcIHyJACW pic.twitter.com/9WHq75ZY7X — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 27, 2026 At guard, Hoffman’s first Steelers start might not have been as flashy, but he still put together a key performance limiting Lawrence’s impact alongside Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick. Despite having two new names on the line, it was the most coordinated the group has looked all season by a mile. And the strong pass protection numbers weren’t juiced by an exceptionally fast time to throw by Rodgers, either. In fact, according to ESPN’s Benjamin Solak, Rodgers’ 3.19-second average time to throw on Sunday was the longest of his Steelers career. The Pittsburgh offensive line finally clicking with Iheanachor in the lineup was great news, not just in the context of the Bengals’ game, but for the long-term prospects of a team that has spent heavy resources trying to rebuild the group in recent seasons. There’s still a lot of football to be played before sweeping pronouncements, of course, but the Steelers’ offensive line looked promising on Sunday. 3. Jaylen Warren is RB1 OK, maybe Jaylen Warren played a little bit too much on Sunday, given his legs were the only thing stopping him by the time the fourth quarter rolled around. Jaylen Warren on his stumble: "I wasn't tired. My body was tired." pic.twitter.com/YGzPYaYkzK — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) September 27, 2026 But overall, Warren’s performance in Week 3 showed exactly why he should be getting a larger workload moving forward. Against the Bengals, he finished with 127 rushing yards and a 7.5-yard average, not including an 87-yard run that was taken back due to a questionable holding call. And in the passing game, Warren added another 49 receiving yards, and continued to shine as a pass protector. Boy did PIttsburgh need this. Steelers came into this game averaging the fewest points and yards thru 2 games in Aaron Rodgers career pic.twitter.com/HVJhJxg14g — trey wingo (@wingoz) September 27, 2026 As those long runs showed, Warren’s long speed isn’t enough to take every big break to the house, but his burst and contact balance remain excellent. He’s an every-down threat who continues to deserve more playing time than he’s usually given. Warren remains one of the NFL’s most underrated running backs. He’s also clearly been the Steelers’ best and most consistent skill position player through three weeks. Sunday finally showed what he can do in a bell-cow role. 4. The defense could’ve used Joey Porter Jr. Despite giving up 27 points on Sunday, I’m far from worried about the Steelers defense. The Joe Burrow/Ja’Marr Chase/Tee Higgins/Chase Brown attack was going to be better than anything Pittsburgh had faced up to that point in the season, and sure enough, that elite offensive core made some elite plays on Sunday. If there’s anything to be slightly perturbed by, it should be the Steelers’ pass rush not making much of an impact until later in the game, only sacking Burrow once. Still, Pittsburgh’s edge room is made up of proven players, and having receivers who get open with the ease of Chase and Higgins remains a great antidote to pressure. And those pass catchers might’ve been better minimized if the Steelers had their best cover corner available on Sunday. Pittsburgh clearly didn’t trust its defensive backs in man coverage against the Bengals’ star duo, but instead, Burrow picked them apart in zone. Asante Samuel Jr. put together a respectable effort matching up against Higgins, but clearly couldn’t match the latter’s size and contested catch ability. Samuel was eventually benched for rookie Daylen Everette, who has more traditional boundary corner size. Porter would’ve given the Steelers a bigger presence at corner to match up with Higgins, and his press-man speciality, along with Jamel Dean, would’ve allowed the team to switch up more coverage concepts. Ultimately, the Steelers will want Porter down the line if they want the defense to live up to its potential this season, and the star corner has said he’ll “ definitely ” play at some point — whatever that means. Of course, it’ll be interesting to see what Porter’s return timeline looks like as the Steelers enter a short week ahead of a matchup against the Cleveland Browns. 5. Odds and ends Sample sizes are a funny thing. In two of the Steelers’ three games so far this season, Rodgers has largely played well and done a better job pushing the ball downfield and extending plays than he did in most of 2025. It’ll be interesting what the trend looks like over the rest of the season. Ben Skowronek caught a touchdown pass and recovered a key fumble when the Bengals muffed a punt. One of the most underrated Steelers had an underrated performance on Sunday. For as impressive as…

title: The Morning After: Jaylen Warren needs to be the Steelers’ bell cow
summary: When you give the ball to Jaylen Warren, good things tend to happen. The former undrafted product of Oklahoma State had one of the best games of his career on Sunday against the Bengals, compiling a career-high 176 yards from scrimmage (127 rushing, 49 receiving) and was the engine that drove the Steelers’ offense out […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you give the ball to Jaylen Warren, good things tend to happen. The former undrafted product of Oklahoma State had one of the best games of his career on Sunday against the Bengals, compiling a career-high 176 yards from scrimmage (127 rushing, 49 receiving) and was the engine that drove the Steelers’ offense out of the abyss and into relevancy. In Weeks 1 and 2, the Steelers’ ranked 27th in EPA per rush. As we head into the final game of Week 3, they sit comfortably in seventh place out of the 30 that have played thus far. Their yards per rush also skyrocketed from 27th in the league in the first two weeks (3.39) to second (6.0). Warren did this as the sole running back. Rico Dowdle was out with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, which left Warren to carry the ball 17 times, which is a new career high. And in his first game as a true bell cow back, Warren showed he is more than capable of being the straw that stirs the drink in the Steelers’ backfield. While the Steelers will certainly feature Dowdle when he is healthy – and they should – it should not be a 50-50 split. Warren showed it when he shared a backfield with Najee Harris and he’s showing it now – he is the Steelers most dynamic playmaker when he gets the ball in his hands. Feeding No. 30 should be a priority for Pittsburgh, especially this coming Thursday against a Browns team that ranks 26th in defensive EPA per rush. It’s the morning after game day, and the Steelers have life. Steelers offensive line dominates The offensive line play from Week 2 to Week 3 was night and day. After being the fourth-most pressured quarterback in the NFL across the first two weeks, per Sumer Sports , Aaron Rodgers was the ninth-lowest pressured quarterback of 30 qualified QBs thus far. Despite facing a Bengals defense that is fourth in the NFL in sacks, the Steelers’ offensive line kept Rodgers clean throughout most of the afternoon. Troy Fautanu allowed just two pressures after a shaky performance against the New England Patriots. Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick cleaned up after a sloppy performance, as well, but it was the new right side that was the ultimate game-changer for Pittsburgh. Right guard Brock Hoffman allowed zero pressures on 59 snaps. Rookie Max Iheanachor allowed just two pressures and was not credited with giving up a sack. The extra time allowed Rodgers to push the ball downfield. Two of his three touchdown passes were on deep balls (20+ yards downfield), and he averaged 8.34 yards per attempt when he had a clean pocket to throw from, which was good for ninth in the league. If the Steelers want to get into the playoffs and actually make a run, this is the type of play they will need – keep Rodgers clean, let him push the ball downfield, and balance it out with a dynamic ground game. They just showed they are capable of doing exactly that. Steelers miss Joey Porter Jr This was the first time this season where it was evident the Steelers were missing Joey Porter Jr. The Steelers showed zone on 48 snaps. Joe Burrow went 24-of-31 against zone coverage for 226 yards and. touchdown. Pittsburgh played man on just five snaps, which is where the services of Porter were really missed. Had he been active, the Steelers almost certainly would have felt more comfortable deploying more man coverages with No. 24 lined up on either Ja’Marr Chase or Tee Higgins. Instead, Burrow went a perfect 4-for-4 against man coverage with a touchdown. When you sit in zone all game against a great quarterback, he’ll happily nickel and dime you to death down the field, which is what Burrow and the Bengals largely did. Of their five scoring drives, four featured at least eight plays, and two totaled at least 11 plays in length. The Bengals weren’t incredible explosive, but they didn’t have to be. Burrow was getting rid of the ball in just over 2.5 seconds, which rendered the Steelers’ pass rush completely null and void until the game’s final drive. The Steelers got the win, but it could have been a bit more decisive had Porter been on the field. Quick hitters Robert Spears-Jennings has been a special teams stud. He registered his eighth special teams tackle on Sunday, per Ross McCorkle . That puts him on pace for 45 on the year – an insane number. I’m kind of over the Roman Wilson experience. It’s constantly one step forward, one step back. He sprung open on the pick play on the first drive for a touchdown, and then let a ball bounce off his hands for an interception later on. Germie Bernard then came in and made a difficult sliding grab for a 14-yard gain and a first down. More of 17, less of 14 going forward. This was the most Ben Skowronek game of all time. One catch for a touchdown and a fumble recovery on a muffed punt that led to a crucial field goal. The ultimate blue collar player. DK Metcalf’s struggles will get overshadowed due to him reaching the end zone and the Steelers winning, but three catches for 31 yards marks another slow day. He also had a pair of penalties, one of which negated an 87-yard run. Can’t go without talking about the incredible play by Derrick Harmon (although I’m unsure why they call him DJ). The Bengals were in Steelers territory, Harmon busts through the center of the offensive line and calls game. The future is bright for him and the Steelers’ defensive interior as a whole. Darnell Washington needs to get no less than five targets per game. 90 percent of the time, he catches a five yard pass and turns it into a big gain because no one can tackle him. Why getting him the ball isn’t a higher priority is beyond me. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!
