title: 3 stars from the 49ers’ resilient win: George Kittle makes a statement
summary: It wasn’t the prettiest. It wasn’t the easiest. But at the end of the day, they don’t ask how; they ask how many. And now the answer is three, with the San Francisco 49ers moving to 3-0 after a 36-30 Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals.  It felt early on the 49ers would run […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t the prettiest. It wasn’t the easiest. But at the end of the day, they don’t ask how; they ask how many. And now the answer is three, with the San Francisco 49ers moving to 3-0 after a 36-30 Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. It felt early on the 49ers would run away with things on Sunday, jumping out to a 17-6 lead at the half. But Arizona just wouldn’t go away, keeping the game within one score for most of the second half; still, the 49ers showed they were the better team, playing mistake-free on offense and posting their highest-scoring output of the early season. While the defense had plenty of concerns, it was the offense that won the game. And because of that, all three stars from Sunday come from that side of the ball: 3rd star: TE George Kittle Sunday was George Kittle bobblehead day, so of course the All-Pro tight end had a big game. It was a slow burn for Kittle, who didn’t really add much to the 49ers offense in the first half. In the first 30 minutes of the game, Kittle was only targeted twice, catching just one of them for 12 yards. On the other side of the half is when Kittle turned it on. He wasted no time getting involved, hauling in a pair of passes for 29 yards on the 49ers’ opening drive of the second half, leading to a Christian McCaffrey one-yard score to put the 49ers up 23-6. After that, the rest of the 49ers’ scores would come from the hands of Kittle.Kittle caught 41 of his 82 yards in the final frame, capping his day with a 10-yard score to open the fourth quarter and put the 49ers up 29-20. He finished with a 20-yard score (after wiping a Brock Purdy 45-yard touchdown scramble off the board with a holding penalty) to mark his first multi-touchdown game since Week 11 of last season, also against the Cardinals. After the slow first half, Kittle finished with a team-high six receptions for 82 yards on seven targets for the two touchdowns. 2nd star: QB Brock Purdy Through three weeks, Brock Purdy has to be the leading MVP candidate. Purdy finished Sunday completing 15-of-27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns. It marked the fifth time in his career he threw four or more touchdowns in a game (second time against Arizona) and his second game with at least four touchdowns and no interceptions. It shouldn’t come as a surprise, but the 49ers are now 5-0 in games where Purdy throws at least four touchdowns. And his best play of the game didn’t even count. On an early game dropback, some pressure forced Purdy to roll to his right. It seemed as if Purdy was going to run himself out of bounds with Dante Stills in pursuit. But instead of throwing the ball away or running out of bounds, Purdy pulled a move that would have made prime Derek Jeter jealous: he jumped before going out and uncorked a laser downfield to Luke Farrell. Farrell’s sliding catch attempt wasn’t enough as he was ruled out. The play apparently didn’t impress Kyle Shanahan enough, since he didn’t challenge what could have been a highlight-reel play. Purdy nearly pulled off one of the craziest throws I've seen. I would have challenged that pic.twitter.com/GlTFNMI8OU — Billy M (@BillyM_91) September 27, 2026 Those are the types of plays that have drawn 49ers fans to Purdy: off-schedule, non-tempo plays only Purdy can make. Oh, and he also finished with 34 yards on the ground. It was the kind of game that would normally have earned Purdy the No. 1 star, however, he had to compete with maybe the most unique stat line in NFL history. 1st star: WR Deebo Samuel Despite Purdy’s all-world game, Deebo Samuel earned the No. 1 star with a stat line never before seen in NFL history. Zero targets, zero receptions, 80 yards, one receiving touchdown. So how does that happen? On the 49ers’ third play from scrimmage, San Francisco faced a third-and-12. Purdy connected with Mike Evans on a short curl route well short of the marker, but watching the play develop, you could see Luke Farrell pushing upfield to block and Samuel cutting across underneath Evans. Evans kept his cool as he was being brought down, hitting Samuel in stride on a lateral. A perfectly executed hook and ladder. Samuel took the pitch, turned upfield, made a Cardinal miss, and was gone. Evans’s two-yard reception turned into an 80-yard score for Samuel. According to Pro-Football-Reference , that is the most receiving yards by a player who didn’t record a reception. The list now is: Samuel, 80 yards (September 27, 2026) Timmy Brown, 65 yards (December 3, 1961) Bob Nussbaumer, 63 yards (November 7, 1948) It might be a stat line we never see again, but we saw it on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium, and somehow, someway, it’s the perfect Deebo Samuel stat line. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 3, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 7 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points WR Deebo Samuel – 3 points
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 49ers vs. Broncos Week 4 odds: Will good offense beat good defense?
summary: What a wild Week 3. The San Francisco 49ers sit atop the NFC West, thanks to a second-half collapse by the Rams and a Seahawks wire-to-wire loss to the Commanders. Every game but two was decided by one possession. That’s the NFL in a nutshell. Whatever you learned about a team last week, forget it. […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a wild Week 3. The San Francisco 49ers sit atop the NFC West, thanks to a second-half collapse by the Rams and a Seahawks wire-to-wire loss to the Commanders. Every game but two was decided by one possession. That’s the NFL in a nutshell. Whatever you learned about a team last week, forget it. It doesn’t apply to the following week. A lot of chaos occurs over a 60-minute sample size. The variance will have you thinking you’re in for a comfortable victory, like the Rams and 49ers probably figured in the first half. But the other team gets paid, too. In San Francisco’s case, they handled the adversity and answered every time with a score. Oddsmakers are expecting another nailbiter in Week 4. The 49ers opened as 2.5-point favorites over the Broncos at FanDuel Sportsbook , with the total set at 46.5. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The 49ers are the first team not to allow a sack in three weeks since the 2015 Bengals. It’s the first time in franchise history during that stretch since 1979. That is a Brock Purdy stat. Heading into Week 3, the Broncos were ninth in the NFL in pressure percentage. Trent Williams should be OK with a stinger, but the Niners will be taking a big step up in class in their opponent. The Rams racked up a bunch of yardage, but they ran 82 plays. Perhaps that’s the key there for Kyle Shanahan: Possess the ball and keep your injury-riddled defense off the field. Had it not been for Davante Adams’s pristine route running, Matthew Stafford might’ve struggled even more than he already did. Mike Evans looked to be in a lot of pain on Sunday. If he can’t overcome his rib injury, the 49ers wide receiver corps will be at a disadvantage, especially against an angry Pat Surtain. We did see cornerback Riley Moss get beaten deep on a double move. Perhaps that’s where Jacob Cowing can make an impact, much like he did as a rookie against the Chiefs? If you’re wondering why the line is so short, we just mentioned injuries to Williams and Evans. Take away Nick Bosa, and you’re down three of the team’s best players. Dre Greenlaw means Garret Wallow plays an entire game. The Broncos are above league average in passing success rate and EPA per pass. We did see the Rams run the ball effectively against Denver. But as Sean McVay tends to do, he got pass-happy. Fifty-five (!) passing attempts for Stafford on a day when your starting running back was averaging nearly six yards per carry cannot happen, not when you’re relying on YOLO balls down the field. I don’t think Kyle Shanahan will be as reluctant to include Christian McCaffrey in the game plan, especially after the way McCaffrey just ran the ball in Week 3. But we can’t ignore the other side of the ball. The total on the game being closer to 50 tells us the 49ers are going to get theirs, but Bo Nix should move the ball as well. It took Denver until the third quarter to find the weaknesses in the Rams’ defense. Arizona moved the ball in the first half, but didn’t start converting those opportunities into touchdowns until the second half. Historically, the 49ers have done well against bigger wideouts but struggled against speedy types. Jaylen Waddle and running back R.J. Harvey are major challenges for a defense that’ll likely be short-handed in the pass rush again. Can they be a bend-but-don’t-break unit for longer than a half, or will it be a game where Purdy has to shoulder the load once again to ensure his team comes out on top?
author: Kyle Posey

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers win and take first place; Cardinals, Rams, and Seahawks all lose
summary: It was a great week of football for San Francisco 49ers fans. The 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals 36-30, while the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and Cardinals all lost. This ends that first-place tiebreaker from last week and puts the 49ers into first place. You couldn’t ask for a better start to the season […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 07: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers shakes hands with Head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks after the game at Lumen Field on September 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a great week of football for San Francisco 49ers fans. The 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals 36-30, while the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and Cardinals all lost. This ends that first-place tiebreaker from last week and puts the 49ers into first place. You couldn’t ask for a better start to the season in the win/loss column. The 49ers are battling injuries and have some tough stretches coming up in their schedule, so stacking wins, including two divisional wins, is going to help in December. With the 49ers in first place, the Seahawks fall to second, and the Cardinals lose the tiebreaker to the Rams, falling to last place. Both of the Cardinals’ losses are in-division, versus one of the Rams’ single divisional loss. Things aren’t going to get any easier for the 49ers, and we aren’t even talking about how the injuries have leveled the playing field (yet again). They have some tough teams coming up. Right now, they are 3-0, and that’s all that matters until next Sunday. San Francisco 49ers (3-0)/Arizona Cardinals (1-2) Many may wonder just how the 49ers let the Cardinals hang 30 points on them after the Cardinals got destroyed by the Seahawks last week. Maybe you wonder how Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett managed to go 38 for 52 without a single interception, dominate the time of possession, etc., etc. Well, it’s simple: the 49ers are. Not. Healthy. So how did the 49ers manage to avoid a disappointing loss? Well, his name is Brock Purdy. The 49ers lost Mike Evans, so Purdy went to George Kittle to catch passes. The 49ers lost Trent Williams, but Purdy was on his feet and still didn’t take a sack—and hasn’t taken one yet this season. The 49ers would not have won this game without Purdy. When things were getting tight late due to two missed 49ers’ extra points while the Cardinals were showing the world they had playmakers, Purdy marched down the field and put a stop to it in the fourth quarter. It’s worth pointing out the Cardinals are much better than their record indicates. They hung with Seattle until the third quarter last week, when the floodgates opened, and the Seahawks are much healthier than the 49ers. Still, if the 49ers game we saw Sunday happened against the Kansas City Chiefs, the outcome might not have been as positive. Regardless, as long as the 49ers have Brock Purdy, they have a chance against anyone. Maybe it won’t be a “good” chance depending on the team, but I’d hate to think what would happen today if, say, Brian Hoyer was under center and had to march down the field in the fourth quarter to put it out of reach. Seattle Seahawks (2-1) This shaped up to be the most Seattle game ever: Sam Darnold returned to the starting quarterback role, while the Seahawks got Washington Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota. Then the game started, and Seahawks running back Jadarian Price fumbled the ball, leading to the Commanders getting a touchdown shortly thereafter. What resulted was a fun half with the Seahawks matching the Commanders, while the Commanders continued to extend their lead. The second half gave us the Commanders getting a nice 14-point lead, and everyone expecting Seattle to come roaring back—which they did. I doubt anyone expected the two picks Sam Darnold threw. One was a costly pick-6 in the fourth quarter after the Commanders took a three-point lead with under five minutes to go. The Seahawks got their touchdown on the next series, but the Commanders offense, in what might be their final series, stayed on the field, forced the Seahawks to burn their timeouts, and went to victory formation 33-31. 31 points. Even the Seahawks defense can get carved. Yes, six of those points came from the Darnold interception, but Mariota had some nice throws to get the Commanders the lead to start this. With the loss, the 49ers return to first place in the division, and the Seahawks’ 12-game winning streak has been snapped. Los Angeles Rams (1-2) As of this writing, the Rams are in third place, only because they’ve played one divisional game while the Cardinals have had two. That’s right, the “dream team” that has yet to play a Sunday afternoon game is slipping in the division. And if you tuned into that Sunday Night Football game before halftime, you may have gone back to cat videos or watching other shows where the 49ers were the focus. Rams were leading 16-0, and nothing was going the Broncos’ way. The Rams got a touchdown in the first quarter and then proceeded to field-goal the Broncos to death with three straight field goals in the second quarter. They wouldn’t get another touchdown—their last— until there was just over four minutes left in the game. The Broncos woke up in the second half, and with some Bill Vinovich magic for strange penalties, they managed to take the lead in the fourth quarter. The Broncos also got a few extra tries to score touchdowns , thanks to those strange calls . Broncos quarterback Bo Nix showed up when needed, but he was far from efficient, completing 17 of 34 passes for 186 yards. Sure, he got two touchdowns, but he also notched a bad interception with them. Meanwhile, Matthew Stafford wasn’t much better, going 30 for 55 for 390 yards, two touchdowns, but also two interceptions, one of which got taken to the house by former 49ers safety Talanoa Hufanga . The other pick was on the final play of the game. Both weren’t very good. At all. At the end of the day, if you look past who scored what points, you’d think the Rams won with nearly 500 yards of offense and a 34:29 time of possession vs. the Broncos’ 25:31. Turnovers, first downs—the Rams won. Where they didn’t win was penalties (13 for 91 yards) and red zone trips; the Broncos were 3 for 3, while the Rams were 1 for 1. All I’m saying is the Rams had decent stats, but they couldn’t put the Broncos away and had to fight for the few points they had against that stingy Broncos defense. Regardless of any positives I may take from this, the Rams are 1-2 now and two games back from the 49ers. Their schedule doesn’t get any better next week either since they have the Philadelphia Eagles next. Onto Week 4 The 49ers will have a new test this week playing the Denver Broncos. This will be an excellent litmus test for Brock Purdy, as the Broncos’ defense is much better than what he’s faced the last two weeks. It should be a fun game. The Seahawks will have the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers haven’t been having a good season, sitting at 0-3. This is very odd for a team coached by Jim Harbaugh. Sure, some may say he was overrated, even when he was coaching in San Francisco, but 0-3 under Harbaugh seems, well, weird. This might be the Chargers’ last gasp, not unlike the Commanders coming in with their hair on fire Sunday, so hopefully they can give us a similar result. The Rams will be traveling to Philadelphia to face the Eagles. With the Denver loss, dropping another game in a row puts the Rams at 1-3. In a competitive NFC West, that’s not exactly ideal for the “dream team”. The Cardinals will travel to face the New York Giants. Since Jameis Winston is quarterbacking (or expected to as of this writing), they may finally have a game where they can come out with a “W”. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next vs. Denver Broncos 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. Los Angeles Chargers 3rd: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Philadelphia Eagles 4th: Arizona Cardinals; Next: at New York Giants
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 6 Winners and 5 losers from the 49ers win over the Cardinals
summary: The San Francisco 49ers held on for dear life at home against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3. The score was 36-30, but Kyle Shanahan’s aggressive approach to ending the game showed how he felt about letting his defense decide it. Here are the winners and losers from Week 3. Winners Kyle Shanahan Shanahan’s ability […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers held on for dear life at home against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3. The score was 36-30, but Kyle Shanahan’s aggressive approach to ending the game showed how he felt about letting his defense decide it. Here are the winners and losers from Week 3. Winners Kyle Shanahan Shanahan’s ability to sequence plays and keep the offense ahead of schedule is uncanny. Historic, even. SF has the fewest plays losing yardage excluding kneels (4) by any team through 3 games in recorded history (play-by-play data exists since 1991) h/t sportradar — Doug Clawson (@doug_clawson) September 27, 2026 Missing Mike Evans, the 49ers still managed explosive plays. They didn’t miss a beat on the ground, either. The passing success rate was over 55%. The rushing success rate was 59%. Both of those are elite figures. Despite missing Mike Evans for much of the game, the Niners still had the league’s highest EPA per play, nearly double the second-place team. The offense ran only 50 plays, but averaged a whopping 8.7 yards per play. The offense is a juggernaut, and Shanahan is to thank for that. Brock Purdy Several measures show when a quarterback is under duress or when their receivers aren’t open. The Cardinals pressured Purdy on nearly 40 percent of his dropbacks. Purdy threw the ball away on 10.7% of his attempts. A couple of close, tight-window throws may have made you nervous, but Purdy ran out of multiple sacks once again to keep the Niners ahead of schedule. Purdy scrambled for 34 yards. He should have a touchdown on his ledger. It’s impressive how he stands stall against pressure in his face and knows where every wideout is. Purdy has a knack for playing on time and making aggressive decisions, and his four-touchdown performance was a big reason why San Francisco hung on against the Cardinals. Purdy recorded his 14th career game with a 130+ passer rating, the most by any player before turning 27 in NFL history. He surpassed Lamar Jackson. George Kittle Kittle led the 49ers with eight impact plays, per Sumer Sports. That is a team-high this season. Fifty percent of Kittle’s targets came in the red zone. He caught six of his seven targets for 82 receiving yards, and averaged an impressive 5 yards after the catch. The broadcast highlighted how well Kittle blocked. That goes without saying. The 49ers are a different team through the air and, more importantly, on the ground, with Kittle on the field. Kittle’s two touchdown receptions bring his career total to 55, tying Vernon Davis for fourth in the franchise. Christian McCaffrey McCaffrey was second on the team with four impact plays. He rushed for a season-high 75 yards, with 39 of those coming after contact. McCaffrey caught four passes on five targets for 41 yards, bringing his total to over 100 scrimmage yards. McCaffrey had two explosive runs against the Cardinals. Add in his production as a receiver, and it’s hard to leave him off this list. Losers The tackling Fred Warner uncharacteristically missed three tackles. Dre Greenlaw also missed three. Jaden Dugger missed one. Osa Odighizuwa missed one. Keion White missed a tackle. Upton Stout missed two tackles. The 49ers are at a disadvantage once they take the field with the plethora of injuries. If they miss 10 tackles a game, they’re not going to have a chance to stay competitive. The soft coverage The 49ers played four cornerbacks. Each of them was targeted at least five times. Every one of them allowed at least two-thirds of their targets to be completed. Upton Stout allowed all five of his targets to be completed for 7.2 yards per target. Jack Jones allowed 8.3 yards per target. The cornerbacks are going to have to step up for a banged-up pass rush. They had two pass breakups, but Deommodore Lenoir had the pass interference in the end zone. Aside from that, the 49ers gave up so many easy completions underneath, that it allowed the Jacoby Brissett to be comfortable and take the short profit. That’s why the Cardinals ran 31 more plays than the Niners. Raheem Morris should look to change the variance and put more pressure on the opposing quarterback with tighter coverage. He can only do so much with so many starters out along the defensive line, but the secondary is fully healthy. There’s no excuse for Sunday’s performance. Winners The offensive line For the second time this season, McCaffrey averaged over 1.5 yards before contact (1.9). He reached that mark just three times in 2025. That is an offensive line stat. The line allowed only four pressures, and Purdy averaged 3.26 seconds to throw across 27 dropbacks. That is an offensive line stat. It’s a unit that remains one of the team’s strengths, and one the 49ers will keep leaning on as injuries pile up. The makeshift defensive tackle group Odighizuwa had four pressures and a tipped pass that probably should’ve resulted in an interception. Before he left with an injury, Halton had three impact plays, including a tackle for loss on a screen. Kevin Givens has a couple of pressures, including a near sack. Sebastian Valdez had a pair of run stops. Naquan Jones had a run stuff. All things considered, the defensive tackle group competed.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers news: Deebo Samuel sets a bizarre record with his touchdown
summary: Nothing like the NFL. We all predicted the Seahawks would lose, or the Rams would blow a two-touchdown lead. The San Francisco 49ers beating the Cardinals was expected, but it didn’t go nearly as smoothly as everyone had hoped. But a win is a win, and Week 3 proved that just because you are a […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nothing like the NFL. We all predicted the Seahawks would lose, or the Rams would blow a two-touchdown lead. The San Francisco 49ers beating the Cardinals was expected, but it didn’t go nearly as smoothly as everyone had hoped. But a win is a win, and Week 3 proved that just because you are a big favorite, it doesn’t guarantee a victory. The 49ers won a game with effectively a backup defensive line that had practice squad members mixed in the rotation. Escaping that game with a win with all of the injuries should not be taken for granted, especially when you look around the league. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . If everybody feels this way, I have no problem bringing back game threads, and that’ll start tonight with a couple of NFC and potential playoff teams. On to today’s links. 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Drops Concerning Mike Evans Injury Update After Cardinals Win “We don’t know yet [if he’ll miss a couple of weeks],” Shanahan told reporters . “We couldn’t tell if it was a broken rib, we couldn’t tell if it was an oblique. It’s something we’ll probably find out more tomorrow.” Shanahan also admitted that losing a player the caliber of Evans really affects the team’s offensive game plan. “When you lose guys, especially guys like Mike, it changes stuff on your call sheet, changes wristbands, things like that,” Shanahan continued. “You don’t have time to think about anything else. So when guys go down, you hope they return, but you adjust and wait until they’re back, and if they don’t [return], you keep it moving.” 49ers to sign veteran DE with 72 career sacks as injuries pile up Tillery reported Judon had a workout with the 49ers on Saturday and will officially sign with the club Monday. It’s unclear whether he’ll be joining via the practice squad or the 53-man roster. Judon in his interview explained how injuries played a role in him joining the 49ers. “With all of the injuries piling up over there I think I can just come in and help until some of those guys get back,” Judon said. “I know the D-line coach. I know him well. He’s a great D-line coach.” How the 49ers Fared When Things Went Against Them in Win Over Cardinals So, despite an aging roster, the 49ers showed they were able to dig in when faced with adversity. This was their biggest test so far, but that doesn’t necessarily mean it will be the story all year. Arizona’s roster punched above its weight, but they are unlikely to be in the playoff hunt. Still, taking confidence from a game like this will be huge with tougher opponents awaiting them. It also provided echoes of last season. Even when injuries impacted many players, which is a recurring challenge this year, Kyle Shanahan can still find ways to ensure his offense scores heavily. The cracks began to show in this matchup with all their injuries, and losing offensive starters is a concern when the defense is already struggling to shut down teams that aren’t going to make the playoffs. 49ers’ stunning trick play helps Deebo Samuel set a bizarre NFL record Samuel was not credited with a catch on the play, which went to Evans ( who later left the game with a rib injury .) But Samuel was credited with 80 receiving yards on the play because of Evans’ lateral to him. The touchdown turned out to be the only time Samuel had the ball on a passing play. (Samuel had two rushes for 14 yards and also returned four kicks.) As it so happens, 80 receiving yards is the most ever for a player who didn’t register a reception. A surprising number of players have recorded receiving yards without recording a catch (although of the top 20 marks, Samuel was one of just three that occurred this century). The previous record for receiving yards without a catch was 65, set by Timmy Brown of the Eagles in 1961. 5 49ers Whose Stock Is Surging After Week 3 Jordan Watkins was inactive for the first two weeks of the 49ers season. However, the injuries to the position were too much, and the team had to activate him. He only played 15 snaps, but he recorded 60 yards. Watkins averaged an impressive 1.73 yards per route run as a rookie; he just barely played and had a small sample of work. Still, when he plays, he produces. With Mike Evans banged up, the 49ers should try to start Watkins.

title: 3 quick takeaways from 49ers narrow win over Cardinals: Health is becoming a problem
summary: The San Francisco 49ers looked like they were cruising to victory after a touchdown on the opening drive of the second half, but things were much closer than expected in their 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. The 49ers compiled 437 yards of offense, as Brock Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers controls the ball during the first quarter of the game A at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers looked like they were cruising to victory after a touchdown on the opening drive of the second half, but things were much closer than expected in their 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. The 49ers compiled 437 yards of offense, as Brock Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns, but the Cardinals scored 24 second-half points as Jacoby Brissett dropped back 52 times in the comeback effort. This game had shades of San Francisco’s 41-22 victory over the Cardinals last season, but ended up being closer. Nonetheless, San Francisco secured the victory, moving to 3-0 to start the season. Here are three takeaways from the 49ers win over the Cardinals in Week 3. Offense continues to roll The 49ers offense has been on point to begin the season, and that continued on Sunday, as they scored on six of their nine offensive drives, which included five touchdowns. Brock Purdy had a ton of explosives in the air, averaging nearly 20 yards per completion, as several skill position players had big games. George Kittle had six catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns, while Deebo Samuel had an 80-yard hook-and-ladder touchdown on the team’s first drive. Mike Evans was balling early before his rib injury. Christian McCaffrey added another two scores, while totaling over 100 yards, and Jordan Watkins had a nice first impression with two catches for 60 yards. San Francisco averaged over 6.0 yards per carry as well. They dominated early downs and were 5 of 8 on third down, continuing their strong success there. Through three games, Brock Purdy looks like a true MVP candidate, and it looks like injuries are really the only thing that can slow this offense down right now. Time of possession The main reason this game was closer than expected? The Cardinals held the ball for over 38 minutes in this game with a very similar outlook to last year’s contest. They averaged only 4.5 yards per play with only 5.0 yards per pass attempt, but they converted 9 of 18 third downs and both of their fourth downs to extend a ton of drives. Arizona had five drives of eight plus plays, including 12, 14, 14 and 14-play drives. The defense started to struggle a bit in the second half, as the Cardinals scored on four of their offensive drives, getting within two at one point in the fourth quarter. The 49ers offense and their strong start was able to put the game at reach, but Arizona gave the defense a run for its money. Jeremiyah Love ran for 90 yards as well on 4.3 yards per carry, which was a potential problem I highlighted earlier in the week. But, the biggest overall takeaway from the game was… Injuries continue to loom The 49ers got another large dose of key injuries from this game. There was the early scare when Mike Evans had to be carted off the field. It ended up being a rib/oblique injury and the 49ers will figure out the severity soon. Trent Williams was also carted off with what was diagnosed as a stinger. Dre Greenlaw left with a quad injury. Gracen Halton had cramps and did not return. Some of the injuries may not be serious, but the 49ers entered the year as one of the NFL’s oldest teams. The injuries, and the long-term ones, are continuing to pile up, and that feels like the main thing that could hold San Francisco back after the start to their season. Evans has been a booming success, but he dealt with injuries last year. He’d be a key loss if he were to miss time. Trent Williams is as vital to the offense as anyone. But the injuries are piling up on the defensive line. The depth is starting to shrink overall. San Francisco has a big test with the Denver Broncos next weekend, and we’ll see if they get good news this week.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Brock Purdy bails out the 49ers’ defense in a shootout win over the Cardinals
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are quickly becoming synonymous with fireworks, the way they’ve been lighting up the scoreboard. The offense didn’t take long to get going. Deebo Samuel opened the scoring on a hook-and-ladder from Mike Evans. That would’ve been the fastest clocked time by a 49ers ball carrier in 2025. After the defense recorded […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are quickly becoming synonymous with fireworks, the way they’ve been lighting up the scoreboard. The offense didn’t take long to get going. Deebo Samuel opened the scoring on a hook-and-ladder from Mike Evans. That would’ve been the fastest clocked time by a 49ers ball carrier in 2025. After the defense recorded its second consecutive three-and-out to begin the game, the offense took over 93 yards away from the end zone. Christian McCaffrey converted a third down, then Jordan Watkins converted the next. Watkins was a 25-yarder. Then, just outside of the red zone, Purdy hit Evans down the right sideline, and Mike Evans didn’t tip that pass by keeping his hands low: If you never flash your hands, the defensive back has no idea the ball is coming. Perfection here by Mike Evans pic.twitter.com/7Id3YFcyia — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 27, 2026 There are late hands, and then there’s what Evans did above. The defense did its job for a third straight time, but Purdy and the offense punted after facing some pressure. The Cardinals mustered multiple first downs on the ensuing drive, including an 18-yard pass where Trey McBride beat Ji’Ayir Brown. Arizona made it inside the red zone and faced a 4th-and-1. Deommodore Lenoir had just been hit by Fred Warner and had to leave the game. His replacement, Jack Jones, allowed a slant for a first down. Lenoir was seen walking to the locker room. He was being evaluated for a concussion. After a Fred Warner tackle for loss, the Cardinals were stuffed on 3rd-and-goal from outside the 10. Chad Ryland’s short field goal was good, to make it 14-3. A bend-but-don’t-break approach will be necessary as long as Nick Bosa is sidelined. The 49ers took over with a little more than two minutes remaining. They’d receive the ball to begin the third quarter, so it was a prime opportunity to double up on the scoreboard. Evans got open on a third down. That’s not surprising. What was surprising, besides Evans, were the wideouts on the field during this two-minute drill: Watkins and Jacob Cowing. After the next third down, Evans grabbed his midsection and needed assistance from the trainers. It seemed like Evans got the wind knocked out of him. The Cardinals moved the ball efficiently, largely thanks to a 17-yard reception from Michael Wilson. In the red zone, Gracen Halton sniffed out a screen pass for a 4-yard loss. That forced a field goal to make it 14-6. No Evans, no problem. Purdy found Watkins wide open before the half for a 34-yard gain. The 49ers finding a way to get into field goal range with 23 seconds left sums up how explosive their offense is, regardless of who is on the field. Eddy Pineiro nailed a 57-yard field goal, answering the Cardinals’ score to make it 17-6 heading into the half. Purdy found Kittle for an 11-yard gain to open the half. And just like that, the 49ers were across midfield. He found Kittle on third down for another chunk play, putting the offense in the red zone. McCaffrey bounced off a tackle on the next reception, giving the Niners first-and-goal. Evans had been ruled out with a rib injury. You couldn’t tell by how quickly the offense scored. McCaffrey leaped over the pile, pushing the 49ers’ lead to 23-6 after Pineiro missed the extra point. Lenoir returned to begin the third quarter. At the same time, Trent Williams was carted to the locker room with what the team called a stinger on a play during McCaffrey’s touchdown. The Cardinals had no trouble moving the ball against a depleted defensive line. After 10 plays, Arizona found themselves in the red zone. This followed another fourth-down conversion from Brissett to Wilson. Rookie Jeremiah Love found enough daylight on third-and-four to extend the drive. Brissett found Wilson again, this time in the end zone, to make it 23-13. To add insult to injury, Gracen Halton limped off the field on the point-after attempt. He went back to the locker room after dealing with cramps. After a punt, the defense took the field without Renardo Green, who was in the injury tent being evaluated for a concussion. Jack Jones came in for him. Kevin Givens had a terrific rush to force a 3rd-and-long. Lenoir jumped Marvin Harrison’s route to force a punt. But the Niners offense wouldn’t get the opportunity to step onto the field after the punt deflected off Siran Neal. Arizona took over with a short field. On 4th-and-1, Lenoir committed pass interference in the end zone. Brissett found Love, and just like that, the score was 23-20. Vederian Lowe remained at left tackle. Purdy found Kittle for a first down, then McCaffrey picked up 10, and the 49ers were across midfield in a blink. Kaelon Black joined the fun with a nine-yard gain. Deebo caught a swing pass, then broke a tackle, and the Niners were knocking on the door of the red zone. KhaDarel Hodge’s first target came on third down. But a penalty on Josh Sweat gave the Niners a fresh set of downs. Kittle, on his bobblehead day, came through after beating a pass rusher in coverage. Pineiro doinked the extra point again, making the score 29-20. After coming close on a couple of different occasions, Keion White recorded a sack. More often than not, sacks are drive killers. But Harrison beat Green, who was back in, on a deep in-breaking route. You miss Bosa’s presence most on third down. Greenlaw was out at this point as well. He was down on the field on the drive before. Garrett Wallow was his replacement. The Cardinals moved the ball once again. Ji’Ayir Brown nearly came up with an interception after Osa Odighizuwa tipped the ball in the air. Brissett found McBride to keep the drive alive. McBride beat Marques Sigle to the 1-yard line. A Brissett sneak made it a one-possession game: 29-27. Gulp. Brock Purdy had a great read where he scrambled for a touchdown, but the play was flagged for a phantom holding call. Purdy got it back on the next play when he found Kittle open downfield for a touchdown. Shanahan made a great call to go for the kill shot. That made it 36-27.

title: Week 3 Game Recap: Mayfield hurt as Buccaneers lose to Vikings
summary: First Quarter: 0-2 with the undefeated Purple People Eaters coming into Tampa, the Buccaneers played defense first. Three jolting plays, a Justin Jefferson chunk and a handful of gashing runs, placed the Vikings into field range. The Buccaneers’ defense found its footing and walled off Minnesota’s drive. holding to 3-0, Vikings. From a three point […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Blake Cashman #51 of the Minnesota Vikings tackles Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter: 0-2 with the undefeated Purple People Eaters coming into Tampa, the Buccaneers played defense first. Three jolting plays, a Justin Jefferson chunk and a handful of gashing runs, placed the Vikings into field range. The Buccaneers’ defense found its footing and walled off Minnesota’s drive. holding to 3-0, Vikings. From a three point play to a three-and-out, Tampa’s offense went to their vintage run, run, pass, punt. That punt would not be the punt of champions— A punt six, run back by Myles Price. Tampa Bay’s special teams has been a substantial problem for years (addressed in the offseason by the hiring of Danny Smith) and the unit dropped the team to a two score deficit. 10-0, Vikings. In an volcanic awakening, the Buccaneers’ offense erupted with its biggest play of the season. Baker Mayfield dropped back finding Ted Hurst III deep down the middle of the field for a 40-yard catch-and-run score. 10-7, Minnesota. Second Quarter: It wasn’t until the second quarter and each team booming punts that offense re-emerged. That offense was Baker Mayfield, Bucky Ivring, and Tampa Bay. The Bucs scooted their way back down the field en route to field goal range and a game-tying Chase McLaughin field goal. Three points from the team’s 2026 MVP, 10-10, tie. The Vikings’ offense quickly untied Tampa’s tied knot, tossing a deep ball up to Jordan Addison who mercilessly dunked on Jacob Parrish for the highlight and the score. 17-10, Vikes. With the half ticking to the two-minute warning, Todd Bowles’ game-managing-ineptitude flashed the viewing audience multiple times. His first decision to send the Buccaneers’ punt team out onto then field with 2:05 on a running clock and over 10 seconds on the play clock took all of the deception out of his decision in the scenario. That simple choice allowed Kevin O’Connell to observe the situation from a clear vantage point, take a timeout before the two minute warning, and would have forced Tampa into punting before the two-minute mark. The only reason the team was not forced into that punt is that that decision was elite-ly covered up when the refs re-spotted the ball giving Baker Mayfield a first down on the previous play. It would not take long for Bowles to reignite his haters as the team would then regain the same 26 seconds they had when the previous play ended. Given new life, the team’s offense just watched the same time tick off the clock for a second time. Even though now they had secured a first down— Rather than calling a play and restarting their drive the Bucs’ offense sat in the huddle and the same 26 seconds ran off the clock again . Just two minutes later, Bowles was at it again. In an unstoppable sequence of playing not to lose rather than choosing to play for the win, Bowles opted to punt with six seconds left in the half instead of attempting a Hail Mary. Post that punt, the Buccaneers sulked into their locker room at the half down 17-10, towels on heads, in a game they could easily be losing 24-3 but also astoundingly could be winning 20-10— Buccaneers football in 2026. Third Quarter: Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers’ offense was back up to take another swing at the start of half two. Bucky Irving would continue to truck forward as the team’s feature chess piece— runs and catches to secure a first down. It wouldn’t take the Vikings’ defense long to catch on to the Bucky-only offense thwart it and force another punt. The Vikings debut drive of the second would also net a punt. Their punt gave fans more Baker Mayfield which meant more missed passes. The Buccaneers gave out two massive contract extensions in the offseason. It would be hard to argue they have anything other then buyer’s remorse regarding one of those contracts, however, the other paid dividends on the next Vikings’ drive. Vita Vea got big expensive hand up in the passing lane of Kyler Murray. That tipped pass would lead to bouncing, bobbling ball that landed in the hands of a diving A’Shawn Robinson. With eight minutes left in third, that beautiful diving interception set the Buccaneers up perfectly for more points. Unfortunately, those points came courtesy of MVP Chase McLaughlin and not the team’s offense. 17-13, Vikes. Fourth Quarter: By the time Sunday’s slog had arrived at the fourth quarter, fans watching might have been as exhausted as the players on the field. The sloppy play was unrelenting, from both sides. Sunday’s game was genuinely hard on the eyes and had the feeling of game being played by two anemic offenses being led by backup or replacement level quarterbacks, not the projected starters at the season’s onset (One of which is a top paid quarterback league-wide), or a game played in extreme weather conditions where Mother Nature hampered each team’s ability to function effectively. That, however, is not what Sunday was. Sunday was two team’s playing terrible undisciplined, uninspired, nonsensical offense. A late field goal from 56 yards out gave the Vikings an extension of their game-long lead. 20-16, Minnesota. With two minutes left Baker Mayfield, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ franchise quarterback had the ball needing just one touchdown to get his team a much need (albeit ugly) victory. That would not be the outcome of Sunday’s contest, it would instead be more awful on top of the awful that was already awful. Baker Mayfield, in a frantic scramble found a Viking defender for an interception and rolled around on the ground in pain. He would slam his helmet on the ground in frustration as his walked into the locker room, ending his day. The Buccaneers’ day would end soon after 23-16— awful all around.

full_text: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers enter Week 3 still searching for their first win of the season, and the early results have clearly taken a toll on the confidence level surrounding the team. In this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 10 percent of Buccaneers fans said they are confident the team is headed in the right direction. After an 0-2 start, that number reflects just how quickly optimism has faded in Tampa Bay. Still, the national results offer at least a little bit of hope. When NFL fans were asked which 0-2 team is most likely to make the playoffs, the Buccaneers finished second with 21 percent of the vote. Only the Houston Texans received more support at 53 percent. title: Did Cam Ward make a bad decision or a bad throw yesterday?
summary: Watching the Tennessee Titans’ final offensive play in real time yesterday, it looked to me like Cam Ward made a terrible decision to throw the ball. On the broadcast, it looked like there was a lot of room to run in front of him when he decided to throw the pass that was ultimately intercepted […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 27: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans attempts a pass against Tremaine Edmunds #49 of the New York Giants during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Watching the Tennessee Titans’ final offensive play in real time yesterday, it looked to me like Cam Ward made a terrible decision to throw the ball. On the broadcast, it looked like there was a lot of room to run in front of him when he decided to throw the pass that was ultimately intercepted to end the game. After rewatching the play about 100 times, not running there was the smart play. There were two defenders between him and the end zone that would have stopped him. The real issue was the throw. Here’s the final play: Cam is catching a ton of heat for this response, and maybe he could have worded it differently, but he is right. EZ angle supports this. If he floats the ball to the corner of the end zone, it’s potentially a TD. Decision wasn’t issue. Type of throw was the problem. https://t.co/0DMYU6elC1 pic.twitter.com/O20Ybhf02j — Superhorn (@Super_Horn) September 28, 2026 Elic Ayomanor is running to the back left corner of the end zone. As old friend SuperHorn mentions, if Ward throws it to that corner, Jevon Holland has no chance to pick it off, and Ayomanor would have had a chance to catch it for a touchdown. The real problem is the accuracy of the throw. Watch it again. There is no shot that ball Ward threw was getting completed, even if he is able to throw it over Holland. With that being said, I also don’t think Ward was being reckless with the ball here. As I mentioned above, a throw to the corner is either a touchdown or an incomplete pass. That means they win the game or live to play another down – which would have been 2nd and goal from the 7. Ward has done more wrong than right this year. The thing that is really starting to scare me is his overall inconsistency. There have still been flashes of a solid quarterback in there, but he can’t put that together consistently from play to play, much less from game to game. The only way he is going to be a franchise quarterback is to play consistently. Through 20 NFL games, he has not shown the ability to do that.

summary: The Commanders entered their first game at Northwest Stadium this season as home underdogs against the defending Super Bowl champions. Now 1-2 on the young season, and with a little momentum going their way, they head overseas […]
full_text: The Commanders entered their first game at Northwest Stadium this season as home underdogs against the defending Super Bowl champions. But, through a gritty performance that saw them secure three turnovers, they pulled off a STUNNING 33-31 victory . Now 1-2 on the young season , and with a little momentum going their way, they head overseas to London to take on the 1-2 Colts before coming back home to face the Giants. These next two games will likely define their season, so all hands need to be on deck if Dan Quinn hopes to move this squad towards respectability. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game followed by some notes. Studs: QB Marcus Mariota: Mariota looked completely in control the entire game. He made appropriate checks at the line, delivered the ball with accuracy and came up big with the game on the line. He finished the contest 19-for-31 passing for 183 yards and three touchdowns and was sacked just twice, but no play was bigger than his read option run on third-and-9 late in the fourth quarter. A great game by the captain. 3rd and 9 – PLAY OF THE GAME by Mariota!!!!! pic.twitter.com/TUM5jvMpT0 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 4th and 1 – Mariota hits Terry for the 1st! pic.twitter.com/HDgPVQcWvo — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 WR Terry McLaurin: Terry had his breakout game of the 2026 season, leading the team with six receptions for 77 yards and a leaping score. It was great to see F1 get on track! Terry goes up over Jones for the TD! 💥 pic.twitter.com/8TbV0awjiV — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 Mariota finds Terry for 18yds before the half pic.twitter.com/IoJTHGE3Rf — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 27, 2026 RT Josh Conerly: The second-year right tackle has come a long way from his difficult rookie season. He is starting to show a better anchor in pass protection, and his run blocking has been excellent. He didn’t allow a pressure against a very good Seattle defense. DL Javon Kinlaw: Kinlaw was a beast inside all afternoon. A lot of his play may have went unnoticed, but a lot of the defensive success stopping the run was because of him. title: Commanders injury update: Leo Chenal to have season-ending surgery
summary: Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal suffered a scary neck injury during Sunday’s win over Seattle that will end his season.   He incurred a neck fracture that will be surgically repaired on Monday, according to multiple reports.   Jordan Schultz was first to report the news.   He is expected to make a full recovery and […]
full_text: Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal suffered a scary neck injury during Sunday’s win over Seattle that will end his season. He incurred a neck fracture that will be surgically repaired on Monday, according to multiple reports. Jordan Schultz was first to report the news. #Commanders LB Leo Chenal, who was taken off the field with a scary-looking injury on Sunday, will undergo season-ending surgery this morning for a fracture in his neck, per sources. Most importantly, Chenal has feeling in all his extremities, and the expectation is that he’ll… pic.twitter.com/6SsFyefj4D — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 28, 2026 He is expected to make a full recovery and has full movement in his extremities. His promising first season with the Commanders was cut short far too early after an incident in the first half of Sunday’s game where he got hurt making a tackle. Chenal was down on the field for an extended period before being placed on a backboard and carted off the field. Prayers up for Leo Chenal 🙏 pic.twitter.com/LLDOzf8Wnr — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 27, 2026 He motioned to the crowd on the way to the locker room, where he was united with his family. Chenal was taken to a Washington area hospital shortly after. “He does have feeling in his extremities,” Quinn told reporters after the game , before the final diagnosis was made. “He’s undergoing further testing as we go through tonight. We are definitely thinking of him. He’s a great teammate. We love him. Anytime a guy gets banged up like that, you’re thinking of him and pulling for him as much as you can.”

full_text: The Commanders are reportedly reuniting with an old friend. Washington is poised to sign running back Austin Ekeler, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported on Monday morning . The pact, the report states, is pending a physical. Ekeler suffered a torn Achilles’ tendon during a Week 2 loss to Green Bay, a non-contact injury that ended his season. He worked out for the Carolina Panthers last week, per the NFL transaction wire. Reunion: The #Commanders are expected to sign FA RB Austin Ekeler to their 53-man roster pending physical, sources tell me and @MikeGarafolo . Ekeler, who is healed from an Achilles tear and worked out for the #Panthers last week, lands back in a familiar place. pic.twitter.com/YZGlmGdFjK — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026 The signing could be considered unexpected considering the Washington running back room, but NBC4’s JP Finlay offered some context to it. Rachaad White left the locker room yesterday with a big ice pack on his shoulder after it seemed like he hurt it in the game but was able to return. And Monday morning they sign Ekeler — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) September 28, 2026 A more official word from the Commanders on Ekeler and White could come later Monday afternoon, when head coach Dan Quinn will hold a press conference. Ekeler spent most of his career as a do-everything running back for the L.A. Chargers, but signed with Washington before the 2024 season. He was productive that year , with 733 yards of total offense and four touchdowns. If signed, he could step in for an injured player and provide some coverage as a third-down back. The offense turned the other two turnovers into touchdowns. Mariota played a key role in each, finishing both drives with touchdown passes. Daniels, injured on the final play of the first half vs. Dallas, is considered week-to-week. There’s a chance Daniels, who won the Heisman in 2013 and was picked second in 2024, will accompany the team to London, but that wouldn’t necessarily mean he would play vs. the Colts. So, Mariota could continue to be an important player. Two years ago, he relieved an injured Daniels in two games, leading Washington to wins. Last year, Mariota started eight games and played in three others, but posted only a 2-6 record as a starter in another injury-filled season for the organization. They… — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) September 28, 2026 More from ESPN: The Commanders forced three turnovers, leading to three touchdowns — two by the offense and another on a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. The offense capitalized on two short fields after a fumble and an interception, while quarterback Marcus Mariota did what was needed. He was smart with the ball, making quick throws and taking checkdowns to keep the chains moving. And he was aggressive when necessary, like on a tight-window throw to WR Trey Burks for his second touchdown. It was an unlikely win without quarterback Jayden Daniels, linebacker Frankie Luvu, tight end Chig Okonkwo, right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross. Trend to watch: Washington did not force any turnovers in its first two games, which continued an ugly trend: Only one team has forced fewer turnovers than the Commanders since 2024. But they harped on it all offseason, and the focus paid off Sunday. Can they sustain it? It helped that they played coverage much better than they did against Dallas in Week 2. But to get more, the front needs to generate more consistent pressure. It’ll help when they get blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu back soon from a groin injury. — John Keim To read more of this second ESPN article, CLICK HERE Washington Post (paywall) Marcus Mariota leads Commanders to upset of Super Bowl champion Seahawks “We had to find a way to get a win,” offensive lineman Nick Allegretti said. “However it was, whatever way it was, we had to find a way.” Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota went 19 for 31 for 183 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions to efficiently fill Daniels’s shoes. “I really believe this team has a chance to do some really, really good things,” Mariota said. “But I think guys in the locker room will definitely say that we are not satisfied yet.” Washington’s defense gave up 437 yards and struggled to contain the Seahawks’ passing attack. They hadn’t created an opponent turnover in what felt like months — and that was actually the case. They had the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, who had won 12 games in a row and hadn’t lost a real football game since last Nov. 16, coming to Northwest Stadium. They were led by new team captain Marcus Mariota who took over for Jayden Daniels last week when he re-injured his left elbow. Mariota took advantage of Washington’s defense forcing multiple turnovers, including a Kain Medrano pick-6, to lead the Commanders to their first win of the season. They won’t have much time to celebrate the win as they get ready for their international game in London against the Indianapolis Colts next Sunday morning. Indianapolis also got their first win of the season over division rival Houston Texans today. They lost to the Ravens and Chiefs the last two weeks, so they were also given a tough opening schedule to start the season by the league. title: Commanders report card: Team grades in NFL Week 3 win vs. Seahawks
summary: What a freaking win.   And what a turnaround from a week ago, when our Week 2 Commanders report card started with: “What an absolute disaster.”  The Commanders went from a devastating loss to Dallas where Jayden Daniels got hurt to beating the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 33-31 seven days later.   What a turn. […]
full_text: What a freaking win. And what a turnaround from a week ago, when our Week 2 Commanders report card started with: “What an absolute disaster.” The Commanders went from a devastating loss to Dallas where Jayden Daniels got hurt to beating the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 33-31 seven days later. What a turn. No way that happens without resolve, resilience and (come on, admit it) good coaching. The Commanders would’ve been 0-3 without all that. While Washington still sits at 1-2, there’s a big break between those records. “I knew coming into this that we were going to be tested,” Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told on-site reporters during his postgame press conference . “The 0-3 test and the 1-2 test – both don’t sound great on paper but they feel a lot different. We didn’t need belief but we needed to execute it and give ourselves a real good shot at it. “For the guys who are stepping in and being able to deliver, that’s a really big deal.” The Commanders were not perfect by any stretch, but they were tough and competed like heck. Let’s dig into some of those performances in this Week 3 Commanders report card: Rushing offense We knew it was going to be tough sledding against the Seahawks front seven, which had allowed 3.7 yards per carry heading into Week 3. The Commanders were inefficient as heck, with 2.6 yards per carry . It was important that Washington stayed committed to it, to the tune of 32 carries overall. And, when Washington absolutely had to have it on the victory-securing final drive, the run game came through. Rachaad got 19 yards on third-and-9 that forced Seattle to burn all its timeouts. Then, on the next third down, with a chance to ice, it Marcus Mariota kept it on a read option and got the first down that led to victory formations. Let's give an atta boy to John Bates on this one. Knocked TWO guys off the spot to clear a path for Mariota. https://t.co/tqFiUZEPfP — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 27, 2026 That took gumption and helped secure the game. Grade: C-plus Passing offense We know who Mariota is at this point. The veteran backup quarterback will get you in the right play. He’ll push the ball down the field, yet protect the football, even with an unspectacular completion percentage. That’s exactly what Mariota did, completing 19-of-31 passes for 183 yards, but…with three touchdowns and no picks. Terry McLaurin was a monster in this one, with six catches for 77 yards and a score on nine targets. Rookie Antonio Williams had some regrettable moments (a dropped touchdown, a TD-negating penalty) that he’ll learn from. Mariota connected with nine different receivers on the game, getting everyone involved. The Commanders allowed three sacks but generally seemed to protect Mariota well despite injuries to Sam Cosmi and a new center Lucas Patrick with Nick Allegretti moving to guard. The stats weren’t otherworldly, but Mariota made it work when it mattered most in Sunday’s win. Grade: A-minus Rushing defense We naturally think of creative pressure being the signature of a Daronte Jones defense, stopping the run may be this group’s calling card. They allowed 2.4 yards per carry against a Seahawks team that can get after it on the ground, making every run hard with a strong push up front, fast linebackers and a secondary committed to stopping the run. These are all pluses for Washington as we move forward. Grade: A Passing defense Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the known as the NFL’s best receiver for a reason. He couldn’t be stopped even when the entire DMV knew he’d be targeted, something clear on a late Seahawks touchdown drive that kept things close. The Commanders were able to pressure Darnold somewhat – they had five QB hits – but never sacked him. The penalty on K’Lavon Chaisson – you know which one I’m talking about — was an absolute farce. Cornerback Amik Robertson was a force to be reckoned with, but secondary can’t be considered good allowing 379 yards and four passing touchdowns. Mike Sainristil barely played but still made a fatal mistake. He’d be relegated to special teams if Washington had better options. Washington has faced three good passers to this point, but there are too many explosives, too many completions to tight ends and not enough plays on the ball to this point. The takeaways are a plus, and interceptions by Sonny Styles and Kain Medrano’s pick-six (and the magnitude of them) saves this phase from another awful grade. Grade: C Special teams Drew Stevens came up huge at the end of the first half with a 57-yard field goal and punched another through from 36 (though he did miss an extra-long extra point). Tress Way was so close to placing one within the 5-yard line had Tyler Owens not slid over the goal line, but he dropped three punts inside the 20. The return game didn’t have many shots to get going. Grade: B Coaching We’ll see how things looked on film review, but my gut says offensive coordinator David Blough called an excellent game. He worked well with Mariota and found ways to get so many involved. The third-down runs mentioned above were excellent calls. Daronte Jones emphasized turnovers and applied the pressure required to get them. He’s working with a lackluster secondary but is finding ways to stop the run consistently. And say what you want about head coach Dan Quinn, but he got Washington through a rough week where the sky seemed to be falling and beat the Super Bowl champs. That’s culture, right there. Grade: A-plus
author: Scott Bair

title: Sonny Styles, Kain Medrano at center of Commanders takeaway explosion
summary: Dan Quinn has a takeaway board outside of his office at the Commanders training complex highlighting defenders creating turnovers.   It was, as Washington’s head coach put it, “devastatingly empty.”   He’ll have some big plays to put on the board after Sunday’s 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. After failing to take the ball away […]
full_text: Dan Quinn has a takeaway board outside of his office at the Commanders training complex highlighting defenders creating turnovers. It was, as Washington’s head coach put it, “devastatingly empty.” He’ll have some big plays to put on the board after Sunday’s 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. After failing to take the ball away in the first two games, they had three (plus a turnover on downs inside the 2-yard line) in this one. The first two were generated by first-round pick Sonny Styles. The last one came from backup linebacker Kain Medrano, who had a fourth-quarter pick-six to help secure the improbable victory. “The whole defensive emphasis was to get after the ball,” Styles said. “We went through the first two weeks with no turnovers. …That’s how you win games.” Let’s start the takeaway discussion with Styles, the No. 7 overall pick and athletic freak expected to make an immediate and profound impact. He certainly did in this one, as a team’s primary defensive catalyst. Check out the stat line: five tackles, an interception, a forced fumble, two passes defensed and a quarterback hit. Styles punched the ball free from Eric Saubert right near the goal line, but the Seahawks tight end recovered it. There were more big plays on the way. A Sam Darnold pass ricocheted off Tim Settle’s helmet in the third quarter and Styles picked it off. SONNY STYLES INTERCEPTION 📺 #SEAvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/iv9cWR33Es — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 27, 2026 “He’s capable of producing the ball, based upon his speed and length,” Quinn told on-site reporters in his postgame press conference. “For that to come to fruition, I thought that was a big deal.” Styles came through in more subtle ways as well. He covered Price well deep down the sideline for a PBU, in a way that few other linebackers can. Sonny Styles with the PBU 🔥 @SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F6KiZsymMY — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Styles is also helping his team from a mental standpoint. He has worn the green dot since Frankie Luvu got hurt in Week 1 and done well with it. And, even in a moment where he deserved glory, Medrano mentioned that Styles made a pre-snap check that helped set up his pick-six. “We’re hunting certain things, man, and he made the right check,” Medrano said on the Commanders postgame show. “We were all on the same page and that put me in the right spot.” OWEH WITH THE PRESSURE….KAIN TO THE HOUSE!!!!! 📺 #SEAvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/7jfhys1A4q — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 27, 2026 Medrano deserves some praise for stepping in after Leo Chenal suffered a scary neck injury . The second-year pro earned his first NFL defensive snaps and made the most of them with that huge interception. “I was on the tight end and about to get the PBU, and he just stepped in front of me,” Styles said. “I’m like, ‘Oh, my gosh,’ as I’m running down the sideline with my hands up. It was a crazy play and I’m glad he was able to make it.”

title: Key takeaways from Washington Commanders Week 3 win over Seattle Seahawks
summary: BOX SCORE News has been kind to the Washington Commanders in the aftermath of Jayden Daniels’ dislocated left elbow. All things considered, anyway.   We first heard that surgery wasn’t on the table and that injured reserve wasn’t being considered. Then came a more definitive timeline, with NFL Network reporting that Daniels could be back […]
full_text: BOX SCORE News has been kind to the Washington Commanders in the aftermath of Jayden Daniels’ dislocated left elbow. All things considered, anyway. We first heard that surgery wasn’t on the table and that injured reserve wasn’t being considered. Then came a more definitive timeline, with NFL Network reporting that Daniels could be back within three weeks . While those are pluses, the Commanders are still 0-2 and must survive a little while without Daniels. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota would have to lead that charge into Week 3 and against the Seattle Seahawks and a bit beyond. Turning the home opener into the season’s first win was borderline essential despite a tough early schedule. The Commanders were super competitive and often the better team, but it didn’t prevent a tight fourth-quarter finish. That’s when the Burgundy and Gold performed well under pressure. Mariota, Sonny Styles and Washington’s defense came up huge to secure a 33-31 victory over the Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium. Here are some key takeaways from Washington’s duel with the Seahawks after watching it live: Marcus Mariota comes through Quarterback play wouldn’t be the only factor in Sunday’s final result. It takes a whole team effort to beat the defending champs. Yet the Commanders wouldn’t stand a chance without Marcus Mariota being poised, in control and finding moments to assert himself. He did that from the jump. The Commanders looked comfortable with him calling signals and found moments to take what was given and others to push the ball down the field. That included this tight-window touchdown pass to Treylon Burks: 🎯🎯🎯 📺 #SEAvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/ckX0p1kOPK — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 27, 2026 Mariota’s stat line was, well, pretty darn good. He completed 19-of-31 passes for 183 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. He took multiple plays to the line of scrimmage and picked the right one. He kept Washington in sync and kept offensive coordinator David Blough’s playbook open. The veteran found also found Terry McLaurin in key moments, none bigger than a contested 30-yard explosive score in the third quarter. WENT UP AND GOT IT. TERRY TOUCHDOWN 🙌 📺 #SEAvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/CLDeeVJobP — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 27, 2026 Mariota also had an explosive touchdown pass taken away by penalty and another by an Antonio Williams drop. Moments like those led to a tight finish, with Washington inside the red zone with six minutes left. They left with just a field goal. He went to the locker room later and returned with a two-point lead and roughly three minutes to preserve it. The Commanders converted one third down with a gutsy Rachaad White run and another with Mariota’s huge run to ice a huge victory. Big-time performance by Marcus Mariota and the #Commanders . pic.twitter.com/mRxbv2Ak18 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 27, 2026 Commanders defense came to play Washington’s defense couldn’t stop much of anything in a Week 2 loss against Dallas, leading coordinator Daronte Jones to talk a ton about needing better communication that would lead to more pressure and improved coverage. He got all that and a few turnovers, paced by an excellent Sonny Styles showing. The No. 7 overall NFL draft pick had a forced fumble that Washington recovered and turned into a touchdown. Then Styles had an interception snatched from the sky in the second half that set up the McLaurin touchdown. SONNY STYLES INTERCEPTION 📺 #SEAvsWAS FOX pic.twitter.com/iv9cWR33Es — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 27, 2026 The Seahawks still found a way to tie it 24-24 early in the fourth quarter, erasing a two-touchdown second-half deficit. The Commanders broke the tie with a field goal and the Seahawks were driving until linebacker Kain Medrano made the play of his early NFL career , intercepting Sam Darnold for a pick-six returned 50 yards for a touchdown. KAIN MEDRANO PICK-SIX! pic.twitter.com/FMEhMeUWsa — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 27, 2026 There was a missed extra point following a unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, creating a nine-point lead that could be bested with a touchdown and a field goal. The Commanders followed that by allowing a quick touchdown, a nightmare scenario that kept things tight. Mariota finished it off, but the defense came up huge with three takeaways that turned into 21 points. Key injuries piling up The second quarter scene was somber after linebacker Leo Chenal suffered a neck injury while tackling Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson. He was down for a long time before being placed on a stretcher and carted off the field. It was a scary situation for the Commanders, who huddled around their fallen teammate. Entire Washington sideline was on the field as medical staff tended to Leo Chenal and loaded him onto the cart. The crowd started chanting “LE-O! LE-O!” as they drove to the tunnel. Chenal was moving his arms. pic.twitter.com/tXX6Mp9LNZ — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) September 27, 2026 That was a blow to a linebacker corps already working without Frankie Luvu (groin) and Jordan Magee (hamstring; on IR) and a defense also operating without safety Nick Cross (internal/illness). Top cornerback Trey Amos has been on IR all year and isn’t terribly close, with all that testing Washington’s defensive depth. Core special teamer Kain Medrano took over for Chenal, last week’s leading tackler, which illustrates the depth concerns Washington’s battling right now. He took that opportunity and got a pick-six after some earlier missed tackles. As an update, Pam Oliver reported on the FOX broadcast that Chenal was able to move his extremities while with his family, but was taken to a local hospital as a precaution. What were your takeaways from this game? Let us know in the comments below:

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, top pick, more

The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.
