title: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
full_text:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season  featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback  Drake Maye  and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back  Jahmyr Gibbs . Commanders backup quarterback  Marcus Mariota  also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

 Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart , while the Browns won their second straight game.

 The late window was filled with close games, with all four contests separated by a touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter. The Ravens-Cowboys matchup was the most exciting of the bunch in Rio de Janeiro, ending on a time-expiring, winning field goal by Baltimore's  Tyler Loop . The Sunday night game was a classic, with the Broncos overcoming a 16-point halftime deficit to stun the Rams in the final minute in Denver.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

 
 Jump to: 
 LAR-DEN | BAL-DAL 
  LV-NO | MIN-TB |  ARI-SF 
 SEA-WSH  |  CAR-CLE |  CIN-PIT 
 TEN-NYG  |  LAC-BUF |  HOU-IND 
 NYJ-DET  |  NE-JAX | KC-MIA 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 ATL-GB 

 
 

 

 Denver 30, L.A. Rams 26 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Broncos 
 Another wild comeback in the books, but can the Broncos continue to survive their chronic slow starts? The Broncos are 2-1 despite the first halves of their first three games being an exercise in offensive pain. The Broncos were held scoreless in the first two quarters Sunday night and have scored only 10 first-half points this season. The defense held Los Angeles to 1-of-3 in the red zone in the first two quarters, keeping the Broncos close enough for a second-half offensive surge. All-Pro safety Talanoa Hufanga had two interceptions, a pick-six and the game-sealing pick on the final play, but this penchant for close calls might come back to haunt Denver.

 What to make of the QB performance: Bo Nix continues to show two personalities. He was out of sorts in the first half, completing 6 of 12 passes for 53 yards and nearly threw an interception. Same quarterback, different story in the second half. Nix once again bounced back despite a second-half interception. The Broncos scored on two of their first three possessions of the second half to tie the score after trailing by 16 points, and Nix led Denver to the winning score with 47 seconds left, capping a 65-yard drive with a 1-yard QB sneak for a touchdown. -- Jeff Legwold 

 Next game: at 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Rams 
 Will Puka Nacua's return fix the Rams' red zone woes? The Rams' offense moved the ball well in the first half against the Broncos, gaining 273 yards, but struggled to convert in the red zone. The Rams were 1-of-4 in the red zone Sunday, with the lone score coming on a 5-yard touchdown pass from Matthew Stafford to tight end Tyler Higbee near the end of the first quarter. On the other two drives, the Rams had to settle for field goals. Nacua has missed the past two games but is expected to be back for Week 4 against the Eagles.

 Key stat to know: In the first half, Davante Adams had four catches for 71 yards on five targets when matched up against Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II , whom Adams called "one of the best DBs in the league." Adams gained 71 yards in the first half, the most Surtain has given up before halftime in his career, according to ESPN Research. Adams finished the game with seven catches for 137 yards. -- Sarah Barshop 

 Next game: at Eagles (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Kyren Williams has had back-to-back games with 34 more rushing yards than expected and at least 15 fantasy points, strengthening his role as the Rams' primary back after Blake Corum totaled 22 carries in Weeks 1-2. Williams remains a weekly fantasy RB2, even with the Eagles up next. -- Cockcroft 

 

 

 Baltimore 34, Dallas 31 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Ravens 
 Did the Ravens exorcise their penchant for fourth-quarter collapses? Lamar Jackson and the Ravens gave an authoritative response to the "same old Ravens" narrative.  Tyler Loop 's 56-yard field goal with no time remaining lifted Baltimore to an improbable comeback. With seven seconds remaining, Jackson completed a 26-yard pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers , who was a game-time decision because of a hamstring injury . It was redemption for Loop, whose errant 44-yard field goal attempt ended Baltimore's playoff hopes last season. Over the past six seasons, the Ravens have lost an NFL-worst 15 games when leading through three quarters. But they found a way to win Sunday.

 Stat to know: With two touchdowns, running back Derrick Henry became the oldest player (32 years, 166 days) in NFL history to score six touchdowns in the first three games of a season. His 34 career games with multiple rushing touchdowns are the most among active players -- 16 more than the next-closest players ( Josh Jacobs and Jonathan Taylor with 18). -- Jamison Hensley 

 Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 

 Cowboys 
 Is this any different than the Cowboys' past two seasons? The Cowboys showed moxie to come back from an 11-point deficit, but ultimately, couldn't hold on. Why? A defense that was worn down and worn out. With 7:29 left, the offense had a chance to run down the clock but held the ball for only 1:44. Similar to 2024 and 2025, the Cowboys are 1-2 after two games. The comeback showed some fight, but now they won't get back to work until Tuesday due to traveling back from Brazil. Can Brian Schottenheimer's team make sure this isn't a repeat of the past two seasons, when they finished 7-10 and 7-9-1?

 Key stat to know: The Cowboys are supposed to have a big-play offense, but Dak Prescott did not have a completion of more than 13 yards until the third quarter. On the go-ahead drive, he hit CeeDee Lamb for a 49-yard bomb from the Dallas 6-yard line. Before the completion to Lamb, Prescott had just one attempt of 20 or more yards and was attempting just 6.2 air yards per attempt. He averaged 7.4 in Weeks 1-2. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: at Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Ravens backup TE Matthew Hibner caught both of his targets for 23 yards and a touchdown (10.3 fantasy points) on an end zone throw from Jackson. Hibner has run a total of only 23 routes over his first three games, but he projects as a potential insurance policy for starter Mark Andrews , who briefly left the game because of a hand injury.  -- Bowen 

 

 

 Las Vegas 35, New Orleans 27 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Raiders 
 With Kirk Cousins playing well, will Fernando Mendoza have to wait longer than expected? The Raiders know Mendoza's time to be the starter is looming, but he might have to wait a little longer. Cousins has the Raiders at 3-0 and has played well. Against the Saints, Cousins completed 22 of 33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. He has thrown nine touchdowns in three games, and the team has fully embraced him as a leader. There's still no need to rush Mendoza on the field.

 Key stat to know: Las Vegas scored 30-plus points in a game for the first time since its 63-21 win over the Chargers in Week 15 of 2023. The Raiders have scored at least 25 points in three straight contests. The Raiders scored more than 25 points only once during the 2025 campaign under former coach Pete Carroll.

 Best quote from the locker room: "It's a 17-game season, so we can't be happy or satisfied with this win," Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said. "Put ourselves in a good position. We know what's coming…

title: Ravens' jab at Cowboys after win in Rio leads Week 3 trolls
summary: The Baltimore Ravens followed up their last-second victory over the Dallas Cowboys with a petty post.
full_text:
The long travel for an international game can make a victory even sweeter. In the Baltimore Ravens ' case, it made the postgame troll just that much better.

 

 The Ravens defeated the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in Rio de Janeiro following a last-second field goal by Tyler Loop . It marked the NFL's first game in Rio, and it surely lived up to the hype.

 With the score tied, Baltimore received the ball with seven seconds remaining. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson connected with wide receiver Zay Flowers for 27 yards to set up a 56-yard boot from Loop. The kicker nailed it, giving Baltimore the win and a happy flight back home.

 On Wednesday, Jackson was asked if he expected the Cowboys to have a large contingent of fans in Rio since they are known as "America's Team." The quarterback said, "This is America, that's Brazil, so we'll see." The Ravens remembered the moment. They shared a video of running back Derrick Henry dashing past defenders toward his throne, while quipping that Baltimore is "Rio's team now." Flowers also said postgame : "We are Brazil's team."

 

 Here are other top trolls from Week 3.

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers 30, Cincinnati Bengals 27 
 An early-season AFC North clash predictably went down to the wire.

 Facing a three-point deficit with 2:15 left in the game, the Bengals received possession and started driving. They reached the Steelers' 38-yard line, but Pittsburgh defensive tackle Derrick Harmon sacked quarterback Joe Burrow , resulting in a fumble the Steelers recovered to win.

 Ever the trollers, the Steelers wouldn't pass up on the opportunity to poke fun at their division rivals with cats being the theme. The Steelers posted a victory image with the caption: "meoW," a video of a cat doing a viral dance and another cat photo captioned: "raWr."

 

 

 Washington Commanders 33, Seattle Seahawks 31 
 Washington defeated the Seahawks on Sunday, snapping Seattle's 13-game win streak. The Commanders entered the game with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center due to Jayden Daniels ' elbow injury.

 Mariota delivered by throwing for 183 yards and three touchdowns. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold started for the first time since an oblique injury forced him out in Week 1. Darnold had 379 passing yards and four touchdowns but two interceptions -- the latter of which resulted in a pick-six with 3:57 left in the game.

 The Commanders went straight to trolling after the win. They shared a video from the hit comedy show "The Office" where Jim delivers coffee to Dwight, who can pick it up only with his toes and ends up spilling the hot drink on himself. In this case, Jim is the Commanders, delivering an "L" to Dwight, the Seahawks.

 

 
 Buffalo Bills 24, Los Angeles Chargers 16 
 Buffalo stormed back to defeat Los Angeles and remain undefeated.

 The Bills began the fourth quarter down 13-10 and fumbled immediately. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert then threw an interception three plays later, which the Bills capitalized on by scoring a touchdown to go ahead for good. They iced the win with a final drive with 1:56 left in the game.

 Los Angeles is known for its elaborate social media posts when announcing its upcoming season's schedule. This year, it posted a Halo-themed video , which Buffalo referenced in its postgame jab.

 

 

 Las Vegas Raiders 35, New Orleans Saints 27 

 It's a 3-0 start for Las Vegas for the first time since 2021 following a road win against New Orleans.

 Las Vegas went ahead 35-27 with 6:22 remaining in the fourth then forced consecutive Saints fumbles to clinch its win. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins threw for 248 yards and three touchdowns, while tight end Brock Bowers showed out in his season debut with 10 receptions for 116 yards and a score.

 While playing in the Big Easy, Las Vegas seemingly picked up on the region's dialect. The Raiders emphasized their 3-0 start in a postgame caption, spelling out "Three & Eaux!" in a reference to Louisiana Cajun culture.

 

 
 Atlanta Falcons 35, Green Bay Packers 14 
 Atlanta is a winner for the first time this season following an emphatic "Thursday Night Football" performance in Green Bay.

 The Falcons put up 498 yards of offense, outscoring the Packers 35-7 after falling behind 7-0 midway through the first quarter. In his first start of the season, Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr . threw for 256 yards and one touchdown, while running back Bijan Robinson had 213 total yards and two scores.

 The big victory came with multiple trolls aimed at the Packers, including a spin on the "Go Pack Go" chant and a reference to rapper T-Pain's "Wiscansin" lyric.

title: Ravens' Rio trio: The players who helped Jackson to walk-off win
summary: Here are the other three players who overcame adversity to help Jackson produce one of the wildest finishes in Ravens history.
full_text:
Inside the Baltimore Ravens ' emotionally charged locker room in Rio de Janeiro, quarterback Lamar Jackson wanted to deliver a message following Sunday's 34-31 walk-off win over the Dallas Cowboys . 
 
 "We had all this adversity going on and we conquered," Jackson told his teammates. "This is the start of the season right here." 
 
 Jackson and the Ravens redeemed themselves by battling back after letting another fourth-quarter lead disappear, which is a trend that has haunted this franchise for years. 
 
 
 Last week, Jackson's interception sealed a fourth-quarter collapse to the New Orleans Saints . On Sunday, after Baltimore failed to hold an 11-point lead, Jackson put the Ravens in position to win by throwing a pass that traveled 36.4 yards in 1.6 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. 
 
 With only seven seconds remaining on Sunday, he didn't take a knee to run out the clock in regulation and instead threw a 27-yard pass that set up Tyler Loop 's winning, 56-yard field goal as time expired.  
 
 "I was prepared for overtime," Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith said, "and then Mr. Houdini [Jackson] made the play." 
 
 Here are the other three players who overcame adversity to help Jackson produce one of the wildest finishes in Ravens history: 
 
 

 
 
 Tyler Loop 
 
 
 Leading up to Sunday's game, rookie punter and holder Ryan Eckley came up with an idea. 
 
 "You know what would be sick is if we hit a game winner," Eckley said. "We go knee-slide in the end zone." 
 
 Loop replied, "Dude, there is no way. I feel like I am going to face-plant." 
 
 After drilling his first career winning kick, Loop sprinted to the opposite end zone as the entire team raced after him. Then, at one of the most storied soccer stadiums, Loop struck the Cristiano Ronaldo signature celebration in which he jumps and lands with arms outstretched while shouting "Siu!" 
 
 The Ravens showed their support for Loop as he lined up for the kick. Jackson yelled encouraging words from the sideline, where teammates felt Loop was going to come through. 
 
 "I thought he was going to make it," running back Derrick Henry said. "I wasn't even doubting [anything]. I knew he was ready; I could just tell." 
 
 Loop's finest moment in the NFL came after a tumultuous offseason. His only previous attempt at a game-winning field goal came in last season's finale, when his 44-yard field goal went wide right and ended the Ravens' season eight months ago. Then, after Loop's uneven preseason, the Ravens signed kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad as competition. 
 
 Now, after Moody was cut earlier this month, Loop has solidified himself with the Ravens, making 5 of 6 field goals (83.3%). This was the Ravens' first winning field goal from 50 yards or longer since September 2021, when Justin Tucker 's 66-yarder beat the Detroit Lions . 
 
 "The amount of flak that [Loop] faced at the end of last year, [he] just put his head down, never complained, just worked his butt off this whole season," safety Kyle Hamilton said. "For that moment to happen like that, on this stage, is pretty cool. The celebration was dope, too." 
 
  
 
 
 
 Zay Flowers 
 
 
 The Ravens wide receiver revealed a secret about his injured left hamstring after the game. 
 
 "I knew I was going to be able to play earlier in the week," Flowers said. 
 
 Although it wasn't a surprise to Flowers that he played, it caught others off guard to see him suit up after he missed Baltimore's only two full practices of the week. Flowers, who was considered a game-time decision, was limited to 17 snaps but still led the Ravens with 84 yards receiving on five catches. 
 
   
 
 This marked Flowers' return after aggravating his left hamstring in the first half of the season opener. 
 
 Flowers' impact on Sunday was felt in the fourth quarter, when he made three receptions for 55 yards. His biggest play was getting open over the middle of the field and catching a 27-yard pass to get Baltimore into field goal range. 
 
 "If some of us might be slow to get started in the game, you just see him blazing past people, and it is like, you better wake up, [and] you have to get on his level," Jackson said. "So, it was wonderful to have Zay back out there. That man -- we call him 'Sonic' from now on because he is amazing."  
 
 
  
 
 
 
 Olaivavega Ioane 
 
 
 It was a couple of weeks ago when Ravens assistant offensive line coach Shawn Flaherty suggested to Ioane, their rookie first-round pick, that he get some reps at center. 
 
 Ioane, the No. 14 pick in this year's draft, was glad he did because he found himself snapping to Jackson in the fourth quarter. Injuries to starter Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and backup Ethan Pocic (left knee) led to Ioane moving from right guard to center. 
 
 "It is unfortunate how it happened, but you just got to step up and be ready for the moment," Ioane said. 
 
 Minter didn't provide any injury updates on Gwyn and Pocic after the game. If both can't play Sunday against the Tennessee Titans , Ioane may have to start at center despite little experience there. 
 
 During his Penn State career, Ioane lined up at center for 17 of his 2,149 college snaps. 
 
 "For a rookie to be in that situation, [Ioane] stepped up and didn't flinch," Henry said. "[He] stepped up and did what we needed to do for us to be able to get in position to win."

title: Big Week 3 losses: Seahawks, Pats, Texans, Chargers, Panthers
summary: The Pats got blown out. The Seahawks lost to a QB2. The Panthers couldn't overcome injuries. The Chargers and Texans fell to 0-3. What now for five of last season's playoff teams?
full_text:
For the second time in three weeks, the opening window of the Sunday afternoon slate of NFL games delivered a delicious bowl of chaos. While Week 1 served up a record number of points, Week 3 brought upsets and heartbreaking defeats for teams that had lofty expectations heading into this season. Five teams that made the playoffs in 2025 lost games in crushing fashion.

 Three of them -- the Chargers, Panthers and Texans -- held leads in the fourth quarter but couldn't hold them. A fourth -- the defending Super Bowl champ Seahawks -- lost to an 0-2 Commanders team that was down to its backup quarterback. And a fifth -- the defending AFC champ Patriots -- were blown out and appear to have secretly replaced their MVP candidate QB from a year ago with a startled, overwhelmed facsimile of Drake Maye . (The Rams also blew a 16-0 lead to the Broncos on Sunday night , but that was a narrow loss on the road to a team that also made last season's AFC title game.)

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 Today, I'm going to break down those five losses from teams that expected to be winning most of their games this season. Which defeat was most painful? Which raised the biggest questions about what happens next? I'll go from most crushing to least ominous, starting in Duval County, where the Jaguars (another 2025 playoff team) had no trouble stomping all over the Patriots.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Chargers | Panthers | Patriots 
 Seahawks | Texans 

 
 

 

 New England Patriots 
 Lost 35-6 to the Jaguars 

 On one hand, there's nothing unrealistic or shocking about the Patriots losing to the Jaguars in Jacksonville. On the other, unlike the other four games I'll talk about, this loss wasn't particularly close. While Mike Vrabel & Co. might feel like they played better than the final score indicated and lost 10 points on sloppy play in the red zone and a missed field goal, the Patriots aren't building on what they put together in 2025. They look like they've gone back in time to the first half of the 2024 season, when Drake Maye was a rookie, Vrabel was out of football and a half-dozen dismal plays per game typically doomed them to losses.

 

 Since A.J. Brown went down in the second half of the Week 1 loss to the Seahawks , the Patriots have looked like a completely different offense. Maye was playing well in that game, continuously taking checkdowns and small profits. With Seattle quarterback  Drew Lock being summoned to play on short notice with  Sam Darnold 's early injury and the Seahawks struggling to score, that was a logical way for the Patriots to try to win.

 Instead, Maye threw three interceptions to turn that game, all on throws he never should have considered making. He was better against the Steelers in Week 2 but badly underthrew a pass on a crosser that was intercepted by linebacker Patrick Queen , one play after he had escaped pressure and found Romeo Doubs on the sort of scramble drill creation Maye had excelled with last season.

 And on Sunday against the Jaguars, Maye continued to unnecessarily put the ball in danger. His first interception was a disaster -- a throw offensive coordinators try to pry out of their quarterbacks after they turn pro. Booting to the right on the same fast-to-the-flat concept so many teams are running these days, Maye's first option, running back Rhamondre Stevenson , was taken away. Under pressure from Foyesade Oluokun , Maye realistically should have thrown the ball away on a third-and-goal situation and either lived to try on fourth down or picked up three points. Instead, he threw against his body to Hunter Henry , and  Travis Hunter  made the interception. It was the wrong risk at the wrong time.

 Maye also had the ball slip out of his hands in the middle of a dropback for a fumble, an issue he attributed after the game to a  bloody football . He lost another one at the end of a scramble, costing the Patriots another drive that ended inside the 5-yard line. And while his second interception might have been more on wide receiver Kyle Williams  (who didn't offer much physicality on a contested catch situation on the sideline), it certainly feels like Maye is pressing or trying to make too much happen.

 Still, Maye does have stretches when he's playing well. He was fine for most of the game against the Seahawks and made several important plays, mostly with his legs, late in the contest to get the Pats back in a position to tie or take the lead before his final ill-advised pick. And there were multiple third downs in this game against Jacksonville where Maye was pressured, escaped, reset and delivered a ball that either hit his receiver in the hands or went through them. Mack Hollins taking a taunting penalty after a 9-yard catch on third-and-10 down 28-3 in the fourth quarter isn't on Maye and probably wasn't a great idea (even if that's a score that might feel comfortable for Patriots fans).

 Is it just that the Patriots are playing tougher opponents than they were in 2025? I think that's certainly part of the issue. If you go back to 2025, Maye wasn't turning the ball over this often against top-tier competition. Including the postseason, Maye played nine games against top-15 defenses by DVOA last season, and he threw eight interceptions in those nine games. We don't know if the Seahawks, Jaguars and Steelers will finish as elite defenses in 2026, but he now has six picks in three games and might have been lucky to leave Jacksonville without adding even more to that total.

 

 I would say more specifically that Maye was not punished anywhere near as often for putting the ball into dangerous situations a year ago. Remember that he had multiple wideouts run remarkable catch rates over expectation  last season, with Kayshon Boutte , Stefon Diggs  and Hollins all coming in 10-plus percentage points ahead of expected. I'm not saying that Maye was careless, but when he did take risks, he typically came out unscathed.

 Maye completed 47.7% of his tight-window throws in 2025, which was 11.4 percentage points better than his expected completion percentage on those attempts. He threw four picks on 88 tight-window attempts. This season, he has more interceptions (three) than completions (two) on tight-window passes, going 2-of-9. And after running a plus-9.0% completion percentage over expectation across all his throws in the 2025 regular season, Maye is at plus-2.4% this season.

 The offense around him hasn't been as effective, in part because of injuries. The Patriots were the sixth-healthiest offense in the league last season by adjusted games lost. This year, they've already lost Brown to a high-ankle sprain and right guard  Mike Onwenu  to a fractured ankle . They miss Diggs, who was one of the NFL's most efficient receivers on a per-snap basis, even if the Patriots used him for only about 50% of their offensive snaps. Hollins has instead been their unlikely lead receiver, as Doubs has been inconsistent. (Doubs' drop against the Seahawks before a Maye interception looms in the memories of Patriots fans.)

 The word that keeps coming to mind when I watch this version of Maye, though, is inexperienced. That ability to calibrate decisions? To know when and where to put the ball in danger? To be a quarterback who both simultaneously makes the best possible decision within a play and the broader context of the game situation? It's tough to watch Maye and say he has a great handle on that part of the job right now. And that's not completely uncommon for a QB in Year 3. But Maye was perhaps able to cover over those issues last season while playing from ahead so often against teams that couldn't make him pay.

 The Patriots might consider acting accordingly now. They're already calling designed runs on first down nearly 57% of the time this season, the ninth-highest rate in the NFL. Could they lean even more into the run on early downs? Could they up the play-action rate to create easy completions for Maye when only…

title: How to bet Eagles-Bears on MNF: Analysis, tips and favorite plays
summary: Odds and analysis to help you bet Eagles-Bears on "Monday Night Football."
full_text:
Week 3 of the NFL season wraps up with the Philadelphia Eagles visiting the Chicago Bears on "Monday Night Football."

 Despite outplaying and outgaining the Tennessee Titans for the bulk of last week's contest, the Eagles struggled to put them away in their 24-20 win in Week 2. A pair of costly interceptions and constant pressure from a Jeffery Simmons -led front allowed the Titans to hang around.

 Ultimately, however, the Eagles' superior ball control, running back depth and DeVonta Smith 's aerial dominance proved too much for Tennessee. The 2-0 Eagles are looking to fly to Chicago and stay perfect on prime time. Expect OC Sean Mannion to establish the running game early while picking on Chicago's banged up-secondary.

 

 Truly meme-worthy, the Bears went from being the highest-scoring offense in the league in Week 1 to ineffective against Brian Flores' Vikings defense in Week 2. From the weather to the game play, Chicago was sloppy. Bogged down by eight penalties and two turnovers, the Bears failed to find any sort of flow or convert on several red zone opportunities.

 The lone offensive bright spot came via the team's RBs. D'Andre Swift led the squad with 99 scrimmage yards, while Kyle Monangai averaged 4.7 yards on 10 carries. Without Caleb Williams on the field, Chicago figures to rely on the aforementioned duo. It's a move that the Eagles will likely anticipate, however, and they will load the box against Chicago, daring the opposition's replacement quarterback to throw the ball downfield.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 Injuries have significantly affected line movement in this matchup. With Saquon Barkley sporting a "cowboy collar" and Case Keenum projected to be the Bears' starter under center, the public appears to be bracing for a low-scoring affair. The game total opened at 43.5 points but has since dropped to 41.5. With Philadelphia failing to catch steam before the fourth quarter in consecutive outings and Chicago limited at QB, the under is a prudent -- but exceedingly boring -- wager to make.

 

 More interesting is the spread. Despite going 2-0, the Eagles are 0-2 against the spread to begin the season. 

 If Chicago can clean up the penalties (the forecast calls for a low chance of rain), lean on the ground game and force Jalen Hurts into costly mistakes, the Bears should cover. It sounds like a lot, but with a coach who knows how to get buy-in, given the home-field advantage and noting the Eagles' slow starts, Chicago can keep it close.

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 

 Kalif Raymond  OVER 24.5 receiving yards   (-110) 

 Raymond has led the receiving corps in targets (14), catches (13) and receiving yards (124). Registering at least 40 yards in back-to-back weeks, the former Lion has shined as a high-volume safety valve. Raymond's success has come via well-paced underneath grabs, as evidenced by his 5.0 aDOT. Given Keenum's reputation as a game manager, and noting his average arm strength, Raymond's deployment should be unaffected and, perhaps, further highlighted.

title: Where has Bears TE Colston Loveland been this season?
summary: The tight end has one catch and faces a tough Eagles defense on MNF. With no Caleb Williams, can he get going?
full_text:
The day before the Chicago Bears hosted the Minnesota Vikings in their home opener Sept. 20, The Wiener's Circle -- a famous Chicago hot dog stand -- offered free dogs if Bears tight end Colston Loveland scored two touchdowns.

 Bears fans were unable to cash in as Loveland finished with just one catch -- not a TD -- for 3 yards. Fantasy managers also have been unable to cash in with Loveland, who was the No. 3 tight end drafted -- after the Arizona Cardinals ' Trey McBride and the Las Vegas Raiders ' Brock Bowers -- but is being started in only 48% of ESPN leagues heading into Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ABC/ESPN ).

 Loveland's 3-yard catch in the 9-3 loss to the Vikings was his only reception on five targets this season, and that includes a 59-37 win against the Carolina Panthers in Week 1. That's not what was expected from last year's No. 10 overall pick out of Michigan who led the NFC North champs with 713 receiving yards and 58 receptions.

 "Everyone in here wants the ball," Loveland said. "We're here for a reason, and we want to make plays and help our team win.

 "But there's other ways to make plays on the ground in the run game. I'm just doing what I'm asked. There's going to be opportunities, so I've just got to take full advantage when it arises."

 

 Could those opportunities come against the Eagles? Philadelphia's defense has allowed the third-fewest receptions (six) and second-fewest receiving yards (42) and is tied for the third-fewest targets faced against tight ends (nine) after wins against the  Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans .

 "It's kind of a bit of a chess match knowing he's a guy that can take off at any moment because that's what he did last year," Eagles linebacker Chance Campbell said.

 Loveland totaled 597 receiving yards over his final 10 games last season. He was a favorite target of Caleb Williams , but the quarterback will be inactive Monday night because of a hamstring injury. Case Keenum will start.

 Keenum threw Loveland his first TD of a training camp that served as a daily highlight reel for the tight end. The offseason seemed to foreshadow another season of high usage in coach Ben Johnson's offense.

 Instead, it has been just the opposite.

 Loveland's disappearance is multifaceted. Offensive coordinator Press Taylor and Johnson are adamant Loveland is built into the game plan, often as the primary receiver. The ball just has yet to find him.

 Loveland has been on the field for 86.6% of the Bears' offensive snaps through two games -- the highest of any offensive player other than Williams or a lineman.

 

 "We had plenty of opportunities against Carolina, just couldn't quite feed them the way we wanted to," Johnson said.

 Against a Vikings defense that sent a blitz at Williams on 78% of his dropbacks, Loveland and other tight ends were called on to max protect on a rainy afternoon when wet conditions affected the passing game.

 "All of our pass catchers, all of our skill players, everybody that we're anticipating to be active, has plays on that game plan," Johnson said. "Some more than others, but we're actively looking to get everybody involved."

 Another reason behind Loveland's lack of production is the way defenses are playing him. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Loveland has faced double coverage on 7% of his routes, which is the highest rate in the NFL regardless of position with a minimum of 40 routes. While he has been targeted only five times, Loveland is averaging significantly less separation, down from 3.7 yards of separation on his targets in 2025 to 2.1.

 "Obviously I want the rock and I want to go make a play for the team," Loveland said, "but as long as I'm doing what I'm asked and I'm getting open, I feel like there's times I'm open on tape, it's just kind of not finding me.

 "Which is how it is, whether it's pressure or whatever. Things just aren't clicking, but it's going to come at some point."

 

 It's not that Loveland hasn't made an impact this season. Late in the third quarter against Carolina, despite not getting any targets in the first half, he stayed focused. On one of D'Andre Swift 's TD runs, Loveland blocked Jaelan Phillips and drove him into the ground.

 "When you've gone through three quarters and you have no touches so far and you continue to fight and continue to help others get in the end zone ... you wouldn't have known if he had 10 catches or zero catches at the end of the game in the locker room from the way he was, as excited as he is for the offensive success," Taylor said.

 This is nothing new for Loveland, who battled a slow start as a rookie. It wasn't until Week 8 when he reached the end zone, scoring two touchdowns against the  Cincinnati Bengals  on a day when he hauled in six catches for 118 yards.

 "I don't think he's a guy who's begging for touches or anything like that," Eagles safety Michael Carter II  said. "When he gets the ball in his hands, he's dangerous. ... I'm sure he'll get his touches eventually but hopefully not against us."

 ESPN Eagles reporter Tim McManus contributed to this report.

title: Joe Burrow, Bengals can't 'close it out' against Steelers
summary: Special teams gaffes and a Burrow fumble late in the fourth sealed Cincinnati's outcome.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Slightly hunched forward and still mostly in his game attire, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow sat and stared at the inside of his locker as he pondered a game that slipped away.

 The Pittsburgh Steelers  (2-1) halted Cincinnati's strong start to the season with a 30-27 victory on Sunday at Acrisure Stadium. And as Burrow pondered what went wrong in a game Cincinnati (2-1) came close to winning, the theme of self-inflicted mistakes jumped out more than anything else.

 And as the Week 3 loss showed, those types of errors can be the undoing of a team with championship aspirations.

 "Like last week with the penalties, we just can't shoot ourselves in the foot like that," Burrow said. "You can't win in this league when you do that. It's really hard. It's really hard. We could have overcome it, but it's hard to win like that."

 Cincinnati was looking to start the season with three wins for the first time since Zac Taylor took over as the team's coach in 2019. Against Houston in Week 2, the Bengals won despite being called for 12 penalties.

 One week later, the mistakes by the entire team were too costly.

 

 A Bengals defense that had big moments in the season's first two games surrendered 411 yards to a Pittsburgh squad that failed to score a touchdown a week earlier. Special teams had two major blunders: a roughing-the-kicker penalty that extended a drive culminating in a touchdown and a muffed punt recovered by the Steelers.

 That fumbled punt led to  Chris Boswell 's 33-yard field goal with 2:15 left that proved to be the winning margin.

 "We just didn't close it out," Taylor said. "That's all there is to it. We had opportunities in all three phases in the fourth quarter. We didn't get it done."

 That includes the offense.

 Following Boswell's field goal, Cincinnati got the ball back and still had two timeouts. The Bengals worked into kicker  Evan McPherson 's range when disaster struck.

 After Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon got a quick pressure, Burrow wriggled out of a potential sack and tried to throw the ball away. But Harmon recovered and knocked the ball loose before Burrow could get rid of it, leading to a fumble the Steelers recovered to ice the game.

 "Trying to take a shot at the end zone," Burrow said of his final play. "Trying not to take the sack, trying to get the ball out. Fumbled it."

 

 It unspooled an otherwise sterling day from Cincinnati's star quarterback -- 28-of-37 passing for 282 yards and three touchdowns, including one on fourth down that put Cincinnati ahead 27-24 with 13:29 left.

 And it also uncovered another trend that has been lurking over the years. Dating to the start of the 2024 season, Burrow is tied for the league lead in lost turnovers in the fourth quarter or overtime, per ESPN Research. He has thrown eight interceptions and lost four fumbles in that span.

 When it comes to fixing some of the self-inflicted mistakes, Burrow believes he knows the elixir for Cincinnati's woes.

 "Guys have to take ownership of their roles, take ownership of themselves and just be smart situational football players," Burrow said.

 For a team that doesn't just want to snap a three-year postseason drought but also wants to be a championship contender, Sunday's setback at Acrisure Stadium was nonetheless a little more palatable to swallow than previous disappointments.

 "It's something that we can control," Bengals wide receiver  Ja'Marr Chase  said at his locker after the game. "It's in our hands, not out of our hands."

title: How are Cowboys reacting to third straight 1-2 start?
summary: Dallas finished 7-9-1 in 2025 and 7-10 in 2024 after winning one of its first three games. Will 2026 be any different?
full_text:
RIO DE JANEIRO -- Whenever and however the 2026 NFL season ends for the Dallas Cowboys , they will look back at Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens  in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro as a defining moment.

 The Cowboys are 1-2 for the third straight season. In 2024, they finished 7-10. In 2025, they finished 7-9-1.

 As elated as they would have been with a comeback victory against the Ravens, they walked out of Maracanã Stadium to their buses knowing they had a 10-hour flight back to Dallas with nothing but time to relive the pain of a last-second defeat.

 "We just got to lean on our brotherhood. We got to lean on the family that we've created. The trust," quarterback  Dak Prescott said. "This is one game. It's early in the season, thankfully. We're 1-2. We would love to be 2-1 going back, going home. We're not. It's a long season. ... After a loss you don't have no choice but to lock arms and run back into the fire and trust what you've done in your process.

 "And so hopefully it's one of the best things that happened for us. Hopefully, look back at this in a month or a couple months and say it was good."

 But they have no way of knowing that now.

 "I'm sure when I land," Prescott said, "I'll be just as pissed."

 

 The Cowboys were 2 yards away from pulling off a potential comeback victory that could have led to a season momentum boost. Then they were seven seconds away from forcing overtime.

 The emotional swings can be deflating.

 "Oh, I don't ever question these guys, man. Watch the way they play," Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I mean, this team doesn't have quit in them. They're hurting right now. I'm hurting. I felt like we made enough plays to go win the game, but we didn't. So give Baltimore credit for that. But at the end of the day, I hurt for the guys in the locker room. They put a lot into this. It's a long trip, but no one cares."

 The Cowboys can point to a number of plays that could have changed the outcome, beyond the last minute of regulation.

 On their first drive, they failed to score a touchdown from the Baltimore 1, settling for a field goal. In the third quarter, there was a controversial lost fumble from tight end Jake Ferguson and a blocked 59-yard field goal attempt from  Brandon Aubrey .

 The defense stopped running back  Derrick Henry  on fourth down in the first and fourth quarters, but they were unable to sack Lamar Jackson  or force a turnover.

 And after kicking off seven seconds left in regulation and the score tied at 31, the defense couldn't make a one-play stop, as Jackson connected with  Zay Flowers for 27 yards with one second left to give Tyler Loop the opportunity to win the game with a 56-yard field goal as time expired.

 

 "Every loss is heartbreaking," rookie defensive back Caleb Downs said. "It's not a good way to lose and we have things to fix."

 So, too, does the offense.

 When the Cowboys had the chance to take the lead late, they got to the 2-yard line with 23 seconds left after receiver  CeeDee Lamb drew a pass interference call, but a second-down false start penalty on tight end Luke Schoonmaker pushed the ball back to the Ravens' 7.

 With 14 seconds remaining, the Cowboys called a timeout after a Prescott scramble. Prescott's third-down pass to receiver  George Pickens was high and wide.

 "I probably overcoached [Prescott] on that because it had to go," Schottenheimer said. "With no timeouts, it had to go to GP or throw away."

 Prescott had regrets.

 "I probably should have just sat on it a little bit longer, sank on my back foot and just put it on that front pylon," he said.

 The Cowboys settled for the tying field goal from Aubrey, thinking they would go to overtime. After having Aubrey go for the touchback, the defense allowed the 27-yard completion with one second left.

 A year ago against the Green Bay Packers , one second remained on the clock in overtime that allowed the Packers to kick a tying field goal. One second remained this time, and the Cowboys lost.

 Schottenheimer said he was honest with the players in the postgame locker room.

 "I told them this one hurts, and I was sorry," Schottenheimer said. "I was sorry that we didn't find a way to win. I was proud of them, how hard they played, how many guys had to step up and make plays and move in and whatnot. It was back and forth. It was a hell of a football game if you didn't care who won. But I told them I was proud of them, but I also told them that it's supposed to hurt. We have to find a way to win football games."

title: NFL Week 3: Wild stats on the Texans, Saints, Chargers, more
summary: Coaching decisions costing the Texans? Milestones for a Commanders LB and Raiders-Saints TEs? A balanced Steelers offense? And the Chargers losing with five takeaways?
full_text:
If you had the Raiders at 3-0 and Texans at 0-3 after three weeks, good on you. The NFL is always wacky in September -- and never wackier than when Marcus Mariota leads the Commanders to a win over the Super Bowl champion Seahawks.

 Every Sunday, I'll find several of the coolest advanced stats from the day's NFL action to share with you -- stats to explain all the action and what it means. Some call them NFL Next Gen Stats. I call them Next Ben Stats: the data that might not make it on the broadcast but will make you a smarter fan (and laugh a little bit, probably).

 Let's start Week 3 's list with coaching mistakes that might have cost the Texans a much-needed divisional win.

 

 
 Jump to an eye-popping stat on: 
 Texans decisions | Jones up the middle 
 Rodgers time to pass | Styles impact 
 Chargers takeaways | Raiders-Saints TEs 

 

 
 

 3.6%: How much win probability the Texans lost when they kicked a field goal on fourth-and-4 
 That was via ESPN's model. The NFL Next Gen Stats model was even worse at 5.5%.

 The Texans are 0-3 for a lot of reasons, and clock and game management is a solid chunk of it. This particular fourth down came with Houston losing 16-7 with 7:36 remaining. The Texans knew they'd need a touchdown to get back into it but elected to instead kick the field goal from inside the 10-yard line.

 

 It looked like it worked out. Houston forced a fumble on the ensuing drive, then scored the go-ahead touchdown with Woody Marks . But with the score at 17-16, all the Colts needed to get back on top was a field goal. They ultimately got it to go ahead 19-17. But that wasn't the real concerning part -- it's how much clock Houston coach DeMeco Ryans let run on Indy's drive before using his timeouts. After a first-and-10 run of 5 yards from  Jonathan Taylor , the clock rolled from 1:04 to 0:29 (and an expiring play clock) ... and then Ryans called the timeout. Houston lost 19-17  after getting the ball back with just 11 seconds on the clock.

 This isn't the first questionable fourth-down call for Ryans. He opted to kick a field goal on fourth-and-1 from the Bengals' 40 in last week's loss , a decision that cost him 7.4% in win probability. Against the Bengals and the Colts, an early fourth-down run was stuffed, and those failures seem to cut Ryans' confidence in fourth-down decisions at the knees. It's often the case that defensive-minded head coaches default to punts and field goals, but in the case of a struggling offense such as the Texans' unit, it's even more important to go for fourth downs when near the end zone -- you're unlikely to keep getting back there!

 

 
 

 198: How many passing yards Daniel Jones had between the numbers 
 Consider that he had only 235 passing yards altogether in the win over Houston. Here are Jones' overall numbers throwing to the middle of the field: 20-for-25, 198 yards and one touchdown. Jones had a 113.0 passer rating there, and it was the eighth-most total dropback EPA (13.3) while throwing between the numbers in a game.

 The Texans' defense remains an overall good unit, but it has a clear weakness in the middle of the field. The injury to starting linebacker  Henry To'oTo'o  has put backups Jake Hansen and Wade Woodaz on the field, and that duo was getting hammered in coverage Sunday. When Azeez Al-Shaair had to miss time because of a groin injury, the Texans had no intermediate-middle presence to speak of in their zone looks.

 Ideally, a strong box safety such as  Reed Blankenship alleviates some of these concerns -- but Blankenship has had some big misses. All too easily, opposing quarterbacks can ignore  Derek Stingley Jr . and Kamari Lassiter on the outside. Jones had such a quick release hitting interior windows in this game, and it minimized the impact of the Texans' pass rush (as much as such a pass rush can be minimized).

 

 

 
 

 3.19: How many seconds  Aaron Rodgers  averaged to throw 
 That's his longest time to throw in a game for the Steelers. And it's an enormous, enormous leap from what he has typically done for Pittsburgh. Since the start of last season, he had averaged 2.73 seconds heading into this game, the fastest among all league passers. He was fearful of taking hits and too quick to go to his checkdown.

 Not on Sunday against the Bengals ! The Steelers looked like a balanced passing attack willing to use prolonged play-action dropbacks to push the ball downfield, and they found more success through the air than either the Texans or Buccaneers did against the Bengals as a reward for their aggression. Rodgers had five completions of at least 20 yards, tied for his most in a game for the Steelers. He had 15 attempts of at least 10 air yards -- also his most in a game for the Steelers.

 Pittsburgh also had a lights-out performance from its offensive line, both in pass protection and in the running game, which allowed for explosive rushes and kept Cincinnati defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II from taking over the game. Right guard ( Brock Hoffman ) and right tackle (first-round pick Max Iheanachor ) were new starters, and the personnel shift worked. Rodgers had time to dissect a Bengals secondary that likes to conceal coverages with clever rotations -- something a savvy vet like him can do with the appropriate amount of protection and aggression.

 

 
 

 3: How many games the Chargers have lost since 2015 in which they won the turnover margin by four or more 
 The rest of the NFL has two combined . The games in question:

 
 The infamous 2022 playoff loss to the Jaguars , in which the Chargers surrendered a 27-0 lead 
 A 2015 end-of-season catastrophe for a 4-11 San Diego team against an 11-4 Denver squad 
 The game we just watched them lose to the Bills 
 
 

 As I wrote Tuesday , the Chargers are a dysfunctional team across the board. Not even five Bills turnovers for a plus-4 overall margin could account for all of their errors. Justin Herbert threw a back-breaking pick against the goal line in the fourth quarter. Coach Jim Harbaugh didn't go for it on fourth downs when he should have ... then attempted a fourth-and-10 late in the fourth quarter he didn't need to try at all. The offense had five penalties in the first quarter, tying its fourth quarter in Week 1 for the most penalties by a unit in one quarter this season.

 Bad team. Takeaways are great, and I liked the play of the pass rush and rookie safety Genesis Smith to generate them. But they don't save a bad team.

 

 
 

 2,870: How many days it had been since a rookie LB last had an interception and a forced fumble in the same game 
 Shaquille Leonard did it Nov. 18, 2018, for the Colts. And  Sonny Styles did it Sunday for the Commanders.

 Want to know what a top-10 pick at off-ball linebacker looks like? Want to see what an upset of the Super Bowl champion Seahawks with a backup quarterback starting requires? The intersection of that Venn diagram is the play of Styles.

 He was a force in his third career game. His interception was the play of a centerfielder, tracking a tipped ball as it pop-flied through the air. His forced fumble was nearly a game-changing play -- he forced it at the 1-yard line and was unlucky to see it ricochet right back into the Seahawks' hands.

 It's the plays that didn't stuff the stat sheet that really impressed, though. Styles shot a gap to hit running back Jadarian Price  at the line of scrimmage in the first quarter, and cornerback  Amik Robertson took the opportunity to punch the ball out. In the second quarter, Styles tracked Price in man coverage on a wheel route -- a nightmare role for a linebacker -- but easily kept stride and swiped his way into a pass breakup without turning his helmet. That's his safety background showing up.

 

 The Commanders' defense didn't have a perfect day, but it made splashy plays when it mattered. Styles was a huge part of that effort. He looks like a cornerstone player in Washington.

title: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter through 2026 season
summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver  Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly.

 "You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will."

 Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30.

 How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

 

 

 

 Week 3 vs. New England Patriots 
 In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

 
 

 Week 2 at Denver Broncos 
 Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton . The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

 After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

 "We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

 "But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

 
 

 Week 1 vs. Cleveland Browns 
 Hunter started at cornerback and played 27 snaps on defense (55.1% of total defensive snaps) and four on offense (7.1% of total offensive snaps) against the Browns. On offense, he had one carry for 3 yards on a jet sweep and one catch for 8 yards on a screen pass. He has had at least one catch in every game in which he played (eight games) to this point. On defense, Hunter was targeted once on defense which resulted in a Deshaun Watson completed a 4-yard pass to KC Concepcion .

title: Chiefs' Mahomes perfect on play-action passes in win vs. Dolphins
summary: Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action attempts for 201 yards, including a touchdown, according to ESPN Research.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Patrick Mahomes ' opening snap in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins was perhaps his easiest pass of the season.

 Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs ' quarterback, took the snap under center and executed a play-action fake with running back Kenneth Walker III . When Mahomes released the ball, not a single defender was close to tight end Travis Kelce , who turned his wide-open catch into a 48-yard gain.

 For the remainder of the game, a 24-10 win for the Chiefs , Mahomes found teammate after teammate open for completion after completion on play-action passes. In total, Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action attempts for 201 yards, including a touchdown, according to ESPN Research. He also tied Russell Wilson (in 2020) for the most completions without an incompletion on play-action in the past 20 seasons.

 

 "It's helping out a ton," Mahomes said of the Chiefs' play-action attack. "I think people look at the stats and they see the touchdowns that Kenneth has and [rookie running back Emmett Johnson] when they're running the ball. But I don't think they really understand how the play-action and the movements [within the pocket] is really opened up in our offense. That's a credit to [the running backs] and the offensive line firing off the ball, run and pass.

 "I thought we did a great job with that."

 Last season, the Chiefs, who finished with a disappointing 6-11 record and missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, were one of the NFL's worst when using play-action. In 178 play-action snaps, the seventh most in the league, the Chiefs recorded just 977 passing yards from, ranking 20th, according to ESPN Research. The Chiefs even surrendered more sacks (nine) than they scored touchdowns (three).

 Coach Andy Reid hired Eric Bieniemy in late January to be the new offensive coordinator -- a role he held with the team from 2018 to 2022. In March, during the NFL's free agency period, general manager Brett Veach made the Chiefs' biggest offseason acquisition in signing Walker to a three-year, $43.05 million contract, including $28.7 million fully guaranteed.

 After Sunday's game, Mahomes has 329 passing yards, four touchdowns and one interception on play-action attempts. He also hasn't been sacked in 38 such snaps, according to TruMedia.

 

 Throughout the Chiefs' locker room Sunday, several offensive players praised Walker and Bieniemy for creating advantageous opportunities for larger passing gains.

 "It's opening up a lot, just knowing our run game has a huge impact," receiver Rashee Rice said. "When it's time for [pass catchers] to be called to make the play downfield when it looks like a run, we have to make that play."

 The opening snap was a perfect example. The Chiefs lined up with three tight ends and just two players -- Kelce and receiver Tyquan Thornton -- went out for a route. Once Mahomes executed his play-action fake with Walker, 10 of the 11 defenders for the Dolphins were behind Kelce, who ran a 15-yard corner route.

 "I think the fact I scrambled out to the right kind of got him open, which it wasn't necessarily supposed to happen like that," Mahomes said of his highlight with Kelce. "How the defensive line stunted, I was able to get outside. What got him opened the most was Tyquan running down the field. You have that speed running at you down the field, the safety got depth and the play action got the second-level [defenders] up and all of a sudden Travis is right there behind everybody."

 Every prominent skill player for the Chiefs had at least one memorable moment Sunday that was a byproduct of play-action.

 Inside the red zone, the Chiefs used one of their most effective plays in that area of the field, one that was prominent during Bieniemy's first stint with the team. Mahomes used play-action from under center and then completed a short shovel pass to Walker, who ran into the end zone with ease following the pulling block from left guard Kingsley Suamataia .

 

 Walker has scored four touchdowns and provided plenty of speed, elusiveness and dynamic ability after contact. In fact, Walker is the first player in the Chiefs' history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within his team's first three games of a season. His 442 scrimmage yards are also the second most in a Chiefs player's first three games.

 "The running game is getting the offensive line comfortable with getting downhill and really moving the line of scrimmage," Kelce said. "On top of that, just being in sync with [No.] 15 back there. I think [it's] Bieniemy, coming from Chicago [as the Bears' running backs coach] with even more of a downhill run game than what we've had in years past. Obviously, Kenneth Walker and EJ coming in and getting those yards early helps it out a lot."

 Late in the first quarter, the Chiefs used Walker as a decoy on a third-and-1 snap for Mahomes to find Thorton for a comfortable 17-yard pass.

 Mahomes' most impressive play-action completion was early in the fourth quarter, when he rolled to his right before throwing a perfect intermediate pass to tight end Noah Gray , who made the catch over linebacker Willie Gay Jr .

 "They played a lot of zone coverage, so I found a soft spot and Pat delivered a good ball," Thornton said of his highlight. "I just had to come down with it. [Against] zone, route depth and being on time is very important. I feel me and Pat have a good sense of timing and where he needs me to be."

 

 Before the season began, Reid and Mahomes knew and acknowledged that the Chiefs needed to improve their play-action passing attack for them to once again become one of the NFL's most potent offenses.

 Through three weeks, the Chiefs have made such strides. The Chiefs rank first in play-action usage (36%) after ranking 13th (25%) last season, according to ESPN Research.

 Last season, Mahomes had just 29 play-action attempts through three games. But this season, Mahomes has already recorded 30 play-action completions, the most in the league.

 "We're running the ball so well that defenses have to change how they play against us," Mahomes said. "We have to continue to do that, continue to run the ball and play-action off of that and keep defenses honest."

title: McCarthy exits Vikings as one of franchise's biggest draft busts
summary: J.J. McCarthy was the No. 10 pick in 2024 but played only 10 games before being traded to the Giants on Monday.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Less than two years ago, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell appeared on the "Rich Eisen Show" and uttered 12 words that will be dissected in Minnesota for years to come.

 "I believe that organizations fail young quarterbacks before young quarterbacks fail organizations," O'Connell said during the interview, which took place in September 2024. 

 Two years later, it's fair to ask: Does that explain Monday's news that the Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy for a fifth-round pick after only two seasons, 10 games and 243 pass attempts? Is that why McCarthy is now headed to the New York Giants to resurrect his career at an age -- 23 years, 9 months -- that makes him younger than most of the quarterbacks drafted this spring? Did the Vikings organization fail him?

 Or was McCarthy simply a spectacularly historic draft bust who wouldn't have made it no matter which organization drafted him?

 

 The truth is that no key player in this debacle -- arguably the biggest personnel miss in franchise history -- is without blame. 

 The general manager who drafted McCarthy, Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, was fired in January . He and O'Connell put McCarthy on the field before he was ready. And before anyone saw anything close to a finished version of the player, the team's remaining decision-makers -- O'Connell, former interim general manager Rob Brzezinski and new general manager Nolan Teasley -- rendered a final judgment on him. 

 Even owners Zygi and Mark Wilf absorb some of the responsibility. Their insistence on never taking a competitive step back usually provides fans with entertaining seasons, but it is not conducive to giving young quarterbacks sufficient time to develop. Sam Darnold took over when McCarthy missed his rookie season with a knee injury. McCarthy undeniably played better at the end of his 10-game stint last season than at the beginning, and in a more forgiving environment, O'Connell and Teasley might have had more patience. 

 In a conversation this summer, former Vikings coach Brad Childress recalled a standard articulated by Hall of Fame coach Bill Walsh and still makes sense today: Give a promising young quarterback 24 games -- one full season and a half of a second, in the days of a 16-game schedule -- before deciding the next steps. During the offseason, the Vikings added free agent Kyler Murray , who is now starting, pushing McCarthy to QB3 behind No. 2 Carson Wentz .

 

 McCarthy, for his part, made some clear mistakes beyond his obvious poor performance. His frenetic play style contributed to four injuries that limited his development, and it contributed to his status as the only quarterback in the NFL's modern draft era to be selected in the first round and miss his entire rookie season for health reasons. During his time in Minnesota, McCarthy suffered knee and ankle injuries, as well as a concussion, while running outside of the pocket. A hairline fracture in his right hand, meanwhile, occurred when he climbed the pocket -- unnecessarily, coaches believed -- and hit his thumb on the helmet of left guard Donovan Jackson . 

 Some of the missteps took place behind the scenes, revealing surprising levels of immaturity. One of them, sources said, was accelerating his knee recovery in the fall of 2024 -- before he was medically cleared to do so. The sources said that's why McCarthy developed swelling, which led to a second surgery. The procedure was successful, and all athletes push boundaries, but the episode left an impression inside the building.

 Another was sometimes working outside the offensive scheme and system in ways that prompted pushback from O'Connell. That assertion does not require unnamed sources to substantiate. O'Connell himself revealed an example during one of his weekly video interviews on the Vikings' website with team play-by-play announcer Paul Allen. 

 Speaking in December 2025, O'Connell recounted his interactions with McCarthy in postgame film sessions.

 "In certain times of the season," O'Connell said, "you would get a response of, 'I thought this player was going to do that,' speaking about a defensive player. Or, 'Hey, I played with [cornerback] Mike Sainristil at Michigan. He's real instinctive, he might try to do this.'"

 O'Connell said he responded by saying, "Stop. Just quiet your mind and let's not overthink anything other than, 'What is my job on the play in making good decisions and putting the ball in play?'"

 

 In 2025, McCarthy referred to a game-day alter ego he called "Nine." Later, in a Week 15 game last season at the Dallas Cowboys , McCarthy began a touchdown celebration five yards before he reached the end zone. McCarthy said afterwards that coaches told him in practice not to celebrate early, which he said made him more determined to do it during a game. 

 Anyway you look at it, McCarthy has been one of the bigger draft letdowns for a team before exiting in recent NFL history. According to the Elias Sports Bureau, he is one of four quarterbacks drafted in Round 1 in the past 25 years to start 10 or fewer games for the team that drafted them, joining Paxton Lynch , Trey Lance and Johnny Manziel , per Elias. And in Vikings history, he is one of four first-round picks -- at any position -- to play in 10 or fewer games for them. He joins safety  Lewis Cine (2022), defensive end  Dimitrius Underwood (1999) and running back Leo Hayden (1971) -- to play 10 or fewer games for the team.

 When a quarterback starts his career the way McCarthy did, criticism can come from all angles and eventually becomes contradictory. That was the case this summer, when sources said McCarthy told team officials he was uncomfortable with playing in the final preseason game because of an injured ankle. It was a 180-degree turn from 2025, when he drew the Vikings' ire for not promptly communicating some of his injuries. The most notable example came in Week 16, when pain in his injured thumb caused him to drop the ball in the pocket. The Giants recovered the fumble and returned it for a touchdown. 

 McCarthy now takes his place in the Vikings' tragicomic quarterback lore. They have tried drafting a quarterback in the first round four times since 1999, and all four have flamed out for various reasons. A catastrophic knee injury felled Daunte Culpepper in 2005. Christian Ponder was benched in 2013, his third season. Teddy Bridgewater was never the same after another catastrophic knee injury in the summer of 2016, prior to his third season. 

 The McCarthy era -- over before it really began -- was the most dramatic yet.

title: NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants
summary: Can J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? Did the Vikings get enough back? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
full_text:
Let's grade deals ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline , which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

 When grading trades, I evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

 Here's my take and evaluation of the  J.J. McCarthy  deal that kicked off trading season. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

 

 

 Vikings send QB McCarthy to Giants 
 Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy 
 Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

 Giants grade: C 
 Vikings grade: B+

 A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension , New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks.

 Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft.

 McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become Minnesota's starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good.

 McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for.

 

 During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray , but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz , too. That is a telling red flag.

 So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan.

 It is difficult to know from the outside which other backup quarterbacks would have been available, but McCarthy still does not seem like an ideal choice. Mac Jones and Spencer Rattler ought to have been the team's first calls (maybe they were). Kirk Cousins probably is off the board with the Raiders sitting at 3-0. Mitchell Trubisky might have been available, considering this already looks like a lost season for Tennessee. And I'm assuming  Gardner Minshew II  surely must be available, considering he sits in veteran no-man's land between Jacoby Brissett and rookie  Carson Beck  in Arizona. Stetson Bennett IV could have been an option, too, after the Rams selected Ty Simpson in the first round of this year's draft. I'll grant that some of those options have less upside than McCarthy.

 But the Giants' front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It's not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn't have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him!

 Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy's ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn't beat out Wentz. If he wasn't going to be the Vikings' backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not.
